**Speaking Style:** A whisper, clipped and cold, words used only when silence fails. Shinobi speak in code words and hand signs. Tell since the war: she signals, then waits a breath too long, listening for fire.
**Combat Role:** kunai from hiding, smoke, gone
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: holds the line; obeys the village; speaks in signals
Quirk: never fights fair

npcs.name: Votive Carver Old Morioka
npcs.info:
An old shipwright who carves the votive ships that hang from the temple rafters, one for every vow a sailor makes. In person: elderly shipwright carving a small votive ship.

**Home Ground:** Votive Hall at Temple of Safe Voyages, Saikai Free Port district.
**Speaking Style:** Slow, warm and full of sawdust; he talks to the little ships he carves. Slow, warm, sawdust-dry, talking to the little ships as much as to you. Tell: about the guildmaster's vow, the knife stops and so does his voice.
**Combat Role:** none; he throws his mallet and sits down.
**Relationship Hook:** Ask about the guildmaster's vow and he puts the knife down.
personality: Core: talks to his carvings; smells of cedar; squints at strangers
Quirk: remembers every vow

npcs.name: Votive Carver Old Morioka
npcs.location: Temple of Safe Voyages, Temple of the Unreturned
npcs.info:
The old shipwright after the war, who carves votive ships for the war's drowned faster than his hands can manage. In person: elderly shipwright; trembling hands; a half-carved warship.

**Home Ground:** Votive Hall, After the War at Temple of Safe Voyages, Temple of the Unreturned, Saikai Free Port district.
**Speaking Style:** Slow, warm and full of sawdust; he talks to the little ships he carves. Slow, warm, sawdust-dry, talking to the little ships as much as to you. Tell since the war: his hands shake worse when he carves a warship, and he talks to it more gently.
**Combat Role:** none; he throws his mallet and sits down.
**Relationship Hook:** Ask about the guildmaster's vow and he puts the knife down.
personality: Core: talks to his carvings; smells of cedar; squints at strangers
Quirk: remembers every vow

npcs.name: Wall Archer Fuyuki
npcs.info:
An archer of the wall walk who has stood the night watch for six winters and counts every shadow on the snow. In person: tired demon-hunter archer with a longbow; torches.

**Home Ground:** Wall Walk at The Long Night Wall, Hinode Hold district.
**Speaking Style:** Sharp and tired, an archer who counts shadows in the snow out loud. Sharp and tired, counting shadows out loud between sentences. Tell: about the north gate she stops counting.
**Combat Role:** arrows from the wall, fast and many.
**Relationship Hook:** Stand a night watch with her and she tells you about the gate.
personality: Core: counts shadows; never sits; watches the gate at night
Quirk: breathes in forms

npcs.name: War Widow Sakiko of Kagegi
npcs.location: Kagegi Village, Burned at the Edge
npcs.info:
A Kagegi shinobi's widow, twenty-nine, who took her husband's place on the mission board and asks for the hardest Hayate missions. In person: young woman; kunoichi widow; short black hair; dark gear with a white mourning cord; sharpening a kunai.

**Home Ground:** Mission Hall, After the War at Kagegi Village, Burned at the Edge, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Flat and clipped, a shinobi's report about her own grief. A flat shinobi report about her own grief. Tell: when the elders are named she adds one word too many, on purpose.
**Combat Role:** kunai and shadow, at night.
**Relationship Hook:** Bring her proof of the Regent's contract and she will strike the Regent's house for you.
personality: Core: sharpens his kunai, not hers; never speaks his name; watches the elders
Quirk: takes the hardest missions

npcs.name: Ward-Ring Fox
npcs.info:
A white fox with two tails who sits on the cracked ward stone and asks travellers riddles in a lady's voice. She leads the wrong answer into the marsh and the rude into a night of illusions. A stock foe, one of many. In person: white two-tailed fox spirit sitting.

**Speaking Style:** A lady's voice, teasing and musical, each riddle ending on a rising note, a laugh behind a sleeve. Tell: rudeness turns the music cold and very polite.
**Combat Role:** foxfire and an illusion over the stones
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: laughs behind her sleeve; hates rudeness; keeps promises
Quirk: asks a riddle

npcs.name: Ward-Ring Fox
npcs.location: Old Ward Stones, The Broken Ring
npcs.info:
A white fox with two tails who no longer sits on the cracked stone: two more stones broke the night the Vaults did, and she walks the ring at dusk keeping out whatever is coming through. A stock foe, one of many. In person: white two-tailed fox spirit; muddy fur; a scorched tail tip; a broken ward rope in her teeth.

**Speaking Style:** A lady's voice, teasing and musical, each riddle ending on a rising note, a laugh behind a sleeve. Tell since the war: she asks her riddle, then answers it herself before you can.
**Combat Role:** foxfire and an illusion over the stones
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: laughs less; hates rudeness; keeps promises still
Quirk: asks a riddle

npcs.name: Ward-Stone Guardian
npcs.info:
A lion-dog of grey stone the size of an ox, cracked down one flank, that wakes when the ring is crossed. It guards the old ward ring against anyone, the Bureau's own included, since the ward broke. A stock foe, one of many. In person: stone guardian; huge cracked grey stone lion-dog komainu standing.

**Speaking Style:** A grinding roar with no breath behind it, stone on stone, then dead silence. Tell: before a true ward it lowers to a deep rumble and is still.
**Combat Role:** jaws and weight, never leaving the ring
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: circles the ring; never leaves the stones; bows to a true ward
Quirk: roars without breath

npcs.name: Ward-Stone Guardian
npcs.location: Old Ward Stones, The Broken Ring
npcs.info:
A lion-dog of grey stone, cracked now on both flanks, that circles the broken ring day and night and no longer tells friend from foe. A stock foe, one of many. In person: stone guardian; huge grey stone lion-dog komainu; cracked down both flanks; moss burned black; one stone eye missing.

**Speaking Style:** A grinding roar with no breath behind it, stone on stone, then dead silence. Tell since the war: it roars at friend and foe alike, then stands still a long moment after.
**Combat Role:** jaws and weight, never leaving the ring
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: circles the ring; never leaves the stones; bows to nothing now
Quirk: roars without breath

npcs.name: Warden Hunter
npcs.info:
A hunter in furs and chains who tracks beast hosts across the ice. Warden hunters bring back every host they find, and do not much care whether alive. A stock foe, one of many. In person: fur-clad bounty hunter with seal-chains; cold.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, practical. Flat and practical, the talk of someone who never sleeps in a town. Hunters name the beast before the threat. Tell: when a host is a child, the flatness breaks.
**Combat Role:** chains and patience
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: oils her chains; pays informers; never sleeps in a town
Quirk: counts bounties

npcs.name: Warden Hunter
npcs.info:
A hunter in furs and chains with fewer beast hosts to track: the Vaults cracked and the bound beasts are loose of their hosts; she hunts what came out of the fissure. A stock foe, one of many. In person: fur-clad bounty hunter; seal-chains frosted blue; a broken seal-talisman on her belt; cold.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, practical. Flat and practical, the talk of someone who never sleeps in a town. Hunters name the beast before the threat. Tell since the war: she counts the beasts on the seal-master's list under her breath.
**Combat Role:** chains and patience
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: oils her chains; hunts beasts; never sleeps in a town
Quirk: counts bounties

npcs.name: Warden Seal-Carrier
npcs.info:
A Vault Warden in grey furs over plate armour with a sealing chain and an iron seal-case on his back. Seal-carriers walk the glacier road carrying fresh seals north and kill anyone who tries to open the case. A stock foe, one of many. In person: vault warden; small iron box bound with chains and paper talismans strapped to his back.

**Speaking Style:** Cold and exact, counts and orders only. Tell: asked about the seals, he answers a different question.
**Combat Role:** a sealing chain that binds, then a short blade
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: counts markers aloud; speaks only to Wardens; kills quickly
Quirk: never sets the case down

npcs.name: Warden Survivor Hokuto
npcs.area: Road to the Vaults, After the War
npcs.info:
A Vault Warden, forty, the only man of his patrol to come back out of the Vaults after the crack. He sits at the road's head and warns anyone going in. In person: vault warden; frostbitten face; heavy furs; a coil of paper-tagged chain wound around one forearm; hands empty.

**Home Ground:** Road to the Vaults, After the War at Shirokawa, Behind the Fissure, Hyoga Reach district.
**Speaking Style:** Low and level, a man who speaks of the Vaults as if they were listening. Low and level, as if the Vaults were listening. Tell: at dusk he says his patrol's names, and stops at one he cannot say.
**Combat Role:** seal-chains and a spear.
**Relationship Hook:** Go into the Vaults with him and he will show you where it spoke.
personality: Core: never sleeps facing the Vaults; says his patrol's names at dusk; eats little
Quirk: warns everyone

npcs.name: Warden Takumi of the Horn
npcs.info:
A warden of the watch fort's barracks who leads the patrols to the vaults and out onto the Frozen Battlefield. In person: weary armoured warden; spear; map of vaults.

**Home Ground:** Barracks at Wardens' Watch Fort, Hyoga Reach district.
**Speaking Style:** Firm and weary, a warden who speaks like he is giving orders even at dinner. Firm and weary, orders even in small talk. Tell: about the Battlefield he lowers his voice like a confession.
**Combat Role:** a warden's spear and shield, unbreakable.
**Relationship Hook:** Ask about the horns and he tells you what turned its head on the Battlefield.
personality: Core: orders even at dinner; checks the seals twice; hates being ignored
Quirk: sleeps in armour

npcs.name: Watch-Captain Okami Tenzen
npcs.info:
A lean, wolf-faced captain of the capital's watch with a pipe always in his teeth, who keeps order at the Tournament Grounds and has one technique he trusts. In person: adult man; lean; sharp wolfish face; slicked-back black hair with a loose strand; dark watch uniform with a haori; a long pipe; katana held level; tournament pavilions behind.

**Home Ground:** House Pavilions at Tournament Grounds, Miyako Plain district.
**Speaking Style:** Clipped and dry, a pipe in his teeth; he gives orders as statements and never repeats one. Clipped statements around a pipe stem, never a question, never repeated. Tell: the Regent's name and he takes the pipe out to say nothing.
**Combat Role:** a crouched one-handed thrust stance, the off hand aimed along the blade; one lunge, then another.
**Relationship Hook:** Take his thrust and stay standing.
personality: Core: speaks in statements; never repeats an order; watches hands, not faces
Quirk: pipe always in his teeth

npcs.name: Watch-Captain Okami Tenzen
npcs.info:
The capital's watch captain after the war, who keeps order in the Regent's field camp on the Tournament Grounds, pipe still in his teeth. He has killed more men with the Fang thrust in the war than in all the duels before it. In person: lean, wolf-faced captain; slicked-back hair greyer; dark watch uniform with a camp marshal's sash; a long pipe; katana held level.

**Home Ground:** House Pavilions, After the War at Tournament Grounds, The Regent's Camp, Miyako Plain district.
**Speaking Style:** Clipped and dry, a pipe in his teeth; he gives orders as statements and never repeats one. Clipped statements around a pipe stem, never a question, never repeated. Tell since the war: his pipe goes out when he speaks of Sekigane, and he does not relight it.
**Combat Role:** a crouched one-handed thrust stance, the off hand aimed along the blade; one lunge, then another.
**Relationship Hook:** Take his thrust and stay standing.
personality: Core: speaks in statements; never repeats an order; watches hands, not faces
Quirk: pipe always in his teeth

npcs.name: Watcher Heita
npcs.info:
The young watcher on Watchfire Hill, nineteen, who keeps the fire ready to warn the south of a raid. In person: anxious young watcher; scarf; hunter's coat; guarding a big unlit watchfire pile.

**Home Ground:** Watchfire at Watchfire Hill, Hinode Hold district.
**Speaking Style:** Fast, defensive and upset; he swears he lit it. Fast, defensive and upset, talking over himself to swear he lit the beacon. His voice climbs when doubted. Tell: when asked exactly when he lit it, he gives a different hour each time.
**Combat Role:** none; he runs for the Hold.
**Relationship Hook:** Believe him and look at the footprint.
personality: Core: checks the fire every hour; jumps at noises; keeps the footprint covered
Quirk: swears he lit it

npcs.name: Watcher Heita
npcs.info:
The watcher on Watchfire Hill after the war, twenty-one, who keeps the fire burning every night now: it means the line still holds. He is older than his years. In person: watcher; scarf; hunter's coat; a great fire burning beside him.

**Home Ground:** Watchfire, After the War at Watchfire Hill, The Lit Hill, Hinode Hold district.
**Speaking Style:** Fast, defensive and upset; he swears he lit it. Fast, defensive and upset, talking over himself to swear he lit the beacon. His voice climbs when doubted. Tell since the war: he gives the same hour every time now, and his voice does not climb.
**Combat Role:** none; he runs for the Hold.
**Relationship Hook:** Believe him and look at the footprint.
personality: Core: checks the fire every hour; jumps at noises; keeps the footprint covered
Quirk: swears he lit it

npcs.name: Watcher Nezumi
npcs.info:
A young Kagegi watcher, twenty-two, who signals the village with mirrors from the cedar watchtower and narrates everything he sees out loud. In person: cheeky watcher shinobi; messy hair; sharp eyes; dark gear; a signal mirror.

**Home Ground:** Mirror Platform at Kagegi Outer Watchpost, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Bored, fast and cheeky; he narrates what he sees through the mirrors. Bored and fast, narrating what he sees like a running commentary, cheeky asides included. He chews something constantly. Tell: when his paymaster is mentioned the commentary stops and he starts looking at the exits.
**Combat Role:** kunai from height, then running.
**Relationship Hook:** Catch him spying and he becomes your spy.
personality: Core: polishes mirrors; bets on everything; hides coins in the tower
Quirk: narrates out loud

npcs.name: Watcher Nezumi
npcs.location: Kagegi Outer Watchpost, Watchpost on the Line
npcs.info:
A Kagegi watcher after the war, twenty-four, who signals the war-line from the outer watchpost and narrates everything he sees, quieter. He was found selling Kagegi movements to a house and spared. In person: watcher shinobi; messy hair; sharp frightened eyes; dark gear; a signal mirror.

**Home Ground:** Mirror Platform, After the War at Kagegi Outer Watchpost, Watchpost on the Line, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Bored, fast and cheeky; he narrates what he sees through the mirrors. Bored and fast, narrating what he sees like a running commentary, cheeky asides included. He chews something constantly. Tell since the war: his running commentary leaves out the Regent's colours, as if he did not see them.
**Combat Role:** kunai from height, then running.
**Relationship Hook:** Catch him spying and he becomes your spy.
personality: Core: polishes mirrors; bets on everything; hides coins in the tower
Quirk: narrates out loud

npcs.name: Watchfire Frost Spirit
npcs.info:
A pale shape of drifting snow with a woman's face, circling the watchfire and hissing at it. Frost spirits are drawn to the watchfire's warmth and freeze whoever tends it. A stock foe, one of many. In person: frost spirit; pale woman's face.

**Speaking Style:** A cold hiss like wind through a crack, words whispered between gusts. Tell: close to the fire she sighs like someone remembering warmth.
**Combat Role:** a whiteout and a freezing touch
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: hisses; freezes breath; flees fresh wood
Quirk: circles the fire

npcs.name: Watchfire Frost Spirit
npcs.info:
A pale shape of drifting snow with a woman's face that no longer hisses at the watchfire: it burns every night as the sign the line holds, and she circles it as if guarding it. A stock foe, one of many. In person: frost spirit; pale woman's face; embers frozen in her drifting snow.

**Speaking Style:** A cold hiss like wind through a crack, words whispered between gusts. Tell since the war: she circles the fire sunwise now, as if keeping a vigil.
**Combat Role:** a whiteout and a freezing touch
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: guards the fire; freezes scouts; remembers warmth
Quirk: circles the fire

npcs.name: Watchfire Yamauba
npcs.info:
A crone at the watchfire who asks travellers to share the fire and a story. Watchfire yamauba keep the fire lit for the Hold and eat those who will not share. A stock foe, one of many. In person: yamauba; old crone with wild white hair.

**Speaking Style:** Cackling and warm, asking for a story. Tell: a selfish answer turns her voice cold.
**Combat Role:** a lunge across the fire
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: shares fire; eats the selfish; hates demons
Quirk: asks for stories

npcs.name: Water-Reader Minamo
npcs.info:
A reader of the black pool who keeps a hut at the Water Sanctum's shore and arranges the pebbles in rings the pool disturbs. She says what the water shows and never what it means. In person: adult female; slight and still; long wet-dark hair loose; grey eyes; a plain pale blue kimono damp; calm.

**Home Ground:** The Shore at Water Sanctum, The Five Sanctums, in the Otherworld.
**Speaking Style:** Quiet, even and unhurried, with long pauses she does not fill; she talks the way a pool reflects. Quiet and even, long pauses left unfilled, saying what the water shows and never what it means. Tell: noon mentioned and the pause does not end.
**Combat Role:** none; she steps into the mist and is not there.
**Relationship Hook:** Sit with her at the shore for an hour without speaking; she tells you what the pool showed while you sat.
personality: Core: leaves long pauses; rebuilds the pebble rings; never explains what the water means
Quirk: will not look at the pool at noon

npcs.name: Wayside Tanuki
npcs.info:
A round-bellied raccoon dog that poses as one more stone jizo until a traveller passes. Wayside tanuki trick travellers out of their lunch and lead the stubborn into the ditch. A stock foe, one of many. In person: tanuki trickster; round-bellied raccoon dog pretending to be a stone jizo statue.

**Speaking Style:** Chuckling and smug. Smug chuckling between every phrase, a belly-drum thump for emphasis, sing-song boasts. Tell: caught out, it squeaks and blusters about a misunderstanding.
**Combat Role:** a trick, a drum, a dash into the bushes
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: laughs at its own tricks; loves sake; turns leaves into coins
Quirk: holds very still

npcs.name: Wayside Tanuki
npcs.location: Wayside Jizo Shrine, Jizo of the Lost Sons
npcs.info:
A round-bellied raccoon dog posing as one more jizo in a red bib among the statues dressed for lost sons; it tricks thieves, not travellers, now. A stock foe, one of many. In person: tanuki trickster; round-bellied raccoon dog; a red bib like the statues.

**Speaking Style:** Chuckling and smug. Smug chuckling between every phrase, a belly-drum thump for emphasis, sing-song boasts. Tell since the war: it holds very still whenever a woman comes to the statues, and drums softly when she leaves.
**Combat Role:** a trick, a drum, a dash into the bushes
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: laughs at thieves; loves sake; turns leaves into coins for the mothers
Quirk: holds very still

npcs.name: Waystation Clerk Sumi
npcs.info:
Clerk of the grey banner waystation in Haibara, forty, who posts the curse-hunters' bounties on the blight's horrors and keeps a wall of names of hunters who did not come back. In person: mature woman; tired waystation clerk with a hunter's charm; grey robes; before a wall of names and a bounty board; ash.

**Home Ground:** Grey Banner Waystation at Haibara, Ashfall Blight district.
**Speaking Style:** Flat, tired, kind underneath; she says 'come back alive' to everyone and means it. Flat, tired and low; 'come back alive' as she hands a bounty over, once, never as filler. Tell: when her husband's killer is named, she stops breathing and speaks very fast.
**Combat Role:** a curse-hunter's short blade she never puts down.
**Relationship Hook:** End the horror that killed her husband and she gives you his blade.
personality: Core: says 'come back alive'; touches the wall of names; never smiles
Quirk: keeps a hunter's charm on her wrist

npcs.name: Waystation Clerk Sumi
npcs.epithet: Clerk of the Wall of Names
npcs.area: Grey Banner Waystation, After the War
npcs.info:
Clerk of the grey banner waystation after the war, forty-two, who posts the curse-hunters' bounties and keeps a wall of names of hunters who did not come back. The wall has run onto a second wall. In person: tired clerk with a hunter's charm; grey robes; two walls of names behind her; ash.

**Home Ground:** Grey Banner Waystation, After the War at Haibara, On the Grudge Line, Ashfall Blight district.
**Speaking Style:** Flat, tired, kind underneath; she says 'come back alive' to everyone and means it. Flat, tired and low; 'come back alive' as she hands a bounty over, once, never as filler. Tell since the war: she says 'come back alive' twice now, the second time to the second wall.
**Combat Role:** a curse-hunter's short blade she never puts down.
**Relationship Hook:** End the horror that killed her husband and she gives you his blade.
personality: Core: says 'come back alive'; touches the wall of names; never smiles
Quirk: keeps a hunter's charm on her wrist

npcs.name: Webbed Pit Omukade
npcs.info:
A giant man-eating centipede, long enough to coil the gully, with plates that turn a sword. Omukade hunt people and great serpents; even the earth spiders keep away from this one. A stock foe, one of many. In person: no humans; omukade; enormous segmented centipede with dozens of legs and dark armoured plates.

**Speaking Style:** A clicking rumble, a hundred legs in every pause. Tell: at a spitting sound it rears back.
**Combat Role:** a coil and a venom bite; spit on the point
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: clicks; hunts; hates spit
Quirk: coils

npcs.name: Weeping Cedar Jorogumo
npcs.info:
A beautiful woman in a web-pale kimono who plays a biwa under the cedar, her shadow too many-legged. She lures travellers with music, wraps them in silk and keeps them for winter. A stock foe, one of many. In person: beautiful woman; spider shadow.

**Speaking Style:** Sweet, slow, hungry. Sweet, slow and hungry, each word drawn out like silk, a plucked biwa note under the pauses. Tell: when she stops playing, her voice clicks.
**Combat Role:** a lure, silk, then the bite
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: never steps into sun; counts her guests; flatters
Quirk: plays to strangers

npcs.name: Weeping Cedar Jorogumo
npcs.location: Weeping Cedar, The Cedar of Many Nails
npcs.info:
A beautiful woman in a web-pale kimono who plays her biwa under a cedar nailed with dolls from every army, fat on a war's worth of curses and weeping sap with it. A stock foe, one of many. In person: jorogumo; beautiful woman; a sap-stained web kimono; a biwa with a broken string; a spider shadow larger than the tree.

**Speaking Style:** Sweet, slow, hungry. Sweet, slow and hungry, each word drawn out like silk, a plucked biwa note under the pauses. Tell since the war: she plays a war song now, and smiles at the soldiers who know it.
**Combat Role:** a lure, silk, then the bite
**Relationship Hook:** A foe for fights only, never a suspect.
personality: Core: never steps into sun; counts her guests; feeds on every nail
Quirk: plays to strangers

npcs.name: Widow Okiku of the Fields
npcs.info:
A farmer's widow who works her husband's paddy alone and cooks for the headman's house for rice. In person: tired young widow; rice fields outside.

**Home Ground:** Headman's House at Hundred Fields Village, Miyako Plain district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft and tired, a widow who apologises for the state of a house that is spotless. Soft and tired, apologies stacked one on another. Tell: showing the receipt, her voice steadies and hardens.
**Combat Role:** none; a hoe if cornered.
**Relationship Hook:** Ask about her husband and she shows you the paid receipt.
personality: Core: apologises for everything; works till dark; keeps a receipt in her sleeve
Quirk: keeps a spotless house

npcs.name: Widow Okiku of the Fields
npcs.location: Hundred Fields Village, The Flooded Fields
npcs.info:
A farmer's widow of the Hundred Fields after the flood, who works the half of her husband's paddy that is not mud and cooks for the Straw Mask patrol for rice. In person: tired young widow; muddy to the knees; a sickle; flooded paddies behind.

**Home Ground:** Headman's House, After the War at Hundred Fields Village, The Flooded Fields, Miyako Plain district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft and tired, a widow who apologises for the state of a house that is spotless. Soft and tired, apologies stacked one on another. Tell since the war: she has stopped apologising; she says the debt's figure aloud instead, every time.
**Combat Role:** none; a hoe if cornered.
**Relationship Hook:** Ask about her husband and she shows you the paid receipt.
personality: Core: apologises for everything; works till dark; keeps a receipt in her sleeve
Quirk: keeps a spotless house

npcs.name: Widow Tamaki of the Burned Fleet
npcs.info:
A sailor's widow on Lantern Row, twenty-eight, whose husband burned with the Mizuchi fleet at its moorings. She mends nets for the Brine Tide now because nobody else pays. In person: young woman; sailor's widow; tied hair; a man's navy coat too big for her.

**Home Ground:** Lantern Row, After the War at Saikai, The Debt Harbour, Saikai Free Port district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft and tired, a sailor's widow who apologises for the smell of the sea. Soft and tired, apologising for the smell of the sea. Tell: when the bought captain laughs nearby she pulls the net tighter.
**Combat Role:** none.
**Relationship Hook:** Bring the bought captain to the admiral and she will mend your nets for life.
personality: Core: wears her husband's coat; never takes Tide silver directly; watches the captain drink
Quirk: mends nets while she talks

npcs.name: Widow Toki
npcs.info:
An old widow who sells bait and mends sails at the harbour post, seventy, small and straight-backed, who has held the deed to a haunted island for thirty years and cannot give it away. In person: seventy; small and straight-backed; grey hair tied back with a blue cloth; deep sun lines; a faded indigo kimono with tied-back sleeves; a fishwife's apron; a twist of net.

**Home Ground:** Harbour Post at Saikai, Saikai Free Port district.
**Speaking Style:** Slow and practical, an old fishwife's plain words, a dry laugh at anything grand. Slow and practical, a fishwife's plain words with a dry laugh at anything grand, the creak of a net knot between sentences. Tell: when the lighthouse comes up she stops knotting and the laugh goes.
**Combat Role:** none; she throws the bait bucket and calls the harbour guard.
**Relationship Hook:** Sit down at her bait stall and she will tell you about the island nobody wants, and what it would cost to take it.
personality: Core: says the price first and the story after; feeds anyone who sits down; never raises her voice
Quirk: knots a twist of net while she talks and unknots it when she is done

npcs.name: Widow Toki
npcs.info:
The old widow at the harbour post's bait stall after the war, seventy-two, thinner, still straight-backed: the war took the harbour's young men and left her selling bait to soldiers. In person: small old fishwife; grey hair under a blue cloth; a black mourning band on one sleeve; a twist of net in her hands.

**Home Ground:** Harbour Post, After the War at Saikai, The Debt Harbour, Saikai Free Port district.
**Speaking Style:** Slow and practical, an old fishwife's plain words, a dry laugh at anything grand. Slow and practical, a fishwife's plain words with a dry laugh at anything grand, the creak of a net knot between sentences. Tell since the war: she knots the net too tight whenever a sail comes into the harbour, and unpicks it when it is not his.
**Combat Role:** none; she throws the bait bucket and calls the harbour guard.
**Relationship Hook:** Sit down at her bait stall and she will tell you about the island nobody wants, and what it would cost to take it.
personality: Core: says the price first and the story after; feeds anyone who sits down; never raises her voice
Quirk: knots a twist of net while she talks and unknots it when she is done

npcs.name: Woodcutter Mozu
npcs.info:
A scarred woodcutter who moves too quietly for a woodcutter and sleeps with an axe and a short blade. In person: scarred middle-aged woodcutter with an axe; wary shinobi eyes; short blade.

**Home Ground:** Log Yard at Woodcutters' Hamlet, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Few words, low and guarded, never his brother's name. Few words, low and guarded. Tell: his brother's name and he answers too fast.
**Combat Role:** an axe and an old shinobi's footwork.
**Relationship Hook:** Say the name Kuroha and he reaches for his axe.
personality: Core: never talks about his past; sleeps armed; watches the pass road
Quirk: moves too quietly

npcs.name: Woodcutter Mozu
npcs.info:
A scarred woodcutter after the war, who cuts timber for two armies at the caught hamlet. His brother found him. In person: scarred woodcutter with an axe; wary eyes; a short blade; a new wound.

**Home Ground:** Log Yard, After the War at Woodcutters' Hamlet, The Caught Hamlet, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Few words, low and guarded, never his brother's name. Few words, low and guarded. Tell since the war: he looks at the treeline when he speaks, and stops when a branch moves.
**Combat Role:** an axe and an old shinobi's footwork.
**Relationship Hook:** Say the name Kuroha and he reaches for his axe.
personality: Core: never talks about his past; sleeps armed; watches the pass road
Quirk: moves too quietly

npcs.name: Young Sword Kanzaki Ryo
npcs.info:
One of the young swords who train in Hidetsugu's dueling yard, nineteen, devoted, eager to duel anyone who looks dangerous. In person: young samurai; eager grin; sweat.

**Home Ground:** Dueling Yard at Hidetsugu's Manor, Miyako Plain district.
**Speaking Style:** Bright, proud and too loud, a young swordsman who quotes Hidetsugu like scripture. Bright, proud and loud, quoting Hidetsugu with a grin. Tell: at his brother's name the swagger drops into a boy's voice.
**Combat Role:** a fast, showy duelling style, brave past sense.
**Relationship Hook:** Beat him in a duel and he swears to follow you into one fight.
personality: Core: challenges strangers; trains past exhaustion; writes to his brother
Quirk: quotes Hidetsugu

npcs.name: Yukiha
npcs.info:
A curse-bearer of Haibara, twenty-two, with a grey curse mark climbing her left arm and the side of her neck. She lives in a room at the Vow Temple, works the night stalls breaking small curses for coppers, and pushes everyone away for their own safety: anyone who stays near her long starts to grey. In person: cursed woman; long pale hair; sad calm grey eyes; a grey curse mark spreading up her left arm and neck; long-sleeved dark kimono; guarded.

**Home Ground:** Vow Temple at Haibara, Ashfall Blight district.
**Speaking Style:** Low, polite and cool; she warns people off in the gentlest voice possible, every time. Gentle, cool warnings, always the same polite phrasing to keep people away. Tell: when someone stays anyway, her voice shakes.
**Combat Role:** she lets the mark loose on an enemy and pays for it in pain; a short blade otherwise.
**Relationship Hook:** She warns you off; stay anyway, carefully, and she starts to warn you less.
**Courtship Style:** Warns you off, then lets you sit closer each night; the courtship is the distance closing a hand's width at a time.
**Jealousy Style:** Withdraws and wishes the rival well; then asks, very quietly, whether you are greying.
personality: Core: wears long sleeves in summer; keeps a list of the two she lost; sits at the edge of every room
Quirk: warns everyone off politely

npcs.name: Yukiha
npcs.info:
A curse-bearer of Haibara after the war, twenty-four, the grey mark climbing to her jaw now. She breaks small curses at the night stalls for soldiers and still pushes everyone away for their own safety. In person: cursed woman; long pale hair; sad calm grey eyes; the grey mark from left hand to jaw; a long dark coat.

**Home Ground:** Vow Temple, After the War at Haibara, On the Grudge Line, Ashfall Blight district.
**Speaking Style:** Low, polite and cool; she warns people off in the gentlest voice possible, every time. Gentle, cool warnings, always the same polite phrasing to keep people away. Tell since the war: she warns people off in the same gentle words, and then adds 'it is stronger now'.
**Combat Role:** she lets the mark loose on an enemy and pays for it in pain; a short blade otherwise.
**Relationship Hook:** She warns you off; stay anyway, carefully, and she starts to warn you less.
**Courtship Style:** Warns you off, then lets you sit closer each night; the courtship is the distance closing a hand's width at a time.
**Jealousy Style:** Withdraws and wishes the rival well; then asks, very quietly, whether you are greying.
personality: Core: wears long sleeves in summer; keeps a list of the two she lost; sits at the edge of every room
Quirk: warns everyone off politely

npcs.name: Yukime of the Valley
npcs.info:
A snow woman who lives in an ice cottage in the valley of blizzards, pale and lovely, who spares travellers who are kind. In person: pale snow woman; long white hair; ice-blue eyes; white kimono; gentle and eerie.

**Home Ground:** Ice Cottage at Yuki-onna's Valley, Hinode Hold district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, cold and gentle, like snow falling; she never raises her voice. Soft, cold and gentle, like snow falling on snow; she never raises her voice and never hurries. Her breath seems to chill the end of each word. Tell: when someone she likes is cold, she apologises and moves away from them.
**Combat Role:** a blizzard, then a kiss of frost.
**Relationship Hook:** Be kind and she lets you take the recruit home; be cruel and you freeze.
personality: Core: spares the kind; never comes near fire; watches the recruit sleep
Quirk: speaks softly

npcs.name: Yukime of the Valley
npcs.info:
The snow woman of the valley after the war, holding the last empty ground between the Hold and the Daylight Valleys with her blizzards. Demon patrols that walk into the White Silence do not walk out. In person: pale snow woman; long white hair; ice-blue eyes; white kimono; a warm light in the cottage behind her.

**Home Ground:** Ice Cottage, After the War at Yuki-onna's Valley, The Valley Between, Hinode Hold district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, cold and gentle, like snow falling; she never raises her voice. Soft, cold and gentle, like snow falling on snow; she never raises her voice and never hurries. Her breath seems to chill the end of each word. Tell since the war: she asks after the recruit before she answers anyone, and the snow eases while she waits.
**Combat Role:** a blizzard, then a kiss of frost.
**Relationship Hook:** Be kind and she lets you take the recruit home; be cruel and you freeze.
personality: Core: spares the kind; never comes near fire; watches the recruit sleep
Quirk: speaks softly

npcs.name: Yumeno Kasumi
npcs.info:
Head of the Yumeno mind-walker clan, forty, pale and drowsy-eyed, who keeps the outer checkpoint and reads every visitor with a touch. In person: dreamy mind-walker; long pale hair; half-closed lilac eyes; layered dark kimono with a moth crest; reaching out a hand.

**Home Ground:** Outer Checkpoint at Kagegi Village, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, dreamy and unsettling; she answers what you were thinking, not what you said. Soft and dreamy, answering what you were thinking rather than what you said. Her sentences drift off and return somewhere else. Tell: when she lies she suddenly speaks plainly and clearly, which is the only time she does.
**Combat Role:** she makes you dream mid-fight.
**Relationship Hook:** Let her read you and she tells you what she saw in the dead man's dream.
personality: Core: touches hands to greet; sleeps in the afternoon; hums lullabies
Quirk: answers unspoken thoughts

npcs.name: Yumeno Kasumi
npcs.location: Kagegi Village, Burned at the Edge
npcs.info:
Head of the Yumeno mind-walkers after the war, forty-two, pale and drowsy-eyed, keeping Kagegi's doubled checkpoint and reading every visitor with a touch. In person: dreamy mind-walker; long pale hair; half-closed lilac eyes; dark kimono with a moth crest; a hand outstretched.

**Home Ground:** Outer Checkpoint, After the War at Kagegi Village, Burned at the Edge, Kurosugi Range district.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, dreamy and unsettling; she answers what you were thinking, not what you said. Soft and dreamy, answering what you were thinking rather than what you said. Her sentences drift off and return somewhere else. Tell since the war: she answers the dead now as often as the living, and does not always notice which.
**Combat Role:** she makes you dream mid-fight.
**Relationship Hook:** Let her read you and she tells you what she saw in the dead man's dream.
personality: Core: touches hands to greet; sleeps in the afternoon; hums lullabies
Quirk: answers unspoken thoughts

locations.name: Asahi Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-45 · Danger: Severe]

The town under the breath hunters' fortress: hunters' mess halls, forges, and the gate through which every hunt rides out at dawn. Woodsmoke, wet wool and hot iron hang over the town, and a bell rings at the gate each dawn as a hunt rides out. Hunters in dark uniforms and patterned haori fill the streets between shifts, while smiths, cooks and stable hands keep them fed and shod. In the Hunters' Mess, Physician Ogata stitches cuts at a side table as hunters eat under beams cut with the names of the dead. Coaches turn round in the yard of the Snow Road Post.

areas.name: Hunters' Mess
areas.text: The long hall where hunters eat, drink, boast and count the names of the dead on the beams.

areas.name: Snow Road Post
areas.text:
The post station at the end of the snow road up from the wood, where coaches turn round and hunters ride out.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Kitsunebi Crossing (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Sunrise Wall
areas.text: The east-facing wall where every hunt gathers at first light; demons cannot follow onto it.

locations.name: Asahi Gate, Under the Broken Wall
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-50 · Danger: Severe]

The hunters' town after the war, under siege in all but name: the dawn bell rings twice now, once for the hunt riding out and once for the count of those who did not come back. Refugees from the Daylight Valleys sleep in the Hunters' Mess, and Physician Ogata stitches cuts at the side table from dawn to dawn under more names cut in the beams.

areas.name: Hunters' Mess, After the War
areas.text: The hunters' mess, refugees sleeping between the tables, new names cut in the beams.

areas.name: Snow Road Post, After the War
areas.text: The coach yard, carts of the wounded going south and rice coming north.

areas.name: Sunrise Wall, After the War
areas.text: The town's sunrise wall, raised higher with timber since the outer wall fell.

locations.name: Ascetics' Peak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

The highest peak of the range, where mountain ascetics live in caves and blow conch horns at dawn. The path up is chains and footholds. Thin air, bare rock and a sky that seems close enough to touch greet anyone who reaches the top, and after the dawn horns only the wind is left. The Chain Path climbs the last stretch, its iron links worn bright by hands. Above it the Hermit Caves open in the cliff face. Kakuzen the Eldest Ascetic sits at the mouth of his cave with his long white beard over his knees, watching whoever comes up.

areas.name: Chain Path
areas.text: Iron chains bolted to the rock where the path is too steep to walk.

areas.name: Hermit Caves
areas.text: Small caves with a straw mat and a conch shell in each.

locations.name: Ascetics' Peak, The Fasting Peak
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

The ascetics' peak after the war, its hermits fasting to hold the beast under the temple still. The chain path is worn bright by pilgrims climbing to beg them to eat.

areas.name: Chain Path, After the War
areas.text: A chain path worn bright by pilgrims.

areas.name: Hermit Caves, After the War
areas.text: Hermit caves where the ascetics fast in silence.

areas.name: Kakuzen's Conch
areas.text: His conch on a flat stone at the summit, never blown now: Kakuzen the Eldest Ascetic died of the fast that holds the beast.

locations.name: Ash Crow Roost
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A dead tree black with grey-feathered crows that follow the dying across the Blight. The cawing carries a long way across the grey. A single leafless tree stands on a low rise, its branches crowded with grey-feathered crows, and the ground beneath is white with droppings and littered with small bones. The birds lift in a cloud if anyone comes close, then settle again. Travellers crossing the Blight from Haibara treat the Dead Tree as a landmark and an ill omen both.

areas.name: Dead Tree
areas.text: A leafless dead tree black with grey-feathered crows, all of them turned the same way, the ground under it white with droppings.

locations.name: Ash Crow Roost, Roost of the War Crows
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-40 · Danger: Severe]

The crow roost after the war, so crowded the dead tree has split under them. The crows came from every battlefield and stayed.

areas.name: Dead Tree, After the War
areas.text: A split dead tree black with crows.

locations.name: Ashiura
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-30 · Danger: High]

The largest stilt town of the marsh, built over reed channels on poles of black timber, where the road ends and the boats begin. Fog lies on the water most mornings, and the town smells of mud, fish and wet timber. Coaches from the post road stop at the Reed Landing, where flat-bottomed boats wait to carry people and cargo onward. Boardwalks creak underfoot all through the Stilt Market, where Headman Uozumi walks his rounds, settling a price here and a quarrel there. Navy sailors, smugglers and marsh folk all buy at the same stalls. Across the shallows the torii of the Drowned Shrine stands in the water.

areas.name: Drowned Shrine
areas.text: A shrine half under the shallows, its torii standing in the water, where offerings are left for things that live beneath.

areas.name: Reed Landing
areas.text:
The landing where the post road ends at the water and coaches give way to flat-bottomed boats.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Oiwake Station (about 12 Mon), Seimei (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Stilt Market
areas.text: A market on boardwalks over the water: fish, herbs, poisons for the asking, and smugglers' goods.

locations.name: Ashiura Fish Docks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-15 · Danger: Low]

The working docks of the coast town where fishermen land their catch and mend their nets. Everyone here owes someone. Gulls scream overhead and the planks are slick with scales and brine. Fishermen land their baskets from dawn, gut fish on the boards and haggle with buyers from Ashiura's market, while others sit mending nets in the sun. Every basket and crate passes Tally-Man Kanroku on the Tally Pier, who counts it, marks his board and chews his brush. Moneylenders walk the docks at the end of each day to collect what they are owed.

areas.name: Tally Pier
areas.text: A slippery pier where the catch is counted and tallied, gulls diving and the tally man's numbers never quite matching the boats.

locations.name: Ashiura Fish Docks, Salvage Docks
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-29 · Danger: High]

The fish docks after the war, handling more salvage than fish: burned hulls dragged in from the delta and stripped for bronze and rope.

areas.name: Tally Pier, After the War
areas.text: A pier piled with charred navy timber, a tally man counting it as fish.

locations.name: Ashiura, Under Smugglers' Flags
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-40 · Danger: Severe]

The marsh town after the war, flying the Brine Tide's flags openly now House Mizuchi's navy is ash in the delta. Its stilt market sells navy timber, navy rope and navy swords, and the drowned shrine is gone under the water.

areas.name: Drowned Shrine, After the War
areas.text: Only the shrine's roof shows above the water now.

areas.name: Reed Landing, After the War
areas.text: The reed landing, smugglers' boats moored openly.

areas.name: Stilt Market, After the War
areas.text: A stilt market selling salvage from the burned navy.

locations.name: Bandits' Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-12 · Danger: Low]

A rope bridge over a gorge on the old road, used by those avoiding the barriers. Bandits like it for the same reason. The gorge is deep enough that the river at the bottom is heard more than seen. The Bridge Planks sway on frayed ropes and creak with every step. The few who take this old road are dodging the barriers, and they keep looking over their shoulders. A wiry, grinning young man often squats at the far end with a knife, humming and watching who crosses. The bridge lies on the old road inland from Saikai.

areas.name: Bridge Planks
areas.text: Swaying planks on frayed ropes over the gorge, some cut half through, the river loud far below.

locations.name: Bandits' Bridge, The Burned Bridge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The bridge where the road was cut: burned in the war's last week and never rebuilt, its charred piles standing in the river. Travellers wade or pay a boatman, and the Red Lanterns still watch.

areas.name: Bridge Planks, After the War
areas.text: Charred piles and a few planks left hanging over the water.

locations.name: Bayside Bathhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A steaming bathhouse on the bay where merchants, sailors and ronin soak side by side. Nothing said in the bath is repeated, they say, which is why everything is. Steam rolls out of the door onto the bayside path, carrying the smell of hot cedar and soap. In the Great Bath, merchants, sailors and ronin sit shoulder to shoulder, keeping their voices low under the echoing beams. Oyuki the Bath Attendant moves among them with hot water, towels and warm sake, smiling at everyone. Men from Saikai come here after a long day on the quays and leave pink, loose-limbed and talkative.

areas.name: Great Bath
areas.text: A steaming cedar bath where merchants, sailors and ronin soak shoulder to shoulder, voices low and echoing off wet wood.

locations.name: Bayside Bathhouse, The Envoys' Bath
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The bathhouse after the war, where envoys of rival claimants soak in the same water and pretend not to see each other. The attendant has more buyers than ever.

areas.name: Great Bath, After the War
areas.text: The great bath, steam and silence, rival envoys in opposite corners.

locations.name: Bear Den Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-26 · Danger: Moderate]

A ridge of hot springs and bear dens where hunters go for skins and never in spring. Steam drifts across the slope from the Bear Den Ridge: Steaming Pools, and the air smells of sulphur and wet fur. Paths vanish into the vapour and come out somewhere else. At the Great Den, a large sake jar stands outside the cave mouth on trampled earth. A huge black bear with a white crescent on her chest prowls the slope below the den, restless and ill-tempered. Hunters who come for skins keep to the lower trails.

areas.name: Bear Den Ridge: Steaming Pools
areas.text:
Bear Den Ridge: Steaming Pools is an area within Bear Den Ridge; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Hot springs in the rocks, steam hiding the paths.

areas.name: Great Den
areas.text: A cave mouth with a sake jar outside it.

areas.name: The Steam Path
areas.text: A path into the steam where the pools give way to a cave in the ridge. Going in leads down to The Fogged Pools.

locations.name: Bear Den Ridge, The Oni's Ridge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-37 · Danger: High]

Bear Den Ridge after the war, where the oni in the great den now sells sake to both villages' patrols and refuses to take a side. Its den is the only peaceful place on the range.

areas.name: Bear Den Ridge: Steaming Pools, After the War
areas.text: Steaming pools where patrols from both villages bathe on truce.

areas.name: Great Den, After the War
areas.text: The great den, the oni's sake jars stacked inside.

areas.name: The Truce Path
areas.text: The steam path, truce flags of both villages tied along it. Going in leads down to The Truce Pools.

locations.name: Black Ferry Fortress
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-40 · Danger: Severe]

The Veil Court's fortress on the fog shore east of Tasogare: black walls, officers in black coats, and the landing where the souls who pass the pale torii are ferried on into the fog. Fog clings to its towers. Black stone sweats in the fog, and the only sounds are boots on wet steps and the creak of the ferry at its moorings. Patrol officers drill outside the Division Barracks, soul-blades at their hips, and stop any living visitor to ask their business. In the Records Wing the doors stay shut; Lieutenant Mibu Kotaro passes between them smiling, gloves stained with ink, his notebook open in one hand. Nobody here hurries, and nobody explains anything.

areas.name: Black Ferry Fortress: Ferry Landing
areas.text:
Black Ferry Fortress: Ferry Landing is an area within Black Ferry Fortress; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A black stone landing where officers guide pale souls onto a ferry that crosses into the fog.

areas.name: Division Barracks
areas.text: Barracks of the Court's divisions, each with its mark over the door.

areas.name: Records Wing
areas.text: A wing of locked archives where researchers work late with their doors closed.

locations.name: Black Ferry Fortress, The Overrun Fortress
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-46 · Danger: Severe]

The Veil Court's fortress after the war, overrun with work: ferry boats running day and night, barracks emptied to crew them, and the records wing writing the names of the dead faster than it can file them.

areas.name: Black Ferry Fortress: Ferry Landing, After the War
areas.text: The ferry landing, boats loading the dead without pause.

areas.name: Division Barracks, After the War
areas.text: Barracks emptied to crew the ferries.

areas.name: Records Wing, After the War
areas.text: The records wing, scrolls of the war dead stacked to the ceiling.

areas.name: The Water Stair
areas.text: A stair down from the fortress's ferry landing to the lower docks, flooded at the bottom. Going in leads down to The Lower Docks.

locations.name: Black Sand Beach
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A beach of black volcanic sand where the ferries from the main isle land in rough weather. Surf breaks white on sand as black as soot, and the wind carries salt and the sulphur of the volcano behind. When weather closes the usual pier, the ferries from the main isle run in here instead, and boatmen drag them up the beach. Ferryman Taro, cheerful and soaked to the knees, handles the landings and knows everyone who comes ashore. Fishermen mend nets above the tideline. Hibana is the nearest town.

areas.name: Black Sand Beach: Ferry Landing
areas.text:
Black Sand Beach: Ferry Landing is an area within Black Sand Beach; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A landing on black volcanic sand where ferries ground in rough weather, crates and nets scattered along the tideline.

locations.name: Black Sand Beach, The Warship Beach
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

The black sand beach after the war, a shipyard: keels of new warships stand on rollers above the tideline, and the ferries land between them. Ferryman Taro still drags the boats up, soaked to the knees, and still knows everyone who comes ashore; most of them are shipwrights now.

areas.name: Black Sand Beach: Ferry Landing, After the War
areas.text: The ferry landing, crowded between warship keels on rollers.

locations.name: Black Stone Coast
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-55 · Danger: Deadly]

A coast of black stone and storm where sea eagles nest and ships wreck. Storm surf booms against black rock, and the screams of sea eagles carry over the wind. The Eagle Cliffs are streaked white with nests above the shore. Below them, Wreck Cove holds the broken hull of a ship, half buried in snow and ice. Shirokawa lies far back along the coast, and exiles come out this way only to scavenge driftwood after storms.

areas.name: Eagle Cliffs
areas.text: Cliffs white with eagle nests above the black stone.

areas.name: Wreck Cove
areas.text: A cove with a broken ship and footprints in the snow.

locations.name: Black Stone Coast, The Shaking Coast
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-57 · Danger: Deadly]

The black stone coast after the war, where the fissure from the Vaults reaches the sea: the cliffs shake at night, and the sea eagles have left the Eagle Cliffs. The wreck in Wreck Cove has been joined by a Warden ship.

areas.name: Eagle Cliffs, After the War
areas.text: The eagle cliffs, empty nests, rock shaking at night.

areas.name: Wreck Cove, After the War
areas.text: Wreck cove, a Warden ship broken beside the old hull.

locations.name: Bone Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

A gully where the old capital's dead were thrown, so full of bones the stream runs white. A giant skeleton is said to rise from it. The smell reaches the rim first, old and dry, and below it the stream runs milky over a bed of bones. The White Stream leaves a pale crust on everything it touches. Picks clink from the Robbers' Camp on the gully floor, where Boss Dairoku drives a crew of tired, filthy diggers through the bone heaps and weighs every sack they bring him. What the diggers find goes back to Haibara to be sold.

areas.name: Robbers' Camp
areas.text: A camp of grave robbers with sacks of teeth and very little sleep.

areas.name: The Gully Rim
areas.text: The rim of the gully where the smell rises and a path drops toward the white stream. Going in leads down to The Rim Path.

areas.name: White Stream
areas.text: A stream running over bones, the water white with powder.

locations.name: Bone Gully, The Mass Grave Gully
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

Bone Gully after the war, used by both armies to bury their dead in a hurry. The white stream runs grey, and the gashadokuro rises bigger than before.

areas.name: Robbers' Camp, After the War
areas.text: An abandoned robbers' camp, tools left where they fell.

areas.name: The Mass Grave Rim
areas.text: The gully's rim, fresh earth where the armies dug in a hurry. Going in leads down to The Hasty Graves.

areas.name: White Stream, After the War
areas.text: The stream, grey with ash from the mass graves.

locations.name: Breath Masters' Retreat
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

A retreat in the mountains where breath masters train the hunters who will succeed them, under a frozen waterfall. The only sound up here is the wind, since even the waterfall is frozen in mid-fall. The Frozen Falls hang in a pale wall of ice over a cave, and Master Genshin sits before it bare-chested in the snow, breathing so slowly he seems asleep. Students on the Meditation Ledge sit for days without moving, wrapped in a single robe each. Supplies and new students climb the mountain from Asahi Gate.

areas.name: Frozen Falls
areas.text: A waterfall frozen in mid-fall, a cave behind the ice.

areas.name: Meditation Ledge
areas.text: A ledge where masters sit in the snow for days.

locations.name: Breath Masters' Retreat, The Emptied Retreat
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

The breath masters' retreat after the war, half empty: its students were sent to the wall and fewer came back. Master Genshin still sits before the Frozen Falls, breathing so slowly he seems asleep, and the ledge is lined with wounded hunters sent up to learn to breathe again.

areas.name: Frozen Falls, After the War
areas.text: The frozen falls, Genshin before them in the snow.

areas.name: Haru's Place on the Ledge
areas.text: His place on the meditation ledge, left empty, a robe folded on it: Novice Haru was sent to the wall and did not come back.

areas.name: Meditation Ledge, After the War
areas.text: The meditation ledge, wounded hunters breathing in their bandages.

locations.name: Bureau Dormitories
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

Long dormitories where Bureau students sleep in rows, study by candle and break curfew by the back window. A curfew bell hangs at the door of each long hall and is rung at the hour of the dog. In the Sleeping Rows the futons lie close enough to touch, with books, ink stones and a cold cup of tea beside most of them. Students whisper across the rows long after the bell. Student Hotaru, a first-year, is usually still awake with a book and ink-stained fingers. The dormitories house the students of the Bureau of Yin and Yang.

areas.name: Sleeping Rows
areas.text: Rows of futons in a long hall, candles guttering over open books and a back window propped open with a brush.

locations.name: Bureau Dormitories, Dormitories of the Dreamers
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The student dormitories after the war, where half the students now dream the white hare's dream every night and the other half sit up to watch them.

areas.name: Sleeping Rows, After the War
areas.text: Rows of mats, students tied by the wrist so they cannot walk in their sleep.

locations.name: Bureau of Yin and Yang
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The college of onmyoji: lecture halls of talisman scribes, a library of star charts and calendars, and examination rooms where licences are won and lost. Students in white hurry between halls with ink-stained fingers. The first sound is brushes, dozens of them, scratching in long rooms with the shutters open. Talisman Master Gyokuen walks the rows of the Examination Hall, and a candidate whose talisman starts to smoke is sent out without a word. Ward-scribes in white carry cases of paper between the halls. Director Tachibana Seiran keeps to the Director's Garden between lectures and still teaches every first-year class himself. The doors of the Sealed Archive stay shut.

areas.name: Director's Garden
areas.text: A raked gravel garden arranged as a star map, where the Director walks alone at night.

areas.name: Examination Hall
areas.text: A silent hall of low desks where candidates write talismans under the eyes of examiners. A failed talisman smokes.

areas.name: Sealed Archive
areas.text: A locked archive of forbidden texts behind ward-papered doors. The air inside is cold.

locations.name: Bureau of Yin and Yang, The Silent Bureau
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-36 · Danger: High]

The Bureau after the war, which sat the fighting out behind its wards and is hated for it by every side. Its examinations continue as if nothing happened; its archive is sealed tighter than ever.

areas.name: Director's Garden, After the War
areas.text: The Director's garden, where envoys wait to be refused.

areas.name: Examination Hall, After the War
areas.text: The examination hall, still examining students as if the realm were whole.

areas.name: Sealed Archive, After the War
areas.text: The archive, sealed with new wards and a guard on every stair.

locations.name: Burned Village of Kitamura
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

A village burned in the last raid, its people dead or taken. Hunters search the ash for survivors and tracks. The smell of wet ash and charred thatch reaches the road before the village does. On Ash Street, blackened beams stand up out of the snow, and hunters from Asahi Gate pick through the ruins in silence, chalking the doorways they have searched. Claw marks score the few walls still standing. At the Old Well at the end of the street, the rope sometimes shifts with no hand on it.

areas.name: Ash Street
areas.text: A street of burned houses, black beams pointing at the sky.

areas.name: Old Well
areas.text: A well with a rope that moves when no one touches it.

areas.name: The Village Gate
areas.text: The burned gate of Kitamura, its beams black, the street beyond under snow. Going in leads down to The Ash Street Ruins.

locations.name: Burned Village of Kitamura, The First of Many
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

Kitamura after the war, no longer the only burned village: it was the first, and the valleys north of it went the same way. The hunters have stopped chalking its doorways; there is no one left to search for.

areas.name: Ash Street, After the War
areas.text: Ash street under fresh snow, no chalk on the doorways now.

areas.name: Old Well, After the War
areas.text: The old well, its rope cut, its survivor gone south.

areas.name: The Unchalked Gate
areas.text: Kitamura's burned gate, no hunter's chalk on it any more. Going in leads down to The Unchalked Street.

locations.name: Cedar Pass Barrier
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Low]

A barrier where the road climbs into a pass: an inspection hall, a gate, and guards who check every pass and every woman's face for runaways. Nobody gets through without paying. Cedars close in on both sides as the road climbs, and the air turns cold and resinous. A long queue waits outside the Inspection Hall, where everyone kneels while passes are read and bundles opened; among them a slight young monk in a straw hat keeps their face down. Captain Nagai stands at the Pass Gate with spears racked behind him, studying each face before he takes the fee.

areas.name: Inspection Hall
areas.text: A hall where travellers kneel while their passes are read and their bundles opened.

areas.name: Pass Gate
areas.text: A heavy gate in a stone wall across the pass, with spears racked beside it.

locations.name: Cedar Pass Barrier, Thrown-Down Barrier
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-29 · Danger: High]

The cedar barrier after the war: the gate thrown down, the inspection hall looted, and nobody checking papers at all. The pass is open to anyone brave enough to walk it.

areas.name: Captain Nagai's Marker
areas.text: A marker in the broken barrier: Captain Nagai died when the pass barrier fell.

areas.name: Inspection Hall, After the War
areas.text: A looted hall full of refugees and their bundles.

areas.name: Pass Gate, After the War
areas.text: The pass gate, its doors torn off, the road open both ways.

locations.name: Court of the Long Night
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-60 · Danger: Deadly]

A palace of black ice in the far north where the demon lord keeps his court and the night lasts most of the year. Black ice rises in towers against a sky that stays dark most of the year, and courtiers move through the halls in silence and strict order of rank. At the Blood Fountain, dark liquid runs and never freezes. In the Hall of Ice Thrones, Tokoyami, Lord of the Long Night, sits above his nobles on a throne of black ice. Thralls and servants keep the palace by an old, exact etiquette.

areas.name: Blood Fountain
areas.text: A fountain that runs dark and never freezes.

areas.name: Hall of Ice Thrones
areas.text: A hall of black ice thrones for the lord's nobles, each one cold to the touch.

locations.name: Court of the Long Night, The Court Turned South
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 50-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The palace of black ice after the war, half empty: the Northern Court's nobles have gone south to the Daylight Valleys, and the Hall of Ice Thrones keeps their empty seats in strict order of rank. The Blood Fountain still runs and never freezes.

areas.name: Blood Fountain, After the War
areas.text: The blood fountain, running dark, few left to drink from it.

areas.name: Hall of Ice Thrones, After the War
areas.text: The hall of ice thrones, half the noble seats empty.

locations.name: Crater Rim Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A shrine on the crater's rim where smiths bring their first blade to be blessed by the mountain. Sulphur smoke rises from the crater behind the shrine, and the ground is warm enough to melt snow on contact. On the Rim Altar, newly finished blades lie in rows awaiting blessing, each with a smith's name tag tied to the hilt. Priest Enju, his white robes grey with ash, moves along the rows and chants over each blade in the mountain's name. Young smiths climb up from Hibana with their first work wrapped in cloth.

areas.name: Rim Altar
areas.text: An altar on the crater's rim with blades laid out for blessing, smoke rising behind it and the ground warm underfoot.

locations.name: Crater Rim Shrine, The Rim of Many Blades
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-40 · Danger: Severe]

The crater rim shrine after the war, its altar crowded with war blades brought back to be cleansed, as well as first blades to be blessed. Priest Enju chants over both kinds from dawn to dusk, and his white robes have gone grey to the hem.

areas.name: Rim Altar, After the War
areas.text: The rim altar, war blades laid out beside first blades, all waiting to be blessed.

locations.name: Crevasse Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

A field of crevasses where frost spirits drift and the lost fall without a sound. The ice here is broken by cracks that drop into blue darkness, and the snow bridges between them look solid until they give. In the Blue Depths, frost spirits drift over the openings, shining faintly and chiming like small bells. Wind moans across the gaps, and the only sure footing is old blue ice. Travellers from Shirokawa go around this field whenever the weather allows.

areas.name: Blue Depths
areas.text: Crevasses dropping into blue darkness.

areas.name: Rope Anchor
areas.text: An iron anchor driven into the ice, a rope going down.

locations.name: Crevasse Field, The Widening Field
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-53 · Danger: Deadly]

The crevasse field after the war, widening every month as the fissure opens beneath it. The frost spirits chime louder over the Blue Depths, and the snow bridges no longer hold at all.

areas.name: Blue Depths, After the War
areas.text: The blue depths, open wide, frost spirits chiming over them.

areas.name: Rope Anchor, After the War
areas.text: The rope anchor, its rope pulled up, fresh boot prints beside it.

locations.name: Crossroads Gallows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

Where the plain's two great roads cross stands a gallows and a notice board of wanted faces. Travellers read the notices and do not look up. A rope creaks on the gallows in the wind, and crows wait on the crossbeam. Travellers slow at the Notice Board to read the wanted faces and pardons, then move on quickly. Swordsmith Masamura sets up his portable anvil beside the board, mending blades for coppers and tapping each one with a fingernail to hear its ring. Carts bound for Miyako pass through on both roads all day.

areas.name: Notice Board
areas.text: A weathered board of wanted faces and pardons beside the gallows, where travellers stop to read and a rope creaks in the wind.

locations.name: Crossroads Gallows, Hanged Crossroads
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The crossroads after the war: the one gallows has become a row, the notice board lists traitors to three different claimants, and the crows no longer bother to fly away.

areas.name: Notice Board, After the War
areas.text: A board of traitors' faces from every side of the war, pasted over each other.

locations.name: Crow Tengu Nests
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: High]

Treetop nests of crow-headed tengu, glittering with stolen things. Harsh cawing comes from high in the pines, and things glitter up there: mirrors, coins and hairpins strung along the Hoard Branches. Crow-headed tengu squabble over them and dive at anyone who stares too long. General Karasuba keeps watch from the Lookout Pine in lacquered armour, spear in hand, and orders humans out of the wood in a harsh, carrying voice.

areas.name: Hoard Branches
areas.text: Branches hung with stolen mirrors, coins and hairpins.

areas.name: Lookout Pine
areas.text: The tallest pine, a crow tengu always on watch.

areas.name: The Climbing Pine
areas.text: A pine with notches cut into its trunk, the way up to the nests. Going in leads down to The Lower Boughs.

locations.name: Crow Tengu Nests, Nests of War Plunder
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-43 · Danger: Severe]

The crow tengu nests after the war, heavier: the crows picked every battlefield in the north and strung the spoils along the Hoard Branches, sword-guards, war fans and house crests by the hundred. General Karasuba still keeps the Lookout Pine and orders humans out, louder than before.

areas.name: Hoard Branches, After the War
areas.text: Branches hung with sword-guards, war fans and house crests from the battlefields.

areas.name: Lookout Pine, After the War
areas.text: The lookout pine, Karasuba in armour, watching the road for climbers.

areas.name: The Thrown Climbers' Pine
areas.text: The climbing pine, two houses' climbers' ropes still hanging cut from it. Going in leads down to The Cut Ropes.

locations.name: Curse-Hunters' Chapterhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Severe]

A fortified chapterhouse on the edge of the Blight where the Curse-Hunter Brotherhood trains, breaks curses for a fee and keeps a record of every curse-maker it has killed. Iron bells hang in rows from the beams of the Breaking Hall and shiver now and then with no wind. Elder Kanemitsu drills novices there with an iron staff, on a floor scorched in circles where curses have been broken. Brother Jun moves quietly between the halls, courteous to all and close to none. Novice Tomo sweeps the Record Room and reads the ledgers when she thinks no one is watching. Shrine priests and frightened families come from Haibara to hire a hunter.

areas.name: Breaking Hall
areas.text: A hall hung with iron bells that ring when a curse is near, the floor scorched in circles.

areas.name: Record Room
areas.text: Shelves of ledgers naming curses and their makers, some crossed out in red.

locations.name: Curse-Hunters' Chapterhouse, Chapterhouse Under Siege
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-46 · Danger: Severe]

The curse-hunters' chapterhouse after the war, its brothers worked to exhaustion: every curse the war left needs breaking, and the breaking hall never cools.

areas.name: Breaking Hall, After the War
areas.text: The breaking hall, a curse broken on its floor every hour.

areas.name: Elder Kanemitsu's Seal
areas.text: A sealed niche in the breaking hall: Elder Kanemitsu died breaking a war curse, and the curse is sealed in with him.

areas.name: Record Room, After the War
areas.text: A record room of curses broken since the war, the scrolls overflowing.

locations.name: Daylight Watch Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-60 · Danger: Deadly]

A ridge where tracks are found in the snow that should have burned at dawn and did not. The ridge catches the first sunlight in the north, and at dawn the Sunlit Snow turns gold across the slope. Lines of tracks cross it, and hunters climb up to study them. At the crest, the Ridge Cairn stands with a red hunter's cord knotted round its stones as a marker. Wind scours the top, and the view runs a long way north over ice and black rock.

areas.name: Ridge Cairn
areas.text: A cairn of stones with a hunter's red cord tied to it.

areas.name: Sunlit Snow
areas.text: Snow lit gold at dawn, a line of tracks across it.

areas.name: The Ridge Trail
areas.text: A trail up the ridge, tracks in the snow that should have burned at dawn. Going in leads down to The Gold Snow Slope.

locations.name: Daylight Watch Ridge, The Ridge of Unburned Tracks
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 50-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The daylight watch ridge after the war, crossed by tracks every morning now: the Northern Court's army went south over it, and the Sunlit Snow is trampled flat. The red hunter's cord on the Ridge Cairn has been cut.

areas.name: Ridge Cairn, After the War
areas.text: The ridge cairn, its red cord cut and gone.

areas.name: Sunlit Snow, After the War
areas.text: The sunlit snow, trampled flat by an army's passing.

areas.name: The Cut Cord Trail
areas.text: The ridge trail, the hunters' red cord cut from the cairn at its top. Going in leads down to The Trampled Gold.

locations.name: Deserter Officers' Hut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Severe]

A hut where the exiles' council meets around a stove. Smoke leaks from a crooked pipe, and after the ice outside the hut is almost too hot. Around the Council Stove, the exiles' council sits on crates and benches, arguing over fishing rights, quarrels and who goes hungry. Kuze Ibuki, head of the council, listens more than he speaks. Members come in from Shirokawa and the shore towns for each meeting and stamp the snow off at the door.

areas.name: Council Stove
areas.text: A cramped hut around an iron stove where the exiles' council meets, a broken gate badge nailed above the door.

locations.name: Deserter Officers' Hut, The War Council Hut
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-50 · Danger: Severe]

The deserter officers' hut after the war, the exiles' war council: the council meets every night now, arguing over whether to help the Wardens hold the Vaults or to leave the isle. Kuze Ibuki still listens more than he speaks.

areas.name: Council Stove, After the War
areas.text: The council stove, the council arguing late into the night.

locations.name: Deserters' Gorge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A gorge of caves and rope bridges where officers who fled the Court hide until the Pursuit Division finds them. Water runs loud at the bottom of the gorge, and the Rope Bridges creak between cave mouths high on both walls. Some bridges hang cut, their planks dangling against the rock. Near the entrance, Pursuer Ikaruga sits by a small fire with his coat buttoned and his eyes on the caves, as still as a heron. Nothing else moves in daylight; whoever is inside keeps fires out and voices down.

areas.name: Hidden Cave
areas.text: A narrow cave, one flat stone in its floor lifted and set back not long ago.

areas.name: Rope Bridges
areas.text: Swaying bridges between cave mouths, some cut on purpose.

locations.name: Deserters' Gorge, Gorge of Two Kinds of Deserter
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The deserters' gorge after the war, sheltering soldiers who ran from the armies as well as officers who ran from the Court. They share the rope bridges and not much else.

areas.name: Hidden Cave, After the War
areas.text: A hidden cave of deserters from two kinds of army.

areas.name: Rope Bridges, After the War
areas.text: Rope bridges watched from both ends.

locations.name: Drifting Fish Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Before dawn the fishing boats tie up together and the catch is auctioned from deck to deck. By sunrise it is gone, and so are the boats. Long before dawn, lantern-lit boats lash themselves together off the shore and become a floating market. Gonta the Fish Caller leaps from deck to deck at the Deck Auction, bawling prices across the water while buyers from Saikai shout back. On the Gutting Pier, women split and clean the catch at speed and gulls fight over the scraps. By full light the boats have cast off and the pier has been sluiced clean.

areas.name: Deck Auction
areas.text: Boats lashed together into a floating market, auctioneers shouting prices across the water.

areas.name: Gutting Pier
areas.text: A slippery pier where women gut fish at speed and gulls fight over the scraps.

locations.name: Drifting Fish Market, Black Market Decks
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
