[Recommended Level: 20-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The floating market after the war: the fish are fewer, the decks carry rice, salt and stolen arms, and the Brine Tide runs the auctions openly now nobody has the ships to stop them.

areas.name: Deck Auction, After the War
areas.text: Lashed decks where rice and arms go to the highest bidder.

areas.name: Gutting Pier, After the War
areas.text: The gutting pier, half the knives now gutting crates instead of fish.

locations.name: Drowned Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: High]

A fishing village the sea took in a great storm, its roofs still showing above the water at low tide. Bells ring under the waves on calm nights. At low tide the sea draws back far enough to show the ridges of drowned roofs, black with weed, in rows where the streets once ran. The Roof Path crosses them from house to house, slippery underfoot, and the smell is salt and rot. At its far end the torii of the Sunken Shrine stands up to its crossbeam in the water. Nobody lives here now; fishermen from Ashiura give the place a wide berth and never cast their nets over it.

areas.name: Roof Path
areas.text: A path across the drowned roofs at low tide, slippery with weed.

areas.name: Sunken Shrine
areas.text: The village shrine, its torii half under water, its bell still hanging.

locations.name: Drowned Village, Deeper Water
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

The drowned village after the war, deeper: the sea took more of it the winter the dykes went unmended, and now only the roof path is above water.

areas.name: Roof Path, After the War
areas.text: A path of roof ridges just above the water.

areas.name: Sunken Shrine, After the War
areas.text: The shrine, now fully under the sea, its bell heard at low tide.

locations.name: Duelists' Teahouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Low]

A teahouse on the road where the Hundred-Duel Circuit's duelists stop to sign books and find opponents. Its yard is the only place the Wardens allow a duel. Swordsmen of every school sit on the teahouse benches with duel books tucked in their sashes, eyeing one another over their tea. Behind the building, the swept Duel Yard is ringed with benches, and Ochiba sits there every day with her sword across her knees. In the Signing Room, Book-Keeper Senzo copies fights into his register with ink-black fingers, and nobody speaks above a whisper.

areas.name: Duel Yard
areas.text: A swept yard behind the teahouse, ringed by benches for watchers.

areas.name: Signing Room
areas.text: A quiet room where duelists sign each other's books after a fight, by tradition in silence.

locations.name: Duelists' Teahouse, Teahouse of the Last Duels
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-29 · Danger: High]

The duellists' teahouse after the war, where the Circuit's survivors drink to the ones who were drafted and did not come back. The duel yard is quieter; Kagero still sits in the signing room.

areas.name: Duel Yard, After the War
areas.text: The duel yard, fewer bouts, each one watched in silence.

areas.name: Signing Room, After the War
areas.text: The signing room, a wall of names of duellists who went to the war.

locations.name: Earth Sanctum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A sanctum of stone: a cave under a standing stone, warm and still, where the Earth keeps a warden shaped from its own rock. Fire is forbidden inside; the stone remembers being burned. The cave is warm the way a stone wall is warm at dusk. The floor is swept and the walls are smooth, and at the centre of the inner hall a stone figure stands with its hands open, worn by weather that never reaches in here. A torch brought inside burns low and sullen, as if the air does not want it.

areas.name: The Cave Mouth
areas.text: A low cave under a standing stone, warm air coming out.

areas.name: The Standing Stone
areas.text: The standing stone over the cave, warm to the touch, the way in at its foot. Going in leads down to The Warm Cave.

areas.name: The Warden's Hall
areas.text: A chamber of stone with a stone figure at its centre.

locations.name: Earth Spider Pits
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: High]

Pits and gullies full of webbed hollows where the old mountain clans fought the first emperor and lost. Hunters do not go in. The ground sinks into gullies roofed with pale silk the colour of soil, and the air is still and close. Nothing sings here. At the Clan Stones, carved slabs lean at old angles, smeared with ochre in the shape of handprints. Hunters from both villages turn back at the edge, and the trails into the Webbed Pits are marked only by bones and old arrowheads half sunk in the dirt.

areas.name: Clan Stones
areas.text: Carved stones of the old clans, smeared with fresh ochre.

areas.name: The Silk Gully
areas.text: A gully roofed with pale silk where the ground first starts to sink. Going in leads down to The Ochre Slabs.

areas.name: Webbed Pits
areas.text: Pits roofed with silk that looks like earth.

locations.name: Earth Spider Pits, The Spider's Bargain
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-40 · Danger: Severe]

The earth spider pits after the war, where the spider of the old clans finally got its alliance: Hayate took it, and the pits are a Hayate stronghold now.

areas.name: Clan Stones, After the War
areas.text: The clan stones, Hayate's mark carved beside the spider's.

areas.name: The Sentry Rim
areas.text: The pits' rim, Hayate sentries posted on it, a way down between their posts. Going in leads down to The Marked Stones.

areas.name: Webbed Pits, After the War
areas.text: Webbed pits, Hayate sentries posted at the rims.

locations.name: Ember Vent Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: High]

Fields of steaming vents where flame-spirits dance and smiths gather sulphur. Vents hiss across the Steam Field, and yellow sulphur crust crunches underfoot over hollow ground. The smell of rotten eggs carries a long way on the wind. Labourers from Hibana come out with baskets and scrapers to gather sulphur in the morning and are gone before dusk. At dusk, in the hollow of the Sprite Dance, ember sprites rise from the vents and dance in rings of flame.

areas.name: Sprite Dance
areas.text: A hollow where flames dance in rings at dusk.

areas.name: Steam Field
areas.text: A field of hissing vents, yellow sulphur crusts underfoot.

locations.name: Ember Vent Fields, The Crowded Vents
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-43 · Danger: Severe]

The ember vent fields after the war, worked day and night for the forges' sulphur. The ember sprites dance thicker and closer to town than they used to, and the labourers no longer leave before dusk.

areas.name: Sprite Dance, After the War
areas.text: The sprite dance, flame rings spilling out of the hollow toward town.

areas.name: Steam Field, After the War
areas.text: The steam field, scraped bare, labourers working by lantern.

locations.name: Exiles' Graveyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-40 · Danger: Severe]

Driftwood grave markers in the snow where the exiles bury those the realm forgot. Grey driftwood markers lean out of the snow above the shore, each carved with a name or only a mark. Among the Driftwood Markers, exiles from Shirokawa leave dried fish, sake and small stones for their dead. The sea wind keeps the snow drifting between the graves. Mourners who come here keep their visits short and walk back to town together.

areas.name: Driftwood Markers
areas.text: Driftwood grave markers in the snow, one grave bare of frost and faintly steaming.

locations.name: Exiles' Graveyard, The Graveyard Over the Crack
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-46 · Danger: Severe]

The exiles' graveyard after the war, split by the fissure: a crack runs between the Driftwood Markers, and the warm grave lies right at its edge.

areas.name: Driftwood Markers, After the War
areas.text: Driftwood markers leaning over the fissure, one grave melted bare.

areas.name: Hyoe's Spade
areas.text: His spade driven in at the fissure's lip: Gravedigger Hyoe fell into the crack that split the graveyard.

locations.name: Exiles' Shore Towns
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Severe]

Three fishing towns along the south shore beyond Shirokawa, where the realm's exiles live hard and proud lives. Fish oil, smoke and drying sealskin give the three towns one shared smell. On the Seal Hunters' Quay, hunters sharpen harpoons, haul seals from the boats and stretch skins on racks to dry. The exiles who live here keep their own customs and are slow to trust outsiders from the south. The towns trade fish and oil with Shirokawa along the shore.

areas.name: Exiles' Shore Towns: Ice Caves
areas.text:
Exiles' Shore Towns: Ice Caves is an area within Exiles' Shore Towns; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Caves under the shore ice where the exiles hide what the south wants.

areas.name: Seal Hunters' Quay
areas.text: A quay of seal hunters and their harpoons, skins drying on racks.

locations.name: Exiles' Shore Towns, Towns Packing to Leave
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-53 · Danger: Deadly]

The exiles' shore towns after the war, packing: boats loaded with nets and sealskin, families arguing on the Seal Hunters' Quay over whether to stay. The exiles are proud, but the ice is cracking under them.

areas.name: Exiles' Shore Towns: Ice Caves, After the War
areas.text: The ice caves, four hosts hidden where there was one.

areas.name: Kitaro's Harpoon
areas.text: His harpoon hung over the quay: Seal-Hunter Kitaro went through the ice when the Vaults cracked.

areas.name: Seal Hunters' Quay, After the War
areas.text: The seal hunters' quay, boats loaded to leave.

locations.name: Expelled Scholars' Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A run-down quarter where onmyoji who failed or were expelled scrape a living reading fortunes and writing illegal charms. They know things the Bureau has forgotten. The streets here are narrower than the rest of Seimei and badly kept, with laundry strung between the eaves and a rain barrel at every door. Fortune Lane is the lively part: stools, low tables and painted signs, every keeper calling an offer to read a palm, a face or a birth date. A nervous young fortune-teller with a messy bob reads palms for coppers near the lane's mouth. Bureau students slip down after dark for charms they cannot buy openly.

areas.name: Fortune Lane
areas.text: A narrow lane of fortune-tellers' stalls and illegal charm-writers, incense and cheap ink, every voice offering to read your future.

locations.name: Expelled Scholars' Quarter, Quarter of the Turned Away
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-33 · Danger: High]

The expelled scholars' quarter after the war, swollen with Bureau students sent home to houses that no longer exist. They sell fortunes and forged wards to the refugees on the shore.

areas.name: Fortune Lane, After the War
areas.text: A lane of fortune stalls, more of them selling wards than fortunes.

locations.name: Ferrymen's Rest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A teahouse below the Black Ferry Fortress where off-duty officers drink and do not talk about work. Steam, roasted tea and the smell of wet wool fill the Ferrymen's Rest: Tea Room, where off-duty officers sit on cushions with their black coats open. Talk runs to weather, dice and the price of sake. Ferryman Gin nurses a cup in the corner, grey-stubbled and tired, and nods at newcomers without inviting them over. The teahouse stands under the walls of Black Ferry Fortress and serves anyone who pays, though the living get looked at.

areas.name: Ferrymen's Rest: Tea Room
areas.text:
Ferrymen's Rest: Tea Room is an area within Ferrymen's Rest; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A low tea room of off-duty officers in black, cups in hand, talking about anything but work until the third cup.

locations.name: Ferrymen's Rest, Rest of the Tired Ferrymen
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

The ferrymen's rest after the war, where ferrymen sleep in their clothes between crossings. The tea is strong and nobody talks after the first cup.

areas.name: Ferrymen's Rest: Tea Room, After the War
areas.text: A tea room of exhausted ferrymen asleep at the tables.

locations.name: Fire Sanctum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A sanctum of fire: an ash field around a crack in the ground that breathes heat, where a sprite keeps the furnace and an ash-tender keeps the field. Water carried in is poured out at the edge; the furnace takes it as an insult. Ash lies to the ankle and is warm underneath. Heat comes up through it in breaths, and with each breath the crack in the ground glows and dims. The air smells of hot stone and nothing else. A tender in a leather apron rakes the ash into lines that the next breath disturbs, and rakes them again.

areas.name: The Ash Edge
areas.text: The edge of the ash field, where carried water must be poured out. Going in leads down to The Ember Field.

areas.name: The Ash Field
areas.text: Grey ash to the ankle, heat coming up through it.

areas.name: The Furnace Crack
areas.text: A crack in the ground that breathes orange, a sprite in it.

locations.name: Fishers' Huts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

Five thatched huts and fish-drying racks along the east shore south of the Landing: the island's hamlet. Ruined until restored: four huts stand empty and one woman mends nets for boats that do not come.

areas.name: Hamlet Drying Racks
areas.text: Racks of bamboo for drying fish and nets, and a bench where Iwa works.

areas.name: Hut Row
areas.text: The five huts in a row above the beach, four of them shuttered.

locations.name: Fog Watch Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A tower where the Court rings a bell when the tide begins. The tower is a tall timber frame on a stone base, and its great bronze bell hums faintly whenever the wind strikes it. Up in the Bell Loft, Bellkeeper Oto sits wrapped in a patched coat, watching the fog line with one hand near the rope. She climbs down only for food and water, and lets visitors up if they mind their feet on the ladder. From the loft, the lanterns of Tasogare show as a smudge of light along the cliffs.

areas.name: Bell Loft
areas.text: A loft with a great bronze bell and a rope that has been spliced twice, fog pressing against the open sides.

locations.name: Fog Watch Tower, The Bell Rung for the Dead
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

The fog watch tower after the war, its bell rung not for tides but for every hundred dead ferried. It rings most of the night.

areas.name: Bell Loft, After the War
areas.text: The bell loft, the rope worn smooth from ringing.

locations.name: Foreign Quay Warehouses
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A row of warehouses behind the foreign quay where cargo from the square-sailed ships is stored before the guild inspects it. Porters work by lantern light and do not ask what is in the crates. Hand-carts rumble over the cobbles of the Loading Yard, where porters with hooks shift crates under oilcloth and the air is thick with tar and pepper. Daikokuya Genta walks the stacks in his foreign coat, checking a pocket watch and hurrying the tally clerks. At the end of the row stands The Black Warehouse, shut and painted black, its door kept by sober men. Mother Urushi comes and goes from it in her lacquer jewellery, renting space to foreign captains.

areas.name: Loading Yard
areas.text: A cobbled yard stacked with crates under oilcloth, porters with hooks and hand-carts. The air smells of tar and spices.

areas.name: The Black Warehouse
areas.text: A warehouse painted black, always locked, guarded by men who do not drink. On auction nights masked guests arrive one at a time.

locations.name: Foreign Quay Warehouses, Bonded Quay
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-33 · Danger: High]

The warehouses after the war, crammed with bonded goods: arms bought for one side and never collected, rice held against debts, and the black warehouse busier than it has ever been. Guild seals hang on every lock.

areas.name: Loading Yard, After the War
areas.text: A yard stacked with uncollected arms and guild-sealed rice.

areas.name: The Black Warehouse, After the War
areas.text: The masked auction house, its lacquer boxes sliding faster than ever.

locations.name: Foreigners' Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low]

A walled quarter where foreign sailors and traders must live while in port: odd houses, odd food, and translators who sell every conversation twice. The smells of baked bread, pipe smoke and unfamiliar spices drift over the wall. At the Quarter Gate guards check passes in both directions, and Hendrik van Aal lounges nearby, a tall red-bearded sailor trading knots and songs for a meal and asking every captain who passes for a berth home. In the Translators' Tea House, Ume the Translator sits with a jade pin in her hair, taking work by the hour and listening to every table at once.

areas.name: Quarter Gate
areas.text: A guarded gate where foreigners show their passes and locals show their reasons.

areas.name: Translators' Tea House
areas.text: A tea house where translators sit waiting for work and listening to everything.

locations.name: Foreigners' Quarter, The Envoys' Quarter
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The foreign quarter after the war, full of envoys as well as traders: the foreign captains sell to whoever wins, and every claimant has sent someone to buy their guns.

areas.name: Quarter Gate, After the War
areas.text: The quarter gate, guarded by foreign marines as well as guild men.

areas.name: Translators' Tea House, After the War
areas.text: The tea house where envoys and captains bargain through translators who sell both sides.

locations.name: Forge Guild Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-35 · Danger: High]

The swordsmiths' guild hall: inspection rooms where every blade is marked, the oldest forge on the isle, and a hall where masters wake soul-blades. Daylight pours through tall windows onto the long tables of the Inspection Room, where examiners turn blades under the light and stamp the guild mark into those that pass. Smiths queue outside with wrapped swords. Deeper in, the Waking Hall is kept silent; Fire Master Homura sits there with a blade across his knees for days at a time. Most guild members keep forges in Hibana.

areas.name: Inspection Room
areas.text: Long tables where blades are examined under daylight and stamped with the guild mark.

areas.name: The Old Forge
areas.text: The oldest forge on the isle, its hearth never let go cold, anvils and quenching troughs open to any guild smith.

areas.name: Waking Hall
areas.text: A quiet hall where a master sits with a sword across her knees for days.

locations.name: Forge Guild Hall, The Hall That Stopped Asking
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-43 · Danger: Severe]

The forge guild hall after the war, richer than any house: the Inspection Room stamps war orders by the hundred, and the Waking Hall is no longer silent. Fire Master Homura sits there with a blade across his knees, and the blades around him whisper.

areas.name: Inspection Room, After the War
areas.text: The inspection room, war orders stamped by the hundred.

areas.name: The Old Forge, After the War
areas.text: The old forge, never cold, hammering war blades day and night for whoever pays.

areas.name: Tsubaki's Bellows
areas.text: Her bellows in the waking hall, nobody pumping them: Smith Apprentice Tsubaki went down to the deep forges to ask, and did not come up.

areas.name: Waking Hall, After the War
areas.text: The waking hall, whispering, Homura with a blade across his knees.

locations.name: Foxfire Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A marsh lit by foxfire at night, where travellers following the lights walk in circles until dawn. Reeds hiss, frogs fall silent at dusk, and cold lights rise over the Light Pools in green, rose and pale violet. The Circle Path loops back to the same dead tree whichever way a traveller turns. Lord Shiranui lounges beside the pools in a dark kimono, silver tails spread behind him, watching passers-by with a contemptuous smile. Mud sucks at every step, and the water smells of rot and mint.

areas.name: Circle Path
areas.text: A path that always leads back to the same dead tree.

areas.name: Light Pools
areas.text: Pools where cold lights hover, each a different colour.

locations.name: Foxfire Marsh, The Marsh of Lost Soldiers
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

Foxfire Marsh after the war, where deserters hiding from both armies followed the lights and have not walked out. The foxfire burns brighter on the Light Pools, and the newcomers circle them without knowing whose lights they follow.

areas.name: Circle Path, After the War
areas.text: The circle path, worn deep by soldiers' boots that never get anywhere.

areas.name: Light Pools, After the War
areas.text: Light pools burning brighter, a deserter's boots left at their edge.

locations.name: Frozen Battlefield
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-60 · Danger: Deadly]

A field where an army froze where it stood fighting the north, still standing under the ice. The field is silent, and the cold lies heavy and still. Under clear ice, the Ice Ranks stand where an army froze in mid-battle: soldiers with spears raised, banners stiff, faces visible a hand's depth down. Exiles from Shirokawa avoid the place. A ranked demon of the Northern Court in black armour has been seen walking slowly among the frozen ranks.

areas.name: Cracked Line
areas.text: Where the ice has cracked and a hand reaches out.

areas.name: Ice Ranks
areas.text: Ranks of frozen soldiers under clear ice.

areas.name: The Field's Edge
areas.text: The edge of the frozen field, the first rank of faces visible under the ice. Going in leads down to The Frozen Front.

locations.name: Frozen Battlefield, The Thawing Field
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 50-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The frozen battlefield after the war, thawing: the ice over the Ice Ranks has thinned to a skin, faces show clearly beneath it, and one or two of the frozen have moved. The ranked demon in black armour walks among them every night now.

areas.name: Cracked Line, After the War
areas.text: The cracked line, ice split along the front rank.

areas.name: Ice Ranks, After the War
areas.text: The ice ranks under a skin of ice, some of the frozen moving.

areas.name: The Thawed Edge
areas.text: The field's edge, the ice thinned to a skin, faces clear beneath it. Going in leads down to The Thin Ice.

locations.name: Frozen Pass of the Long Night
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

The pass beyond the Long Night Wall that the demons come through on the Demon Nights, frozen nine months of the year. The wind is the first thing, a steady scream between the ice walls that drowns out speech. The Pass Floor is a narrow, drifted road, and snow sliding off the cliffs fills old tracks within the hour. Grey-skinned thralls in farmers' clothes shelter in the lee of the rocks after dark. By day, travellers have met Hakuro the Daylight Demon walking the pass in a dark cloak, and he lets hunters go on their way.

areas.name: Frozen Pass of the Long Night: Ice Caves
areas.text:
Frozen Pass of the Long Night: Ice Caves is an area within Frozen Pass of the Long Night; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Caves in blue ice above the pass, smelling of old blood.

areas.name: Pass Floor
areas.text: A narrow road between ice walls, wind screaming through it.

areas.name: The Last Marker
areas.text: The last hunters' marker before the pass, a sun-steel spike in the snow. Going in leads down to The Screaming Road.

locations.name: Frozen Pass of the Long Night, The Open Pass
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

The frozen pass after the war, open: the demons come through it every night now, not only on Demon Nights, and the Pass Floor is trampled to ice by thralls marching south. Footprints that did not burn at dawn cross it, and the hunters who see them do not follow.

areas.name: Frozen Pass of the Long Night: Ice Caves, After the War
areas.text: The ice caves, emptied of packs, a cold light deep inside.

areas.name: Pass Floor, After the War
areas.text: The pass floor trampled to ice by the marching dead.

areas.name: The Trampled Marker
areas.text: The last hunters' marker, knocked flat by marching thralls. Going in leads down to The Marching Road.

locations.name: Ghost Pine Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-15 · Danger: Low]

A hill where the road runs through a cutting, notorious for lanterns that float along it at night with no one carrying them. Station masters warn travellers to be indoors by dark. Wind hisses in the twisted pines on the slope, and the road drops into The Cutting between earth walls taller than a rider. By day it is only a gloomy stretch where walkers lengthen their stride. At dusk a figure in grey robes and a deep straw hat walks the road, asking travellers the way to a shrine. A narrow path climbs to the Hilltop Shrine, tiny and abandoned, its bell cord rotted through.

areas.name: Hilltop Shrine
areas.text: A tiny abandoned shrine at the top, its bell cord rotted away.

areas.name: The Cutting
areas.text: A narrow cutting through the hill, the road sunk between earth walls.

locations.name: Ghost Pine Hill, The Lantern Hill
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-29 · Danger: High]

The ghost hill after the war, thick with empty lanterns: the war's unburied dead drift in from the road, and the hilltop shrine is lit every night by someone nobody sees.

areas.name: Hilltop Shrine, After the War
areas.text: The hilltop shrine, lit every night, lanterns crowding its eaves.

areas.name: The Cutting, After the War
areas.text: The cutting, where lanterns drift across the road at dusk.

locations.name: Glacier Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Severe]

Beyond the last poles of Shirokawa's road, the marked way across the open glacier to the Vaults, crevasses on both sides. Past the last poles the road becomes a line of cairns across bare ice, and the wind never stops. Along the Marker Line, crevasses open blue on both sides, some only a pace from the cairns. Travellers rope together and probe the snow ahead with spears. Exile Kanbe, frost on his furs, often walks the line with a sled, a spear and a lantern. The road runs from Shirokawa to the Vaults.

areas.name: Marker Line
areas.text: A line of cairn markers across the glacier, crevasses opening blue on both sides.

locations.name: Glacier Road, The Broken Road
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-50 · Danger: Severe]

The glacier road after the war, broken by the fissure halfway to the Vaults: the Marker Line ends at a crack too wide to jump, and Exile Kanbe ropes travellers across it one at a time.

areas.name: Marker Line, After the War
areas.text: The marker line, ending at a fissure, Kanbe's rope across it.

areas.name: The Fissure Lip
areas.text: The edge of the fissure that broke the road, ropes and markers dangling into it. Going in leads down to The Rope Descent.

locations.name: Grey Pilgrims' Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: High]

A road across the Blight walked by pilgrims in grey who come to pray for the cursed. Few walk it twice. Small prayer bells ring along the Ash Road, and the packed ash closes over each footprint behind the walker. Pilgrims in grey robes and straw hats walk in loose files, praying aloud for the cursed and helping the weakest along. Shun the Biwa Monk walks among them with his lute on his back and sings the fall of the old capital at rest stops in return for food. The road starts at Haibara and runs out across the Blight.

areas.name: Ash Road
areas.text: A road of packed ash walked by pilgrims in grey, prayer bells ringing faintly and every footprint filling in behind them.

locations.name: Grey Pilgrims' Road, The Penitents' Road
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-38 · Danger: High]

The pilgrims' road after the war, thronged with soldiers walking to the Vow Temple to atone. The ash is ankle-deep and the prayers never stop.

areas.name: Ash Road, After the War
areas.text: An ash road crowded with penitent soldiers.

locations.name: Grey Thread Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A small shrine on a cliff path where pilgrims tie grey threads to a sacred rope and quiet keepers sweep the steps. Few pilgrims stay long. Wind combs through the Thread Rope, and the grey threads hiss against one another like rain on a roof. Keeper Ito sweeps the same steps over and over, glancing down the cliff path at every footfall. The shrine is small: a worn stair, an offering box, and a plain Keepers' Room behind a sliding door. Pilgrims buy a thread from the keepers, tie it on, bow once and go back down.

areas.name: Keepers' Room
areas.text: A plain room with a writing desk and a boy's wooden sword hung on the wall.

areas.name: Thread Rope
areas.text: A sacred rope hung with thousands of grey threads, stirring in the cliff wind.

locations.name: Grey Thread Shrine, Shrine of the Hidden Heir
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: High]

The grey thread shrine after the war, guarded day and night: the boy raised here is the emperor's hidden son, and now the emperor is dead, every claimant wants him found or gone.

areas.name: Keepers' Room, After the War
areas.text: The keepers' room, guarded, a council in whispers.

areas.name: Thread Rope, After the War
areas.text: The grey thread rope, cut and retied in a new knot.

locations.name: Grudge Well Sanctum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

A ring of curse wells inside a broken wall, tended by sorcerers in grey who draw up grudges in long iron ladles and bottle them for sale. The air tastes of ash and old anger. The broken wall encloses a bare yard and seven wells, and the first thing noticed is a low murmur, like many voices far away, rising from the Well Ring. A Grudge Well Sorcerer in ash-grey robes stands watch at each well beside its chained ladle. Master Hai runs the Bottling House, a long shed where she inspects each dark bottle before it is sealed and shelved. Buyers come from Haibara and further, and they do not linger once their business is done.

areas.name: Bottling House
areas.text: A long shed of dark bottles on shelves, each holding a whispering grudge.

areas.name: The Deepest Well
areas.text: A well wider than the rest, its rope cut, a cold wind rising from it.

areas.name: Well Ring
areas.text: Seven stone wells in a ring, each with a ladle chained to it and a sorcerer watching.

locations.name: Grudge Well Sanctum, The Overflowing Wells
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

The grudge wells after the war, overflowing: the war poured a generation of new grudges into them, and the sorcerers bottle faster than they can sell. Grey smoke stands over the sanctum like a second sky.

areas.name: Bottling House, After the War
areas.text: A bottling house working through the night, grey jars stacked to the roof.

areas.name: The Deepest Well, After the War
areas.text: The deepest well, its grudge-water risen almost to the lip.

areas.name: Well Ring, After the War
areas.text: The ring of wells, every one of them smoking.

locations.name: Guild Counting House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-15 · Danger: Low]

The Saikai Merchant Guild's counting house: three floors of clerks at abacuses, money changers at the front counters, and a vault of ledgers at the back. Half the isles' debts are written down in this building. The clack of abacus beads reaches the street before the door does. Downstairs, changers at the Money Counters weigh coin, bite silver and write receipts for a queue of captains, farmers and shrine stewards. Upstairs, Guildmaster Daikokuya Sohei sits on his cushion in the Council Room, laughing with whoever is in favour while the windows show him every quay. Clerks run between floors with ledgers under their arms and talk only in figures.

areas.name: Council Room
areas.text: An upstairs room with a long table where the Guild Council meets. The screens are painted with ships, and the windows look down on every quay.

areas.name: Ledger Vault
areas.text: A fireproof storehouse of ledgers behind iron doors, with a clerk who knows where every page is. There is a gap on one shelf.

areas.name: Money Counters
areas.text: Long counters where changers weigh coin, test silver with their teeth and write receipts. The clack of abacus beads never stops.

locations.name: Guild Counting House, Seat of the Debt
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-29 · Danger: High]

The counting house after the war, swollen into the real capital of the isles: a new wing for the houses' debts, guards in guild colours at every door, and a queue of envoys from every claimant waiting to beg for terms.

areas.name: Council Room, After the War
areas.text: The council room where the guild decides which house survives the winter.

areas.name: Ledger Vault, After the War
areas.text: An iron vault of debts; the Regent's ledger sits on its own shelf.

areas.name: Money Counters, After the War
areas.text: Long counters where envoys sign away their houses' rice for loans.

areas.name: The Guildmaster's Shrine
areas.text: A family shrine in the counting house, an abacus on the altar: Guildmaster Daikokuya Sohei died the week the debts were called in.

locations.name: Haibara
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-45 · Danger: Severe]

The one town on the edge of the Blight, a waystation built from the timbers of the war's fortresses, where curse-bearers and the desperate trade. Grey ash lies in the gutters and settles on every sill, and people in the street wear cloth over their mouths. The road from the north ends in the yard of the Grey Banner Waystation, where Keeper Hisako rents beds and puts out anyone who starts trouble. Curse-bearers, curse-hunters, relic buyers and pilgrims all pass through. Yukiha keeps a rented room at the Vow Temple and goes out at night to break small curses for coppers.

areas.name: Grey Banner Waystation
areas.text:
The waystation where the road from the north ends, its yard hung with the faded banners of both armies.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Oiwake Station (about 12 Mon), Saikai (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Sealed Well
areas.text: The town well under a cracked stone seal, rope around it, ash that never settles near it.

areas.name: Vow Temple
areas.text: A low temple where binding vows are sworn before a monk who asks only whether you understand the price.

locations.name: Haibara Ash Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A market held at night in Haibara's back streets where cursed relics, bottled grudges and stranger things are sold. After dark grey awnings go up in the back streets of Haibara, and the Night Stalls open by candlelight. Buyers wear masks or hoods and speak low, and nobody asks anyone's name. Dolls, swords, mirrors and sealed bottles lie out on cloths, each with a price chalked beside it. Dealer Tomekichi keeps the best-lit stall, gloved and well dressed, and tells each relic's history at length. The market packs away before dawn.

areas.name: Night Stalls
areas.text: Back-street stalls under grey awnings selling relics and bottled grudges by candlelight, buyers masked and voices hushed.

locations.name: Haibara Ash Market, Market of War Relics
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-40 · Danger: Severe]

The ash market after the war, selling relics from the battlefields: cursed swords pulled from the dead, banners that still bleed, and grudge-jars labelled by army.

areas.name: Night Stalls, After the War
areas.text: Night stalls of battlefield relics, each one wrapped in prayer paper.

locations.name: Haibara, On the Grudge Line
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-50 · Danger: Severe]

The blight's town after the war, no longer at the blight's edge but deep inside it: the grey has spread north past the road, the sealed well smokes day and night, and a ring of new shrines, the Grudge Line, has been raised a day's walk north to hold it. The Vow Temple has never had so many penitents.

areas.name: Grey Banner Waystation, After the War
areas.text: The waystation, crowded with soldiers come to atone at the temple.

areas.name: Lady Shizune's Grave
areas.text: A grave behind the Vow Temple, ringed with dog charms: the inugami found Lady Shizune.

areas.name: Sealed Well, After the War
areas.text: The well in the square, smoking through a broken seal.

areas.name: Vow Temple, After the War
areas.text: The vow temple, a queue of penitents from every army.

locations.name: Halls of the Nine-Tailed Lady
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-40 · Danger: Severe]

A court of vermilion halls deep in the wood, lit by cold foxfire and attended by foxes in human shapes. Humans who come with good manners and a gift are received; others find themselves walking home in circles. Pale flames float at shoulder height along Foxfire Avenue, giving no heat and no smoke, and the vermilion halls beyond smell of cedar and old paper. Fox servants in human shape move silently, now and then with a tail showing. Lady Nanao, dressed in grey, keeps the accounts of the Hall of Bargains and writes each favour on a leaf. Guests wait there until Lady Tsukiha agrees to see them in The Lady's Pavilion.

areas.name: Foxfire Avenue
areas.text: An avenue of floating cold flames leading to the halls, never the same length twice.

areas.name: Hall of Bargains
areas.text: A hall where foxes trade favours and promises, every deal written on a leaf.

areas.name: The Lady's Pavilion
areas.text: A pavilion of white silk where the nine-tailed lady receives guests behind a screen.

locations.name: Halls of the Nine-Tailed Lady, The Court of Refuge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-46 · Danger: Severe]

The vermilion halls after the war, crowded: yokai driven out of burned shrines and half-blood children from the houses' camps have come to the Lady's court, and the Hall of Bargains has never written so many favours. Lady Nanao's leaves fill baskets. The court holds the wood's edge as its own now, and humans who come without a gift are walked home before they arrive.

areas.name: Foxfire Avenue, After the War
areas.text: Foxfire Avenue, lit twice over, refugee yokai sleeping in its side halls.

areas.name: Hall of Bargains, After the War
areas.text: The Hall of Bargains, favours written on leaves by the basket.

areas.name: The Lady's Pavilion, After the War
areas.text: The Lady's pavilion, the Regent's envoy waiting outside it.

locations.name: Hanging Bridge Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A high pass crossed by a long hanging bridge over a gorge, with a toll hut on each side kept by Hayate shinobi. Wind moans through the gorge, and the bridge ropes creak under every gust. The planks of The Hanging Bridge are worn pale, with a few newer, darker boards where someone patched them. Hayate shinobi in grey-blue keep the Toll Huts at either end and take coin, rice or news. Michiru of the Straw Hat crosses here often, face hidden under her deep hat, and the toll-keepers argue about her after she has gone. Grey wolves sometimes circle the huts at dusk.

areas.name: The Hanging Bridge
areas.text: A long rope bridge swaying over the gorge, its planks worn pale.

areas.name: Toll Huts
areas.text: Two huts at either end, each keeping its own tally and its own grudges.

locations.name: Hanging Bridge Pass, The War-Line Pass
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-34 · Danger: High]

The hanging bridge pass after the war, the front line between the villages: patrols cross it under truce flags only, and Brother Ganseki keeps the toll huts as a neutral ground nobody dares break.

areas.name: Denpachi's Toll Box
areas.text: His toll box nailed to the bridge post: Toll-Keeper Denpachi was killed on the bridge in the first raid.

areas.name: Tamae's Cairn
areas.text: A cairn at the gorge's edge where the ropes were cut: Porter Tamae fell with the bridge.

areas.name: The Hanging Bridge, After the War
areas.text: The hanging bridge under truce flags, patrols watching each end.

areas.name: Toll Huts, After the War
areas.text: Ganseki's toll huts, neutral ground on the war-line.

locations.name: Hanging Lantern Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A village clinging to the cliffs, every house hung with a lantern to keep the dead from mistaking it for theirs. Surf booms below the Cliff Path, and the steps between houses are slick with spray and fish scales. Nets dry on poles, gulls quarrel over the gutting tubs, and the lanterns on the eaves creak in the wind. A young woman with wrapped hands mends nets on a doorstep and keeps her back to the light. The villagers fish, salt their catch and carry it up the coast to sell in Tasogare.

areas.name: Cliff Path
areas.text: A path of steps cut into the cliff between lantern-hung houses, fishers' nets drying and the sea booming below.

locations.name: Hanging Lantern Village, Village of Lanterns for Sons
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The cliff village after the war, a lantern hung on every house for a son the war took. The Court is too busy to collect its fish.

areas.name: Cliff Path, After the War
areas.text: A cliff path lined with lanterns for the village's dead.

locations.name: Haunted Teahouse Lane
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A lane of abandoned teahouses on the city's edge where lights are seen at night and laughter heard from empty rooms. By day the lane is quiet, its door curtains faded and its shutters warped, with weeds pushing up through the paving. At Lane End an old wall is hung thick with paper umbrellas that open and close on their own, rustling in still air. The door of the Empty Teahouse stands open on laid tables and a kettle that is somehow still warm. Few people from Seimei come here after dark, and those who must pass walk quickly with a charm in hand.

areas.name: Empty Teahouse
areas.text: A teahouse with its tables laid and its kettle warm, and no one inside.

areas.name: Lane End
areas.text: Where the lane ends at an old wall covered in umbrellas that open on their own.

locations.name: Haunted Teahouse Lane, The Guarded Lane
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: High]

The haunted lane after the war, quieter: the tsukumogami keep to their teahouse, and Shizume keeps the empty one at the lane's end with her two blades.

areas.name: Empty Teahouse, After the War
areas.text: The empty teahouse, two cups set out, Shizume at the door.

areas.name: Lane End, After the War
areas.text: The lane's end, offerings left in a row by someone unseen.

locations.name: Hayate Ridge Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-28 · Danger: High]

The wind village on the ridges above the passes: houses lashed against the gales, wind chimes on every eave, wolf pens and herb gardens. Its shinobi run the ridges at speed and laugh loudly. Wind chimes ring from every eave at once, and the gale carries the smell of wolf and crushed herbs across the ridge. Hayate Oboro is usually at the Ridge Gate, laughing with runners as they come in. Kazakiri Daigo works the Wolf Pens with the handlers, iron war fans at his belt, and Hayate Tsumugi turns up in the Healers' Gardens whenever she has not found a reason to leave them. Contracts, herbs and wolf pups are the village's trade.

areas.name: Healers' Apothecary
areas.text: The healer clan's drying lofts and mortar benches, where the gardens' herbs become salves, tonics and poisons.

areas.name: Healers' Gardens
areas.text: Terraced gardens of medicinal herbs tended by the healer clan.

areas.name: Ridge Gate
areas.text: A gate of lashed timber on the ridge, the wind howling through it.

areas.name: Wolf Pens
areas.text: Pens of grey fighting wolves and their handlers, who smell the same.

locations.name: Hayate Ridge Village, Burned on the Ridge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-38 · Danger: High]

The wind village after the war: the healers' gardens trampled, a burnt patch on the ridge where Kagegi's raid came closest, and the wolf pens empty because the wolves are on patrol.

areas.name: Healers' Apothecary, After the War
areas.text: The apothecary, its shelves half bare, grinding salves for the war-line day and night.

areas.name: Healers' Gardens, After the War
areas.text: Trampled healers' gardens, tended again by the wounded.

areas.name: Ridge Gate, After the War
areas.text: The ridge gate, barricaded, archers on the gatehouse.

areas.name: Wolf Pens, After the War
areas.text: Empty wolf pens; the wolves patrol the war-line.

locations.name: Heron Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-28 · Danger: High]

An island in the marsh where herons nest by thousands and the old marsh clan buried its dead. The noise reaches a boat long before the island does: thousands of herons calling from the trees of the Heron Colony, which stand white with birds above ground white with droppings. The smell is strong. Further in, at the Old Graves, weathered posts of the old marsh clan lean in a ring, half sunk in mud and dark with moss. Smugglers and fishermen from Ashiura pass the island in the channels but rarely land.

areas.name: Heron Colony
areas.text: Trees white with nesting herons, the noise deafening, the ground white below.

areas.name: Old Graves
areas.text: Weathered grave posts in a ring, half sunk in mud.

areas.name: The Mud Landing
areas.text: A mud bank where boats run aground and the herons' noise begins. Going in leads down to The Nesting Trees.

locations.name: Heron Island, Island of the Drowned Navy
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-38 · Danger: High]

Heron Island after the war, its channels choked with sunk warships the herons nest in. The nure-onna hunt fatter prey now.

areas.name: Heron Colony, After the War
areas.text: Herons nesting in the masts of sunk warships.

areas.name: Old Graves, After the War
areas.text: Old graves and new ones, the new ones dug by the smugglers.

areas.name: The Mast Landing
areas.text: A landing among sunk warships' masts, the herons nesting in their rigging. Going in leads down to The Mast Rookery.

locations.name: Hibana
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-40 · Danger: Severe]

The largest forge town on the volcano's slopes: chimneys glowing all night, the ring of hammers, hot springs used for quenching, and masters who choose their customers. Hammers ring from Forge Row day and night, and the air tastes of coal smoke and hot iron. Each forge door carries its master's crest, and customers wait on benches outside to be accepted or turned away. Old Kanetsugu sits outside one of the forges every day, watching the younger smiths work. Down at the Ember Pier the ferry puts passengers ashore into ash and steam, where Troupe-Master Sanshiro and his actors unload a cart of costumes.

areas.name: Ember Pier
areas.text:
The pier where the Ember Strait ferry from Oiwake puts in, in a haze of ash and steam.

The post road serves this yard: ferries sail to Oiwake Station (about 30 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Forge Row
areas.text: A street of forges up the slope, each master's crest over the door.

areas.name: Quenching Springs
areas.text: Hot springs where blades are quenched and smiths bathe, steam rising into the dusk.

locations.name: Hibana, The Brighter Forges
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-46 · Danger: Severe]

The forge town after the war, brighter: chimneys glowing all night and all day, hammers ringing without rest, and masters who no longer choose their customers because the Regent's agents choose for them. Old Kanetsugu still sits outside his forge, watching smiths younger than ever at work.

areas.name: Ember Pier, After the War
areas.text: The ember pier, warship iron loaded beside actors' carts.

areas.name: Forge Row, After the War
areas.text: Forge row, every chimney glowing, the Regent's agents at the doors.

areas.name: Quenching Springs, After the War
areas.text: The quenching springs, running too hot to touch, steam hiding the far bank.

locations.name: Hidetsugu's Manor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The regent's nephew keeps a lively manor on the edge of the capital: a dueling yard full of young swords, a hall for speeches, and a stable of fine horses. Hidetsugu himself trains at dawn where anyone can watch. The clack of wooden swords carries into the street before the gate comes into view. In the Dueling Yard, young retainers spar and cheer each other's cuts, and Lord Takamori Hidetsugu trains among them at first light, sharing sake afterwards with whoever fought well. The Speech Hall stands open for lords and officials, gold-striped banners hanging behind its dais. Grooms walk fine horses up and down the stable lane.

areas.name: Dueling Yard
areas.text: A sanded yard where Hidetsugu's young swords spar from morning to night, cheering each other's cuts. The clack of wooden swords carries to the street.

areas.name: Speech Hall
areas.text: A hall with a raised dais where the nephew speaks to lords and officials about the reign to come. Banners with a single gold stripe hang behind him.

locations.name: Hidetsugu's Manor, Camp-Lord's Hall
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-33 · Danger: High]

The nephew's manor turned into a war camp: the duelling yard churned to mud by drilled levies, the speech hall full of maps, and banners of the claimants who backed the nephew hung upside down in the stable where his enemies can see them.

areas.name: Dueling Yard, After the War
areas.text: Mud and drill-lines where young swords once duelled for show.

areas.name: Kanzaki Ryo's Practice Post
areas.text: His practice post in the dueling yard, a death tablet tied to it: Young Sword Kanzaki Ryo died in his first battle at Sekigane.

areas.name: Speech Hall, After the War
areas.text: Maps of the plain on every wall, pins where every village still holds rice.

locations.name: Hinode Fortress
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-45 · Danger: Severe]

The Breath Hunters' fortress on the crag above Asahi Gate: barracks, training yards for the eight breathing schools, and a forge where sun-steel is worked. The sunrise banner flies over it day and night. The first sounds inside the walls are hard breathing and the crack of wooden blades from the Breathing Yards, where hunters drill until steam rises off their shoulders. Hinode Saya trains there apart from the others of her year. Above the yards, Commander Asahina Tetsu works in the Commander's Tower over a map of the north studded with pins. Day to day the fortress is a barracks: meals, kit inspection, and rotations out to the wall.

areas.name: Breathing Yards
areas.text: Eight yards, one per school, where hunters drill forms in the snow until they steam.

areas.name: Commander's Tower
areas.text: A tower with a map of the north on its table, pins for every demon sighting.

areas.name: Sun-Steel Forge
areas.text: A forge facing east, its fire lit only at dawn, its steel pale as morning.

locations.name: Hinode Fortress, The Last Fortress
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-50 · Danger: Severe]

The Breath Hunters' fortress after the war, the north's last wall: the sunrise banner still flies, the Breathing Yards drill children who would not have been called for three more years, and Commander Asahina Tetsu's map of the north has more black pins than white. Hinode Saya trains apart, as ever, and harder.

areas.name: Breathing Yards, After the War
areas.text: The breathing yards, drilling children in uniforms cut down to fit.

areas.name: Commander's Tower, After the War
areas.text: The commander's tower, black pins crowding the map of the north.

areas.name: Sun-Steel Forge, After the War
areas.text: The sun-steel forge, never cold, blades forged for hands too young.

locations.name: Hiwada Horse Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The horse house's open country: pastures to the horizon, a manor on a low rise, and archery butts where riders shoot at the gallop from dawn. The plain's farmers ride out here to beg help against bandits. Hooves drum like rain across the Gallop Range, where riders loose arrows at straw targets at full speed. Lord Hiwada Tamenori rides and shoots among them, laughing at misses louder than anyone. Grooms in the long Hiwada Stables know every horse by name, and Steward Kosaka Gen walks the aisles with an account book. The smell of hay, leather and horse sweat is everywhere.

areas.name: Gallop Range
areas.text: A long straight run lined with straw targets where riders loose arrows at full speed. Hooves drum the ground like rain.

areas.name: Hiwada Stables
areas.text: Long stables of fine horses and grooms who know every one by name. One stall is barred and guarded, and the horses near it are nervous.

locations.name: Hiwada Horse Fields, The Empty Pastures
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-32 · Danger: High]

The horse house's pastures after the cavalry rode to war and mostly did not come back: fences down, half the stables empty, the archery butts used for firewood. Widows of the riders work the remaining herd themselves.

areas.name: Gallop Range, After the War
areas.text: Open ground where a few riders still train, more of them women than before.

areas.name: Hiwada Stables, After the War
areas.text: Long stables, most stalls empty, a captured raider's chains still on one post.

areas.name: Lord Hiwada's Barrow
areas.text: A barrow on the horse fields, his saddle and bow laid on it: Lord Hiwada Tamenori fell at Sekigane leading his riders.

locations.name: Hot Spring Inn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: Moderate]

An inn of hot springs where swordsmen wait for their commissions. Steam drifts over black rocks around the Steam Bath, and the smell of minerals hangs over the whole inn. Swordsmen with wrapped blades lodge here for weeks while the forges of Hibana finish their commissions, passing the days soaking, drinking and sizing each other up. Buyer Shinpei is usually in the water, his sword wrapped and within reach. Maids carry towels and sake between the bath and the rooms.

areas.name: Steam Bath
areas.text: An outdoor bath among black rocks, swordsmen soaking and eyeing each other through the steam.

locations.name: Hot Spring Inn, The Buyers' Inn
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-33 · Danger: High]

The hot spring inn after the war, full of buyers rather than swordsmen: house agents, Debt Harbour factors and foreign captains waiting in the Steam Bath for orders. Buyer Shinpei is still in the water, his sword wrapped and within reach.

areas.name: Steam Bath, After the War
areas.text: The steam bath, buyers soaking, swords wrapped within reach.

locations.name: Hundred Fields Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A rice village of thatched roofs and flooded paddies, typical of the hundred that feed the capital. Its people are tired, taxed and quiet when samurai pass. Frogs croak in the flooded paddies, and the air smells of mud and woodsmoke. Villagers walk the Paddy Dikes in single file and bow low when samurai pass; at night wild boars root along the dikes. Headman Tahei keeps the tax register in the Headman's House and greets every visitor with a nervous smile and a long memory. Like the hundred villages around it, it sends its rice to Miyako.

areas.name: Headman's House
areas.text: The largest thatched house, where the headman keeps the tax register and a nervous smile.

areas.name: Paddy Dikes
areas.text: Narrow earth dikes between flooded paddies, where everyone walks in single file.

locations.name: Hundred Fields Village, The Flooded Fields
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

A rice village after the dykes broke: half the paddies are mud, half the thatch is new, and the village feeds a Straw Mask patrol and a Regent's tax post on the same day. Nobody looks at anyone.

areas.name: Headman Tahei's Grave
areas.text: A grave by the burned tax house: Headman Tahei stayed when the village burned. The register lies on the stone, unburned.

areas.name: Headman's House, After the War
areas.text: The headman's house, a tax post nailed to one wall and a straw mask hung on the other.

areas.name: Paddy Dikes, After the War
areas.text: Broken dykes and drowned paddies, villagers mending them with bare hands.

locations.name: Hunters' Graveyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

Where the Breath Hunters bury their dead with their blades set as markers, rows of pale steel in the snow. The graveyard is silent except for the wind ringing faintly off the steel. The Blade Rows stretch across the slope, each pale sun-steel sword driven point-down over a hunter's grave, with cords and charms tied to the hilts by friends. Hunters come up from Asahi Gate after each Demon Night to scrape frost from the blades and read the names cut near the guards.

areas.name: Blade Rows
areas.text: Rows of sun-steel blades standing in the snow as grave markers.

areas.name: Empty Grave
areas.text: A grave with its blade missing and the earth undisturbed.

locations.name: Hunters' Graveyard, The Graveyard of Steel
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

The hunters' graveyard after the war, spread down the slope: the Blade Rows run twice as far, and the pale steel rings in the wind like a field of bells. The hunters stopped cutting names when they ran short of time.

areas.name: Blade Rows, After the War
areas.text: Blade rows running down the slope, unnamed steel among the named.

areas.name: Empty Grave, After the War
areas.text: The empty grave, three more beside it now.

areas.name: Kurogi's Blade
areas.text: His own blade planted at the head of the rows: Grave-Warden Kurogi was killed guarding the empty graves.

locations.name: Hunters' Supply Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The road that carries rice and steel from the south to the Hold. Ox carts creak up the Cart Track in a slow line, loaded with rice bales and bundles of bar steel for the Hold. Drivers stamp their feet and beat their arms at every halt. Quartermaster Kuwabara rides alongside with his ledger, counting bales and grumbling about the cold. Recruiter Gonnosuke walks the other way, south toward the villages, in a sunrise haori. The road ends at Asahi Gate.

areas.name: Cart Track
areas.text: A rutted track of supply carts and oxen, the drivers stamping their feet in the cold.

locations.name: Hunters' Supply Road, The Starving Road
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-33 · Danger: High]

The supply road after the war, half empty: the south's rice went to the houses' armies and has not come back. Quartermaster Kuwabara still counts bales and grumbles, but the carts are few, and Recruiter Gonnosuke comes back north with children.

areas.name: Cart Track, After the War
areas.text: The cart track, few carts, ruts filled with snow.

locations.name: Ice Shrine of the White Stag
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-55 · Danger: Deadly]

An ancient shrine carved into the ice, its walls covered in carvings of a white stag. Cold blue light filters through ice walls carved with stags in every pose: running, grazing, standing with heads raised. The Antler Hall is carved floor to roof with a thousand antlers, so fine that each tine catches the light. Priestess Shirane, pale and silver-haired, walks the walls tending the carvings. Few exiles visit, and those who do leave offerings of salt and pine at the door.

areas.name: Antler Hall
areas.text: A hall carved with a thousand antlers.

areas.name: Melting Altar
areas.text: An altar of ice dripping onto the floor.

locations.name: Ice Shrine of the White Stag, The Melting Shrine
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-57 · Danger: Deadly]

The ice shrine of the white stag after the war, melting: the carvings drip, the thousand antlers in the Antler Hall have lost their tines, and water pools at the Melting Altar. Priestess Shirane carves new stags as fast as the old ones fade.

areas.name: Antler Hall, After the War
areas.text: The antler hall, its fine tines melted to stubs.

areas.name: Melting Altar, After the War
areas.text: The melting altar, water pooling at its foot.

areas.name: Shizuku's Stag
areas.text: A small stag carved fresh in the melting wall: Acolyte Shizuku of the Stag drowned in the melt under the shrine.

locations.name: Inugami Kennels
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Ruined kennels of an old curse-family who made dog spirits by a cruel rite. The family is gone; the dogs are not. Scratch marks score every board of the Kennel Rows, deep enough to lay a finger in, and the broken pens still smell faintly of dog. Now and then something like panting comes from an empty pen. At the far end the Family Shrine holds dog skulls lined up on shelves before grudge tablets dark with age. Nobody from Haibara comes here willingly, and the path in is overgrown with grey grass.

areas.name: Family Shrine
areas.text: A small shrine of dog skulls and grudge tablets.

areas.name: Kennel Rows
areas.text: Rows of broken pens, scratch marks on every board.

locations.name: Inugami Kennels, The Unleashed Kennels
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The inugami kennels after the war, half empty: the family set its dogs on the war's enemies and not all of them came back to their pens.

areas.name: Family Shrine, After the War
areas.text: The family shrine, prayers for dogs that did not return.

areas.name: Kennel Rows, After the War
areas.text: Kennel rows, half the pens open and empty.

locations.name: Kagegi Outer Watchpost
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A cedar watchtower on the outer edge of Kagegi land, signalling the village with mirrors. The cedar tower creaks in the wind, and flashes of light from the Mirror Platform blink toward the valley at set intervals. Watcher Nezumi sits on the watcher's mat up top, describing everything below out loud whether anyone is listening or not: carts, birds, a woodcutter, the weather. The watchpost answers to Kagegi Village, and its ladder is pulled up when strangers approach.

areas.name: Mirror Platform
areas.text: A platform at the top of the cedar tower with signal mirrors and a watcher's mat, the valley spread out below.

locations.name: Kagegi Outer Watchpost, Watchpost on the Line
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-33 · Danger: High]

The outer watchpost after the war, a fort now: its mirror platform signals Kagegi's lines every hour, and its watchers sleep in their armour.

areas.name: Mirror Platform, After the War
areas.text: The mirror platform, flashing signals down the war-line.

locations.name: Kagegi Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-30 · Danger: High]

The hidden village of the southwestern slopes, built into a mist-filled valley among black cedars: training grounds, clan compounds, and the mission hall that sells its shinobi to the realm. Mist lies in the valley until midmorning, and the thud of thrown kunai carries from the Cedar Training Grounds before the sun clears the ridges. Visitors meet Yumeno Kasumi first at the Outer Checkpoint, where she takes each traveller's hand in a drowsy greeting before anyone is escorted up. Kagegi Rin drills the younger apprentices hard among the scarred posts, and clients sit waiting in the Mission Hall for Kagegi Sojun to name a price.

areas.name: Cedar Training Grounds
areas.text: Clearings among the cedars, posts scarred by blades, where children learn to throw before they learn to read.

areas.name: Mission Hall
areas.text: Where contracts are posted, ranked and handed out, and where clients wait to be told the price.

areas.name: Outer Checkpoint
areas.text:
The checkpoint below the village where the post road ends and every visitor is met, searched and escorted; a guarded path runs down to the north cove where the White Strait ferry puts in.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Kitsunebi Crossing (about 12 Mon), Miyako (about 12 Mon), Tasogare (about 12 Mon); ferries sail to Shirokawa (about 30 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Kagegi Village, Burned at the Edge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-40 · Danger: Severe]

The hidden village after the war, no longer hidden: a burnt patch on its eastern slope where Hayate fire-talismans fell, smoke rising from the cedars, and every genin on the walls. The cold war ended the year the realm went to war, and became a hot one.

areas.name: Cedar Training Grounds, After the War
areas.text: Training grounds turned to drill for war, burnt cedars at their edge.

areas.name: Mission Hall, After the War
areas.text: The mission hall, every mission now against Hayate.

areas.name: Outer Checkpoint, After the War
areas.text: The checkpoint, doubled, nobody let through without a seal.

locations.name: Kappa River Fords
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Shallow fords on the plain's great river where travellers cross on foot. Cucumbers are left on the bank, and children are told never to wade alone. Reeds rustle along the river, and the Offering Bank is strewn with cucumbers, some fresh and some soft and rotting. The Shallow Ford runs knee-deep over smooth stones, quick and cold, and something small and green ducks beneath the surface now and then. Travellers cross in groups, holding hands, and farmers set down a fresh cucumber before they step in.

areas.name: Offering Bank
areas.text: A grassy bank strewn with cucumber offerings, some fresh, some rotting.

areas.name: Shallow Ford
areas.text: Knee-deep water over smooth stones, quick and cold. Something moves under the surface.

areas.name: The Kappa Steps
areas.text: Worn steps cut into the bank where the river runs under an overhang into the kappa's holes. Going in leads down to The Undercut Bank.

locations.name: Kappa River Fords, The Drowned Ford
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-32 · Danger: High]

The fords after an army crossed them: the banks trampled, cucumbers rotting in heaps nobody remembers leaving, and more drowned men in the reeds than the kappa ever took. Travellers wait for a guide or go a day round.

areas.name: Offering Bank, After the War
areas.text: A bank heaped with cucumbers from frightened soldiers, most of them rotting.

areas.name: Shallow Ford, After the War
areas.text: The ford, deeper now where the banks gave way under cavalry.

areas.name: The Trampled Steps
areas.text: The kappa steps, broken by cavalry, leading down under the overhang into flooded holes. Going in leads down to The Flooded Undercut.

locations.name: Kirisame Stilt Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-28 · Danger: High]

Houses on stilts deep in the reeds, joined by plank walks and hidden by fog most of the day. The rain clan lives here and lets very few visitors leave by a different channel than they came. Fog hides the village until a boat is already among the stilts, and then voices go quiet on every porch. The Plank Walks are narrow and wet, and Kirisame Nagi waits on them with a tea tray and a smile for each new face. Herbs and gourds hang drying from the eaves of the Poison House, where the matriarch Kirisame Shigure receives anyone the clan allows that far. Clan members in rain-patterned clothes mend nets and watch strangers without speaking.

areas.name: Plank Walks
areas.text: Narrow walks between stilt houses, slick with fog, with water dark below.

areas.name: Poison House
areas.text: A stilt house hung with drying herbs and gourds, where nobody eats.

locations.name: Kirisame Stilt Village, Village of the Grey Mark
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 27-38 · Danger: High]

The rain clan's village after the war, quieter and more careful: more of its children carry the curse's grey mark, and Amenbo still runs messages across the plank walks faster than any boat.

areas.name: Plank Walks, After the War
areas.text: The plank walks, Amenbo's blur crossing them twice an hour.

areas.name: Poison House, After the War
areas.text: The poison house, its vats now brewing a cure for the grey mark.

locations.name: Kitsune Shrine Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-15 · Danger: Low]

A road of small fox shrines leading into the wood, each with a stone fox and a bowl of rice. Small shrines no taller than a child line the road, and the path smells of incense and moss. Rice in the bowls at the Fox Statues is replaced every morning, though nobody is seen doing it. The Begging Monk of the Fox Road walks the road daily with his bowl, blessing travellers and asking for rice. At dusk a lovely traveller with a blue-burning lantern sometimes offers to walk with lone pilgrims toward the Halls of the Nine-Tailed Lady.

areas.name: Fox Statues
areas.text: A road lined with stone foxes and rice bowls, one statue broken, its head in the grass.

locations.name: Kitsune Shrine Road, The Closed Road
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-29 · Danger: High]

The fox shrine road after the war, closed by the Court to anyone carrying a house's colours. The rice bowls are still filled each morning, and the Begging Monk of the Fox Road still walks it, but soldiers who try it find themselves back at the start.

areas.name: Fox Statues, After the War
areas.text: Fox statues with fresh rice, the broken one replaced by a new stone fox.

locations.name: Kitsunebi Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-40 · Danger: Severe]

A crossing town at the wood's edge where the human road and the yokai paths meet, kept by a fox shrine that both sides respect. Fried tofu and incense scent the Fox Shrine Post, and coaches stop just long enough to change passengers. Priestess Kohaku tends the shrine in red and white robes, greeting humans and yokai with the same small bow. Paper lanterns come up at dusk over the Lantern Market of the Wood, where odd stallkeepers call their wares in voices not quite human. Mame the Go-Between keeps the gate of the Refuge Go-Between House, apron on, cheerful with everyone.

areas.name: Fox Shrine Post
areas.text:
The post stop beside the fox shrine, where travellers leave fried tofu and coaches leave quickly.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Asahi Gate (about 12 Mon), Kagegi Village (about 12 Mon), Seimei (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Lantern Market of the Wood
areas.text: A night market where yokai sell to humans and humans try not to buy anything that costs a name.

areas.name: Refuge Go-Between House
areas.text: A walled house at the wood's edge where the half-yokai Refuge's go-betweens meet humans; the Refuge itself lies deep in the wood, and its way is not told.

locations.name: Kitsunebi Crossing, The Last Open Gate
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-46 · Danger: Severe]

The crossing town after the war, the last place where humans and the wood still trade: the Court allows the crossing because the market feeds the refuge. Priestess Kohaku bows to more yokai than humans now, and Mame the Go-Between's house is full every night with half-bloods waiting to be taken in.

areas.name: Fox Shrine Post, After the War
areas.text: The fox shrine post, more yokai than humans at the bow.

areas.name: Lantern Market of the Wood, After the War
areas.text: The lantern market, selling war salvage to the wood and fox charms to the road.

areas.name: Refuge Go-Between House, After the War
areas.text: The go-between's house, full of half-bloods waiting their turn.

locations.name: Kodama Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A grove of trees older than the empire where small pale spirits echo your voice back to you, a little wrong. Trunks wider than a house rise into green gloom, and the moss underfoot swallows footsteps. Along the Echo Path, every cough and word returns from the trees a beat late, slightly changed. The Elder of the Kodama watches from a root with its round head tilted. Near the Marked Trees, a cloud of giant hornets drones around a nest, and the sound carries through the whole grove.

areas.name: Echo Path
areas.text: A path where every word comes back, sometimes before you speak.

areas.name: Marked Trees
areas.text: Great trees with logger's marks painted on them, the paint running like sap.

locations.name: Kodama Grove, The Grove That Grew
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: High]

Kodama Grove after the war, wider: the trees have walked out past the Marked Trees and over the loggers' clearings, and the echoes on the Echo Path come back in soldiers' voices. The Elder of the Kodama no longer tilts its head; it stares.

areas.name: Echo Path, After the War
areas.text: The echo path, returning soldiers' voices a beat late.

areas.name: Marked Trees, After the War
areas.text: The marked trees, the loggers' marks grown over with new bark.

locations.name: Kurogane Armoury
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

The house armoury, where every Kurogane warrior's harness is fitted and repaired. Hammers ring off lacquered plates, and the air smells of lacquer, oil and leather. In the Fitting Room, armourers strap Kurogane warriors into black iron harness piece by piece and chalk dents for repair. Clerk Mitsu sits at a desk by the door with the record books, entering every harness fitted or sent out for mending. The armoury serves the castle guard and every warrior of the iron house.

areas.name: Fitting Room
areas.text: A room of lacquered iron plates on racks and armourers fitting harness, hammers ringing.

locations.name: Kurogane Armoury, The Armoury of the Victors
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

The Kurogane armoury after the war, working for the Regent: black iron harness fitted by the hundred for the peacekeeping companies, and Clerk Mitsu's record books stacked to the beams.

areas.name: Fitting Room, After the War
areas.text: The fitting room, harness for the Regent's companies on every rack.

locations.name: Kurogane Iron Castle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-40 · Danger: Severe]

The iron house's castle on the volcano's flank: black iron walls, armoured guards who never step back, and smoke from the upper forges rising behind the keep. Black iron plates cover the walls, and smoke from the upper forges drifts over the keep. At the Iron Gate, ironclads stand without moving while Kurogane Moritaka commands the guard. Kurogane Akane is often there too, ready to duel anyone who calls her lady. In the Lord's Hall, Lord Kurogane Tadakatsu holds audience under rows of empty armour, and Lady Kurogane Sen works through the mine accounts.

areas.name: Iron Gate
areas.text: A gate of black iron plates, guarded by men in full harness.

areas.name: Lord's Hall
areas.text: A hall hung with armour of every Kurogane lord, each suit empty and watching.

locations.name: Kurogane Iron Castle, The Iron Victor
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-46 · Danger: Severe]

The iron house's castle after the war, the richest seat in the isles: new iron on the walls, warship banners beside the house crest, and the empty armour in the Lord's Hall joined by the harness of the war's dead. Kurogane Moritaka still commands the Iron Gate, and Kurogane Akane still duels anyone who calls her lady.

areas.name: Iron Gate, After the War
areas.text: The Iron Gate, ironclads under warship banners.

areas.name: Lord's Hall, After the War
areas.text: The lord's hall, new harness for the dead hanging among the old.

locations.name: Lake of Stars
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The great lake the city sits on, so still on clear nights that the stars lie on its surface. Fishermen will not row out after dark. By day the lake is busy: fishing boats from Seimei work the shallows, ferries cross to the far shore, and children skip stones off the Night Shore. Out on the water the Island Shrine is small enough to hide behind a raised thumb. The air smells of weed and cold stone. Toward dusk the boats come in together, and the fishermen haul them high up the pebbles before the light goes.

areas.name: Island Shrine
areas.text: A tiny shrine on an island in the lake, its offering table empty and cracked.

areas.name: Night Shore
areas.text: A pebble shore where the stars are reflected so clearly that the water seems to vanish.

locations.name: Lake of Stars, The Hungry Lake
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: High]
