The star lake after the war, its serpent unfed for two years and growing bolder: boats cross only in convoys, and the island shrine is lit with offerings again, paid for by the refugees.

areas.name: Island Shrine, After the War
areas.text: The island shrine, relit, heaped with refugee offerings.

areas.name: Night Shore, After the War
areas.text: The night shore, refugee fires along the water's edge.

locations.name: Lakeside Pleasure Boats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-12 · Danger: Low]

Lantern-hung boats on the lake where scholars and merchants drink, listen to music and say things they regret. Koto music and laughter carry across the water from the moored boats, and the air smells of warm sake and lamp oil. Kocho of the Lantern Boat pours for her guests and takes up the shamisen when the talk slows, saying little herself. Poet Ariwake drifts from boat to boat with his brush and flask, offering a verse for a coin. Small skiffs ferry guests out from the Seimei shore at dusk and bring them back unsteady before dawn.

areas.name: Lantern Boat
areas.text: A lantern-hung boat on still water, a hostess pouring sake, music from a koto and laughter carrying across the lake.

locations.name: Lakeside Pleasure Boats, The Envoys' Boats
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The pleasure boats after the war, hired out to envoys who need to talk where no wall can hear. The hostesses earn more than ever and repeat less.

areas.name: Lantern Boat, After the War
areas.text: A lantern boat moored far out, an envoy's guards on the deck.

locations.name: Lantern Row Gambling Den
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low]

The loudest den on Lantern Row: dice, cards, sake and a debt book kept by a smiling woman. Everyone loses here eventually, and some lose more than money. Rattling dice cups and the smell of spilled sake carry out under the red lanterns well before the door. The Dice Room is packed shoulder to shoulder with sailors, clerks and ronin. Smiling Okon sits by the debt book on its lacquer stand, lending to anyone with a cheerful word and writing every coin down. Mizuchi Toranosuke is usually at the busiest table in an open sea-blue kimono, flushed and certain the next throw is his. The den sits among the tea houses of Saikai's pleasure district.

areas.name: Dice Room
areas.text: A smoky room of dice tables and shouting players, the debt book open on a lacquer stand and the smell of spilled sake everywhere.

locations.name: Lantern Row Gambling Den, Soldiers' Den
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The gambling den after the war, full of soldiers spending their pay and deserters spending what they stole. The debt book is thicker; some of its names are dead.

areas.name: Dice Room, After the War
areas.text: A packed dice room of uniforms, deserters and debt collectors.

areas.name: Toranosuke's Dice
areas.text: His dice set on a shelf behind the den's counter, a cup beside them: Mizuchi Toranosuke died aboard the burning fleet.

locations.name: Lava Tubes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Tunnels of old lava under the volcano, too hot to walk without wet cloths, home to magma crawlers. The heat hits like an open oven door, and anyone going in wraps a wet cloth over mouth and nose. The Glowing Tube runs ahead with orange walls and shimmering air, the rock ticking as it warms and cools. In the Crawler Nest, magma crawlers lie in heaps on the warm stone, their bellies glowing through the cracks in their plates. Hibana is the nearest town, and few come down from it without good reason.

areas.name: Crawler Nest
areas.text: A wide chamber where great lizards sleep on warm stone.

areas.name: Glowing Tube
areas.text: A tunnel whose walls glow orange, the air shimmering.

locations.name: Lava Tubes, The Busy Tubes
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The lava tubes after the war, a road: carts move through them at night between the deep forges and the beach yards, and the magma crawlers have been driven out of the Glowing Tube into the Crawler Nest, crowded and angry.

areas.name: Crawler Nest, After the War
areas.text: The crawler nest, crowded with the crawlers driven from the road.

areas.name: Glowing Tube, After the War
areas.text: The glowing tube, cart ruts in the cooled rock.

locations.name: Lighthouse of the Dragon's Eye
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A Mizuchi signal tower on the eastern cliff that watches for pirates and signals the fleet with fire. Wind hits the cliff top hard enough to lean against, and the smell of pine pitch hangs around the tower. A long stair climbs to the Signal Platform, where fire baskets stand ready beside stacked pitch and the whole eastern sea is in view. Keeper Sabu tends the baskets and complains about every step of the stair to anyone who has just climbed it. Sailors from the Mizuchi Naval Anchorage bring up his oil, food and pitch.

areas.name: Signal Platform
areas.text: A stone platform with fire baskets and a stack of pine pitch, the wind off the sea strong enough to lean on.

locations.name: Lighthouse of the Dragon's Eye, The Wrecker's Light
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The dragon's eye lighthouse after the war, lit for the Brine Tide every night now there is no navy to stop it. Ships that do not pay break on the reef below.

areas.name: Signal Platform, After the War
areas.text: The signal platform, a smugglers' fire burning in the lamp.

locations.name: Loggers' Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A camp of plain loggers pushing into the wood for the capital's lumber merchants. Fresh stumps and sawdust mark the camp's edge, and the steady rasp of two-man saws fills the morning. Along the Saw Line, loggers rest on felled trunks between cuts, eyes on the trees around them. Boss Ganzo strides the line with his sleeves rolled, shouting for more pace. The timber goes out by cart toward Miyako for the capital's lumber merchants, and at night the men sleep close to their fires.

areas.name: Saw Line
areas.text: A line of felled trunks and two-man saws, loggers resting and glancing at the trees around them.

locations.name: Loggers' Camp, The Swallowed Camp
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: High]

The loggers' camp after the war, swallowed: saplings stand where the stumps were, the Saw Line is grown over, and Boss Ganzo keeps a handful of men cutting at the edge for an army that no longer pays.

areas.name: Saw Line, After the War
areas.text: The old saw line, saplings shoulder-high between the stumps.

locations.name: Mask Shore
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Severe]

A grey beach where broken white masks wash up on the tide line. Beachcombers sell them; most regret it. Waves drag across grey sand with a dry clatter, because the shallows are thick with broken white masks. The beach smells of kelp and cold ash. Beachcomber Sute works the shoreline with cloth-wrapped hands, sorting pieces into baskets, and sells the best of them from the Beachcomber's Hut, where masks cover every wall and face the door. Collectors come down from Tasogare to haggle; locals will not touch the masks bare-handed.

areas.name: Beachcomber's Hut
areas.text: A driftwood hut with masks hung on every wall.

areas.name: The Tide Line Path
areas.text: A path down the dunes to where the masks begin. Going in leads down to The Clattering Sand.

areas.name: Tide Line
areas.text: A line of broken white masks along the grey sand, like teeth.

locations.name: Mask Shore, Shore of Washed-Up Masks
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-46 · Danger: Severe]

The mask shore after the war, where the tide brings in masks every night: the war fed the masked devourers, and their masks wash up by the dozen.

areas.name: Beachcomber's Hut, After the War
areas.text: A hut hung with masks from the tide.

areas.name: The Mask Dunes
areas.text: Dunes above the shore, masks half buried in the sand. Going in leads down to The Mask Tide.

areas.name: Tide Line, After the War
areas.text: A tide line strewn with pale masks.

locations.name: Mask-Maker's Workshop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A small workshop in a back alley of the lake city where an old woman carves theatre masks of rare quality. Actors and collectors queue for her work; she turns most of them away. The Shop Front is so crowded with hanging masks that the walls seem to be made of faces: demons, maidens, foxes and old men in fresh lacquer. The smell of lacquer and cedar shavings comes through the curtain from the Carving Room, with the tap of a chisel. Customers are met by an old woman who studies each face a long while and then, more often than not, refuses the order. Actors from Seimei's theatres wait in the alley outside anyway.

areas.name: Carving Room
areas.text: A back room of chisels, lacquer pots and a locked chest. A fox's tail hangs over the door.

areas.name: Shop Front
areas.text: A narrow shop hung with finished masks: demons, maidens, old men, foxes. Their eyes follow you.

locations.name: Mask-Maker's Workshop, Workshop of Borrowed Faces
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-34 · Danger: High]

The mask-maker's workshop after the war, doing a trade it never had: soldiers who want to go home as someone else, and widows who want one more night with a face.

areas.name: Carving Room, After the War
areas.text: A carving room of half-finished faces, some of them famous dead.

areas.name: Shop Front, After the War
areas.text: A shop front with a queue of soldiers and widows.

locations.name: Miners' Town
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A sooty town of miners and their families on the volcano's lower slopes. Everyone works for the house. Soot coats every roof and doorstep, and the shift bells at the mine heads set the hours. Miners trudge along Soot Street with lamps and picks, black to the elbows, while their families carry water and haul ore baskets. Everyone here draws wages from House Kurogane. Mother Tome, a widow with grey hair loose, stops each passing samurai with a petition in her hand. The forges of Hibana are a short climb up the slope.

areas.name: Soot Street
areas.text: A street of soot-black houses and tired miners, a mother with a petition at every corner.

locations.name: Miners' Town, The Hollowed Town
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-34 · Danger: High]

The miners' town after the war, short of men: the house sent its miners to dig siege works and few came back, and the shafts are worked by their sons. Mother Tome still stops every passing samurai with her petition.

areas.name: Soot Street, After the War
areas.text: Soot street, boys with picks and lamps where their fathers walked.

locations.name: Miyako
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The walled castle city: the regent's keep and the emperor's palace side by side, samurai mansions, markets, temples, and the river bridges where duels are fought at dawn. Temple bells, hawkers and the clatter of wooden sandals fill the streets under the white castle. The Castle Market sells silk, rice and blades beside stalls of gossip from every house, and the river docks smell of mud and fish. At the Riverside Post House, Ofuku of the Post House ladles soup for Warden riders and books coach seats at the top of her voice. White lotus badges and crane crests pass each other in the street without a word.

areas.name: Castle Market
areas.text: The market under the castle walls: silk, rice, blades, gossip from every house.

areas.name: Dawn Bridge
areas.text: The arched bridge where duels are fought at first light and the river carries the loser away.

areas.name: Riverside Post House
areas.text:
The post house by the river docks, where road coaches depart.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Oiwake Station (about 12 Mon), Kagegi Village (about 12 Mon), Seimei (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Miyako Castle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The regent's white castle above the capital: keep, councils and the crane banners of House Takamori. Officials in grey hurry through its gates with warrants and ledgers, and samurai watch every stair. Wet stone and ink smell strongest at the Grey Gate, where petitioners queue with their papers and clerks stamp or refuse them. Takamori spearmen in conical iron hats stand in threes, and Treasury Magistrate Sakuma Chiyo passes through with her ledgers, nodding to nobody. Deeper in, Lord Takamori Masanobu presides in the Council Hall, where councillors murmur in rows and every footstep echoes.

areas.name: Council Hall
areas.text: A long hall of polished boards where the regent's councillors sit in rows and argue in murmurs. Every footstep echoes; nobody raises a voice.

areas.name: Grey Gate
areas.text: The outer gate where petitioners queue with their papers and clerks in grey stamp them or turn them away. The smell of ink and wet stone never leaves it.

areas.name: Keep Ramparts
areas.text: The high stone walk around the keep, where Takamori retainers keep watch over the whole plain. Wind snaps the crane banners like whips.

locations.name: Miyako Castle, The Blackened Keep
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-36 · Danger: High]

The Regent's castle after the siege: soot climbing the white walls to the third roof, a breach in the outer gate patched with timber, and crane banners flying beside the guild's coin-mark. Inside, clerks count debts instead of taxes, and the council hall never empties.

areas.name: Council Hall, After the War
areas.text: A council that sits day and night and decides nothing, guild factors in the back row.

areas.name: Grey Gate, After the War
areas.text: The petitioners' gate, half its doors burned, a timber barricade where the other half stood.

areas.name: Keep Ramparts, After the War
areas.text: Soot-black ramparts where archers watch the burned quarters below.

locations.name: Miyako, Besieged
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-36 · Danger: High]

The capital after the war: the white keep stands but blackened, the imperial palace beside it roofless, and a ring of siege earthworks still circles walls nobody has the money to mend. Half the markets reopened under guild awnings; the other half are ash where the Straw Masks' fire-arrows fell. Regent's soldiers stand at every bridge, and nobody duels at dawn any more.

areas.name: Castle Market, After the War
areas.text: Half the stalls are ash; the rest sell under guild awnings at guild prices.

areas.name: Dawn Bridge, After the War
areas.text: The duelling bridge, its rail broken by a siege engine and patrolled by the Regent's pikemen.

areas.name: Riverside Post House, After the War
areas.text: Still booking coaches, though the road west stops at the barricade; the soup is thinner.

locations.name: Mizuchi Naval Anchorage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-28 · Danger: High]

The sea house's anchorage: warships with river-dragon pennants, a shipyard, and an admiral's hall on the bluff. Sailors drill on the decks from dawn. Pine tar, rope and salt are the smells, and mallets ring from the Shipyard, where half-built hulls stand on the slipways and Mizuchi marines in light armour keep guard. Admiral Mizuchi Naotora works among his charts in the Admiral's Hall on the bluff, while his elder son Mizuchi Hayato lies in a room there with a fever three days old. A quiet man from the marsh, Kirisame Raizo, waits near the slipways with a box of medicines and a white flag.

areas.name: Admiral's Hall
areas.text: A hall on the bluff with charts on every wall and a view of the whole coast.

areas.name: Shipyard
areas.text: Slipways and half-built hulls, the smell of pine tar, shipwrights hammering.

locations.name: Mizuchi Naval Anchorage, The Burned Fleet
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-38 · Danger: High]

The navy's anchorage after the war: half the fleet burned at its moorings, blackened ribs standing in the water, and the admiral's hall shuttered. The shipyard builds nothing.

areas.name: Admiral's Hall, After the War
areas.text: The shuttered admiral's hall, its banners taken down.

areas.name: Mizuchi Hayato's Pyre
areas.text: A burned pyre-stone by the admiral's hall: Mizuchi Hayato's fever took him the night the fleet burned.

areas.name: Shipyard, After the War
areas.text: A silent shipyard of half-built hulls and burned ribs.

locations.name: Monks' Herb Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

Terraced fields where monks grow herbs for the temple and the poor. Narrow terraces step down the hillside, and the air smells of mint, bitter root and turned earth. Monks from the Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls work the Herb Terraces in straw hats, weeding and carrying water up on shoulder yokes. They hand out bundles of dried herbs to the poor who walk up from the valley, and a plain shed at the top holds the season's drying racks.

areas.name: Herb Terraces
areas.text: Terraced beds of medicinal herbs tended by monks, a failed patch brown and bare.

locations.name: Monks' Herb Fields, The Failed Fields
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The monks' herb fields after the war, failed two harvests running: the herb that dulls the beast's voice will not grow in ground that took this much blood.

areas.name: Herb Terraces, After the War
areas.text: Herb terraces of withered plants.

locations.name: Moonview Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

An arched bridge over the lake's outflow where the city comes to watch the moon. Lovers leave ribbons on its rails. The bridge rises steeply in a single arch of grey wood, its rails knotted with ribbons of every colour, the oldest faded white. Couples, students and whole families from Seimei climb to the Bridge Crown on moon nights. On other evenings it is quiet except for Ryuan the Komuso, whose shakuhachi can be heard from either bank. Student Akitsu, a Bureau scribe with a weakness for bad poetry, is often at the rail with a scrap of paper and a brush.

areas.name: Bridge Crown
areas.text: The arched crown of the bridge, its rails knotted with lovers' ribbons and the moon doubled in the water below.

locations.name: Moonview Bridge, The Mourning Bridge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The moonview bridge after the war, where the Bureau student still waits every full moon for a fox who did not come back.

areas.name: Bridge Crown, After the War
areas.text: The bridge's crown, a lantern left lit for someone who does not come.

areas.name: The Moon Fox's Ribbon
areas.text: A ribbon tied to the bridge rail, a lantern beside it: The Moon Fox was killed in the fighting in Ayakashi Wood.

locations.name: Moorland Graves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A graveyard on the moor where the poor of the coast are buried. Wisps in cracked masks drift over it at night. Heather and low grave markers stretch to a gravedigger's hut at the field's edge, a lantern hanging by its door. By day the Grave Rows are quiet but for spades and crows. Gravedigger Hyozo digs in a slow stoop, and Nun Seigan walks between the graves with her prayer beads, stopping to chant over the newest mounds. Families from the coast villages bury their poor here because the ground costs nothing.

areas.name: Grave Rows
areas.text: Rows of simple graves in the heather, a gravedigger's hut at the edge and pale lights drifting after dark.

locations.name: Moorland Graves, The Overfilled Graves
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: High]

The moorland graves after the war, overfilled: new rows dug for soldiers carried home, the wisps thick as fog between them.

areas.name: Grave Rows, After the War
areas.text: Rows of new graves among the old, wisps drifting between.

areas.name: Nun Seigan's Grave
areas.text: A grave among the new rows, a sutra scroll weighted on it: Nun Seigan died laying the war dead to rest.

locations.name: Moth Dell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

A dell where black moths cover every surface and the air is thick with wings. Sound dies in it. The ground dips into a hollow where every surface is black and velvety: stones, dead branches and grass all covered in resting moths. Each step raises a cloud of them. The Hatching Stones at the bottom are crusted with eggs and give off a faint warmth. Further in, the Wing Cloud closes overhead so thickly that daylight turns grey, and wings brush the face at every breath. Nothing else that lives has been found here.

areas.name: Hatching Stones
areas.text: Stones crusted with moth eggs, warm to the touch.

areas.name: Wing Cloud
areas.text: A cloud of black moths so thick the sun is grey.

locations.name: Moth Dell, The Swarm's Dell
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

Moth Dell after the war, where the grudge swarm has grown into a cloud that blots the sun at noon. It has reached the pilgrims' road.

areas.name: Hatching Stones, After the War
areas.text: Hatching stones crusted grey with eggs.

areas.name: Wing Cloud, After the War
areas.text: A cloud of grey moths thick enough to hide the sky.

locations.name: Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The Order's oldest temple, built among seven waterfalls where ascetics fast under the cold water and the sutras are chanted day and night. Travellers are given rice and a mat without question. The roar of falling water covers every other sound, and cold spray drifts across the Falls Courtyard, where monks stand under the falls chanting. Grey-robed monks with naginata keep the gate and the courtyard. High Abbot Ryokai spends the hours before dawn in the Sutra Hall and the rest of the day greeting guests by name. In the Guest Cells, Old Nurse Tsuru, frail and white-haired, rests on her mat and accepts visitors.

areas.name: Falls Courtyard
areas.text: A courtyard ringed by seven falls, spray hanging in the air, monks under the water.

areas.name: Guest Cells
areas.text: Plain cells for travellers, a mat and a bowl in each.

areas.name: Sutra Hall
areas.text: A dim hall where monks chant in shifts so the sutras never stop.

locations.name: Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls, The Falls Temple at War
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-36 · Danger: High]

The falls temple after the war, a hospital for both villages' wounded under a truce the abbot enforces with his own staff. Hermit Shirakumo still practises under the falls every morning.

areas.name: Falls Courtyard, After the War
areas.text: The falls courtyard, Shirakumo cutting the water each dawn.

areas.name: Guest Cells, After the War
areas.text: Guest cells turned into a ward for the wounded.

areas.name: Nurse Tsuru's Grave
areas.text: A plain grave below the falls: Old Nurse Tsuru died in the temple ward, her confession given to the abbot.

areas.name: Sutra Hall, After the War
areas.text: The sutra hall, chanted by half the monks it needs.

locations.name: Oiwake Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-15 · Danger: Low]

The crossroads station where the highway forks: north for the capital, south down to Ember Strait, east for the marsh coast, west along the ash for the port. Inns, a post stable and the busiest toll barrier on the road. Horse dung, woodsmoke and boiling rice greet arrivals, and the noise of four roads meeting never quite stops. At the Toll Barrier, Captain Kajiwara chats amiably with travellers while road guards in Warden blue read papers and fill the toll ledger. Coaches swap tired horses for fresh ones in the Post Stable yard. Inside the Honjin Inn, Gensuke the Medicine-Seller unpacks his tall box of drawers and asks after everyone's aches.

areas.name: Honjin Inn
areas.text: The great inn reserved for lords on the road, and for whoever pays like one when no lord is staying.

areas.name: Post Stable
areas.text:
The relay stable and coach yard, where the post road's coaches change horses and take on passengers, and the road south runs down to the Ember Strait ferry.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Haibara (about 12 Mon), Ashiura (about 12 Mon), Miyako (about 12 Mon), Saikai (about 12 Mon); ferries sail to Hibana (about 30 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Toll Barrier
areas.text: A gate across the highway with a guardhouse, where papers, station and luggage are checked.

locations.name: Oiwake Station, Behind the Barricade
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-29 · Danger: High]

The crossroads station after the war, right behind the Straw Mask barricade: the honjin inn turned into a peasant army's headquarters, the post stable full of captured horses, and the toll barrier thrown down and burned for warmth.

areas.name: Captain Kajiwara's Stone
areas.text: A stone beside the barricade, his toll list nailed to it: Captain Kajiwara was killed when the Straw Masks took the barrier.

areas.name: Honjin Inn, After the War
areas.text: The lord's inn, now the barricade's headquarters, straw masks at the door.

areas.name: Post Stable, After the War
areas.text: Stables of captured cavalry horses, branded with three different crests.

areas.name: Toll Barrier, After the War
areas.text: The toll barrier, thrown down, its timbers burned in the guards' fires.

locations.name: Old Battle Barrow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A barrow of warriors from a war against the dead, its stones carved with old officers' marks. Cold air flows from the Barrow Mouth even at midday, smelling of old iron and stone dust, and frost rims the grass around the opening. Nobody tends the mound. Beyond the entrance the Warriors' Hall runs back into the dark, lined with armoured skeletons seated in rows as if waiting to be called. The carvings on the outer stones are weathered but still sharp at the edges, and moorland birds do not nest on the barrow.

areas.name: Barrow Mouth
areas.text: A low stone door pulled aside, cold air flowing out.

areas.name: The Pulled Stone
areas.text: A low stone door pulled aside at the barrow's mouth, cold air flowing out. Going in leads down to The Frost Passage.

areas.name: Warriors' Hall
areas.text: A long chamber of armoured skeletons sitting in rows.

locations.name: Old Battle Barrow, The Opened Barrow
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-46 · Danger: Severe]

The old battle barrow after the war, open: the warriors who refused the ferry came out to fight in the war, and some of them have not gone back in.

areas.name: Barrow Mouth, After the War
areas.text: The barrow mouth, open, an armoured dead warlord seated in it.

areas.name: The Open Door
areas.text: The barrow's stone door, wide open now, cold air flowing out. Going in leads down to The Warlord's Mouth.

areas.name: Warriors' Hall, After the War
areas.text: The warriors' hall, half its benches empty.

locations.name: Old Battlefield of Sekigane
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A wide field of grave mounds where two houses fought a hundred years ago; rusted armour still surfaces after rain. Farmers will not plough it, and travellers cross it by day. Crows sit on the stones topping the Grave Mounds, rows of low grassy hummocks that stretch across the field. Scraps of rusted armour poke from the earth where the rain has washed it. On one side of The Great Mound a fresh hole has been dug, and cold air breathes out of it. Grave-Robber Hachi works nearby with a spade and a wrapped sword, glancing at the hole more often than he digs.

areas.name: Grave Mounds
areas.text: Rows of low grassy mounds, each topped with a stone. Crows sit on the stones and watch.

areas.name: The Great Mound
areas.text: A mound larger than the rest, freshly dug into on one side. Cold air breathes out of the hole.

locations.name: Old Battlefield of Sekigane, Twice Fought
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-36 · Danger: High]

The old battlefield fought over again: fresh banners rotting beside rusted armour, new grave mounds beside the old ones, and a great mound of this war's dead raised in a week. Farmers will not cross it even by day now.

areas.name: Grave Mounds, After the War
areas.text: Rows of mounds, old grass beside raw earth, both kinds topped with stones.

areas.name: The Great Mound, After the War
areas.text: The great mound of this war's dead, raised in a week, already sinking.

areas.name: The Robbers' Cut
areas.text: A trench the grave robbers cut into the newest war mound, shored with broken spears. Going in leads down to The Spear-Shored Trench.

locations.name: Old Coast Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: Moderate]

A fort built against pirates a century ago, half ruined, its sea wall still standing. The navy keeps a few men here. Surf booms against the foot of the Sea Wall and spray comes up through the old gun ports. Behind the wall most of the fort is roofless, with grass in the courtyards and rusted cannon lying where they fell. A handful of navy sailors keep watch from the wall and play cards in what is left of the barracks. Sergeant Utsumi runs the garrison from beside the Powder Store, unshaven, his coat worn to a pale sea-blue.

areas.name: Powder Store
areas.text: A dark vault of barrels, most of them empty when tapped.

areas.name: Sea Wall
areas.text: A thick stone wall over the surf, with gun ports looking out to sea.

areas.name: The Breach in the Wall
areas.text: A collapsed stretch of the fort's landward wall where anyone can climb in. Going in leads down to The Roofless Courtyard.

locations.name: Old Coast Fort, The Abandoned Fort
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-37 · Danger: High]

The coast fort after the war, abandoned by a garrison that sold its last powder and walked home. Smugglers use the sea wall as a quay.

areas.name: Powder Store, After the War
areas.text: An empty powder store, scratch marks inside the door.

areas.name: Sea Wall, After the War
areas.text: The sea wall, used as a smugglers' quay.

areas.name: The Quay Stair
areas.text: A stair from the smugglers' quay on the sea wall into the empty fort. Going in leads down to The Smugglers' Quay.

locations.name: Old Ward Stones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A ring of standing stones on the moor beyond the lake, carved with wards older than the Bureau. Grass will not grow inside the ring. Out on the open moor beyond the lake, wind and the bleating of sheep are the only sounds. The Stone Ring stands on a low rise, each grey stone worn smooth except where carved wards still show. Shepherd Moku grazes his flock on the grass around it, crook across his shoulders, and keeps every animal well back from the stones with a whistle. From the ring the towers of Seimei are a grey smudge across the water.

areas.name: Cracked Stone
areas.text: The cracked stone, its ward split in two, frost on it even in summer.

areas.name: Stone Ring
areas.text: Grey stones in a ring, each carved with fading wards, the ground inside bare.

locations.name: Old Ward Stones, The Broken Ring
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 27-36 · Danger: High]

The ward stones after the war: two more stones cracked the night the Vaults did, and the moor's sheep no longer come near. Something walks the ring at dusk.

areas.name: Cracked Stone, After the War
areas.text: The first cracked stone, two new cracks beside it.

areas.name: Stone Ring, After the War
areas.text: The ring of stones, a scorched path worn round the inside.

locations.name: Orphans' Lodge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A lodge where children orphaned by demon raids are raised and, when old enough, trained as hunters. Smoke rises from the long roof, and inside the lodge is loud with children's voices and the clack of wooden swords. In the Hearth Room, children eat, sleep and practise breathing forms in rows while an older hunter corrects their stance. Orphan Shiro, white-haired and thin, is usually the first up and the last to put his practice sword down. The lodge answers to the fortress above Asahi Gate, and every child here hopes to wear the uniform one day.

areas.name: Hearth Room
areas.text: A long room around a hearth where children eat, sleep and practise breathing forms with wooden swords.

locations.name: Orphans' Lodge, The Crowded Lodge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-33 · Danger: High]

The orphans' lodge after the war, crowded past its walls with the valleys' orphans, sleeping three to a mat. Orphan Shiro is the oldest now, and teaches the breathing forms to the small ones.

areas.name: Hearth Room, After the War
areas.text: The hearth room, children sleeping three to a mat, Shiro teaching the forms.

locations.name: Paper Familiar Workshop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Where Bureau students learn to fold and wake paper familiars: long tables of paper cranes, warriors and hounds that twitch when no one is looking. Paper rustles everywhere though no window is open, and the room smells of rice glue and scorched chalk. Bureau students sit shoulder to shoulder at the Folding Tables, creasing cranes and hounds from stacks of white sheets, while Instructor Shirokane walks behind them, his own hands folding as he corrects theirs. At the Waking Circle one student at a time kneels to wake a familiar under his eye. The workshop is part of the Bureau of Yin and Yang.

areas.name: Folding Tables
areas.text: Long tables covered in folded paper creatures in every stage of waking.

areas.name: Waking Circle
areas.text: A chalk circle on the floor where familiars are woken, scorched in places.

locations.name: Paper Familiar Workshop, The Folded Army
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-32 · Danger: High]

The paper workshop after the war, folding familiars for every house's spies and messengers. The tables never empty.

areas.name: Folding Tables, After the War
areas.text: Tables of folded paper birds and hounds, waiting to wake.

areas.name: Waking Circle, After the War
areas.text: The waking circle, scorched by one familiar that woke wrong.

locations.name: Pilgrims' Hostel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A hostel where mourners stay while they wait for word that their dead have crossed. Paper lanterns hang for each. Rice gruel, damp wool and candle smoke fill the low building, and conversations stay at a whisper. Mourners eat at a long table, then go back to sit under their lanterns in the Lantern Hall. Mourner Asa, young and calm in a white kimono, keeps the same place every evening and speaks to almost no one. The hostel charges little, feeds everyone, and lies a short walk from Black Ferry Fortress, whose towers show on a clear day.

areas.name: Lantern Hall
areas.text: A hall hung with paper lanterns, one for each soul awaited, mourners sitting quietly beneath them.

locations.name: Pilgrims' Hostel, Hostel of the Living Lanterns
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: High]

The pilgrims' hostel after the war, full of families lighting lanterns for the dead, and some for the living they have given up on.

areas.name: Lantern Hall, After the War
areas.text: A lantern hall crowded with families and lights.

locations.name: Pine Avenue
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

A long stretch of road shaded by ancient pines planted by an old shogun. Pilgrims rest under them and peddlers sell rice cakes. The road runs a long way in green shade here, between pines so old their trunks are split and propped with poles. Pilgrims sit on the Shaded Verge among fallen needles, and peddlers work the verge with trays of rice cakes. Pilgrim Oharu rests in her white robe, showing her stamp book of shrine seals to anyone who sits near. A tired samurai in a faded kimono with the crest cut off sits a little apart, murmuring poetry.

areas.name: Shaded Verge
areas.text: A verge under the ancient pines where pilgrims rest and peddlers sell rice cakes, pine needles soft underfoot and resin sharp in the air.

locations.name: Pine Avenue, The Deserters' Avenue
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The pine avenue after the war, where deserters from three armies hide in the trees and rob anyone the Red Lanterns miss. The pines are scarred with arrow marks.

areas.name: Shaded Verge, After the War
areas.text: A verge under scarred pines, deserters' camp smoke in the trees.

areas.name: Shiba Tadaoki's Pine
areas.text: A pine with a poem tied to its lowest branch: Shiba Tadaoki joined an army to clear his name and fell.

locations.name: Pirate Graves Reef
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A reef off the western cape littered with wrecks, where pirates were once hanged in chains. Fog sits on it most mornings. Fog lies low on the water most mornings, and the reef shows itself in pieces: a black rock, a broken mast, the curve of a hull. At low tide the Wreck Field bares the ribs of old ships wedged among the rocks, crusted with barnacles and kelp. Gibbet Rock rises at the reef's edge, rusted chains still knocking against its iron post in the wind. The fishing boats of Saikai give the whole reef a wide berth.

areas.name: Gibbet Rock
areas.text: A rock with rusted gibbet chains still hanging from an iron post.

areas.name: The Reef Boat Landing
areas.text: A shelf of rock where a boat can tie up at low tide and the reef can be walked. Going in leads down to The Fog Shelf.

areas.name: Wreck Field
areas.text: Broken hulls on the rocks, ribs of old ships showing at low tide.

locations.name: Pirate Graves Reef, The Wreck Reef
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The reef after the war, crowded with new wrecks: war-junks that ran from the chain-boom in the dark, and a guild silver ship still stuck on the rocks with guards camped on its deck.

areas.name: Gibbet Rock, After the War
areas.text: The gibbet rock, a new pirate hanging beside the old bones.

areas.name: The Guild Landing
areas.text: A rope landing the guild's guards rigged to reach the silver ship. Going in leads down to The Fogged Wrecks.

areas.name: Wreck Field, After the War
areas.text: A field of new wrecks among the old, a guarded silver ship in the middle.

locations.name: Polishers' Street
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A quiet street of sword polishers who spend weeks on a single blade. After the hammers of the forge town, the quiet is the first thing noticed: only the soft scrape of steel on whetstone. The Polishing Shops stand open-fronted along the street, each with a polisher bent over a blade on a low bench. Master Polisher Togi, fussy and bespectacled, checks his apprentice's work under lamplight. Hagane Suzu sits at the next stone, murmuring to the sword in her hands. Blades come here from the forges of Hibana for their finish.

areas.name: Polishing Shops
areas.text: A quiet street of open-fronted shops where polishers bend over whetstones for weeks, the only sound a soft scrape.

locations.name: Polishers' Street, The Street of Long Queues
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-34 · Danger: High]

The polishers' street after the war, its quiet broken by queues: war blades waiting for their finish and soldiers waiting for their blades. Master Polisher Togi still fusses over his apprentice's work, and Hagane Suzu still murmurs to the sword in her hands, more often than before.

areas.name: Kanemori's Whetstone
areas.text: His whetstone left on his bench, a war blade half polished on it: Old Master Kanemori died at his stone.

areas.name: Polishing Shops, After the War
areas.text: The polishing shops, war blades queued on every bench.

locations.name: Porters' Lodge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Where the road's porters and palanquin bearers sleep between jobs, and where they decide which travellers are worth carrying. Snoring, sweat and straw fill the Bunk Room, a long hall lined with bunks and empty palanquins. Bearers lie about between jobs, mending straps and telling stories about the people they carried. Big Ushi sits among them, huge and calm, settling who works tomorrow. A thin man in a borrowed porter's coat that does not fit keeps to the back corner and flinches when a samurai goes by. The lodge serves the traffic out of Oiwake Station.

areas.name: Bunk Room
areas.text: A long room of straw bunks and empty palanquins, porters snoring and swapping secrets of the people they carried.

locations.name: Porters' Lodge, Porters for the Army
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The porters' lodge after the war, half empty: the armies took the strongest porters and paid them in promises. Those left carry the wounded home for a few coins.

areas.name: Big Ushi's Carrying Pole
areas.text: His great carrying pole set upright by the lodge door: Big Ushi died carrying the wounded off the road.

areas.name: Bunk Room, After the War
areas.text: A half-empty bunk room, a porter's crutch by every other bed.

locations.name: Red Lantern Roost
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

A ravine off the road where the Red Lantern Federation's bands meet: tents, stolen goods, and red lanterns in the trees. The Lantern Mother holds court on a fallen log. Red paper lanterns hang in the pines of the Lantern Trees, lighting the ravine like a festival, and cookfire smoke pools beneath them. Cutthroats in mismatched stolen armour sort plunder, play dice and sharpen hatchets. Kurokami lounges among them in a lord's armour with his long black hair loose. At Mother's Log, the Lantern Mother sits in her red-lacquered coat, hearing quarrels and counting her share.

areas.name: Lantern Trees
areas.text: Pines hung with red paper lanterns, lighting the ravine like a festival of thieves.

areas.name: Mother's Log
areas.text: A great fallen log where the Lantern Mother sits to hear quarrels and take her share.

locations.name: Red Lantern Roost, The Federation's Fort
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-29 · Danger: High]

The bandit roost after the war, fortified with the war's leftovers: captured palisades, stolen spears and a watchtower taller than the lantern trees. The Federation plays both halves of the road.

areas.name: Lantern Trees, After the War
areas.text: Trees hung with red lanterns above a new palisade.

areas.name: Mother's Log, After the War
areas.text: The Federation's council log, a war map carved into its top.

locations.name: Reed Channels
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-26 · Danger: Moderate]

A maze of channels through tall reeds where fog sits for days. Only the rain clan and the smugglers know the way through. Inside the reeds the world shrinks to a lane of brown water between two green walls, and the fog muffles every sound but dripping. The Channel Maze turns and turns again with no landmark to steer by. Chidori the Runner is the one most often met here, poling a flat boat at speed with a message for the Brine Tide. Herons stand at the Heron Pool, a still opening deep in the reeds. The channels run between Ashiura and the Kirisame Stilt Village.

areas.name: Channel Maze
areas.text: Water lanes between reed walls taller than a man, every turn the same.

areas.name: Heron Pool
areas.text: A still pool where herons stand and the water is too clear.

locations.name: Reed Channels, Channels of the Lost Patrols
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 27-37 · Danger: High]

The reed channels after the war, where navy patrol boats went in and never came out. Their lanterns still drift deep in the maze at night.

areas.name: Channel Maze, After the War
areas.text: A maze of reeds, drifting lanterns deep inside.

areas.name: Heron Pool, After the War
areas.text: A still pool where the last patrol boat sank.

locations.name: Revenant Shaft
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

An old shaft where miners hear weeping and see a lantern moving below. An old winch stands over the Shaft Head, its rope hanging into the dark and swaying with no one on it. Miners down in Miners' Town will not work this shaft, and they talk of weeping heard from it at night. In the Lower Gallery far below, shapes with lanterns stand at old bellows and pump them, though no forge is lit. The air from the shaft smells of cold ash.

areas.name: Lower Gallery
areas.text: A gallery where figures work bellows that are not lit.

areas.name: Shaft Head
areas.text: A winch and a rope going down into dark, the rope moving.

areas.name: The Winch Head
areas.text: The old winch over the shaft, its rope swaying with no one on it. Going in leads down to The Swaying Winch.

locations.name: Revenant Shaft, The Climbing Dead
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-46 · Danger: Severe]

The revenant shaft after the war, where the soulless no longer stay below: they climb at night, lanterns in hand, and the winch rope sways with their weight. Miners' Town bars its doors after dark.

areas.name: Lower Gallery, After the War
areas.text: The lower gallery, bellows pumping, half the lanterns gone up the shaft.

areas.name: Shaft Head, After the War
areas.text: The shaft head, the rope swaying, handprints in the soot.

areas.name: The Barred Winch
areas.text: The winch over the shaft, its rope swaying with the weight of climbers. Going in leads down to The Swaying Rope.

locations.name: Rice-Cake Peddlers' Rest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A cluster of stalls selling rice cakes and tea to walkers, the best gossip on the road for the price of a cup. Steam and the smell of toasted rice cakes drift across the road from a huddle of stalls. Under the awning of the Tea Benches, walkers rest their feet and trade news over cheap tea. Granny Kiku keeps the end stall, toothless and cackling, pressing cakes on customers and asking where they are headed. Porters and riders out of Oiwake Station stop here from habit, whether they are hungry or not.

areas.name: Tea Benches
areas.text: Benches under an awning where walkers sip tea and gossip, the old woman's stall steaming with fresh rice cakes.

locations.name: Rice-Cake Peddlers' Rest, Rest of the Thin Cakes
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-23 · Danger: Moderate]

The peddlers' rest after the war, where the rice cakes are smaller and dearer and the old woman at the end stall still hears everything. Refugees sit on the benches with nowhere to go.

areas.name: Tea Benches, After the War
areas.text: Benches crowded with refugees, cakes small and dear.

locations.name: River Ferry Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

Where the road meets the great river, a flat ferry poles travellers across and porters carry the rest on their shoulders. When the river rises, the road stops. The river is wide and brown here, and its current can be heard from the road. A flat ferry crosses on a pole, worked most days by Osen the Ferryman's Daughter, a red cloth in her hair, trading cheek with her passengers. Those waiting for the water to fall sit in the Waiting Shed, gambling to pass the time. Rider Kanbei is among them, sharpening arrows with his dispatch bag beside him.

areas.name: River Ferry Crossing: Ferry Landing
areas.text:
River Ferry Crossing: Ferry Landing is an area within River Ferry Crossing; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A muddy landing where the ferry ties up and porters bargain over their backs.

areas.name: Waiting Shed
areas.text: A shed of tired travellers waiting for the water to fall, gambling to pass the time.

locations.name: River Ferry Crossing, The Only Crossing
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The ferry crossing after the bridge burned: now the only way over the river for a day either side, its ferry running night and day, the queue on both banks a camp of its own.

areas.name: Rider Kanbei's Post
areas.text: A post-rider's marker on the riverbank, his dispatch bag hung on it: Rider Kanbei was shot carrying a dispatch across the river.

areas.name: River Ferry Crossing: Ferry Landing, After the War
areas.text: A crowded landing where the queue waits days for a place on the ferry.

areas.name: Waiting Shed, After the War
areas.text: A shed full of travellers sleeping in shifts.

locations.name: Road Commissioner's Office
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low]

The headquarters of the Post-Road Wardens: a long office where station registers are copied, riders are dispatched and the road's charter hangs framed on the wall. Every station master answers here. The long office smells of ink, horse and lamp oil. In the Register Room, clerks bend over year-books of station names and dates, copying by lamplight, and Road Commissioner Hayashi walks the rows with his hands behind his back. Out in the Rider Yard, saddled horses stamp in the straw, and Rider Tomoe dozes beside her grey mare, Fog, until the bell sends her off with a dispatch bag over her shoulder.

areas.name: Register Room
areas.text: Shelves of station registers, each a year of names and dates. Clerks copy them by lamplight.

areas.name: Rider Yard
areas.text: A yard of fast horses saddled and waiting, riders napping in the straw until a bell sends them off.

locations.name: Road Commissioner's Office, The Office of a Cut Road
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The commissioner's office after the war, governing half a road: the register room counts stations the commissioner can no longer reach, and the rider yard is empty.

areas.name: Register Room, After the War
areas.text: Registers for stations behind the barricade, nobody to write in them.

areas.name: Rider Yard, After the War
areas.text: An empty yard; the post riders were drafted as scouts.

locations.name: Ronin Hiring Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A big drinking hall where masterless swords wait for work and clients come to hire them. Contracts are pinned to boards by the door, and the best bands have their own tables. Sake, sweat and lamp oil fill the long hall, and the din rises each time a client comes through the door. Gonroku the Broker stands at the Contract Boards with his one arm, pinning up escort and guard jobs and taking the hall's tenth. Masterless swords in faded kimono and straw hats read the boards or sleep against the wall. In the corner, Captain Ishimura laughs at the best of the Captains' Tables, where a sword laid flat means business.

areas.name: Captains' Tables
areas.text: Corner tables where band captains drink and bargain with clients. A sword laid on the table means the talk is serious.

areas.name: Contract Boards
areas.text: Boards covered in pinned contracts: escorts, collections, guard duty, and a few no one will touch. A clerk takes the hall's cut.

locations.name: Ronin Hiring Hall, The Hall of Unpaid Blades
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-32 · Danger: High]

The hiring hall after the war, full of ronin whose houses lost and could not pay them: unpaid contracts nailed to the board in rows, and captains hiring for a peace nobody believes in.

areas.name: Captains' Tables, After the War
areas.text: Tables of captains hiring for escorts, debts and private wars.

areas.name: Contract Boards, After the War
areas.text: Boards of unpaid war contracts nailed up in rows.

areas.name: The Ishimura Table
areas.text: The best table in the hall, left empty, a cup poured at every seat: Captain Ishimura's band was hired by a house and died to a man.

locations.name: Ruined Summer Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A summer palace abandoned three reigns ago, its roofs fallen and its gardens gone wild. Black clouds gather over it on still nights, and the plain's people say an old reign's curse lives there. Weeds push up through the steps. The Fallen Hall stands with half its roof gone and its tatami rotted into the floor, and in one corner something large has flattened a sleeping place. The Wild Garden has grown thick around a stagnant pond where the frogs stop croaking all at once. The air is heavy, and no birds nest in the eaves.

areas.name: Fallen Hall
areas.text: A great hall with half its roof gone, tatami rotted into the floor. Something has been sleeping here.

areas.name: Wild Garden
areas.text: A garden run to wilderness around a stagnant pond. The frogs fall silent all at once.

locations.name: Ruined Summer Palace, Under the Storm
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

The ruined palace after the emperor's death: the black clouds over it never lift now, rain falls on it alone, and the wild garden has grown over the road. Lightning strikes the same fallen hall every night.

areas.name: Fallen Hall, After the War
areas.text: The half-fallen hall, struck by lightning every night, the beams scorched black.

areas.name: Wild Garden, After the War
areas.text: A garden gone to thorn and black water under a cloud that never moves.

locations.name: Ruins of the Old Capital
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

Broken walls and fallen gates of a capital older than Miyako, half buried in ash. Grudge fog pools in its streets. The ash lies thinner among the ruins, and old paving shows along the main avenue until the Fallen Gate blocks it, a great gate lying face down from wall to wall. Roofless houses stand on either side, and fog thickens in the low streets. Beyond them the Ruined Palace rises in black beams open to the sky. Brother Seiji is often there with a lantern and an ink-smeared notebook, sketching the carvings and measuring the halls.

areas.name: Fallen Gate
areas.text: A great gate lying on its face across the old main avenue.

areas.name: Ruined Palace
areas.text: A palace of black beams with no roof, its throne room full of fog.

areas.name: The Old Avenue
areas.text: The old main avenue, its paving showing through thin ash. Going in leads down to The Face-Down Gate.

locations.name: Ruins of the Old Capital, The Waking Ruins
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

The old capital's ruins after the war, stirring: the struck-out names are being spoken again by the war's grudges, and the fallen gate is standing straighter every month.

areas.name: Fallen Gate, After the War
areas.text: The fallen gate, leaning upright again, a fresh name carved in it.

areas.name: Ruined Palace, After the War
areas.text: The ruined palace, whispering in a language nobody speaks.

areas.name: The Rising Avenue
areas.text: The old main avenue, the fallen gate leaning upright at its end. Going in leads down to The Upright Gate.

locations.name: Saikai
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The free port town on the bay: warehouses, quays, foreign ships at anchor among the junks, and lantern-lit streets that never close. The merchant guild's flag flies over the customs house and the regent's does not. Tar, fish and incense hang over the quays, and gulls work the rubbish behind the warehouses. Coaches rattle out of the Harbour Post yard, where Harbourmaster Watanuki stands with spyglass and ledger, checking anchor fees against the hulls in the bay. Foreign sailors in striped shirts haggle along the Foreign Quay, and after dark the crowd drifts up to Lantern Row for dice, music and tea. Guild clerks in dark blue coats are everywhere.

areas.name: Apothecary Lane
areas.text: A narrow lane of herb sellers and apothecary shops behind the quays, foreign remedies beside the isles' own.

areas.name: Foreign Quay
areas.text: Where the square-sailed ships tie up: strange cargo, strange sailors, and guild inspectors who can be paid.

areas.name: Harbour Post
areas.text:
The post-horse stable and ferry office at the head of the quays, where coaches leave east along the post road and foreign ships put in.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Haibara (about 12 Mon), Oiwake Station (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Lantern Row
areas.text: The pleasure district: gambling halls, tea houses, musicians, and the debts that start here.

locations.name: Saikai Lighthouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A stone lighthouse on the rocky point that guides ships into the bay. Its keeper is old, deaf and very sharp-eyed. Wind and surf hit the rocky point hard, and the stone stair up the tower smells of lamp oil and salt. Gulls scream against the glass of the Lamp Room, where Old Rokubei trims the great lamp, polishes the lens and watches the water with narrowed eyes. He hears nothing, but he reads lips from across the room and answers cheerfully. The light marks the approach to Saikai for every ship coming in from the open sea.

areas.name: Lamp Room
areas.text: The round lamp room at the top, its great lamp trimmed and its shuttered signal lamp hidden in a cupboard; gulls scream against the glass.

locations.name: Saikai Lighthouse, Chain Light
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The lighthouse after the war, now the signal tower for the chain-boom: the keeper raises and lowers the harbour chain by lamp code, and nothing enters at night without the guild's word.

areas.name: Lamp Room, After the War
areas.text: The lamp room, shutters and chain-signals, a guild clerk beside the keeper.

areas.name: Old Rokubei's Lamp
areas.text: His old lamp, cold, set on the rocks below the lighthouse: Old Rokubei died at the lamp during the blockade.

locations.name: Saikai, The Debt Harbour
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-33 · Danger: High]

The free port after the war, untouched by fire and richer than ever: new warehouses on every quay, war-junks moored among the foreign tall ships, and an iron chain-boom across the harbour mouth that the guild raises at dusk. Every house in the isles owes this town money, and the town knows it.

areas.name: Apothecary Lane, After the War
areas.text: The apothecary lane, every shop selling war salves at war prices.

areas.name: Foreign Quay, After the War
areas.text: Crowded quays of foreign ships and war-junks, guild clerks counting every crate.

areas.name: Harbour Post, After the War
areas.text: The post house, busier than ever, selling passage to anyone fleeing the plain.

areas.name: Harbourmaster's Marker
areas.text: A marker on the harbour post's steps: Harbourmaster Watanuki drowned when the blockade burned the pilots' boats.

areas.name: Lantern Row, After the War
areas.text: The lantern quarter, brighter and louder; soldiers spend their pay here.

locations.name: Salt Marsh Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small shrine on a boardwalk over the salt marsh, where fishermen leave cucumbers for the river folk. A long boardwalk runs out over the salt marsh, grey planks over grey water, with reeds whispering on both sides. At its end stands the Boardwalk Altar, a small roofed shrine with cucumbers laid on it, some fresh and some going soft. Priest Mokuren keeps it, barefoot and thin, and blesses the nets of fishermen who stop on their way out from Ashiura. The marsh around is quiet except for frogs and the odd splash too heavy for a fish.

areas.name: Boardwalk Altar
areas.text: A small altar at the end of a boardwalk over the marsh, cucumbers laid on it and reeds whispering all around.

locations.name: Salt Marsh Shrine, Shrine of Dear News
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: High]

The salt marsh shrine after the war, where the kappa's priest still trades in news, and news is worth more than it has ever been.

areas.name: Boardwalk Altar, After the War
areas.text: The boardwalk altar, cucumbers and folded letters left side by side.

locations.name: Saltpan Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

A village of salt pans and drying racks on the shore south of the port. Everyone here is in debt to the guild for their pans. The glare off the Salt Pans is hard on the eyes, and the air tastes bitter. Families rake the white crust into heaps while Headwoman Oshio walks the banks between the pans, shouting orders that carry across the shore. Mule-Driver Hachibei loads sacks onto his mule, Princess, for the climb to the post road and chats with anyone who will stop. Most of the salt raked here is weighed and sold in Saikai, a short walk up the shore.

areas.name: Salt Pans
areas.text: Flat pans of evaporating seawater crusted white, families raking salt in the glare and the air bitter on the tongue.

locations.name: Saltpan Village, The Taxed Pans
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The salt village after the war, taxed by the guild instead of the shogunate: collectors on the pans every week, and half the families gone to the Brine Tide's boats.

areas.name: Salt Pans, After the War
areas.text: Salt pans worked by the few who stayed, a collector's booth at the end.

locations.name: Sea Monk's Shallows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: High]

Rich fishing grounds off the coast where the sea goes glassy-calm on certain nights and a vast black shape rises beside the boats. By day these are busy fishing grounds a short row from Ashiura, with boats spread across the swell and gulls following the nets. The water is deep blue and thick with fish. Barrel Rock, low and black and streaked white by the birds, marks the edge of the best grounds. On some evenings the wind drops away and the sea flattens into the Glass Water, so still and silent that the crews call to one another to start for home.

areas.name: Barrel Rock
areas.text: A rock where fishermen used to leave bottomless barrels, now bare.

areas.name: Glass Water
areas.text: Water so calm it reflects every star, with no wind and no sound.

locations.name: Sea Monk's Shallows, The Unpaid Shallows
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-40 · Danger: Severe]

The sea monk's shallows after the war, where the guild's forbidden offerings finally ran out and the umibozu has taken three ships.

areas.name: Barrel Rock, After the War
areas.text: The barrel rock, offerings left in secret at night.

areas.name: Glass Water, After the War
areas.text: Still glass water over three new wrecks.

locations.name: Seimei
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The onmyoji city on the lake, laid out on a grid that is itself a ward, with an observatory tower at its heart and talismans on every gate. Coaches roll in at the Lake Gate Post, where a clerk holds a paper charm to each traveller's sleeve and watches it before waving them through. Beyond the gate the streets run dead straight, every crossing marked by a seal post, and bells from the Star Tower call the hours. Students in white, pilgrims buying luck and merchants off the lake boats fill the avenues by day; at night paper lanterns along the Ward-Wall Walk show the carved stones in a long pale line.

areas.name: Lake Gate Post
areas.text:
The post office at the lake gate, where coaches arrive and visitors are checked for curses.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Kitsunebi Crossing (about 12 Mon), Ashiura (about 12 Mon), Miyako (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Star Tower
areas.text: The Bureau's observatory, where star readers name lucky days and unlucky births.

areas.name: Ward-Wall Walk
areas.text: The walkway along the star-shaped wall, its stones carved with seals and lit by paper lanterns at night.

locations.name: Seimei, Behind Two Walls
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-36 · Danger: High]

The onmyoji city after the war, untouched and closed: a second star-shaped ward wall raised around the first, paper charms strung along both, and the lake gate opened twice a day. Refugees camp on the shore outside and are not let in.

areas.name: Lake Gate Post, After the War
areas.text: The lake gate, opened twice a day, refugees camped on the shore beyond it.

areas.name: Star Tower, After the War
areas.text: The star tower, lit all night, its readers never off the instruments.

areas.name: Ward-Wall Walk, After the War
areas.text: The wall walk, now between two walls, charms rustling on both.

locations.name: Seventh Station Inn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

One of the busiest post stations: an official inn for lords, cheaper inns for everyone else, and a lantern gate that closes at dusk. Travellers swap news in the bath. Porters, pilgrims and samurai crowd the street between the inns, and maids call room prices from every doorway. The Common Bath is loud with news from both ends of the road, and Tsurube the Storyteller sits in the steam with his folding fan, telling ghost tales for a cup. Behind their own gate the Honjin Rooms stay hushed, and Innkeeper Jinbei bustles between them and the street, bowing and sweating.

areas.name: Common Bath
areas.text: A long wooden bath where porters, pilgrims and samurai soak and talk.

areas.name: Honjin Rooms
areas.text: The lords' inn, quiet and expensive, with its own gate and its own guards.

locations.name: Seventh Station Inn, The Last Inn East
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The seventh station after the war, the last inn east of the barricade under the shogunate's flag: soldiers in the honjin rooms and refugees in the bath, the red lantern taken down and hidden.

areas.name: Common Bath, After the War
areas.text: A common bath shared by soldiers and refugees in shifts.

areas.name: Honjin Rooms, After the War
areas.text: The lord's rooms, quartered by an officer of the Regent's army.

locations.name: Shirokawa
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The exiles' town on the ice isle's sheltered shore: black stone houses, smoke, and people who do not ask where you came from. Smoke drifts from black stone houses, and the White Strait ferry knocks against the floes at the Ice Pier. Warden hunters in furs and chains watch who comes ashore. Nobody asks newcomers their business, and the town's quarrels are settled over drink in the Exiles' Hall. On the Road to the Vaults, Hunter Captain Gaku, scarred and cold, stops travellers among the warning poles and seals.

areas.name: Exiles' Hall
areas.text: A hall where the exiles meet, drink and settle what passes for law.

areas.name: Ice Pier
areas.text:
The pier where the White Strait ferry ties up between the floes.

The post road serves this yard: ferries sail to Kagegi Village (about 30 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Road to the Vaults
areas.text: The road climbing the glacier toward the Sealing Vaults, marked by poles and warning seals.

locations.name: Shirokawa, Behind the Fissure
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The exiles' town after the war, with the fissure at its back: the Road to the Vaults is cut, the White Strait ferry brings Warden recruits instead of exiles, and Hunter Captain Gaku stops everyone at the Ice Pier now, not just at the poles.

areas.name: Exiles' Hall, After the War
areas.text: The exiles' hall, arguments over staying or going settled over drink.

areas.name: Ice Pier, After the War
areas.text: The ice pier, Gaku stopping everyone who comes ashore.

areas.name: Road to the Vaults, After the War
areas.text: The road to the Vaults, cut by the fissure past the warning poles.

locations.name: Shogunate Rice Granary
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Low]

A great timber granary on stilts where the plain's tax rice is stored before it goes to the capital. Guards walk the walls day and night, and hungry villagers walk past slowly. A great timber storehouse stands high on stilts above the damp, its walls walked by spearmen in conical hats. Inside, on the Granary Floor, guards count bales by lamplight while mice run in the rafters. Sergeant Ishida makes his rounds without rest, watching villagers on the road with tired eyes. Carts of tax rice roll in from the villages of the plain after every harvest, bound in the end for Miyako.

areas.name: Granary Floor
areas.text: A dim timber floor of stacked rice bales on stilts above the damp, where guards count sacks by lamplight and mice run the rafters.

locations.name: Shogunate Rice Granary, Under Guild Seal
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-29 · Danger: High]

The great granary on its stilts, now under two guards: the Regent's soldiers at the gate and the guild's seal on every door. Hungry villagers queue below for rice they grew.

areas.name: Granary Floor, After the War
areas.text: A timber floor of sealed sacks, each stamped with the guild's coin-mark.

areas.name: Sergeant Ishida's Stone
areas.text: A stone at the granary gate, spearheads planted round it: Sergeant Ishida died holding the gate.

locations.name: Shrine of the Fallen Feather
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A shrine where would-be students of the tengu leave a sword and wait to be noticed. A single black feather lies on the altar, and the only sound is the rustle of name tags on the Sword Rack. Swords of every quality hang there: farm-forged blades, fine heirlooms, even a wooden practice sword. Hopeful students camp nearby for days, sharpening, praying and staring up toward Tengu Peak. Some lose heart and take their blades back; most leave them and wait.

areas.name: Sword Rack
areas.text: A rack of swords left by hopeful students, each with a name tag fluttering, a black feather on the altar.

locations.name: Shrine of the Fallen Feather, Rack of the Unclaimed Swords
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The fallen feather shrine after the war, its sword rack crowded with blades left by soldiers who went to war first and never came back for them. The hopefuls camped there are fewer and older.

areas.name: Sword Rack, After the War
areas.text: The sword rack, crowded with blades nobody came back for.

locations.name: Smugglers' Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Moderate]

Sea caves under the cliffs north of the bay, flooded at high tide and dry at low. Fishermen avoid them; smugglers do not. The Tide Mouth booms like a drum as the sea surges in and drains away, and the rocks are slick with weed. At low water a path climbs to the Dry Gallery, where crates sit above the tideline beside a fire that is laid but never lit. Small bare footprints cross the sand up there, and Hana, a thin girl with tangled hair, watches from the shadows, ready to bolt at the sound of boots. The caves are a long scramble along the shore from Saikai.

areas.name: Dry Gallery
areas.text: A high gallery above the tideline where crates are stacked and a fire is laid but never lit.

areas.name: The Low-Tide Path
areas.text: A weed-slick path down the cliff that only shows at low water, leading into the booming caves. Going in leads down to The Booming Mouth.

areas.name: Tide Mouth
areas.text: The cave mouth where the sea surges in and out, booming like a drum.

locations.name: Smugglers' Caves, The Arms Caves
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-33 · Danger: High]

The caves after the war, stacked with arms the Brine Tide bought from both armies' quartermasters. The old shrine at the back has been swept and lit again by someone.

areas.name: Dry Gallery, After the War
areas.text: A dry gallery stacked with captured spears, bows and powder.

areas.name: The Arms Path
areas.text: The low-tide path, worn deeper by crates of arms carried up and down it. Going in leads down to The Drowned Tide Mouth.

areas.name: Tide Mouth, After the War
areas.text: The tide mouth, drowned soldiers washing in with the water.

locations.name: Smugglers' Cove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A narrow sea cave at the island's southern tip, hidden behind rocks: deep enough for a small boat to slip inside at high tide. Brine Tide smugglers use it every new moon.

areas.name: Cove Mouth
areas.text: The cave's mouth, half-flooded at high tide, a dark boat tied inside.

areas.name: Smugglers' Tunnel
areas.text: A tunnel running back under the island, stacked with crates and lit by a shuttered lantern.

locations.name: Smugglers' Rice Paddies
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Rice paddies on the marsh edge where boats are hidden in the dikes and rice sacks hold more than rice. Frogs sing across the flooded paddies and fall silent in a wave as anyone walks the raised paths. The fields are worked like any others, farmers bent to the rice and egrets stepping through the shallows. Farmer Oyone is usually out on the Hidden Dike, muddy to the knees, leaning on her hoe to greet whoever passes. A small boat lies tucked into the reeds along her dike. The paddies sit on the marsh edge within reach of Ashiura.

areas.name: Hidden Dike
areas.text: An earth dike with a boat hidden in its reeds and rice sacks heavier than rice, frogs falling silent as anyone passes.

locations.name: Smugglers' Rice Paddies, The Paddies of Plain Rice
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: High]

The smugglers' paddies after the war, growing real rice now there is money in it: the plain's flooded villages buy it at five times the price.

areas.name: Hidden Dike, After the War
areas.text: A hidden dike, rice sacks stacked where cargo used to be.

locations.name: Snow Monkey Springs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

Hot springs in the snow where red-faced monkeys bathe and steal from travellers. Steam rolls off the pools and freezes into rime on the surrounding rocks, and the air smells of sulphur and wet fur. Red-faced snow monkeys sit up to their necks in the hottest water, and travellers who bathe here learn to keep packs and food tied shut. Hunters riding between Asahi Gate and the northern posts stop to thaw their hands in the steaming pools before going on.

areas.name: Snow Monkey Springs: Steaming Pools
areas.text:
Snow Monkey Springs: Steaming Pools is an area within Snow Monkey Springs; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Hot pools in the snow where red-faced monkeys bathe and watch the treeline, their chatter suddenly gone quiet.

locations.name: Snow Monkey Springs, The Silent Springs
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

The snow monkey springs after the war, deserted: the monkeys went quiet before the wall fell and have not screamed since. Hunters still thaw their hands in the pools, and keep one eye on the treeline.

areas.name: Nanae's Hut
areas.text: The bathing hut, its door broken and its towels frozen: Bath-Keeper Nanae was killed when the demons came south.

areas.name: Snow Monkey Springs: Steaming Pools, After the War
areas.text: The steaming pools, nearly empty, a few old monkeys among the hunters.

locations.name: Snowbound Trading Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A trading post where trappers sell furs and buy salt, and where some things come south that should not. The post smells of tallow, salt and raw pelts drying by the stove. Trappers come in stamping snow off their boots, drop bundles of fur on the Fur Counter, and leave with sacks of salt. Trader Bunzo, wrapped in furs of his own, weighs every pelt twice and argues the price of each. Sledges bound for Asahi Gate stop here to trade gossip and warm up.

areas.name: Fur Counter
areas.text: A counter piled with furs and salt sacks, a trader weighing goods and a crate in the corner nobody looks at.

locations.name: Snowbound Trading Post, Post on the Front
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

The trading post after the war, a front post: trappers no longer come north of it, and Trader Bunzo trades furs for steel with the hunters instead of salt.

areas.name: Fur Counter, After the War
areas.text: The fur counter, stacked with steel and bandages instead of salt.

locations.name: Snowline Huts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

Stone huts at the snowline where travellers wait out storms. Snow lies banked against the walls, and the wind finds every gap in the stonework. Inside the Stone Hut, the fire pit gives more smoke than heat, and the hut book lies open on a ledge beside a brush and frozen ink. Genin Kotetsu, a frightened boy in torn grey-blue shinobi gear, sits close to the fire with two kunai in reach. The huts stand on the high trail above Hanging Bridge Pass.

areas.name: Stone Hut
areas.text: A stone hut with a fire pit and a hut book of travellers' names, snow banked against the door.

locations.name: Snowline Huts, The Deserters' Huts
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The snowline huts after the war, sheltering deserters from both villages through the winter. The yuki-onna comes more often.

areas.name: Stone Hut, After the War
