areas.text: A stone hut crowded with deserters from both villages.

locations.name: Spider Woman's House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: High]

A lonely house in the wood where music plays at night and a beautiful woman invites travellers in for tea. Koto music drifts through the trees at dusk, and the house stands tidy and well swept in a clearing that no path seems to reach. Lanterns glow in its windows. The Spider Woman of the Wood greets travellers at the door in a dark kimono patterned with webs and leads them into the Spider Woman's House: Tea Room, where the tea is excellent and the cushions faintly tacky. No birds sing near the house.

areas.name: Attic
areas.text: An attic of silk cocoons in rows.

areas.name: Spider Woman's House: Tea Room
areas.text:
Spider Woman's House: Tea Room is an area within Spider Woman's House; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A perfect tea room, everything slightly sticky.

locations.name: Spider Woman's House, House of Many Guests
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-43 · Danger: Severe]

The spider woman's house after the war, busier: lone soldiers walking home are glad of tea and music, and the house in the clearing has had more guests in a year than in a century.

areas.name: Attic, After the War
areas.text: The attic, crowded, one silk bundle still moving.

areas.name: Spider Woman's House: Tea Room, After the War
areas.text: The tea room, a soldier's helmet set politely by the door.

locations.name: Straw Mask Hill Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A camp in the wooded hills above the rice country where the Straw Masks gather between raids: lean-tos, hidden fires, and farmers practising with flails. The villages below feed it and say nothing. Smoke from hidden fires seeps through the trees, and lean-tos huddle under the canopy. In the Flail Drill Clearing, farmers swing flails and sickles under Old Gensai, an eyepatched veteran who curses them fondly. At the Masked Fire Ring, Ine of the Hundred Fields sits in her woven straw mask with the camp's leaders. Sukezo runs in and out with messages from the villages, always asking whether there is anything to eat.

areas.name: Flail Drill Clearing
areas.text: A clearing where farmers drill with flails, sickles and spears under a scarred old soldier. The drills are clumsy and getting less so.

areas.name: Masked Fire Ring
areas.text: A ring of logs around a low fire where the leaders talk behind their straw masks. Nobody uses a real name here.

locations.name: Straw Mask Hill Camp, The Peasant Army's Camp
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-34 · Danger: High]

The hill camp grown into an army's: palisades, drilled ranks with captured spears, and banners of straw masks over a forge that turns ploughshares into blades. The villages below still feed it, and now they are proud to.

areas.name: Flail Drill Clearing, After the War
areas.text: A drill ground where farmers in straw masks practise with captured spears.

areas.name: Masked Fire Ring, After the War
areas.text: The council fire, wider now, where captains argue about what to do with a peace.

areas.name: Old Gensai's Spear
areas.text: His stolen spear stuck in the drill clearing, straw masks hung on it: Old Gensai fell taking the Oiwake barricade.

locations.name: Sun-Rite Shrine of the Plain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low]

An old shrine of the sun rites where the court's priests come each spring to bless the plain's rice. Its torii glow red at dawn, and farmers leave the first sheaf of every harvest here. A line of vermilion gates, the Dawn Torii, faces the sunrise, and pilgrims pass under them at first light. The Sheaf Hall smells of straw and incense, stacked with the first sheaves of a hundred villages. Priest Ujibe Kiyonari tends it, listening to farmers ask for rain and for sons and writing their prayers on slips of paper. Priests in white sweep the gravel between rites.

areas.name: Dawn Torii
areas.text: A line of vermilion gates facing the sunrise, where pilgrims pass through at first light.

areas.name: Sheaf Hall
areas.text: A plain hall stacked with the first sheaves of a hundred villages, smelling of straw and incense.

locations.name: Sun-Rite Shrine of the Plain, Mourning Shrine
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The sun shrine after the emperor's death: its vermilion gates hung with white, the first sheaves of a thin harvest left on an altar no priest blesses. The priests pray for an heir instead of a harvest.

areas.name: Dawn Torii, After the War
areas.text: The gates of the sunrise, hung with white mourning cloth.

areas.name: Sheaf Hall, After the War
areas.text: The harvest hall, a few thin sheaves on a long empty altar.

locations.name: Sunken Well Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: High]

A village that lives by selling clean water drawn from shallow wells, its people masked against the ash. Everyone in the village wears a cloth mask against the ash, and buckets knock and ropes creak in the Well Square from first light. Water is drawn, strained through cloth and poured into jars for travellers, who pay by the jar. Headman Gosuke oversees the trade in his own ash mask, sweating and counting coins. The houses are low and patched. Travellers out of Haibara stop here to fill their flasks.

areas.name: Well Square
areas.text: A square of shallow wells with masked villagers drawing water, one well roped off and smelling of rust.

locations.name: Sunken Well Village, The Turned Village
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-41 · Danger: Severe]

The well village after the war: all its wells have turned now, the village drinks rainwater, and the headman's trade in turned water has made him rich and hated.

areas.name: The Turned Well Head
areas.text: The village's oldest well, its water turned black, a ladder down its side. Going in leads down to The Black Water Shaft.

areas.name: Well Square, After the War
areas.text: A square of capped wells and rain barrels.

locations.name: Talisman Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-12 · Danger: Low]

A market of stalls selling talismans, charms and lucky-day almanacs, some licensed and many not. Pilgrims crowd it before festivals. The smell is paper, cheap ink and incense, and stallholders shout the lucky days of the coming month over each other. Along the Licensed Row each stall shows its Bureau tablet beside its prices, and careful buyers hold the seals up to the light. The Back Lane Stalls are cheaper and busier; there a slick-haired man with a nervous grin and a beautiful hand writes wards to order while customers wait. The market is one of Seimei's busiest streets.

areas.name: Back Lane Stalls
areas.text: Cheaper stalls in a back lane, their seals a little blurry.

areas.name: Licensed Row
areas.text: Stalls with Bureau licence tablets displayed, prices high and talismans real.

locations.name: Talisman Market, Market of Real and False Wards
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The talisman market after the war, its trade tripled: every refugee and soldier wants a ward, and forgeries outsell the real ones four to one.

areas.name: Back Lane Stalls, After the War
areas.text: Back-lane stalls of forged wards sold by the armful.

areas.name: Licensed Row, After the War
areas.text: The licensed row, Bureau seals checked at every stall and still forged.

locations.name: Tanuki Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A night market in a clearing where tanuki sell anything for money that turns to leaves at dawn. Lanterns, roasting chestnuts and loud bargaining fill the clearing once night falls. The Leaf-Money Stalls are run by round-bellied tanuki in straw hats, who pour sake for customers and swear every item is genuine. Ponta of the Tanuki Market holds the biggest stall in the middle, laughing louder than the rest. The market lies a long night's walk into the wood from Kitsunebi Crossing and packs up before first light.

areas.name: Leaf-Money Stalls
areas.text: A clearing of lantern-lit stalls run by round-bellied tanuki, piles of goods priced in coins that smell faintly of leaves.

locations.name: Tanuki Market, Market of the Soldiers' Pay
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The tanuki market after the war, swollen with soldiers spending their back pay, and with soldiers spending pay that was leaves all along: the houses paid some of their armies in tanuki money.

areas.name: Leaf-Money Stalls, After the War
areas.text: Leaf-money stalls crowded with soldiers, some paying in leaves they do not know are leaves.

locations.name: Tasogare
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-40 · Danger: Severe]

The shrine city on the cliffs, its streets climbing to the great pale torii at the edge where the dead pass through, its lanterns drifting out over the Sea of Fog at night. Incense and lamp oil hang in the damp air, and temple bells answer one another down the steep streets. Coaches unload at the Pilgrim Post, where Lantern-Seller Oiwa writes names on paper lanterns for a queue of mourners. Higher up, Commander Kirigaya Shion stands at The Great Pale Torii in her black coat, and Captain Shirasagi Ren oversees the releases on Lantern Cliff with open impatience for the crowd. Most of the city earns its rice from grief: lodging, lanterns and prayers.

areas.name: Lantern Cliff
areas.text: A terrace where farewell lanterns are lit and let go over the fog sea.

areas.name: Pilgrim Post
areas.text:
The post station at the foot of the shrine streets, where pilgrims arrive by coach and leave lighter.

The post road serves this yard: coaches run to Kagegi Village (about 12 Mon); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: The Great Pale Torii
areas.text: The gate itself, white as bone, standing at the cliff's edge with nothing behind it but fog.

locations.name: Tasogare, The Long Procession
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-46 · Danger: Severe]

The torii city after the war, in mourning: black banners on every street, twice the ghost-lanterns drifting out over the fog sea, and the war's dead queueing at the great pale torii faster than the officers can ferry them. The living walk quietly here.

areas.name: Lantern Cliff, After the War
areas.text: The lantern cliff, lanterns drifting out in an unbroken line.

areas.name: Pilgrim Post, After the War
areas.text: The pilgrim post, busy with families looking for their dead.

areas.name: The Great Pale Torii, After the War
areas.text: The great torii, a queue of the dead stretching back from it.

locations.name: Temple of Safe Voyages
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A temple on the hill above the harbour where sailors pray for safe voyages and hang carved ships from the rafters. Its bell rings for every ship that comes home. Incense and sea wind meet at the top of the temple steps. Sailors climb up to clap and bow before they sail, and their families climb them again while they are away. In the Votive Hall hundreds of carved ships hang from the rafters, some draped in black, and Priest Kaison moves among them with his sleeves rolled up over tattooed arms. On the Bell Terrace the great bronze bell looks out over Saikai's bay, its rope worn smooth by his hands.

areas.name: Bell Terrace
areas.text: A terrace with a great bronze bell looking over the bay. Its rope is worn smooth.

areas.name: Votive Hall
areas.text: A hall hung with hundreds of carved ships, each for a voyage prayed over. Some are draped in black.

locations.name: Temple of Safe Voyages, Temple of the Unreturned
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: Moderate]

The sailors' temple after the war, its votive hall hung with the names of ships that went to war and did not come back. The priest's list fills a second scroll.

areas.name: Bell Terrace, After the War
areas.text: The bell terrace, rung once for every ship that did not return.

areas.name: Votive Hall, After the War
areas.text: A votive hall crowded with new tablets and the names of drowned crews.

locations.name: Tengu Peak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Severe]

A crag above the wood where the tengu keep their court and their sword dojo. Students climb for days to be thrown off again. Wind howls across the crag, and the clack of wooden swords carries from the Cliff Dojo, along with Kuro's insults and now and then the yell of a student going over the edge. Tengu swordsmen in yamabushi robes watch from the rocks. Swordsman Hayabusa, a quiet human in a straw hat, trains alone at the far end of the floor. Above it all, Tarobo the Great Tengu sits on the Feather Throne and laughs.

areas.name: Cliff Dojo
areas.text: An open dojo on a ledge, the floor polished by centuries of bare feet.

areas.name: Feather Throne
areas.text: A throne of black feathers where the great tengu sits, laughing at students.

locations.name: Tengu Peak, The Peak Above the War
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-46 · Danger: Severe]

Tengu Peak after the war, where the tengu court stayed out of the fighting and trained twice as many students. The Cliff Dojo rings all day, Swordsman Hayabusa trains alone at the far end of the floor, and Tarobo laughs from the Feather Throne at the houses' envoys climbing up to hire his swordsmen.

areas.name: Cliff Dojo, After the War
areas.text: The cliff dojo, twice as crowded, students going over the edge twice as often.

areas.name: Feather Throne, After the War
areas.text: The feather throne, Tarobo laughing at the envoys below.

locations.name: The Ash Plain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

A plain of grey ash where nothing grows and dead trees stand like grave markers. Ghouls walk it in packs at dusk. Grey stretches to every horizon, broken only by white dead trees, and the wind lifts the ash in thin veils that sting the eyes. In the Ash Drifts footprints fill in within minutes, so travellers from Haibara mark their way with piled stones. The Dead Grove creaks though the air is still. No birds sing and no insects hum. An Ash Plain Oni has been seen wading through the drifts, an iron club over its shoulder.

areas.name: Ash Drifts
areas.text: Drifts of fine grey ash that swallow footprints within minutes.

areas.name: Dead Grove
areas.text: A grove of white dead trees that creak with no wind.

areas.name: The Cairn Line
areas.text: A line of piled stones marking the way out into the ash. Going in leads down to The Swallowing Drifts.

locations.name: The Ash Plain, The Wider Plain
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

The ash plain after the war, wider: it has crept north past the old road, and the war's burned villages have joined the old capital's outer city in the ash.

areas.name: Ash Drifts, After the War
areas.text: Ash drifts over the bones of burned war villages.

areas.name: Dead Grove, After the War
areas.text: A dead grove, newly dead, still standing.

areas.name: The New Cairns
areas.text: A new line of cairns, built since the war, leading out into wider ash. Going in leads down to The Village Drifts.

locations.name: The Ash Street Ruins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

Blackened beams standing out of the snow, claw marks on the few walls left, chalk on the searched doorways. Ways on: The Burned Register House. The way back up and out is here, to Burned Village of Kitamura.

areas.name: Chalked Door
areas.text: A doorway chalked as searched, fresh tracks going in.

locations.name: The Black Water Shaft
locations.region: Sunken Well Village, The Turned Village Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-41 · Danger: Severe]

A ladder down a well shaft into black water that does not wet the skin. Ways on: The Bucket Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to Sunken Well Village, The Turned Village.

areas.name: Dry Black Water
areas.text: Black water that does not wet the skin.

locations.name: The Booming Mouth
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The sea cave's mouth, where the surf surges in and drains away with a sound like a drum. Weed hangs from the roof, and the rocks are slick underfoot. Ways on: The Crate Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to Smugglers' Caves.

areas.name: Surge Channel
areas.text: A channel where the sea rushes in to waist height and drains away again.

locations.name: The Boulder
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A boulder the size of a house, scored with the marks of every hunter who tried to cut it in one breath and failed. A keeper sweeps the chips away each morning and says the boulder is slightly smaller than it was. The boulder sits on flat ground with the sky behind it and nothing else. Its face is a history of failure: cuts a hand deep, cuts a finger deep, thousands of scratches, and the ground around it is white with chips. The keeper sweeps them into a pile each morning and the pile is as tall as he is.

areas.name: The Cutting Ground
areas.text: Flat ground before a scored boulder, chips of stone underfoot.

locations.name: The Clattering Sand
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Severe]

Grey sand strewn with broken white masks like teeth, waves dragging over them with a dry clatter. Ways on: The Mask Collector's Shack. The way back up and out is here, to Mask Shore.

areas.name: Mask Drift
areas.text: A drift of masks piled by the tide, one face-up and watching.

locations.name: The Cliff House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A two-storey house on the west cliff with a deep tiled roof and a walled yard, looking out over the open sea: the keeper's family's home, the household behind the shop. Ruined until restored: the roof is patched with sailcloth, the guest rooms are full of nesting gulls and worse, and only the hearth room is dry.

areas.name: Cliff Guest Rooms
areas.text: A row of matted rooms along the upper floor, for whoever comes to live here.

areas.name: Keeper's Hearth
areas.text: The house's heart: a sunken hearth, a kettle hook, a long table and the sea through the shutters.

areas.name: Master Room
areas.text: The household's own room at the cliff end, a window over the sea and the lighthouse to the north.

locations.name: The Count Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A stone at the top of the stair where the count of a student's ninety-nine bouts is checked. Ways on: The Bout Floor. The way back up and out is here, to The Hundredth Terrace.

areas.name: Tally Marks
areas.text: Tally marks cut into the stone, a hundred to a row.

locations.name: The Court of the Dead
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

The Veil Court's true seat: a pale hall of clerks who were dead before the isles had a name, keeping black ledgers of every soul ferried and every soul owed. The living are tolerated here if they pay a memory at the door. The hall is lit by nothing and is not dark. Clerks in grey write in black ledgers at desks that run out of sight, and the scratch of their pens is the only sound. At the door a clerk holds out a hand for the living visitor's memory and takes it like a coin, and for a breath the visitor cannot recall what they paid.

areas.name: The Ledger Hall
areas.text: Rows of desks, black ledgers, and clerks who do not look up.

areas.name: The Toll Door
areas.text: A door where a clerk takes a memory from each living visitor and writes it down.

locations.name: The Court Proper
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

The yokai court itself, a hall of roots and lanterns where the courtiers hold session under their own law. Steel drawn here without a declared challenge is the worst manners the Court knows, and the Court has a long memory. Roots form the walls and the lanterns in them never gutter. Courtiers sit in session on cushions of moss, masked and unmasked both, and stop talking when the living enter, then resume as if they had not. A low table at the hall's side holds slips of paper weighed down with stones: favours, owed and owing. Steel at the hip draws every eye in the room.

areas.name: The Favour Table
areas.text: A low table where favours are weighed, written and owed.

areas.name: The Session Hall
areas.text: A hall of living roots, lanterns in every hollow, courtiers in session.

locations.name: The Cut Ropes
locations.region: Crow Tengu Nests, Nests of War Plunder Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-43 · Danger: Severe]

The lower boughs, two houses' cut climbing ropes hanging from them, crow tengu jeering above. Ways on: The Plunder Boughs. The way back up and out is here, to Crow Tengu Nests, Nests of War Plunder.

areas.name: Hanging Ropes
areas.text: Cut ropes swinging from the boughs.

locations.name: The Dark Side
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

The side of Sun Peak the sun never reaches, a slope of black rock and old snow where demons come to test the hunters and the hunters come to be tested. A kill before dawn is forbidden on the mountain; the demons know it and use it. The light goes out of the air as if a door has shut. Black rock and old grey snow, cold enough to bite through boots, and a silence with something in it. Tracks cross the slope that are not a man's and not an animal's. Far up, a ledge shows against a sky that is dark at noon, and a shape on it is standing very still.

areas.name: The Hunting Ledge
areas.text: A ledge at the slope's top where a demon waits for the next hunter.

areas.name: The Shadow Line
areas.text: The line on Sun Peak where the light stops, as if a door has shut. Going in leads down to The Lightless Slope.

areas.name: The Snow Slope
areas.text: Black rock and old snow, no sun on it ever.

locations.name: The Deep Forges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Abandoned forges deep under the mountain, closed for repairs, the house says. Heat and red light leak from the tunnels. Heat rolls up the tunnel mouths, and red light from lava seams shows chains bolted along the walls of the Mine Tunnels. The house calls the place closed for repairs, and few miners come down this far. Onmyoji Kurenai, in soot-stained white robes, moves through the tunnels pasting paper talismans to the rock. Further in, Tetsuo works alone, a thin smith with ruined hands bent over an anvil that glows red with no fire under it.

areas.name: Mine Tunnels
areas.text: Hot tunnels lit by lava seams, chains bolted to the walls.

areas.name: The Soul Anvil
areas.text: An anvil inscribed with talismans, the floor around it scorched in the shape of kneeling men.

locations.name: The Deep Forges, The Open Forges
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The deep forges after the war, no longer closed for repairs: the house works them openly, red light pours from the Mine Tunnels, and Onmyoji Kurenai pastes talismans faster than the rock can hold them. Tetsuo still works alone at the Soul Anvil, his hands worse.

areas.name: Mine Tunnels, After the War
areas.text: The mine tunnels, red light and fresh chains along the walls.

areas.name: The Open Shaft
areas.text: The deep forges' shaft, no longer hidden: a lift and a ladder, both worked day and night. Going in leads down to The Lift Landing.

areas.name: The Soul Anvil, After the War
areas.text: The soul anvil, glowing with no fire, Tetsuo bent over it.

locations.name: The Drowned Causeway
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A stone causeway running out under the grey tide, knee-deep then waist-deep, to a drowned court where what the ferrymen could not carry has gathered. The water does not move and the things in it do. The stones of the causeway are slick and the water over them is warm, which is wrong. Shapes move under the surface with no ripple above. At the far end a sunken roof shows above the tide, and from under it comes a voice reading charges in the isles' oldest legal form. A ferryman's lantern pole stands in the shallows with no lantern on it.

areas.name: The Drowned Court
areas.text: A sunken hall at the causeway's end, its roof just above the tide.

areas.name: The Lantern Pole
areas.text: A ferryman's lantern pole at the causeway's start, where the stones go under the tide. Going in leads down to The Warm Shallows.

areas.name: The Shallows
areas.text: The causeway's first reach, water to the knee, shapes under it.

locations.name: The Drowned Lantern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A tavern on Ashiura's harbour where the Brine Tide's captains drink, settle quarrels and divide cargoes. Everyone knows what it is; nobody says so. Smoke, spilled sake and the click of dice fill the Tap Room, where Brine Tide smugglers in salt-stained clothes drink under a lantern hung from a drowned ship's rib. Talk stops for a moment whenever the door opens, then starts again. Captain Odaka holds the Back Room, his laugh heard through the wall, and crews go in one at a time to settle their shares. The tavern stands on Ashiura's harbour and stays open as long as anyone is still drinking.

areas.name: Back Room
areas.text: A room with one table and a black pearl on a stand, where the captains meet.

areas.name: Tap Room
areas.text: A smoky room of sailors, dice and sake, a lantern hanging from a drowned ship's rib.

locations.name: The Drowned Lantern, Lantern of the New Masters
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: High]

The smugglers' tavern after the war, the Brine Tide's open headquarters: captains drinking at the tap, the auction's crates in the back room, and nobody hiding anything.

areas.name: Back Room, After the War
areas.text: The back room, crates of sealed goods stacked to the beams.

areas.name: Tap Room, After the War
areas.text: A loud tap room of smuggler captains and salvage dealers.

locations.name: The Drowned Lighthouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The island's northern rock, joined by a narrow causeway: a tall stone lighthouse whose lamp has been dark for thirty years, waves breaking at its foot and wreck timbers in the water below. Islanders do not climb the stair at night.

areas.name: Lower Stair
areas.text: The lighthouse's bottom floors: a stair spiralling up past storerooms, the keeper's log on a shelf.

areas.name: The Lamp Room
areas.text: The top of the tower: a great dead lamp, a ring of glass, the whole sea visible in every direction.

areas.name: The Rock Causeway
areas.text: A narrow causeway of rock over the breakers, slick with spray.

locations.name: The Drowned Tide Mouth
locations.region: Smugglers' Caves, The Arms Caves Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-33 · Danger: High]

The booming mouth, drowned sailors in the Regent's colours washing in and out with the surge. Ways on: The Armoury Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to Smugglers' Caves, The Arms Caves.

areas.name: Colours in the Surge
areas.text: Regent's colours tangled in the weed, a hand still holding them.

locations.name: The Ember Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Grey ash to the ankle, heat breathing up through it, a tender raking it into lines the next breath disturbs. Ways on: The Ember Walk. The way back up and out is here, to Fire Sanctum.

areas.name: Raked Lines
areas.text: Ash raked into lines, a footprint across them.

locations.name: The Face-Down Gate
locations.region: Ruins of the Old Capital Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

A great gate lying face down across the avenue, roofless houses on either side, fog pooling in low streets. Ways on: The Struck Streets. The way back up and out is here, to Ruins of the Old Capital.

areas.name: Gate Underside
areas.text: The gate's carved underside, names scratched out.

locations.name: The Ferry Stones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A field of standing stones out on the flats, each cut with the names of the dead a ferryman carried across. The dead who were not carried wait between the stones, patient, and ask every passer-by for their name. The stones rise out of the flats taller than a man, grey on grey, their cut names filled with silt. Between them figures stand very still and turn their heads to follow the living. One asks, politely, for a name. A Veil Officer's hand goes to their blade here without being told to, and the blade is heavier than it was on the isles.

areas.name: The Stone Field
areas.text: Standing stones on the flats, names cut into every face.

locations.name: The First Terrace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The lowest of a hundred terraces climbing a cliff, where every visitor lays their sword down for the keeper to look at before a step is taken up. Swords left by those who never came back line the wall. The cliff goes up in steps of swept stone, each terrace a little smaller than the last, to a top the eye cannot be sure of. A flat stone at the first terrace's centre is scored with the marks of swords laid on it. Along the back wall swords hang in rows, hundreds of them, and a few are rusting while most are bright.

areas.name: The Laying Stone
areas.text: A flat stone where swords are laid for the keeper's look.

locations.name: The Flooded Undercut
locations.region: Kappa River Fords, The Drowned Ford Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-32 · Danger: High]

The tunnel under the bank, flooded to the chest now, soldiers' helmets bobbing in the current. Ways on: The Rout Shelf. The way back up and out is here, to Kappa River Fords, The Drowned Ford.

areas.name: Bobbing Helms
areas.text: Soldiers' helms circling in the flood and not sinking.

locations.name: The Fog Shelf
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A shelf of black rock in the fog, the reef showing itself in pieces: a broken mast, the curve of a hull. Waves slap somewhere unseen. Ways on: The Barnacle Ribs. The way back up and out is here, to Pirate Graves Reef.

areas.name: Mast Stump
areas.text: A broken mast standing out of the black reef, a frayed flag tied to it.

locations.name: The Fogged Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-26 · Danger: Moderate]

Hot pools under drifting steam, the path between them vanishing and coming out somewhere else. The air smells of sulphur and wet fur. Ways on: The Bone Slope. The way back up and out is here, to Bear Den Ridge.

areas.name: Scalding Pool
areas.text: The hottest pool, bubbling, great claw marks on the rocks around it.

locations.name: The Fogged Wrecks
locations.region: Pirate Graves Reef, The Wreck Reef Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

Fog over new wrecks among the old, war-junks broken on the rocks, the guild's silver ship in the middle. Ways on: The Silver Deck. The way back up and out is here, to Pirate Graves Reef, The Wreck Reef.

areas.name: Smoking Wreck
areas.text: A war-junk's broken frame, still smoking faintly.

locations.name: The Frost Passage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A low passage of fitted stone, frost rimming the grass at its opening, cold air flowing out smelling of old iron. Ways on: The Hall of Seated Dead. The way back up and out is here, to Old Battle Barrow.

areas.name: Frost Line
areas.text: A line on the floor where the frost begins, scratched with old officers' marks.

locations.name: The Frozen Front
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-60 · Danger: Deadly]

Ranks of frozen soldiers under clear ice, spears raised, banners stiff, faces a hand's depth down. Ways on: The Reaching Crack. The way back up and out is here, to Frozen Battlefield.

areas.name: First Rank
areas.text: The first rank under the ice, a soldier's eyes open.

locations.name: The Garden Terraces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

Stepped garden beds on the south slope below the house, and an orchard of three old persimmon trees. Ruined until restored: the beds are thick with weeds and sea-bramble, and only the persimmons are tended.

areas.name: Persimmon Orchard
areas.text: Three old persimmon trees, one far older than the others, a grave marker in its roots.

areas.name: Terrace Beds
areas.text: Stone-walled beds stepping down the slope, the soil black and good under the weeds.

locations.name: The Gate Ring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-30 · Danger: High]

Ten weathered posts in a ring, each carved with one isles gate's name: the torii, the grove, the fox road, the five shrines, the peak and the feather. A party that names a post and walks between them is home. The posts stand on bare earth worn into a ring by feet going home. Each name is cut deep and old, the torii's deepest of all. The keeper sits on a three-legged stool at the ring's edge with a kettle, asks every party which post they want, and does not get up until they have said it. Between the posts the air shivers like heat over a road.

areas.name: The Ten Posts
areas.text: Ten carved posts in a ring on bare ground, one name each.

locations.name: The Gold Snow Slope
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-60 · Danger: Deadly]

Snow lit gold at dawn, lines of tracks across it, the north spread out beyond. Ways on: The Red Cord Cairn. The way back up and out is here, to Daylight Watch Ridge.

areas.name: Unburned Tracks
areas.text: A line of tracks that should have burned and did not.

locations.name: The Great Gate Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

High cliffs over the Sea of Fog where the Veil is thinnest. On tide nights masked spirits climb out of the fog. The fog below moves in slow swells and breaks against the rock without a sound. A row of Watch Stones runs back from the Cliff Edge, each with a worn notch where a sentry's spear rests on tide nights. By day the cliffs are empty except for gulls that circle and will not land, and the few travellers who come up keep well back from the drop and speak quietly.

areas.name: Cliff Edge
areas.text: A sheer edge over a sea of white fog, the fog moving like water.

areas.name: Watch Stones
areas.text: A line of stones where the Court posts sentries on tide nights.

locations.name: The Great Gate Cliffs, Cliffs of the Great Mask
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The great gate cliffs after the war, where a great mask now rises from the fog on tide nights, larger than the torii, eating the dead before they reach the ferry.

areas.name: Cliff Edge, After the War
areas.text: The cliff edge, the great mask's shape in the fog below.

areas.name: Watch Stones, After the War
areas.text: Watch stones where officers stand guard over the fog.

locations.name: The Grey Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A shingle landing on the far side of the Weeping Torii, where the grey tide lies flat and never turns. Lantern poles mark the path inland, and the ferryman's boat is drawn up on the stones. The shingle gives under the boot with a sound like teeth. There is no wind and no smell of salt; the tide lies flat as poured lead. Inland, lantern poles lean away from the water in a slow line, and one of them is dark. The ferryman stands by his boat with an oar he does not need and looks at each arrival as if checking a list.

areas.name: The Shingle
areas.text: Grey stones, a drawn-up boat, and lantern poles leading inland.

locations.name: The Hall of Threads
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A hall of grey strands converging on a point the eye slides off, lit from nowhere, with no shadows. Ways on: The Quiet Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to Void Sanctum.

areas.name: Converging Strands
areas.text: Strands running in from every wall toward the middle.

locations.name: The Hasty Graves
locations.region: Bone Gully, The Mass Grave Gully Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

Graves dug in a hurry by both armies, boots and hands showing through the soil. Ways on: The Grey Stream. The way back up and out is here, to Bone Gully, The Mass Grave Gully.

areas.name: Showing Hand
areas.text: A hand showing through the soil, a ring on it.

locations.name: The Hot Spring Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A sea cave at the foot of the west cliff below the house, reached by a cliff path, where a hot spring steams into a rock pool before it runs to the sea. A kappa lives in it.

areas.name: Cave Ledge
areas.text: A dry ledge above the pool where clothes and towels are left, and the kappa's cucumber ledger is kept.

areas.name: The Steaming Pool
areas.text: A wide rock pool of hot water under the cave roof, steam rolling out over the sea.

locations.name: The Hundredth Terrace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

The top of the cliff, a terrace of swept stone where the sword saints hold their last lesson. A student fights a hundred bouts on the way up and the saint on arrival; the hundredth duellist, who never passed, fights anyone who makes it. The terrace is swept so clean the stone shows its grain. The cliff's edge is a step away on three sides and the drop is the whole climb. In a shaded corner a figure sits with a sword across their knees and does not move; before it stands another, in armour from a school nobody teaches now, who moves as soon as a foot touches the terrace.

areas.name: The Last Stair
areas.text: The last stair up the cliff to the hundredth terrace. Going in leads down to The Count Stone.

areas.name: The Saint's Shade
areas.text: A shaded corner where the saint sits and the duellist stands.

areas.name: The Swept Stone
areas.text: A terrace swept clean, bout marks on it.

locations.name: The Inner Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-15 · Danger: Low]

Behind its own walls inside the capital, the emperor's palace keeps the old rites: cypress roofs, raked gravel, poets and priests and court ladies in layered silks. Nobody carries a sword inside, and every word is chosen. Raked gravel crunches underfoot past the Gate of Ceremonies, where swords are left behind and Grand Chamberlain Ochikane greets visitors with a soft smile and a scroll of names. Courtiers trade verses in the Hall of Poems while carp rise in the pond, and Dowager Empress Shoshi listens far more than she speaks. Captain Mori Sayo stands outside Princess Ayame's Rooms with her naginata, day and night.

areas.name: Gate of Ceremonies
areas.text: A vermilion gate where guards in court dress check names against a scroll. Visitors leave their swords and their manners are watched.

areas.name: Hall of Poems
areas.text: A pavilion over a pond where courtiers trade verses and allusions, and where a lot of politics is done in seventeen syllables. Carp rise for the crumbs of rice cakes.

areas.name: Princess Ayame's Rooms
areas.text: The Dowager's ward lives in quiet rooms behind paper screens, watched by her guards and her tutors. A lotus is painted on every lantern.

areas.name: The Sleeping Chamber
areas.text: The emperor's innermost chamber, dim with incense, where physicians and the Grand Chamberlain come and go and nobody else is let past the last screen.

locations.name: The Inner Palace, Without an Emperor
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-29 · Danger: High]

The emperor's palace with no emperor: roofs open to the sky where fire took them, raked gravel trampled by soldiers who were never meant to enter, court ladies in mourning white keeping the rites for a throne nobody sits on.

areas.name: Captain Mori's Naginata
areas.text: A naginata driven into the ground before the inner gate: Captain Mori Sayo fell holding it for Princess Ayame.

areas.name: Chamberlain's Marker
areas.text: A stone by the seal room's door: Grand Chamberlain Ochikane was cut down here keeping the seals from the Regent's men.

areas.name: Gate of Ceremonies, After the War
areas.text: The ceremonial gate, its doors taken for firewood during the siege.

areas.name: Hall of Poems, After the War
areas.text: The poetry hall, roofless, the last poems still pinned to the burned screens.

areas.name: Princess Ayame's Rooms, After the War
areas.text: Her rooms, kept swept by one loyal maid, the princess's brush still on the desk.

areas.name: The Dowager's Ashes
areas.text: A small shrine where the palace fire burned hottest: Dowager Empress Shoshi died here the night the capital was stormed. Her poems are pinned to its posts.

areas.name: The Emperor's Tomb
areas.text: A sealed tomb in the palace garden, its doors unpainted: Emperor Kiyohito, whose death began the war. Nobody tends it.

areas.name: The Sleeping Chamber, After the War
areas.text: The chamber where the emperor slept a year and died; the court keeps vigil over an empty bed.

locations.name: The Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

A short stone quay on the island's east side, where the strait from Saikai comes in calm. One small boat is tied up, a net shed leans against the cliff, and a path climbs from the quay to the Workshop and the Cliff House above.

areas.name: Net Shed
areas.text: A leaning shed of old nets, floats and oars; the island's boat gear, and a bench out of the wind.

areas.name: Stone Quay
areas.text: The quay's worn stones, an iron ring for the boat, the strait to Saikai grey and calm beyond.

locations.name: The Lantern Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

An arch of living branches hung with paper lanterns, on the far side of the kodama grove and the fox road. Lights move in the trees beyond it, and a keeper sits at the arch counting who comes in. The arch is alive; the branches have grown around the lanterns and the paper has grown into the bark. Beyond it fox lights drift between the trunks at the height of a hand held out. The keeper at the arch has a tail she does not hide and a tally stick she notches for every visitor, with a different notch for the living.

areas.name: The Arch
areas.text: Living branches bent into an arch, lanterns hanging from them.

locations.name: The Lantern Walk
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A long path under the old trees where the yokai promenade after dark in masks and their true faces both, buying lanterns, trading favours and watching the living for a slip in manners. A half-yokai who walks it in full form is greeted as kin. Lantern light here is warm and shows faces as they are: a merchant with a cat's ears, a lady whose neck is longer than it should be, children who are foxes between one step and the next. The living are watched for a slip in manners and smiled at when they make one. Lanterns hang at every height, and a stall sells new ones for a favour, not a coin.

areas.name: The Promenade
areas.text: A lantern-lit path under old trees, masked yokai walking it.

locations.name: The Lift Landing
locations.region: The Deep Forges, The Open Forges Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The bottom of the lift, crates of war blades stacked for hauling up. Ways on: The Quench Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to The Deep Forges, The Open Forges.

areas.name: Blade Crates
areas.text: Crates of new blades waiting to be hauled up.

locations.name: The Lightless Slope
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Black rock and old snow with no sun on it ever, tracks that are not a man's and not an animal's. Ways on: The Blade Rock. The way back up and out is here, to The Dark Side.

areas.name: Strange Tracks
areas.text: Tracks across old snow, neither man nor beast.

locations.name: The Lodges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-30 · Danger: High]

Eight low lodges in a half-ring, one for each tradition's master, with a long mess between them and a bunk hall behind where a party sleeps off a day's drills. Each lodge door carries its tradition's mark and nothing else. Smoke from the mess rises straight up, which is the first sign the wind here is not the isles' wind. Each lodge door is shut and marked; a student waits outside one with their hands folded, and has been waiting a while. From the mess comes the knock of a ladle on a cauldron and the voice of the keeper telling someone the board is for anyone who can read it.

areas.name: Masters' Lodges
areas.text: Eight doors in a half-ring, each marked with one tradition's sign.

areas.name: The Bunk Hall
areas.text: Rows of bunks, a stove, and the quiet of people too tired to talk.

areas.name: The Mess
areas.text: A long table, a cauldron that is never empty, and a board of jobs by the door.

locations.name: The Long Night Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-45 · Danger: Severe]

A wall of stone and timber across the neck of the land, manned by hunters who watch the north through the long nights. Wind comes over the wall from the north without a break, and the braziers on the Wall Walk hiss when snow blows into them. Hunters pace between the fires in pairs, spears on their shoulders, calling to the next post as they pass. Gatekeeper Daisuke keeps the North Gate, a small iron door set low in the stone, and notes every change of watch. Relief shifts come up from Asahi Gate each morning.

areas.name: North Gate
areas.text: A small iron gate in the wall, rusted shut except for one hinge.

areas.name: Wall Walk
areas.text: A walk along the top of the wall, braziers every fifty paces.

locations.name: The Long Night Wall, The Broken Line
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-50 · Danger: Severe]

The Long Night Wall after the war, broken: a breach where the North Gate stood, braziers dark on half the Wall Walk, and the hunters' line pulled back to the stretches they can still hold. Gatekeeper Daisuke keeps a gate that is no longer there.

areas.name: Fuyuki's Bow
areas.text: His bow lashed to the wall at the breach: Wall Archer Fuyuki fell the night the wall broke.

areas.name: North Gate, After the War
areas.text: The North Gate's breach, rubble and frozen blood, Daisuke at his post.

areas.name: The Breach Mouth
areas.text: The broken length of the wall, rubble and frozen blood, a hole under it going north into the dark. Going in leads down to The Rubble Throat.

areas.name: Wall Walk, After the War
areas.text: The wall walk, dark braziers on the lost half, hunters pacing the rest.

locations.name: The Lower Boughs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: High]

The first platform of branches, lashed with rope, hung with stolen mirrors that flash in the wind. Ways on: The Glittering Boughs. The way back up and out is here, to Crow Tengu Nests.

areas.name: Mirror Bough
areas.text: A branch hung with mirrors, one cracked by a beak.

locations.name: The Lower Docks
locations.region: Black Ferry Fortress, The Overrun Fortress Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-46 · Danger: Severe]

The fortress's old lower docks, under the ferry landing, where the war's dead wait in the water. Ways on: The Queue Hall. The way back up and out is here, to Black Ferry Fortress, The Overrun Fortress.

areas.name: Waiting Water
areas.text: Black water crowded with the waiting dead.

locations.name: The Marching Road
locations.region: Frozen Pass of the Long Night, The Open Pass Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

The pass floor trampled to ice by thralls marching south every night. Ways on: The Daylight Track. The way back up and out is here, to Frozen Pass of the Long Night, The Open Pass.

areas.name: Ice Road
areas.text: A road of trampled ice, thrall footprints frozen in it.

locations.name: The Marked Stones
locations.region: Earth Spider Pits, The Spider's Bargain Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-40 · Danger: Severe]

The clan stones with Hayate's mark carved beside the spider's, sentries watching from the rim. Ways on: The Bargain Pit. The way back up and out is here, to Earth Spider Pits, The Spider's Bargain.

areas.name: Double Mark
areas.text: Hayate's wind mark cut beside the spider's ochre hand.

locations.name: The Mask Tide
locations.region: Mask Shore, Shore of Washed-Up Masks Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-46 · Danger: Severe]

A tide line strewn with masks by the dozen every night, clattering in the surf. Ways on: The Wearer's Shack. The way back up and out is here, to Mask Shore, Shore of Washed-Up Masks.

areas.name: Dozen Masks
areas.text: A dozen masks in a row, all turned to the sea.

locations.name: The Mast Rookery
locations.region: Heron Island, Island of the Drowned Navy Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-38 · Danger: High]

Herons nesting in the masts of sunk warships, the water below them full of hulls. Ways on: The Smugglers' Graves. The way back up and out is here, to Heron Island, Island of the Drowned Navy.

areas.name: Rigging Nests
areas.text: Nests in the rigging of a sunk warship.

locations.name: The Narrow Ledge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A narrow ledge over nothing, prayer flags shredding in the wind, the drop beside it bottomless. Ways on: The Leaning Wall. The way back up and out is here, to Wind Sanctum.

areas.name: Shredded Flags
areas.text: Flags torn to threads streaming out over the drop.

locations.name: The Nesting Trees
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-28 · Danger: High]

Trees white with nesting herons, the noise deafening, the ground white below. The smell is strong. Ways on: The Clan Graves. The way back up and out is here, to Heron Island.

areas.name: White Ground
areas.text: Ground white with droppings under the nests, tracks pressed into it.

locations.name: The Ochre Slabs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: High]

Carved slabs of the old clans leaning at old angles, smeared with ochre handprints. The air is still and close. Ways on: The Silk Roof. The way back up and out is here, to Earth Spider Pits.

areas.name: Ochre Slab
areas.text: A slab with fresh ochre handprints over the old carving.

locations.name: The Old Observatory
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

The Bureau's first observatory, a lone tower of bronze instruments on the hills south of the city, kept by a few star-readers who prefer its dark to the city's lanterns. The path up from Seimei ends at a squat stone tower with no lanterns lit, and the wind on the hill carries the creak of turning bronze rings. On the Instrument Deck the armillary spheres are green with age and the charts are pinned flat under stones. Tsukimi is usually there, squinting close at a chart, and she tends to tell a visitor what she reads in their stars before asking their name. The readers sleep by day and work through the night.

areas.name: Instrument Deck
areas.text: An open deck of bronze armillary spheres and star charts weighted with stones, cold wind and the hum of a reader counting under her breath.

locations.name: The Old Observatory, Watch of the Cracked Seals
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-29 · Danger: High]

The old observatory after the war, its instruments trained north on the Vaults day and night. The star-readers no longer sleep.

areas.name: Instrument Deck, After the War
areas.text: The instrument deck, every lens turned north toward Hyoga.

locations.name: The Pebble Rings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Rings of pebbles on the near shore that someone keeps repairing, mist so thick the far shore cannot be seen. Ways on: The Reader's Hut. The way back up and out is here, to Water Sanctum.

areas.name: Mended Ring
areas.text: A ring of pebbles, one stone freshly replaced.

locations.name: The Rim Path
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

A crumbling path down the gully wall, bones in the soil, the white stream below. Ways on: The Milk Stream. The way back up and out is here, to Bone Gully.

areas.name: Bone Soil
areas.text: Soil packed with bones, a skull grinning from the path.

locations.name: The Roofless Courtyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: Moderate]

Grass in the courtyard, rusted cannon lying where they fell, the sea booming beyond the wall. A few navy sailors' hammocks hang under the one roof left. Ways on: The Gun Gallery. The way back up and out is here, to Old Coast Fort.

areas.name: Fallen Cannon
areas.text: A cannon on its side in the grass, its muzzle full of rainwater.

locations.name: The Root Stair Down
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A spiral of knotted wood winding inside the trunk, kodama clinging to the walls above the first landing. Ways on: The Closed Landing. The way back up and out is here, to The Rooted Deep.

areas.name: Last Kodama Landing
areas.text: A landing of knotted roots where the last kodama watch.

locations.name: The Rooted Deep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A tree so old its hollow trunk is a country, with roots going down past where a torch reaches. Something crowned keeps the deepest chamber and the kodama fall silent on the way down. The trunk's inside is wide enough to lose a house in and goes down in a spiral of roots that serve as a stair. Kodama cling to the walls at the top and there are none past the first landing. The air is wet and smells of leaf mould and something sweeter. Far below a sound like branches settling comes up at intervals, as if something large is making itself comfortable.

areas.name: The King's Chamber
areas.text: The deepest hollow, roots knotted into a throne.

areas.name: The Trunk Door
areas.text: A split in the great trunk where the root stair begins. Going in leads down to The Root Stair Down.

areas.name: The Trunk Stair
areas.text: A stair of roots spiralling down inside the trunk.

locations.name: The Rope Descent
locations.region: Glacier Road, The Broken Road Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-50 · Danger: Severe]

A climb down the fissure's wall on the exiles' ropes, the cold rising from below. Ways on: The Patrol's Ledge. The way back up and out is here, to Glacier Road, The Broken Road.

areas.name: Cut Ropes
areas.text: Exile ropes hanging cut, their ends frayed.

locations.name: The Rubble Throat
locations.region: The Long Night Wall, The Broken Line Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-50 · Danger: Severe]

A crawlway through the wall's own fallen stones, the frost on them scored by claws. Ways on: The Thralls' Ramp. The way back up and out is here, to The Long Night Wall, The Broken Line.

areas.name: Scored Stones
areas.text: Fallen wall stones scored by claws.

locations.name: The Sanctum Steps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A landing where five stairs part, one to each Sanctum: stone, water, fire, wind and the void. A hermit keeps a hut at the parting and tells visitors which stair their Element will suffer them on. Five stairs leave the landing in five directions and five kinds of weather: warm stone, wet mist, ash heat, a tearing wind, and a stair that is simply dim. Moss has taken the hut at the parting and the hermit in it has let it. He asks each visitor their Element before he asks their name, and points with his chin.

areas.name: The Parting
areas.text: Five stairs leaving one landing, a moss-roofed hut at the join.

locations.name: The Screaming Road
locations.region: Frozen Pass of the Long Night Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Severe]

A narrow road between ice walls, wind screaming through it, snow filling old tracks within the hour. Ways on: The Thrall Shelter. The way back up and out is here, to Frozen Pass of the Long Night.

areas.name: Drift Road
areas.text: A drifted road, a thrall's footprint frozen into it.

locations.name: The Sealing Vaults
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-60 · Danger: Deadly]

A prison fortress cut into the glacier, its doors sealed with paper and iron, its Wardens in furs. The bodies of the great beasts lie bound in its depths. The cold inside the glacier is dry and still, and every sound echoes off the ice. Visitors are stopped in the Outer Hall and searched by Seal-Master Hisame, who keeps the record of every beast. Beyond lies the Seal Gallery, door after door papered with talismans, where Keeper Yorikane walks the line in heavy furs, inspecting each seal. Wardens stand at every passage.

areas.name: Outer Hall
areas.text: A hall of ice where visitors are searched and seals checked.

areas.name: Seal Gallery
areas.text: A gallery of sealed doors, each papered with layers of talismans.

areas.name: The Deep Vault
areas.text: A vault so cold the air hurts, chains as thick as trees going down into dark.

locations.name: The Sealing Vaults, The Cracked Vaults
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The Sealing Vaults after the war, cracked: a fissure runs from the Deep Vault out through the glacier, and cold blue light leaks from it. Seal-Master Hisame keeps the record of every beast still bound, and of the ones that are not. Keeper Yorikane walks the Seal Gallery replacing paper talismans that burn out in a night.

areas.name: Outer Hall, After the War
areas.text: The outer hall, Hisame keeping a list of beasts that are no longer bound.

areas.name: Seal Gallery, After the War
areas.text: The seal gallery, talismans burning out on the doors, Yorikane replacing them.

areas.name: The Deep Vault, After the War
areas.text: The deep vault, a crack of blue light in its door.

locations.name: The Shrine on the Rock
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A tiny red-roofed shrine on a sea rock off the island's south-west tip, joined to the shore by stepping stones that the tide covers twice a day: the lamp shrine of the sea's kami. Ruined until restored: its lamp is cold and its roof leaks.

areas.name: Lamp Shrine
areas.text: The shrine itself: a red roof, a stone lamp, offerings of salt and a scroll box.

areas.name: Shrine Stepping Stones
areas.text: A line of flat stones across the shallows, dry only at low tide.

locations.name: The Smugglers' Quay
locations.region: Old Coast Fort, The Abandoned Fort Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-37 · Danger: High]

The sea wall used as a quay, smugglers' boats moored along it, the fort behind empty. Ways on: The Empty Barracks. The way back up and out is here, to Old Coast Fort, The Abandoned Fort.

areas.name: Moored Boats
areas.text: Smugglers' boats tied to the old gun ports.

locations.name: The Spear-Shored Trench
locations.region: Old Battlefield of Sekigane, Twice Fought Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-36 · Danger: High]

A trench into the new mound, its walls shored with the spears of the men buried in it. Ways on: The Levy Rows. The way back up and out is here, to Old Battlefield of Sekigane, Twice Fought.

areas.name: Broken Spear Shoring
areas.text: Spear shafts driven into the earth to hold the walls.

locations.name: The Swallowing Drifts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-45 · Danger: Severe]

Drifts of fine grey ash that swallow footprints within minutes, the wind lifting veils that sting the eyes. Ways on: The Creaking Grove. The way back up and out is here, to The Ash Plain.

areas.name: Fresh Cairn
areas.text: A cairn of piled stones, newly built.

locations.name: The Swaying Rope
locations.region: Revenant Shaft, The Climbing Dead Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-46 · Danger: Severe]

The shaft head, the rope swaying with climbers, handprints in the soot. Ways on: The Climbers' Ladder. The way back up and out is here, to Revenant Shaft, The Climbing Dead.

areas.name: Sooty Handprints
areas.text: Handprints in soot around the shaft's lip.

locations.name: The Swaying Winch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A winch and a rope going down into the dark, the rope moving by itself. The air from below smells of cold ash. Ways on: The Ladder Drop. The way back up and out is here, to Revenant Shaft.

areas.name: Winch
areas.text: An old winch with a handle polished by hands that are not there.

locations.name: The Thin Air Steps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

Steps cut into the mountain above the ascetics' peak, where the air is thin enough that the first hundred leave a hunter gasping. A cook keeps a fire at the first landing and feeds anyone who makes it up. The first fifty steps are easy and the next fifty are not; breath comes short and the head goes light. Cloud lies below and the peak above is a shape in brighter cloud. At the landing a cook's fire burns small and blue in the thin air, with a row of bowls beside it and the smell of barley and dried fish.

areas.name: The First Landing
areas.text: A landing with a cook's fire, bowls and a view of nothing but cloud.

locations.name: The Thin Ice
locations.region: Frozen Battlefield, The Thawing Field Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 50-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The ice over the ranks thinned to a skin, faces clear beneath it, some of them moving. Ways on: The Split Front. The way back up and out is here, to Frozen Battlefield, The Thawing Field.

areas.name: Moving Face
areas.text: A face under thin ice, its eyes following.

locations.name: The Training Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A flat sandy clearing among the pines between the Workshop and the house, with wooden striking posts and a sword rack under the trees. Ruined until restored: the posts are rotten and deadfall covers half the sand.

areas.name: Pine Sword Rack
areas.text: A roofed rack of wooden blades and staves, and the posts, scarred by fifty years of practice.

areas.name: Sand Floor
areas.text: Raked sand between the pines, the ring where bouts are fought.

locations.name: The Trampled Gold
locations.region: Daylight Watch Ridge, The Ridge of Unburned Tracks Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 50-60 · Danger: Deadly]

The sunlit snow, trampled flat by an army's passing, tracks crossing it every morning. Ways on: The Cut Cairn. The way back up and out is here, to Daylight Watch Ridge, The Ridge of Unburned Tracks.

areas.name: Army Tracks
areas.text: Snow trampled flat by thousands of feet.

locations.name: The Truce Pools
locations.region: Bear Den Ridge, The Oni's Ridge Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-37 · Danger: High]

Hot pools where patrols of both villages bathe on truce, weapons stacked on opposite banks. Ways on: The Sake Cellar. The way back up and out is here, to Bear Den Ridge, The Oni's Ridge.

areas.name: Weapon Banks
areas.text: Two banks with two stacks of weapons, watched by both sides.

locations.name: The Unchalked Street
locations.region: Burned Village of Kitamura, The First of Many Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

The ash street under fresh snow, no chalk on the doorways, nobody left to search for. Ways on: The Empty Well. The way back up and out is here, to Burned Village of Kitamura, The First of Many.

areas.name: Bare Doorway
areas.text: A doorway with no chalk, tracks going in.

locations.name: The Undercut Bank
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A low hollow under the river bank, knee-deep in cold water, its roof matted with old leaves. Cucumber rinds float in the current, and the walls are smeared with webbed handprints. Ways on: The Wrestling Shelf. The way back up and out is here, to Kappa River Fords.

areas.name: Rind Pool
areas.text: A still pool where cucumber rinds gather, a webbed footprint pressed in the mud beside it.

locations.name: The Upright Gate
locations.region: Ruins of the Old Capital, The Waking Ruins Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

The fallen gate leaning upright again, a fresh name carved in it overnight. Ways on: The Speaking Streets. The way back up and out is here, to Ruins of the Old Capital, The Waking Ruins.

areas.name: Fresh Name
areas.text: A name freshly carved in the gate's old wood.

locations.name: The Village Drifts
locations.region: The Ash Plain, The Wider Plain Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-50 · Danger: Severe]

Ash drifts over the bones of war-burned hamlets, roof beams showing through. Ways on: The Two Ghost Roads. The way back up and out is here, to The Ash Plain, The Wider Plain.

areas.name: Beam Tips
areas.text: Burned roof beams poking through the ash.

locations.name: The War Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A cut in the yard's eastern bank where a road the Otherworld never had runs down into mist. Its keeper says plainly what it is: the road home to a home that has changed, and it runs one way. Past the last lodge the yard's dust gives way to a cut in the bank and a road that was not there when the masters came. Banners in colours no house on the isles flies hang from stakes either side, limp. The mist below smells of wet ash, and now and then a sound comes up out of it that could be a bell or a gate. The keeper does not stop anyone; he only counts them, and says the road runs one way.

areas.name: The Cut
areas.text: A notch in the bank, the road beginning, banners staked either side.

locations.name: The Warlord's Mouth
locations.region: Old Battle Barrow, The Opened Barrow Depths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-46 · Danger: Severe]

The barrow mouth, open, an armoured dead warlord seated in it, asking passers-by for terms. Ways on: The Half-Empty Hall. The way back up and out is here, to Old Battle Barrow, The Opened Barrow.

areas.name: Seated Warlord
areas.text: A dead warlord seated in the doorway, a sword across his knees.

locations.name: The Warm Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A low cave under the standing stone, warm air coming out, a torch burning low and sullen inside it. Ways on: The Weight Hall. The way back up and out is here, to Earth Sanctum.

areas.name: Swept Floor
areas.text: A floor swept clean, footprints of stone feet on it.

locations.name: The Warm Shallows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

The causeway's first reach, water to the knee and wrongly warm, shapes moving under it with no ripple above. Ways on: The Docket Steps. The way back up and out is here, to The Drowned Causeway.

areas.name: Gripping Water
areas.text: Warm water over slick stones, pale fingers just under the surface.

locations.name: The Whetstone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A terrace halfway up with a whetstone the size of a millwheel, turned by an armourer who remembers every blade he has ever touched. A duellist who died on the terraces keeps him company and offers bouts to anyone who looks bored. The whetstone is the size of a millwheel and turns with a sound like a long breath drawn in. Sparks go up in a fan and die on the stone floor. The armourer at the crank does not look up from the blade he is working, and a woman in a duellist's half-armour leans on the parapet beside him, translucent at the edges, watching the stair for someone to fight.

areas.name: The Wheel
areas.text: A great whetstone, sparks, and an armourer at the crank.

locations.name: The Workshop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A long low workshop on the lane up from the quay: a forge with a cold chimney, a workbench under a collapsed skylight, a stillroom of cracked jars, and an open counter facing the lane where the keeper's family once sold rope, lamp oil and repairs. Ruined until restored: the forge is choked with wreck timber and the counter's shutter hangs by one hinge.

areas.name: The Counter
areas.text: The open shop front on the lane: a long scarred counter, a shutter, a board for orders and prices.

areas.name: The Forge Room
areas.text: A forge and an anvil of black ship-iron, bellows, racks for tools; the heart of the workshop.

areas.name: The Stillroom
areas.text: Shelves of jars and a copper still for medicines and lamp oil, under a window to the garden.

locations.name: The Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-30 · Danger: High]

A wide trampled yard under five different skies, one for each quarter at the horizon. Sparring circles are scraped in the dirt, racks of wooden blades stand along the edge, and the sound is always the same: breath, feet and wood on wood. Dust hangs in the air at knee height and never quite settles. In one circle two shinobi trade feints without a sound; in the next a samurai drills the same cut forty times while a breath hunter counts for her. Nobody watches the sky, which is five skies, and nobody mentions it. A master crosses from the lodges now and then, says four words to a student, and goes back.

areas.name: Blade Racks
areas.text: Racks of wooden blades, staves and padded fists, worn smooth by hands.

areas.name: Sparring Circles
areas.text: Rings scraped in the dirt, each with its own rule chalked on a post.

locations.name: Tournament Grounds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-25 · Danger: Moderate]

The Capital Tournament's grounds: a sand ring under the castle walls, ringed by stands and the pavilions of the great houses. Champions train here for months; crowds come to watch and to bet. The roar of the Bettors' Stands carries across the grounds, where merchants, farmers and gamblers shout odds and pass tally sticks. Otama the Bookmaker sits with her lacquered box and tally board, sending four runners into the crowd. Along the far side the House Pavilions stand in silk of house colours, each with its own guards. Between bouts attendants rake The Sand Ring smooth, and on quiet days champions spar there under the castle walls of Miyako.

areas.name: Bettors' Stands
areas.text: Wooden stands packed with merchants, farmers and gamblers shouting odds. Coins and tally sticks change hands faster than the eye.

areas.name: House Pavilions
areas.text: Silk pavilions in house colours where champions rest, lords watch, and seconds whisper. Each pavilion has its own guards and its own rumours.

areas.name: The Sand Ring
areas.text: A ring of pale sand, raked smooth before every bout, where reputations are made in a single cut. The silence before a draw is louder than the crowd.

locations.name: Tournament Grounds, The Regent's Camp
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-36 · Danger: High]

The tournament grounds turned into the Regent's field camp: tents where the house pavilions stood, a quartermaster's stockade over the bettors' stands, and the sand ring used for drill. The Capital Tournament is a memory and a grievance.

areas.name: Bettors' Stands, After the War
areas.text: The stands boarded into a quartermaster's stockade, ledgers where bets were.

areas.name: House Pavilions, After the War
areas.text: Tents and command pavilions where the great houses' silks once hung.

areas.name: The Sand Ring, After the War
areas.text: The ring, drill-trampled, still fought in when the camp needs a bout.

locations.name: Two-Blooded Refuge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-30 · Danger: High]

A hidden village under a great tree where children of humans and yokai live together, behind wards no hunter finds. Lanterns hang in the branches of the Great Tree, and children with ears, tails or scales play among roots as thick as houses. The air smells of leaf mould and cooking fires. Old Kagari sits at the roots with the small ones around her, teaching in a slow voice. At the Ward Ring the carved stones hum faintly, and Kiyo of the Refuge stands guard there with her ears uncovered, studying every newcomer with open suspicion.

areas.name: Great Tree
areas.text: A tree so vast the village lives in its roots, lanterns hung in its branches.

areas.name: Ward Ring
areas.text: A ring of carved stones that hums when hunters come near.

locations.name: Two-Blooded Refuge, The Overfull Refuge
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-40 · Danger: Severe]

The Two-Blooded Refuge after the war, overfull: half-blood children from every burned village have been carried here, and the Great Tree's branches hold more lanterns than leaves. Old Kagari teaches in shifts, and Kiyo of the Refuge has stopped pretending newcomers are welcome.

areas.name: Great Tree, After the War
areas.text: The Great Tree, lanterns crowding its branches, children sleeping in its roots.

areas.name: Ward Ring, After the War
areas.text: The ward ring humming loud, one stone cracked, Kiyo guarding it.

locations.name: Valley of the Rank Exams
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A deep cedar valley below Kagegi where the rank exams are held among traps and posts, far from the daily training grounds. Outsiders who wander in are escorted out, or not. The cedars grow close and dark, and every breeze sets small bells ringing somewhere in the Trap Grove. Wires catch the light at ankle height along the paths. Proctor Kagegi Isshin walks the Exam Clearing between exam days, resetting traps and checking posts, polite to anyone he finds and firm about walking them back to the trail. Out of season the valley stays empty but for birds and the proctor.

areas.name: Exam Clearing
areas.text: A clearing with a stone where examinees kneel, stained dark.

areas.name: Trap Grove
areas.text: A grove of cedars strung with wires and bells, every path a test.

locations.name: Valley of the Rank Exams, The Battlefield Valley
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: High]

The exam valley after the war, a battlefield: the joint exam's clearing was where the village war began, and its trap grove is full of real traps now.

areas.name: Exam Clearing, After the War
areas.text: The exam clearing, scarred with the first battle of the village war.

areas.name: Trap Grove, After the War
areas.text: A grove of live traps from both villages.

locations.name: Village Border Stones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

A line of stones marking the old border between the two villages' lands, each carved with both villages' marks. The meadow is open and windy, with long grass that hides the bases of the stones. Each stone along the Stone Line bears both villages' marks, chipped and recut over the years. Herb-pickers from Kagegi Village and Hayate Ridge Village cross here without stopping, and patrols from both sides walk the line at dusk, each keeping to its own end and watching the other.

areas.name: Stone Line
areas.text: A line of carved border stones across a meadow, one freshly set, its earth still dark.

locations.name: Village Border Stones, The Fortified Line
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-29 · Danger: High]

The border stones after the war, a fortified line: palisades behind every stone, and both villages' dead buried on their own side of it.

areas.name: Masaki's Stone
areas.text: A border stone with his name cut in it, on Kagegi's side: Border Watcher Masaki was the first killed in the village war.

areas.name: Stone Line, After the War
areas.text: A line of border stones with palisades behind them.

locations.name: Void Sanctum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A sanctum of the void: a hall where the grey thread shrine's threads all end, lit by nothing, where something that is not there waits to be noticed. A shinobi learns the void style by being as absent as it is. Grey threads run in from every wall toward a point in the middle of the hall, and the eye slides off that point. There is light, from nowhere, and no shadows. Footsteps make no echo. The sense of being looked at is strong and comes from the one place a visitor cannot make themselves look.

areas.name: The Point
areas.text: The place the strands end; nothing is there, and it is hungry.

areas.name: The Thread Hall
areas.text: A hall of grey threads converging on a point that is not there.

areas.name: The Threshold Thread
areas.text: A grey thread across the doorway where the hall begins. Going in leads down to The Hall of Threads.

locations.name: Wardens' Watch Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Severe]

A fort that watches the north for anything coming over the ice toward the Vaults. Walls of packed ice and timber face north, and the bone horns of the Horn Tower point out over the glacier. Hornkeeper Yuzuru stands his watch at the top with a spyglass, ready to sound them. Below, the Barracks are warm and crowded with off-duty Wardens mending furs, sharpening spears and sleeping in shifts. Supplies come up from Shirokawa and across from the Vaults.

areas.name: Barracks
areas.text: Warm barracks of tired Wardens.

areas.name: Horn Tower
areas.text: A tower with great horns of bone pointed north.

locations.name: Wardens' Watch Fort, The Fort Facing Both Ways
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-53 · Danger: Deadly]

The Wardens' watch fort after the war, watching south as well as north: the Northern Court went past it in the war, and now the danger is in the Vaults behind it. Hornkeeper Yuzuru stands his watch with a spyglass turned the wrong way.

areas.name: Barracks, After the War
areas.text: The barracks, half the bunks empty, furs left folded.

areas.name: Horn Tower, After the War
areas.text: The horn tower, Yuzuru's spyglass turned toward the Vaults.

areas.name: Takumi's Empty Bunk
areas.text: His bunk, furs folded, a horn on the pillow: Warden Takumi of the Horn went into the Vaults and did not come out.

locations.name: Watchfire Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-25 · Danger: Moderate]

A hill where a watchfire is kept ready to warn the south of a raid. From the hilltop the view runs north to a dark line on the horizon and south toward the lowland villages. The Watchfire is a great stack of pitch-soaked logs under oiled hides, with a small shelter beside it. Watcher Heita, a young man in a hunter's coat and scarf, keeps a pot of embers alive in the shelter and checks the north every hour. The post is supplied from Asahi Gate.

areas.name: Watchfire
areas.text: A great pile of pitch-soaked logs on the hilltop with a watcher's shelter beside it, the north dark on the horizon.

locations.name: Watchfire Hill, The Lit Hill
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-36 · Danger: High]

Watchfire Hill after the war, its fire burning every night now: the warning that once meant a raid now means the line still holds. Watcher Heita keeps it fed, older than his years.

areas.name: Watchfire, After the War
areas.text: The watchfire, burning all night, Heita beside it.

locations.name: Water Sanctum
locations.info:
