[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A sanctum of water: a still black pool under mist, where a serpent keeps the depths and a water-reader keeps the shore. Nothing is thrown into the pool; what goes in is answered. Mist lies on the black pool and the far shore cannot be seen. Pebbles on the near shore are arranged in rings someone keeps repairing. Nothing breaks the surface, and the surface is not quite still: a long slow swell crosses it now and then from no wind. A reader's hut stands at the water's edge with its door open to the pool.

areas.name: The Black Pool
areas.text: A still pool, black and deep, mist on it.

areas.name: The Mist Shore
areas.text: A pebble shore under mist, rings of stones leading to the water. Going in leads down to The Pebble Rings.

areas.name: The Shore
areas.text: A pebble shore under mist, a reader's hut at the water's edge.

locations.name: Wayside Jizo Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-5 · Danger: Low]

A row of small stone Jizo statues in red bibs by the road, where travellers leave coins for safe journeys and parents leave toys for lost children. Wind chimes tinkle over the Statue Row, a line of small stone figures in red bibs with coins and toys at their feet. Travellers stop to bow and set down a coin before walking on. Kichibei the Charm-Peddler usually works the spot, his pack hung with paper wards and lucky frogs, cheerfully selling protection to anyone who has just prayed for it. The shrine stands beside the road a short walk from Oiwake Station.

areas.name: Statue Row
areas.text: A row of small stone Jizo in red bibs with coins and toys at their feet, a folded note tucked under one, wind chimes tinkling.

locations.name: Wayside Jizo Shrine, Jizo of the Lost Sons
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-23 · Danger: Moderate]

The roadside jizo after the war, every statue dressed in a red bib for a son who did not come home, coins and notes heaped at their feet.

areas.name: Statue Row, After the War
areas.text: A row of jizo in red bibs, coins and folded notes at every foot.

locations.name: Weeping Cedar
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-40 · Danger: Severe]

A vast old cedar at an abandoned shrine, its bark studded with straw dolls nailed there at the hour of the ox. The cedar shows from far off, and closer in its trunk turns out to bristle with straw dolls and nails, the old ones rusted black and a few still bright. The Nailed Bark creaks in the wind, and loose straw drifts around the roots. The Empty Shrine stands behind it with its doors hanging open and an iron hammer left on the altar. No priest keeps the place; those who come here come alone, and late.

areas.name: Empty Shrine
areas.text: A shrine with its doors hanging open, an iron hammer on the altar.

areas.name: Nailed Bark
areas.text: The cedar's trunk covered in straw dolls and iron nails, some fresh.

locations.name: Weeping Cedar, The Cedar of Many Nails
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 34-46 · Danger: Severe]

The weeping cedar after the war, its bark nailed with dolls from every army: curses on generals, on houses, on the dead emperor himself. It weeps sap all day.

areas.name: Empty Shrine, After the War
areas.text: The empty shrine, nailed dolls on its doors too.

areas.name: Nailed Bark, After the War
areas.text: Bark crowded with nailed dolls, some of them twitching.

areas.name: Old Nao's Pincers
areas.text: Her nail pincers laid at the cedar's roots: Nail-Puller Old Nao died under the cedar, and nobody pulls the nails now.

locations.name: Weeping Torii
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A lone torii on the moor that is always wet with dew, as if it were weeping. Pilgrims pray beneath it for the lost. The moor is quiet here except for wind in the heather and a slow drip from the crossbeam. Pilgrims kneel on the Torii Ground with their knees soaked through, holding written names or small belongings of the lost. Some tie folded paper to the posts, and the damp takes the ink within a day. Many of them walk out from the Pilgrims' Hostel in the morning and back again before dark.

areas.name: Torii Ground
areas.text: The ground beneath the lone torii, always damp, pilgrims kneeling in the wet grass to pray.

locations.name: Weeping Torii, Salt-Weeping Torii
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-33 · Danger: High]

The weeping torii after the war, its dew running salt and grey: the other side is crowded, and the torii weeps for all of them. It still opens the dead's side for those who are its kin.

areas.name: Torii Ground, After the War
areas.text: Ground soaked with salt dew under the torii.

locations.name: Whaling Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Severe]

A whaling station of the exiles, rendering oil that lights the north. The stink of boiling blubber reaches the boats long before the shore. In the Rendering Yard, great vats bubble over fires among whale ribs taller than a man, and exiles in oil-black furs work the flensing knives. Foreman Isana walks the yard calling orders and testing the oil. Barrels go out by sled and boat, and the lamps of Shirokawa burn this oil all winter.

areas.name: Rendering Yard
areas.text: A yard of whale bones and boiling vats of oil, the smell thick enough to taste.

locations.name: Whaling Station, The Station of Hungry Lamps
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-50 · Danger: Severe]

The whaling station after the war, working for the whole north: every lamp south of the Vaults burns its oil now, and Foreman Isana's yard runs night and day among whale ribs taller than a man.

areas.name: Rendering Yard, After the War
areas.text: The rendering yard, vats bubbling night and day.

locations.name: Whispering Bamboo
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High]

A bamboo forest where the wind whispers and travellers come out with cuts they never felt. Stalks knock together overhead, and the wind runs through the Bamboo Corridor in long hushes that sound like speech. Light falls in green stripes across the path. Old Moss wanders here with his basket, picking mushrooms and talking about yokai to anyone who will listen, fresh nicks on his arms that he cannot explain. Gatherers from Kitsunebi Crossing come for the shoots in spring and leave before dusk.

areas.name: Bamboo Corridor
areas.text: A corridor of tall bamboo, light in green stripes.

areas.name: Cut Grove
areas.text: Bamboo slashed into strange letters.

locations.name: Whispering Bamboo, The Bamboo of Written Names
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-40 · Danger: Severe]

The whispering bamboo after the war, where the sickle weasels have cut names into every stalk: soldiers' names, villages' names, and the dead emperor's. Old Moss reads them aloud to anyone who will listen.

areas.name: Bamboo Corridor, After the War
areas.text: The bamboo corridor, stalks scored with names.

areas.name: Cut Grove, After the War
areas.text: The cut grove, fresh names on every stump.

locations.name: Wind Sanctum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A sanctum of wind: a ledge on a cliff that has no bottom, where a gale lord lives in the air itself and prayer flags tear themselves to threads in a day. A shinobi learns the wind style by standing where the gale wants them to fall. The ledge is a stride wide and the drop beside it has no bottom that the eye can find. The wind comes in gusts that lean a body outward, then inward, then outward again, as if testing. Prayer flags along the ledge are rags by the second day, and their threads stream level. Speech is possible only between gusts.

areas.name: The Flag Post
areas.text: The first prayer flag post, where the ledge begins. Going in leads down to The Narrow Ledge.

areas.name: The High Ledge
areas.text: The ledge's far end, where the gale lives.

areas.name: The Ledge
areas.text: A narrow ledge over nothing, flags shredding in the wind.

locations.name: Wind Shrine of the Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-15 · Danger: Low]

A shrine on the pass hung with prayer flags snapping in the wind, where travellers pray for good weather. Prayer flags crack in the wind like whips, hundreds of them, faded red, white and blue. The shrine itself is barely the size of a cupboard. Keeper Fuyo sits on her stool beneath the Prayer Flags, sweeping when the wind allows and chatting with every traveller who stops to pray. Most are on their way to or from Hanging Bridge Pass and want only fair weather for the crossing.

areas.name: Prayer Flags
areas.text: A tiny shrine under a cloud of snapping prayer flags, its keeper watching the pass from a stool.

locations.name: Wind Shrine of the Pass, The Neutral Shrine
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-29 · Danger: High]

The wind shrine after the war, the one place on the pass both villages respect: its keeper, a retired Hayate elite, turns away soldiers of both sides with the same look.

areas.name: Prayer Flags, After the War
areas.text: Prayer flags for the dead of both villages, side by side.

locations.name: Woodcutters' Hamlet
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-12 · Danger: Low]

A hamlet of woodcutters who fell the range's cedars and float them down to the plain. They pay both villages for safety. Axes ring on the cedar slopes above, and the Log Yard smells of fresh sap and sawdust. Woodcutters work the sawpits in pairs, stripping bark and dragging logs to the stream to float them down toward Miyako. Headman Mokichi hovers over the stacks with a sweaty face and a travel bag he never seems to put down. Children carry water between the sheds, and smoke from cooking fires hangs in the trees.

areas.name: Log Yard
areas.text: A yard of stacked cedar logs and sawpits, woodcutters at work and the smell of fresh sap.

locations.name: Woodcutters' Hamlet, The Caught Hamlet
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-27 · Danger: Moderate]

The woodcutters' hamlet after the war, caught between the villages: its headman sold news to both, both found out, and the hamlet pays both in timber for its life.

areas.name: Log Yard, After the War
areas.text: A log yard cut for two armies, half the logs marked for each.

locations.name: Yuki-onna's Valley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A valley where blizzards come without warning and travellers are found frozen with peaceful faces. Snow lies deep and smooth across the valley floor, and the light goes flat and white when a blizzard rolls in. In the White Silence, footsteps and voices stop carrying a few paces out, and companions lose each other within arm's reach. Further on, the Ice Cottage stands with a warm light in its window. Yukime of the Valley, a pale woman in a white kimono, sometimes waits at its door. Few from Asahi Gate cross the valley alone.

areas.name: Ice Cottage
areas.text: A cottage of ice with a warm light inside.

areas.name: White Silence
areas.text: A snowfield where sound vanishes.

locations.name: Yuki-onna's Valley, The Valley Between
locations.region: The Asagiri Isles, After the War
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-46 · Danger: Severe]

The snow woman's valley after the war, the last empty ground between the Hold and the Daylight Valleys. Blizzards come more often, and the demons' patrols that walk into the White Silence do not walk out. Yukime of the Valley waits at the Ice Cottage door.

areas.name: Ice Cottage, After the War
areas.text: The ice cottage, its warm window the last light before the valleys.

areas.name: White Silence, After the War
areas.text: The white silence, a demon patrol frozen where it stood.

factions.name: Hayate Village
factions.info: Hayate Village is the younger shinobi village of the Kurosugi Range, built on the windy ridges above the passes where the Kazakiri cut the wind into blades, the Kusurigi keep their field-medicine herbs and the Okamura raise their fighting wolves. Hayate shinobi are fast, loud by Kagegi standards and proud of it, and they take the contracts Kagegi thinks beneath it: escorts, rescues, hunts. The passes owe Hayate their safety. Kagegi calls them upstarts; Hayate calls Kagegi a village that has forgotten how to laugh.

factions.name: House Hiwada
factions.info: House Hiwada is the horse house of the plain: mounted archers who ride from childhood and shoot from the saddle at full gallop. Their sun-arrow crest guards the open country between the capital and the mountains, and Hiwada riders hunt bandits down the long roads that the post barriers do not reach. The house breeds the best horses in the isles and sells them dear. Farmers of the plain trust Hiwada riders more than any other samurai, because the Hiwada come when the bandits do; the capital thinks them rustic, loud and very hard to command.

factions.name: House Kurogane
factions.info: House Kurogane is the iron house: the great samurai family that holds Tetsuyama, its forges and its mines, and arms half the isles. Kurogane warriors fight in heavy lacquered iron that no ordinary blade can open, and they advance slowly and never step back. The house sends the regent its tribute in swords rather than rice, and every house's armoury carries the black iron crest, three interlocking rings in a circle, somewhere. The people of the volcanic isle call the Kurogane hard and fair: they work their miners to the bone and feed them well. In the capital they are called smiths with titles, and Kurogane lords have long memories for that.

factions.name: House Mizuchi
factions.info: House Mizuchi is the sea house, the great samurai family whose river-dragon crest flies from every warship in the isles. Its fleet holds the straits, escorts the rice barges to the capital and hangs pirates from the yardarm at Ashiura. Mizuchi samurai fight on rolling decks in light armour, with spear and grappling hook, and swim like seals. The coast loves them for keeping the sea lanes safe and hates them for the harbour dues. The other houses think them half fishermen; the Mizuchi think the other houses have never seen what comes out of the deep water at night.

factions.name: House Takamori
factions.info: House Takamori is the regent's own house, the oldest of the four great samurai houses of Miyako Plain, and its crane crest flies over the capital's inner gate. Takamori swordsmen are famous for the draw-cut: the blade leaves the scabbard and the fight is over. The house holds the regency in the dying emperor's name, keeps the post road's toll barriers, and judges disputes between the other houses. Its retainers are drilled in poetry as hard as in the sword, and they are expected to die well. To the common people of the plain the Takamori are order itself: taxes collected on time, bandits hanged at the crossroads, festivals paid for. To the other houses they are a family that has ruled in someone else's name for three generations and has forgotten it was ever borrowed.

factions.name: Kagegi Village
factions.info: Kagegi Village is the older of the two shinobi villages of the Kurosugi Range, hidden in a cedar valley where the sun reaches the floor for an hour a day. Its clans (Kurobane shadow-binders, Mushiro insect-hosts, Yumeno mind-walkers, Karakuri puppeteers) sell their skills to the houses as spies, guards and assassins under contract, and the village takes its cut. Kagegi shinobi are patient, quiet and thorough, and the village's word on a contract is worth more than a samurai's oath. The valley folk revere the village; the houses use it and fear it.

factions.name: The Breath Hunters of Hinode
factions.info: The Breath Hunters of Hinode are the demon-hunting order of the snowy north-east, sworn to kill the demons that come south from the Northern Court. They fight with sun-steel blades and the breathing forms of their schools (Ember, Tide, Gale, Stone, Thunder, Mist, Blossom, Beast), and they hold the fortress of Hinode Hold and the wall below it. Most hunters are orphans of demon raids. The north worships them; the capital forgets them until the Demon Nights come.

factions.name: The Brine Tide
factions.info: The Brine Tide are the smugglers of the east coast: a brotherhood of captains, fishermen and harbour rats who run salt, sake, foreign silver and anything else untaxed through the Mistmarsh channels to Saikai and back. They pay off Mizuchi captains, hire Kirisame guides and settle quarrels at the Drowned Lantern in Ashiura. Coast villages live on their trade. The navy hunts them when the admiral is watching and drinks with them when he is not.

factions.name: The Curse-Hunter Brotherhood
factions.info: The Curse-Hunter Brotherhood are sorcerers who turned their craft against curses: they track curses to their makers, break them, and kill the makers when nothing else works. Many are curse-bearers themselves, carrying a family curse or a bonded relic they have mastered rather than been mastered by. They work for fees from anyone, rich or poor, and keep a chapterhouse on the edge of the Blight. People hire them gratefully and are afraid to have them stay the night.

factions.name: The Fox Court
factions.info: The Fox Court is the court of fox spirits in the Ayakashi Wood, ruled by a nine-tailed lady who has watched three dynasties rise and fall. Its foxes are tricksters, shrine messengers, lovers of humans and keepers of debts, and they move among people in borrowed shapes. The Court trades in favours and promises and never forgets either. Villages near the wood leave rice at fox shrines; travellers who eat fox food and break fox promises are seldom seen again.

factions.name: The Grudge Well Sorcerers
factions.info: The Grudge Well Sorcerers draw power from the curse wells of the Ashfall Blight, where centuries of grudges have pooled into something a skilled hand can bottle. They brew curses to order, bind cursed relics, and sell both through Saikai's black market to anyone who can pay: a widow wanting a husband's killer dead, a lord wanting a rival's heir sickly. The Blight's few villages pay them to keep the wells quiet. Everyone else calls them poisoners of the soul.

factions.name: The Half-Yokai Refuge
factions.info: The Half-Yokai Refuge is a hidden village deep in the Ayakashi Wood where the two-blooded live: children of humans and foxes, tengu, oni, kappa, snow-women and stranger things, who are hunted or shunned everywhere else. The Refuge takes in anyone with yokai blood, teaches them to live with what they are, and defends itself fiercely. Neither the Fox nor the Tengu Court owns it, though both claim to protect it. Few humans know the way in.

factions.name: The Hundred-Duel Circuit
factions.info: The Hundred-Duel Circuit is the brotherhood of wandering duelists who travel the post road seeking a hundred duels: one at each of the Fifty Stations, there and back. Duelists keep a book of their fights signed by each opponent, and a duelist who completes the hundred is honoured at every dojo in the isles. The Circuit has rules (no duel without consent, no fight in a station's yard) and a Book-Keeper who keeps the record of every duelist alive and dead. The Post-Road Wardens hate the Circuit; the crowds love it.

factions.name: The Hyoga Exiles
factions.info: The Hyoga Exiles are the people the isles sent away: political prisoners, disgraced samurai, deserted Veil officers and beast hosts who escaped the Wardens, living in three fishing towns on the ice isle's south shore. They fish, hunt seals and smuggle, and they owe nothing to the regent who exiled them. Exiles are hard, proud and loyal to each other. The south has forgotten them; the Vault Wardens, whose fortress they live beside, have not.

factions.name: The Imperial Court
factions.info: The Imperial Court is the emperor's own household: the old noble families, priests of the sun rites, poets, ladies-in-waiting and keepers of the regalia who live within the palace walls and have no swords and no armies. They hold the one thing the Shogunate cannot make: legitimacy. Every title, every house's right to its lands and every regency was granted with an imperial brush. The people bow to the court's processions and know nothing of what happens inside. The Shogunate pays the court's bills and expects it to stay ornamental.

factions.name: The Kirisame Clan
factions.info: The Kirisame Clan are the marsh shinobi of the Mistmarsh Coast, belonging to neither village: rain-callers and poisoners who live in stilt houses among the reeds and know every channel the fog hides. They hire out as smugglers' guides and as assassins whose victims die of a fever three days later. The marsh folk pay them in rice and silence. The Mizuchi navy has tried to burn them out three times and lost ships each time.

factions.name: The Lotus Ward
factions.info: The Lotus Ward is the faction around Princess Ayame, the Dowager Empress's ward, a young woman of nineteen descended from an old imperial branch line. She is the claimant with the best blood, the gentlest manner and no army. Her cause has drawn court ladies, temple abbots, the Hiwada riders and the village elders of the plain, because she has promised to halve the rice tax and dissolve the Shogunate. Her followers wear a white lotus. The houses think her a puppet; the Dowager thinks her the last chance the isles have to be ruled rather than owned.

factions.name: The Mountain Temple Order
factions.info: The Mountain Temple Order is the oldest religious order of the isles: mountain ascetics, exorcist monks and shrine keepers who walk the high paths of the Kurosugi Range, fast under waterfalls and drive out possessing spirits with staff, sutra and fire. The Order shelters travellers, keeps the mountain roads and takes in anyone who asks, sworn killers included, if they shave their heads and keep the rule. The people trust the monks more than any lord. The Bureau thinks them superstitious; the monks think the Bureau sells what should be given.

factions.name: The Nephew's Banner
factions.info: The Nephew's Banner is the faction behind Lord Takamori Hidetsugu, the regent's nephew, who claims that the throne should pass to the house that has carried it for three generations. His banner gathers young Takamori swords, ambitious magistrates and lords who would rather back the strong than the rightful. Hidetsugu is a brilliant duelist and a better speaker, and he means to win the Capital Tournament himself. His followers call him the only claimant who could hold the isles together; his enemies call him the regent's ambition with a younger face.

factions.name: The Northern Court
factions.info: The Northern Court is the court of demons in the frozen north, ruled by a demon lord no living person has seen. Its demons are humans who drank the lord's blood and became something that cannot die except by sunlight or sun-steel, and they raid the south on the long winter nights the isles call the Demon Nights. The Court keeps ranks, titles and etiquette as old as the empire's. To the north it is terror itself. To a few desperate people in the south it is the only power that offers eternal life to anyone who asks.

factions.name: The Post-Road Wardens
factions.info: The Post-Road Wardens keep the Fifty Stations Road: the station masters, toll clerks, post riders and road guards who run the highway from Saikai to Mistmarsh under the Shogunate's charter. They keep the stables fed, the inns licensed, the mail moving and the barriers manned, and they hate anything that disturbs the road's order: bandits, duelists, ronin bands and rumours of a station that is not on the map. Travellers grumble at their fees and are glad of their patrols.

factions.name: The Red Lantern Federation
factions.info: The Red Lantern Federation is a league of bandit bands along the post road and the plain, named for the red lanterns they hang in the inns that pay them. They rob convoys, kidnap merchants for ransom and sell what they take in Saikai's back streets. Each band has its own boss; the Federation has a code (no robbing a paying inn, no killing a paid-up traveller, and a share for the Lantern Mother). Travellers fear them; innkeepers pay them; Hiwada riders hang them.

factions.name: The Regent's Shogunate
factions.info: The Regent's Shogunate is the government of the isles in all but name: the councils, magistrates, tax offices, toll barriers and soldiers that rule from the castle at Miyako in the dying emperor's name. It writes the laws, sets the rice tax, licenses the schools and the schools' swords, and keeps the great houses from each other's throats. Its officials wear grey and carry warrants; its magistrates are hard and mostly honest. To the people it is simply the law. To the Imperial Court it is a usurper with good handwriting.

factions.name: The Ronin Bands
factions.info: The Ronin Bands are the masterless swords of the isles banded together for safety and pay: free companies of ronin who hire out as caravan guards, debt collectors, tournament seconds and, in hard times, as bandits. Each band has a captain and a reputation; the best are booked a year ahead from the hiring halls of Saikai. Ronin have no house and no honour by the houses' reckoning, and they say the houses have no honour by anyone's.

factions.name: The Saikai Merchant Guild
factions.info: The Saikai Merchant Guild runs the free port: its customs house, its warehouses, its harbour pilots, its money changers and its foreign trade. Guild merchants carry abacus and ledger rather than swords, and they lend to anyone with land, a title or a harvest to pledge. The guild keeps Saikai free of the regent's tax and the houses' quarrels, and in return everyone needs Saikai. Townsfolk call the guild fair and rich; samurai call it a pack of moneylenders; the guild calls itself the only power in the isles that keeps its word on paper.

factions.name: The Seimei Bureau
factions.info: The Seimei Bureau is the college of onmyoji in its lake city: summoners of paper familiars, readers of the stars, talisman scribes and calendar-keepers who decide which days are lucky for a wedding, a war or a coronation. It licenses every onmyoji in the isles and keeps the great wards on the capital. Its scholars are learned, ambitious and very precise. The people buy its talismans; the houses ask it for lucky days; the temples think it practises spirit-craft without enough humility.

factions.name: The Straw Masks
factions.info: The Straw Masks are the peasant uprising of the plain: farmers, porters and village women who hide their faces behind woven straw masks and fight with flails, sickles and stolen spears. They rose when the regent doubled the rice tax for the succession fight, and they burn tax registers, open granaries and hang guild land-agents. Villages feed and hide them. The Shogunate calls them bandits and hunts them; the Straw Masks call themselves the only army in the isles that fights for the people who grow the rice.

factions.name: The Tengu Court
factions.info: The Tengu Court rules Tengu Peak above the Ayakashi Wood: winged mountain spirits, proud masters of the sword and the wind who take a few human students each generation and break most of them. Tengu despise arrogance in others and excel at it themselves. Their court is all ranks and duels and ancient insults, and its great tengu teach swordsmanship that no human school can match. Mountain folk leave the peak alone. Every swordsman in the isles dreams of being taken as a tengu's student.

factions.name: The Tetsuyama Forge Guild
factions.info: The Tetsuyama Forge Guild is the guild of swordsmiths on the volcanic isle, older than House Kurogane's rule there: smiths, polishers, scabbard-makers and the few masters who can wake a soul-blade from a sword with a spirit in it. The guild keeps its secrets by oath and its quality by inspection, and no blade leaves the isle without a guild mark. Warriors all over the isles save for years for a Tetsuyama blade. The Kurogane rule the isle; the guild rules the fire.

factions.name: The Vault Wardens
factions.info: The Vault Wardens keep the Sealing Vaults on the ice isle of Hyoga, where seven of the nine great beasts of the isles lie bound under seals older than the empire. Wardens are seal-masters, guards and record-keepers who renew the seals each winter and hunt down anyone who carries a beast's power out into the world. They live hard, cold lives and marry late or never. Most people think the Vaults a legend. Those who carry a sealed beast inside them fear the Wardens more than any demon.

factions.name: The Veil Court
factions.info: The Veil Court guards the boundary between the living isles and the land of the dead from its post at Veilgate. Its officers ferry lost souls across, cut down the hungry spirits that come back through, heal what spirits wound, and hunt officers who desert. They are organised in divisions (Ferry, Healing, Pursuit, Records and Research, Gate Guard) and carry soul-blades bound to their own spirits. The living fear them as death's officials; the houses fear them because the Court answers to no regent.

creatures.name: Ash Crow
creatures.info: A grey-feathered crow of the Blight that eats what the curse wells leave. Flocks follow the dying and the cursed. Sorcerers say they carry grudges; nobody kills one twice.

creatures.name: Ashfall Ghoul
creatures.info: A body the Blight's curse would not let rest, grey as ash and hungry. Ghouls wander the wells in packs, drawn to the living and to fresh grudges. They feel no pain and no fear.

creatures.name: Ashigaru
creatures.info: Foot soldiers of the houses: farm boys with spears and borrowed armour. They hold a line while an officer watches, break when he falls, and can be bribed, frightened or reasoned with like anyone who would rather be home for the harvest.

creatures.name: Bakeneko
creatures.info: A cat grown old enough to walk on two legs and wear its owner's face. It dances with the dead on bad nights, curses those who mistreated it, and is loyal to those who were kind.

creatures.name: Black Bear
creatures.info: A mountain bear, huge and short-tempered. It avoids people unless they come between it and food or cubs, then charges. Backing away slowly works more often than fighting.

creatures.name: Blood-Sworn Thrall
creatures.info: A human who drank a little of the demon lord's blood and serves the Northern Court for more. Fast, strong, hungry, and still afraid of dying, a thrall can be bargained with until the hunger takes it.

creatures.name: Coast Smuggler
creatures.info: Brine Tide crews and their like: tough, practical, armed with knives and boat hooks. They fight to protect a cargo, deal with anyone who pays, and sell out anyone who threatens the coast's silence.

creatures.name: Commoner
creatures.info: The ordinary people of the isles: farmers, porters, innkeepers, merchants, servants, priests and children. They fight only when cornered, run when they can, and know more about their own street than any samurai ever will.

creatures.name: Courtier
creatures.info: Nobles, officials and ladies of the court and the great houses: no armour, few blades, and a hundred ways to have someone else do the fighting. Their weapons are seals, letters, favours and memory.

creatures.name: Crow Tengu
creatures.info: A crow-headed tengu, the peak's scout and messenger. It dives from the trees, steals what shines, and reports everything to the Tengu Court. Arrows bring it down; insults bring it back.

creatures.name: Curse Sorcerer
creatures.info: A grudge-brewer from the Ashfall wells. Years of handling curses have dulled their bite on the sorcerer. They fight with hexes and cursed relics, sell anything to anyone, and cannot resist a bargain that costs someone else.

creatures.name: Cursed Relic Bearer
creatures.info: A person owned by the cursed relic they carry: a sword, a mirror, a comb. The relic fights through them and protects itself. Separate them and the bearer may thank you, or die.

creatures.name: Daylight Demon
creatures.info: The demon said to walk in daylight: it endures the sun for hours where others burn in moments, though sun-steel still bites. It avoids fights, wants something other than blood, and seems to have reasons of its own for coming south.

creatures.name: Demon Noble
creatures.info: One of the Court's nobles: centuries old, courtly and appalling. It fights with several blood arts, commands lesser demons and thralls, and offers eternal life to anyone who will kneel.

creatures.name: Drowned Grudge
creatures.info: The curse of the drowned: a dripping figure that follows a ship or a family for generations. It pulls the guilty under and remembers every name on the manifest of the ship it sank with.

creatures.name: Eldest Demon
creatures.info: One of the demon lord's three eldest, older than the empire's walls. It has not been wounded in a hundred years and fights as if bored. Only sun-steel at full strength or the dawn itself will end it.

creatures.name: Ember Sprite
creatures.info: A dancing flame-spirit born of the volcano's vents. Curious and quick-tempered, it sets fire to what interests it and flees from water. Smiths leave it charcoal for luck.

creatures.name: Empty Lantern
creatures.info: A paper lantern lit with a light that gives no light, floating on the post road at night. Travellers who follow it forget where they were going. Dawn puts it out.

creatures.name: Exile Hunter
creatures.info: One of the Hyoga Exiles: hard, proud, armed with harpoon and knife. They protect their own fiercely, distrust anyone sent from the south, and can be won only by keeping a promise.

creatures.name: Fox Spirit
creatures.info: A kitsune in a borrowed human shape. Clever, playful and dangerous, it trades favours, punishes broken promises and tests travellers with illusions. Foxfire does not burn it; a plain stick hurts more than a sword.

creatures.name: Frost Spirit
creatures.info: A drifting spirit of ice and snow that freezes what it touches. It follows lost travellers, offering a cold sleep. Earth and stone break its hold.

creatures.name: Funayurei
creatures.info: The ghosts of drowned sailors who rise around ships in fog asking for a ladle, to fill the boat with sea. Blades barely bite them; a ladle with no bottom sends them away.

creatures.name: Gaki
creatures.info: Hungry ghosts: the dead who were greedy in life, or whose families never made the offerings, wasted to thin necks and swollen bellies with a hunger and thirst nothing fills. They swarm forgotten graves and kitchens that skip the offering for the dead. A blade scatters them; a proper offering and rite quiets them.

creatures.name: Gale Spirit
creatures.info: A wind-spirit of the high passes, all howl and invisible blades. It plays with travellers, pushes them off ledges, and calms when someone sings to it. Fire eats the air it is made of.

creatures.name: Gashadokuro
creatures.info: A giant skeleton built from the bones of the unburied dead. It walks at night, bites off heads, and rattles before it comes. Swords pass between its ribs; a hammer cracks it.

creatures.name: Giant Hornet
creatures.info: A hornet as long as a thumb whose sting can kill a horse. A nest defends itself in a cloud. Mushiro insect-hosts keep tamer cousins; wild ones answer nobody.

creatures.name: Great Mask
creatures.info: A towering masked spirit that has eaten hundreds of lesser ones. It walks through Veilgate's fog during the tides, mindless and ravenous. Only void, or a Veil officer's blade, truly wounds it.

creatures.name: Grudge Swarm
creatures.info: A cloud of black moths hatched from a curse, each carrying a sliver of grudge. They settle on the living and sicken them. Smoke and wind drive them off; swords barely touch it.

creatures.name: Grudge Wraith
creatures.info: A vengeful dead woman or man with long black hair and a single purpose: the one who wronged them, and everyone in the way. It cannot be reasoned with; only finishing its grudge, or breaking it, ends it.

creatures.name: Highway Bandit
creatures.info: Road robbers of the post road and the hills. They ambush in numbers, flee when the odds turn, and can be talked down, paid off or scared away. A Red Lantern bandit honours the Federation's code; a desperate one honours nothing.

creatures.name: Hinode Hunter
creatures.info: A demon hunter of Hinode with a sun-steel blade and a breathing form. Grim, fast and tireless, a hunter aids anyone fighting demons, distrusts anyone who smells of the north, and rarely smiles.

creatures.name: House Samurai
creatures.info: Sworn retainers of a great house: trained from childhood in sword, bow and etiquette. They fight for their lord's honour, accept a fair challenge, refuse a dishonourable one, and treat a stranger by the stranger's rank and manners.

creatures.name: Hungry Mask
creatures.info: A soul that refused the ferry and grew a bone mask over its face. It hunts the living for their souls, wearing the shape of what it was. It can still speak, and sometimes it remembers its name.

creatures.name: Inugami
creatures.info: A dog spirit made by a cruel rite and bound to a family's grudge. It hunts whoever the family names, possessing and sickening them. It can be turned against its masters by someone who learns its name.

creatures.name: Ironclad Samurai
creatures.info: Kurogane warriors in heavy lacquered iron. Blades and arrows skate off their plates; a hammer or a club rings them like a bell. They advance slowly and never step back, and they respect only someone who stands in front of them.

creatures.name: Jorogumo
creatures.info: A spider-woman who lures travellers to a lonely house with music and beauty. Her silk binds, her bite poisons, and she enjoys conversation with her meals. She can be bargained with by someone she finds interesting.

creatures.name: Kamaitachi
creatures.info: Three sickle-clawed weasels riding a whirlwind: one trips, one cuts, one heals the cut so nobody notices. They cut for fun and vanish before the victim feels it.

creatures.name: Kappa
creatures.info: A river yokai with a water-filled dish on its head. It drags the careless under, loves cucumbers and wrestling, and keeps any promise it makes. Bow to a kappa and it bows back, spilling its strength.

creatures.name: Kodama
creatures.info: The spirit of an ancient tree, a small pale figure that echoes voices in the wood. It curses those who fell its tree and guides those who leave offerings.

creatures.name: Magma Crawler
creatures.info: A slow, glowing lizard of the volcanic isle's lava tubes, as big as an ox. It guards its warm tunnels, melts what it bites, and hisses into stone under a bucket of water.

creatures.name: Marsh Viper
creatures.info: A grey viper of the reeds whose bite brings a burning fever. It strikes when stepped near and flees otherwise. Kirisame poisoners milk them; marsh folk carry the antidote.

creatures.name: Mask Lord
creatures.info: A masked spirit that has regained its mind and its will: human-sized again, articulate, cruel and ambitious. It commands lesser masks, bargains with the living, and wants a body.

creatures.name: Mask Wisp
creatures.info: The smallest of the hungry dead: a wisp in a cracked white mask, drifting toward the living to drink their warmth. Alone it is a chill and a whisper; in numbers it drains a sleeper dry. It flees light and loud prayer.

creatures.name: Masked Devourer
creatures.info: A masked spirit that feeds on other spirits and grows a new mask for each one eaten. It hunts in the tides' wake, ignoring the living unless they carry a strong soul.

creatures.name: Mountain Wolf
creatures.info: Grey wolves of the high ranges, hunting in packs. They test a traveller from the dark, take the weak and the alone, and back away from fire and a steady stance. A Hayate wolf-handler's partner obeys only its handler.

creatures.name: Mounted Archer
creatures.info: Horse-house riders who shoot at the gallop. They harry from range and never close until their quarry is wounded. Plain folk welcome them as bandit-hunters; a rider will listen to a traveller's complaint and act on it if it smells true.

creatures.name: Mud Wraith
creatures.info: A shapeless thing of marsh mud and old bones that rises from the paddies. It drowns the slow and swallows what it drowns. Dry wind cracks it apart.

creatures.name: Night Hunter Demon
creatures.info: A demon of the Court's hunting packs, sent south on the Demon Nights. It tracks by blood, fights with claws and a single blood art, and laughs at wounds that close as fast as they open.

creatures.name: Nopperabo
creatures.info: A faceless yokai that looks like an ordinary person, sometimes someone you know, until it wipes its face away to smooth blank skin. It lives to frighten and is usually otherwise harmless; many are a fox's, tanuki's or badger's trick, and the same blank face often waits a second time down the road. The real danger is the panic, the fall and the night road.

creatures.name: Nue
creatures.info: A chimera with a monkey's face, a tiger's legs and a serpent's tail that brings sickness on black clouds. It haunts palaces and is a sign of bad reigns. It flees arrows of a righteous archer.

creatures.name: Nure-onna
creatures.info: A serpent with a woman's head who waits on riverbanks holding a bundle. Take the bundle and it grows heavy as stone while she feeds. She speaks little and lies well.

creatures.name: Omukade
creatures.info: A giant man-eating centipede of the mountains, long enough to coil a hill, armoured in plates that turn a sword. It hunts people and preys on great serpents and river-dragons. Its old weakness is strange and true: a point wet with human spit bites where clean steel does not.

creatures.name: Oni
creatures.info: A horned mountain ogre with an iron club. Strong as a landslide, fond of sake and gambling, and quick to anger. An oni can be outdrunk, out-bet or out-wrestled, and pays its debts in full.

creatures.name: Onmyoji Practitioner
creatures.info: A licensed spirit-worker with talismans, a paper familiar and a calendar of lucky days. They fight from behind wards and summons, prefer to negotiate, and are always curious about anything strange the player carries.

creatures.name: Raiju
creatures.info: The thunder beast: a blue-white wolf of lightning that falls with storms and sleeps in sleepers' navels. It panics in storms and bolts through anything in its way.

creatures.name: Ranked Demon
creatures.info: A demon with a rank in the Court and a blood art of its own: ash that remembers, a bell that stops the heart, ink that opens wounds. It hunts hunters for sport and talks to its prey, and its rank plate is its pride.

creatures.name: River Serpent
creatures.info: A lesser river-dragon of the lakes and rivers, silver-scaled and moody. It demands offerings for safe crossings and floods the fields of those who refuse. Earth dams it.

creatures.name: Rokurokubi
creatures.info: A woman by day whose neck stretches out at night to spy, frighten and drink lamp oil. Most do not know what they are. Startled, she flees; cornered, she bites.

creatures.name: Ronin Swordsman
creatures.info: A masterless sword selling the only thing they have. Proud, poor and often drunk, a ronin fights hard for pay and harder for a grudge, and will switch sides for a better offer or a better reason.

creatures.name: Sea Eagle
creatures.info: A great white-tailed eagle of the northern coasts. It takes fish, lambs and anything carrying food, and defends its cliff nest from climbers with talons and beak.

creatures.name: Sea Raider
creatures.info: Pirates who prey on rice barges and fishing villages. They board fast and loot faster, respect strength above all, and will ransom anyone who looks rich enough to be worth feeding.

creatures.name: Shikigami Construct
creatures.info: A paper familiar given form by an onmyoji: a paper warrior, crane or hound. It obeys its maker to the letter, burns easily, and turns back into paper when its talisman is torn.

creatures.name: Shinobi Operative
creatures.info: A village shinobi on contract: patient, quiet, armed with hidden blades and smoke. They avoid a fair fight, finish the job they were paid for, and will trade information for their life if the contract is already lost.

creatures.name: Snow Monkey
creatures.info: A red-faced monkey of the snow country. Troops raid camps for food, steal anything shiny, and scream warnings that carry for miles. They are clever, bold and surprisingly hard to catch.

creatures.name: Soul-Forged Revenant
creatures.info: A miner whose soul was taken into a blade somewhere in the deep forges and whose body walks the deep forges without it. It works the bellows, guards the tunnels, and weeps when it hears its old name.

creatures.name: Stone Guardian
creatures.info: A temple guardian of carved stone woken by old seals: it defends a gate, a tomb or a shrine and nothing else. It cannot be persuaded; it can be worn down by wind and grit.

creatures.name: Straw Doll Curse
creatures.info: A straw effigy nailed to a sacred tree at the hour of the ox, risen to finish its curse. It walks stiffly, is hard to pierce, and burns like dry straw.

creatures.name: Swarming Masks
creatures.info: A cloud of tiny masks that move as one hungry thing, pouring through cracks and doorways. Blades barely thin the swarm; fire scatters it; void tears whole handfuls away.

creatures.name: Tanuki Trickster
creatures.info: A raccoon-dog shapeshifter, round-bellied and shameless. It plays tricks for fun, cheats at dice, and turns into teakettles and monks. It rarely means harm and always means mischief.

creatures.name: Tengu Warrior
creatures.info: A long-nosed mountain tengu with a sword and a feather fan. Proud, contemptuous of arrogance in others, and the finest swordsman most humans will ever face. It fights to humble, rarely to kill, and respects anyone who keeps getting up.

creatures.name: The Drowned Crane
creatures.info: A crane of black water whose wings bring floods: sealed in the Vaults since the great drowning of the coast. It speaks softly, sorrowfully, and wants the sea back.

creatures.name: The Ember Ox
creatures.info: A burning ox the size of a hill whose hooves crack mountains: the first of the nine great beasts, sealed in the Vaults. It hates the seal and its host, offers power for a little freedom, and remembers every forge it ever lit.

creatures.name: The Empty Moon Hare
creatures.info: A white hare with nothing behind its eyes that once ate the moon for a month: sealed in the Vaults. It is quiet, curious and utterly without mercy, and it makes its host forget things on purpose.

creatures.name: The Gale Serpent
creatures.info: A serpent of storm a league long, sealed in the Vaults. It flies on typhoons, laughs at walls, and wants to see the whole sky again. Its host feels every storm coming.

creatures.name: The Grudge Centipede
creatures.info: A centipede of iron and grudges that mountain folk say lies coiled under one of the Kurosugi peaks, held by prayer rather than by the Vaults. It hears every grudge in the isles and feeds on them.

creatures.name: The Stone Tortoise
creatures.info: A tortoise whose shell is a mountain range, sealed in the Vaults. Slow, patient and ancient, it would be content to sleep forever, and it crushes whatever wakes it.

creatures.name: The Sun-Eating Crow
creatures.info: A three-legged crow of black fire that once swallowed the sun: the ninth beast, which the old tales put somewhere high in the Ayakashi Wood, far from any Vault. Proud, clever and contemptuous, it wants the sky and a worthy rider.

creatures.name: The Thunder Boar
creatures.info: A boar of lightning whose charge splits forests, sealed in the Vaults. It is rage and joy at once, it loves a fight, and its host is never quite calm.

creatures.name: The White Stag of Frost
creatures.info: A white stag whose antlers hold a winter: sealed in the Vaults, and the reason Hyoga is ice. It is the gentlest of the nine and the most dangerous to set free, because the winter comes with it.

creatures.name: Tsuchigumo
creatures.info: A great earth spider of the old mountain clans, long-legged and armoured. It ambushes from pits, despises the emperor's line and everyone who serves it, and remembers wars a thousand years old.

creatures.name: Tsukumogami
creatures.info: A household object, a lantern, umbrella or sandal, that turned a hundred years old and woke. Mostly harmless and resentful of being thrown away, a tsukumogami helps a careful owner and haunts a careless one.

creatures.name: Umibozu
creatures.info: A vast black sea monk that rises beside ships on calm nights and asks for a ladle. Give it one with the bottom knocked out and it leaves; give it a whole one and it fills the ship with sea.

creatures.name: Vault Warden
creatures.info: A seal-master of the Sealing Vaults in furs and rope belts. They fight with seals and short spears, hunt beast hosts without mercy, and treat every stranger on Hyoga as a thief until proven otherwise.

creatures.name: Veil Court Officer
creatures.info: An officer of the Veil Court in black, soul-blade at the hip. Their spirits are hardened against soul strikes. They hunt hungry spirits and deserters, treat the living with cold courtesy, and do not bargain over a soul.

creatures.name: Void Shade
creatures.info: A shadow with nothing inside it, born where the Veil is thin. It swallows sound and light, and things it touches go missing from memory. Sunlight thins it to nothing.

creatures.name: Wanyudo
creatures.info: A burning ox-cart wheel with a tormented monk's face at its hub, rolling the roads at night. Those who look at it lose their souls. A paper charm on the door reading 'This place is the village of Shobo' keeps it from a house; on the open road only shut eyes and running water help.

creatures.name: Warhorse
creatures.info: A trained war mount of the horse houses: brave, heavy, and taught to kick and trample. It follows its rider's commands and nobody else's, and a riderless warhorse is a prize worth a fight.

creatures.name: Warrior Monk
creatures.info: Monks of the mountain temples with naginata and iron staves. They fight to protect the helpless and the temple, offer a foe the chance to yield, and can be appealed to with honest need, though never with money.

creatures.name: Well Horror
creatures.info: A thing that lives at the bottom of a curse well, made of every grudge poured into it. It reaches up for whoever leans over the edge, and it whispers the names of their enemies.

creatures.name: Wild Boar
creatures.info: A tusked boar of the plain's woods. It charges anything that startles it and does not stop for wounds. Farmers hunt them, and a boar that has tasted a field comes back every night.

creatures.name: Yamauba
creatures.info: A mountain crone with wild white hair who lives alone in a hut far up a trail. Some yamauba feed lost travellers and spin thread for the villages below; others eat them. Which one opens the door is decided by the guest's manners.

creatures.name: Yuki-onna
creatures.info: The snow woman of the blizzard, white-skinned and silent. Her breath freezes a sleeper to death; she spares those who are kind to her or who move her, and she never forgets a face.

items.name: A Blotted Exam Brush
items.info: The same brush, its tip clotted with old ink. It still helps a little with seals, but now and then it writes a wrong character on its own. Found, never sold: Old Ward Stones.

items.name: A Blotted Register Page
items.info: The same page with the names smeared. It still sharpens the bearer's cut a little, but in a duel they hear a voice counting, and it is never their count. Found, never sold: Duelists' Teahouse, Teahouse of the Last Duels.

items.name: A Child's Reed Whistle
items.info: A small whistle cut from a reed, worn smooth by a child's mouth. Its note calms anyone who hears it, and the bearer keeps their nerve when everyone else breaks. Left when the Reed Mother found her son. Found, never sold: Reed Channels.

items.name: A Cut Sword-Knot
items.info: The same knot, cut through. It still steadies the bearer a little, but in a hard fight their grip loosens at the worst moment. Found, never sold: Shrine of the Fallen Feather, Rack of the Unclaimed Swords.

items.name: A Forged Name-Tablet
items.info: A tablet with the right name in the wrong hand. It still lends the bearer some authority, but people who look closely sense that something about them is false. Found, never sold: Ruined Summer Palace.

items.name: A Forged Tax Receipt
items.info: The same receipt in the wrong hand, the seal a copy. It still makes clerks hesitate, but the bearer's own name keeps appearing on lists they never signed. Found, never sold: Crossroads Gallows, Hanged Crossroads.

items.name: A Frayed Well Rope
items.info: The same rope, frayed to threads. It still helps the bearer endure a little, but on cold nights they hear a counting song stop in the middle. Found, never sold: Burned Village of Kitamura, The First of Many.

items.name: A Half-Burned Register
items.info: The same register with half its pages ash. It still sharpens the bearer's memory a little, but at night they hear names they cannot place. Found, never sold: Grey Pilgrims' Road, The Penitents' Road.

items.name: A Loaded Die
items.info: The same bone die with lead in it. It still tells the bearer when a table is crooked, but it rolls against them whenever someone they owe is watching. Found, never sold: Lantern Row Gambling Den, Soldiers' Den.

items.name: A Pardon That Will Not Thaw
items.info: The same pardon, still sealed in ice. It still sharpens the bearer's sense for lies a little, but their hands are always cold. Found, never sold: Glacier Road.

items.name: A Scorched Whistle
items.info: The same whistle, its mouthpiece melted. It still carries the bearer's orders a little, but every order it gives smells of smoke. Found, never sold: Mizuchi Naval Anchorage, The Burned Fleet.

items.name: A Split Reed Whistle
items.info: The same whistle, split along its length. It still steadies the bearer a little, but its note breaks off halfway, like the lullaby. Found, never sold: Reed Channels.

items.name: A Thread of the Hungry Nothing
items.info: A thread that is not there, and is. Whatever it is sewn into is overlooked. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Void Sanctum, never sold.

items.name: A Waterlogged Token
items.info: The same token, split and cold. It still eases the bearer through a door now and then, but every gate they pass through shuts a little too fast behind them. Found, never sold: Seimei, Behind Two Walls.

items.name: Abbot's Sanctuary Seal
items.info: A seal that marks a house or a person as under the Order's protection.

items.name: After the War
items.info:
A veteran's account, written after the war for the ones who were not there.

The war is reached by The War Road, in the Otherworld. Its keeper tells the party who the masters have finished with and who they have not when the party first stands on it. Once he has spoken, march and the party goes. The road does not come back: the isles before the war are closed behind you.

The isles after the war are a harder country, for levels 20 to 60. Places and people have changed: the war's mark is on them, some are dead, and new faces hold what the old ones lost. Who you knew, and what they thought of you, carries over. The villains' fates are what your choices made them. Eight War-Born walk the ruins, and every hub's board carries war bounties. Tomoshibi Isle is still yours, reached from post-war Saikai.

Four story starts open on the isles after the war at level 20, for those who would rather begin there. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Alpha's White Fang
items.info: The pack alpha's fang, white and cold, that leaves frost where it touches. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Frozen Pass of the Long Night, never sold.

items.name: Antidote Pills
items.info: Black charcoal pills in a paper packet. Swallowed soon after a poisoning they stop most common poisons from working further. 5 Mon, sold at any apothecary or temple dispensary.

items.name: Apprentice's Leather Apron
items.info: A scorched leather apron stamped with the guild's hammer mark.

items.name: Apprentice's Well Gourd
items.info: A small gourd for well water, stoppered with grey wax.

items.name: Archer's Glove
items.info: A three-fingered deerskin glove with a hardened thumb for drawing a bow all day. 5 Mon, sold at Hiwada Horse Fields.

items.name: Armoured Gauntlets
items.info: Mail-backed gloves with iron plates over the knuckles and wrists. 12 Mon, sold at Kurogane Armoury.

items.name: Artificer's Tool Roll
items.info: A leather roll of awls, files, pins and fine saws for locks and mechanisms. Artifice +1. 6 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Ascetic's Conch
items.info: A conch shell horn blown on the mountain paths to call the monks.

items.name: Ash Mask Filter
items.info: A fresh packet of herbs for a cloth mask. Keeps ash and curse-fog out of the lungs for a day in the Blight. 2 Mon, sold at Haibara.

items.name: Ash Oni's Ember Heart
items.info: A coal from the ash oni's chest that never goes out. A lair rarity: left by the boss of The Ash Plain, never sold.

items.name: Ash Salt
items.info: Grey salt boiled out of the Blight's springs. Curse-bearers cook with it, and sealers bind grudges with it. 4 Mon, sold at Haibara Ash Market.

items.name: Auctioneer's Lot Book
items.info: A book of lots sold, with the buyers' true names in cipher.

items.name: Badger Pelt Pouch
items.info: A pouch of tanuki fur sold with a wink. Shape-changers say it helps a borrowed face sit right. 8 Mon, sold at Tanuki Market.

items.name: Bamboo Bundle
items.info: Seasoned bamboo canes, the raw stuff of bows, pipes, ladders and paper. 1 Mon, sold at Whispering Bamboo.

items.name: Band Boss's Lantern Banner
items.info: A tall red lantern on a pole that a whole band rallies to.

items.name: Band Captain's Standard
items.info: A small standard with the band's mark, carried into every fight.

items.name: Band Sword's Colours
items.info: A strip of cloth in a band's colours, worn on the arm.

items.name: Banner Follower's Armband
items.info: A white armband with the Takamori crane over a single gold stripe.

items.name: Banner Sword's Tassel
items.info: A gold sword tassel worn by Hidetsugu's sworn duelists.

items.name: Barrier Captain's Pass Block
items.info: A block for printing travel passes at a barrier.

items.name: Battle Sutra Strip
items.info: A strip of sutra paper written in cinnabar, wound round a hilt or a wrist before a fight. Damage +1. 5 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Battle Talismans
items.info: A stack of talismans inked for fighting.

items.name: Beast Hide
items.info: A cured hide with the fur on, thick enough to turn a careless blade. Armourers line cuirasses with it. Taken from a beaten Black Bear, Mountain Wolf, Wild Boar, Snow Monkey, Warhorse, Inugami; a market pays 4 Mon.

items.name: Beast-Kin Fang
items.info: A dog's fang wrapped in red cord. Animals read its wearer as one of their own. 12 Mon, sold at Inugami Kennels.

items.name: Behind the Gates
items.info:
A master's note left at the Gate Ring for whoever comes through next.

The Otherworld lies behind the isles' oldest gates. A gate opens for a party when one member holds its kin at level 20 or higher, and then the whole party crosses. The gates and the kin they know:
- Weeping Torii: Veil Officer or Curse-Bearer
- Kodama Grove: Half-Yokai or Onmyoji
- Kitsune Shrine Road: Half-Yokai or Onmyoji
- Crater Rim Shrine: the Fire Element or Shinobi
- Salt Marsh Shrine: the Water Element or Shinobi
- Wind Shrine of the Pass: the Wind Element or Shinobi
- Sun-Rite Shrine of the Plain: the Earth Element or Shinobi
- Grey Thread Shrine: the Void Element or Shinobi
- Ascetics' Peak: Breath Hunter
- Shrine of the Fallen Feather: Samurai or Ronin

It is one country with five faces: The Far Shore, The Hidden Court, The Five Sanctums, Sun Peak, The Hundred Blades, around The Training Ground, where the masters of all eight traditions keep lodges, so no one has to split up to train. Ask a master for your tradition's training there; each tradition's trial is set in its own quarter. The Gate Ring sends you home to any gate you name.

Those who would rather start here can: one story start opens on the Training Ground already through the gates, at level 20. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Bidder's Lacquer Mask
items.info: A black lacquer mask with no mouth, worn at the Society's auctions.

items.name: Bird-Lime Pot
items.info: A small pot of sticky lime. Smeared on a branch or a step it holds birds, small yokai and careless feet. 2 Mon, sold at Woodcutters' Hamlet.

items.name: Blade Waker's Whetstone
items.info: A pale whetstone that hums when a blade's spirit wakes.

items.name: Blank Ward Paper
items.info: A sheaf of mulberry paper sized with rice starch, ready to take ink and a ward. 2 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Blood on the Ledger
items.info:
A ledger kept at Haibara's Vow Temple, copied for every traveller: what the isles do to a killer.

Infamy is a counter from 0 to 100, kept for each character. Every needless killing adds 15: someone who posed no threat, a surrendered, fleeing or helpless foe, a bystander, a merchant, a servant, a guard doing their job, a child, a quest-giver, anyone in a peaceful scene. It never counts self-defence or defending others, an ordered execution, a contract or bounty the story set up, an accepted duel, a battle or raid, a villain the story set up as a target, or demons, spirits, beasts and yokai. A victim already counted is not counted again.

At 25 you are Notorious: recognised, prices rise, nobles refuse you. At 50 you are Barred: no coach or ferry will carry your party while you travel with it, and lawful offices refuse you. At 75 you are Kill on Sight: guards attack on sight, and bounty hunters come for you every 30 turns. Each brand lifts again only below a lower mark (Notorious below 15, Barred below 40, Kill on Sight below 65).

The way back is penance at Haibara's Vow Temple: confess and atone there, and infamy falls by 10, at most once every 30 turns. One penance never erases one killing. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Blood-Sworn Ring
items.info: An iron ring with a drop of dark blood sealed under glass: the Court's servants wear it.

items.name: Blowpipe
items.info: A bamboo blowpipe and a quiver of thorn darts. Silent, short-ranged and much worse with venom on the darts. 6 Mon, sold at Reed Channels.

items.name: Bo Staff
items.info: A plain six-foot staff of white oak, the first weapon of every temple student and pilgrim. 4 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Bone Whistle
items.info: A whistle carved from a deer bone that only dogs and some yokai can hear. 4 Mon, sold at Inugami Kennels.

items.name: Bone-Setter's Poultice
items.info: Comfrey and rice paste wrapped in cloth, bound over a break or a deep bruise overnight. Restores a good share of health by morning; it needs the night's rest to work. 6 Mon, sold at any apothecary or temple dispensary. Restores 30 Health when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Book Duelist's Station Stamp
items.info: A wooden stamp for marking each station's duel in the book.

items.name: Bound Relic
items.info: The thing your curse lives in, or lived in: a comb, a sword guard, a doll, a strip of a dead man's sash. It is never quite cold.

items.name: Breath Master's School Haori
items.info: A coat in the colours of the master's breathing school.

items.name: Breath-Hunter's Bell
items.info: A small iron bell rung at the start of every breath drill on the Wall. Its sound keeps a hunter's count steady. 14 Mon, sold at Hinode Fortress.

items.name: Brewer's Grudge Bottle
items.info: A dark glass bottle that holds a single bottled grudge.

items.name: Brine Tide Shell Token
items.info: A pierced cowrie shell on a cord: shown in a coastal tavern, it means you run with the Tide.

items.name: Broken Shikigami Paper
items.info: A torn paper body still warm with a summoner's will. Talismans written on it hold. Taken from a beaten Shikigami Construct; a market pays 7 Mon.

items.name: Broker's Ledger of Faces
items.info: A small book listing whose face is for sale and to whom.

items.name: Broodmother's Heart-Silk
items.info: Silk drawn from the earth spider's heart, grey and unbreakable. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Earth Spider Pits, never sold.

items.name: Broodmother's Silk Haori
items.info: A haori woven from the earth spider's grey silk. It turns a blade's edge and drinks the light. The one unique piece of the depths under Earth Spider Pits, left by The Earth Spider of the Old Clans. Found, never sold: Earth Spider Pits.

items.name: Brush and Ink Set
items.info: Three brushes, an inkstone and a stick of pine-soot ink in a wooden case. 5 Mon, sold at Seimei.

items.name: Bureau Master's Star Chart
items.info: A star chart only Bureau masters may copy.

items.name: Bureau Student's Brush
items.info: A fine talisman brush with the Bureau's star mark on the handle.

items.name: Burial Tools
items.info: The tools of the work: a spade, a knife, cloths and incense.

items.name: Burned Banner Scrap
items.info: A scrap of a war banner from Sekigane. The bearer does not break, and dreams of the battle every night it is carried. Found, never sold: Old Battlefield of Sekigane.

items.name: Cabal Master's Screaming Blade
items.info: A short blade with a soul in it that whispers to its wielder.

items.name: Cabal Smith's Spirit Tongs
items.info: Tongs inscribed with talismans for handling a soul in the fire.

items.name: Calligraphy Ink Stick
items.info: A pine-soot ink stick for grinding. Enough ink for a scroll of letters or a few talismans. 2 Mon, sold at Seimei.

items.name: Caltrop Pouch
items.info: A pouch of iron caltrops. Scattered behind a fleeing runner they slow pursuers who are not watching their feet. 3 Mon, sold at Hayate Ridge Village.

items.name: Captain's Demon Ledger
items.info: A ledger of demons hunted and their weaknesses, kept by each captain.

items.name: Cedar-Haft Spear
items.info: A straight iron spearhead on a cedar haft, the soldier's weapon of the isles. Damage +1. 8 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Chain-Sickle
items.info: A sickle with a long weighted chain.

items.name: Chamberlain's Courier Box
items.info: A small black box with the chamberlain's knot that no guard may open.

items.name: Chapter Master's Ash Seal
items.info: A seal that marks a house as under the Brotherhood's protection.

items.name: Chitin Plate
items.info: A curved plate of insect shell, light and hard as lacquer. Armourers lace it into sleeves. Taken from a beaten Giant Hornet, Omukade; a market pays 5 Mon.

items.name: Cinnabar Ink
items.info: A cake of red cinnabar ink, the colour wards and seals are written in. 6 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Circle's Paper Mask
items.info: A plain grey paper mask worn at the Circle's meetings.

items.name: Circuit Duel Book
items.info: A blank duel book with the Circuit's mark: each opponent signs a page.

items.name: Clam-Shell Salve
items.info: A grey-green salve of crushed healing herbs in beeswax, carried in a clam shell. Spread on a wound, it restores a minor amount of health. 3 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 10 Health when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Climbing Claws
items.info: Iron hooks strapped across the palms. Walls, trees and cliffs become stairs. 9 Mon, sold at Kagegi Village.

items.name: Cloth Face Wrap
items.info: A dark cloth wrapped over head and face, leaving only the eyes. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 3 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Commander's Gate Key
items.info: A bone key that opens the lesser gates of Veilgate.

items.name: Companion's Short Sword
items.info: A short sword from Hidetsugu's own armoury, given to his companions.

items.name: Composite Bow
items.info: A Hiwada rider's short bow of horn and bamboo, made to shoot from a galloping horse. 30 Mon, sold at Hiwada Horse Fields.

items.name: Councillor's Castle Pass
items.info: A wooden pass that opens the inner gates of Miyako Castle.

items.name: Councillor's Driftwood Staff
items.info: A staff of bleached driftwood carried by the Exiles' councillors.

items.name: Court Gentleman's Fan
items.info: A painted court fan in the palace colours, carried by gentlemen of the court.

items.name: Court Messenger's Fox Mask
items.info: A white fox mask painted with red lines, worn on the Court's errands.

items.name: Courtier's Hairpin
items.info: A lacquered hairpin with a coral bead. At court, the right pin opens doors before the wearer speaks. 12 Mon, sold at Miyako.

items.name: Curse Breaker's Iron Bell
items.info: A bell rung to shake a curse loose.

items.name: Curse Hunter's Mirror
items.info: A mirror of polished black stone that shows a curse's threads.

items.name: Curse-Breaking Charm
items.info: A hunter's charm of knotted grey thread and a sliver of temple bell. Grudges and lesser curses slide off it; it knots tighter when one tries. 15 Mon, sold at Curse-Hunters' Chapterhouse.

items.name: Cursed Iron Nail
items.info: A rusted nail pulled from a straw curse doll. Curse-bearers keep them; everyone else should not. 3 Mon, sold at Haibara Ash Market.

items.name: Cutthroat's Tanto
items.info: A plain tanto with a red cord on the hilt, carried by sworn Red Lantern cutthroats.

items.name: Dairoku's Gold-Tooth Ingot
items.info: A small ingot cast from a hundred robbed graves' gold teeth. It weighs more than it should. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Bone Gully, never sold.

items.name: Dairoku's Grave-Digger Spade
items.info: A grave robber's spade with a sharpened iron blade, notched by a hundred coffins and a few heads. The one unique piece of the depths under Bone Gully, left by Boss Dairoku. Found, never sold: Bone Gully.

items.name: Dark-Side Demon's Night Horn
items.info: A horn of the demon that walks the mountain's dark side, black as a moonless night. A lair rarity: left by the boss of The Dark Side, never sold.

items.name: Deep-Forge Soot Mark
items.info: A soot handprint on a scrap of cloth: the Cabal's hands carry it as a pass below.

items.name: Demon Noble's Ice Crown
items.info: A circlet of black ice that does not melt, worn by the Court's nobles.

items.name: Demon Noble's Rime Plate
items.info: A plate of the demon noble's armour, rimed with frost that never melts. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Frozen Battlefield, never sold.

items.name: Demon's Black Blood
items.info: A stoppered vial of blood black as lacquer that will not dry. Smiths quench cursed steel in it. Taken from a beaten Daylight Demon, Demon Noble, Eldest Demon, Night Hunter Demon, Ranked Demon, Blood-Sworn Thrall; a market pays 18 Mon.

items.name: Devourer's Unfinished Face
items.info: A mask the devourer never finished, smooth and waiting for a face. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Mask Shore, never sold.

items.name: Disguise Kit
items.info: Face paints, false brows, a wig of real hair and a change of sleeves in a flat box. 12 Mon, sold at Foreigners' Quarter.

items.name: Divination Sticks
items.info: Numbered bamboo sticks in a cylinder, shaken until one falls. The Bureau's diviners read more than the number. 8 Mon, sold at Seimei.

items.name: Drowned Bell Clapper
items.info: The clapper of a temple bell that sank with its village. The bearer hears it ring under water when the dead are near, and sleeps badly. Found, never sold: Drowned Village.

items.name: Drowned Crane Plume
items.info: A white plume always wet, shed by the Drowned Crane under the village water. Wards hold near it; the bearer dreams of drowning. Found, never sold: Drowned Village.

items.name: Drowned Lantern Key
items.info: The key to the back room of the Drowned Lantern in Ashiura.

items.name: Drowned Magistrate's Seal
items.info: A jade seal that stamps wet even on dry paper; the dead obey its mark. A lair rarity: left by the boss of The Drowned Causeway, never sold.

items.name: Earth Ward Talisman
items.info: A brown-inked ward pressed between two thin stones. Falls and crushing blows land a little softer. 10 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Earth-Spider Silk
items.info: A skein of grey spider silk, strong enough to hang a man. It drinks the light. Taken from a beaten Jorogumo, Tsuchigumo; a market pays 10 Mon.

items.name: Ember Ox Horn Tip
items.info: A splinter of horn warm as a coal, found where the vents breathe. Strikes land harder; the bearer's temper runs hot. Found, never sold: Ember Vent Fields.

items.name: Examiner's Mirror
items.info: A small bronze mirror that shows a talisman's true writing.

items.name: Exile's Bone Hook
items.info: A fish hook carved from seal bone, given to those the Exiles accept.

items.name: Exorcist's Iron Staff
items.info: A ringed iron staff that rattles at a spirit's presence.

items.name: Face-Taker's Blood Vial
items.info: A crystal vial for keeping a subject's blood fresh for a mask.

items.name: Family Seal
items.info: A carved seal with your family's name: it opens doors and obligations.

items.name: Festival Firecrackers
items.info: A string of red firecrackers. Loud enough to scatter birds, scare a horse or cover a sound nobody should hear. 2 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Festival Yukata
items.info: A bright cotton yukata for summer festivals, drawn with fireworks or goldfish. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 6 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Field Captain's Rice Sickle
items.info: A sickle notched once for every raid, carried by a captain of the rising.

items.name: Fifty-Station Sash
items.info: A sash embroidered with fifty small station marks.

items.name: Fighting Puppet
items.info: A jointed puppet with hidden blades.

items.name: Fine Artificer's Tool Roll
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A leather roll of awls, files, pins and fine saws for locks and mechanisms. Artifice +1. 12 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Battle Sutra Strip
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A strip of sutra paper written in cinnabar, wound round a hilt or a wrist before a fight. Damage +2. 10 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Cedar-Haft Spear
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A straight iron spearhead on a cedar haft, the soldier's weapon of the isles. Damage +2. 16 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Clam-Shell Salve
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A grey-green salve of crushed healing herbs in beeswax, carried in a clam shell. Spread on a wound, it restores a moderate amount of health. 6 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 18 Health when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Fine Katana
items.info: A guild-stamped katana with a clean temper line and a well-wrapped grip, a step above a soldier's issue. 30 Mon, sold at Forge Guild Hall.

items.name: Fine Lacquered Cuirass
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. Iron plates lacquered black and laced with silk cord into a cuirass that sits close to the body. Armour +15. 28 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Mountain Root Tonic
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. Ginseng root steeped in rice wine, bitter and warming. Drunk, it eases fatigue and restores a moderate amount of Soul. 8 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 10 Soul when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Fine Naginata
items.info: A naginata with a long curved blade and a weighted butt, balanced for the turning cuts temple guards practise. 28 Mon, sold at Forge Guild Hall.

items.name: Fine Paper Ward-Charm
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A strip of blessed paper written in shrine ink, folded and worn against the body. Warding +1. 8 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Spring Trap
items.info: Fine work: cleaner, truer and better made than the plain make. A coil of spring steel on a wooden stake that snaps shut on whatever steps into it. Set, it catches and holds a creature with moderate force. 6 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Fine Yari
items.info: A Kurogane spear with a triangular blade and a lacquered haft, made for formations and good in a single hand. 25 Mon, sold at Kurogane Armoury.

items.name: Fire Ward Talisman
items.info: A red-inked ward folded into a cloth pouch, worn against the chest. Fire and heat find the wearer a little harder to burn. 10 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Fishing Rod and Line
items.info: A split-bamboo rod and silk line. Patient people eat on any coast. 3 Mon, sold at Drifting Fish Market.

items.name: Flash Powder Twist
items.info: Foreign powder in a twist of paper that bursts white when struck. Blinds everyone looking at it for a moment, the thrower too if careless. 5 Mon, sold at Foreign Quay Warehouses.

items.name: Foreign Coat
items.info: A long wool coat with brass buttons, bought off a foreign ship in Saikai; sailors trust it. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 10 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Foreign Coin
items.info: A heavy foreign gold coin, worth more than its weight to the right buyer.

items.name: Foreign Musket
items.info: A long foreign musket with powder horn and shot. One deafening shot, then a long reload; the houses are afraid of them. 60 Mon, sold at Foreign Quay Warehouses.

items.name: Foreign Pistol
items.info: A flintlock pistol, powder and shot. Loud, slow and frightening.

items.name: Fox Courtier's Foxfire Lantern
items.info: A paper lantern that holds a flame of cold foxfire.

items.name: Fox Mask
items.info: A white festival fox mask with red markings; behind it nobody is sure who you are. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 4 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Fox Shrine Bell
items.info: A small red bell from a fox shrine: foxes treat its bearer as a friend.

items.name: Fox Tofu Offering
items.info: Fried tofu wrapped for a fox shrine. Left properly, it buys a fox's good mood for a day; forgotten, it buys the opposite. 1 Mon, sold at Kitsune Shrine Road.

items.name: Fox-Favoured Fur Charm
items.info: A tuft of white fox fur in a silk bag.

items.name: Fox-Fire Bead
items.info: A glass bead with a pale flame inside that never goes out. Foxes trade them to people they find amusing. 18 Mon, sold at Kitsunebi Crossing.

items.name: Fox-Fire Tail Hair
items.info: A lock of tail hair that glows faintly blue in the dark. Shape-changers' charms are bound with it. Taken from a beaten Fox Spirit, Bakeneko, Tanuki Trickster, Rokurokubi; a market pays 14 Mon.

items.name: Fragment of the Old Regalia
items.info: A shard of gilded bronze from the first emperor's regalia, found in the old capital's ash. Holding it, the old court's memories come unasked; some of them are not the bearer's to know. Found, never sold: Ruins of the Old Capital.

items.name: Frost Crystal
