items.info: A shard of ice that does not melt, broken from the Crevasse Field. Smiths quench special blades in its water. 15 Mon, sold at Crevasse Field.

items.name: Funeral Candle
items.info: A white candle sold at every Veilgate stall. Lit at a death, it keeps the newly dead calm until a Veil officer arrives. 1 Mon, sold at Tasogare.

items.name: Fur-Lined Cloak
items.info: A cloak lined with seal fur, the Reach's only real answer to its wind. 10 Mon, sold at Shirokawa.

items.name: Furnace Sprite's Coal
items.info: A coal from the furnace sprite that burns without fuel. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Fire Sanctum, never sold.

items.name: Gale Lord's Breath-Glass
items.info: A bubble of glass holding the gale lord's last breath; it never stops moving. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Wind Sanctum, never sold.

items.name: Gale Serpent Scale
items.info: A scale the wind will not let rest, shed by the Gale Serpent in the pass. The bearer's feet are quick; their words are quicker. Found, never sold: Wind Shrine of the Pass.

items.name: Gale-Cut Claw
items.info: A sickle-curved claw that whistles when swung. Blades quenched with it cut like wind. Taken from a beaten Gale Spirit, Kamaitachi; a market pays 9 Mon.

items.name: Gambler's Dice
items.info: A pair of bone dice that roll honestly, mostly. Every den in Saikai knows the face of someone who carries them. 3 Mon, sold at Lantern Row Gambling Den.

items.name: Gashadokuro Bone Kabuto
items.info: A helmet made from the starving skeleton's own skull plate. The wearer does not tire and does not panic. The one unique piece of the depths under Old Battle Barrow, left by Barrow Gashadokuro. Found, never sold: Old Battle Barrow.

items.name: Gashadokuro's Crown Bone
items.info: The skull plate of the starving skeleton, still hungry. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Old Battle Barrow, never sold.

items.name: Ghost Station Room Key
items.info: A wooden room key from an inn that is on no map.

items.name: Ginseng Tonic
items.info: A bitter brown tonic in a sealed gourd. Drunk at rest it brings back a share of Soul spent on techniques; drunk in a fight it only makes the stomach hot. 8 Mon, sold at any apothecary or temple dispensary. Restores 12 Soul when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Gonbei's Sake-Barrel Club
items.info: A club cut from a sake barrel's iron-bound stave, still smelling of rice wine, heavier than it looks. The one unique piece of the depths under Bear Den Ridge, left by Gonbei the Sake Oni. Found, never sold: Bear Den Ridge.

items.name: Gonnojo's Returned Sword-Knot
items.info: A plain silk sword-knot, frayed, tied fresh. The bearer keeps their nerve and their weapon in the worst of a fight. Left when the Soldier Who Left His Sword had it back from a hand that knew. Found, never sold: Shrine of the Fallen Feather, Rack of the Unclaimed Swords.

items.name: Granary Key Ring
items.info: A ring of iron keys taken from tax granaries the rising has opened.

items.name: Grappling Hook and Rope
items.info: Three iron hooks and fifty feet of hemp rope. 6 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Grave Ash
items.info: A twist of paper holding grey ash that stays cold. Sealers mix it into ink that binds the restless dead. Taken from a beaten Ashfall Ghoul, Grudge Wraith, Drowned Grudge, Mud Wraith, Funayurei, Gaki, Well Horror, Grudge Swarm; a market pays 6 Mon.

items.name: Great Mask's Sun-Glaze
items.info: A shard of the great mask's glaze that holds a day's sunlight. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Daylight Watch Ridge, never sold.

items.name: Grey Clerk's Brush Case
items.info: A grey lacquer brush case bearing the Shogunate's seal, carried by its clerks.

items.name: Grey Mouth's Tooth
items.info: A grey tooth on a cord: the sorcerers answer whoever wears it.

items.name: Grey Wrist Thread
items.info: A grey silk thread tied at the wrist: the Circle's sign of recognition.

items.name: Grudge Centipede Leg
items.info: A jointed leg as long as a forearm, shed by the Grudge Centipede in the barrow. Curses obey it; the bearer itches always. Found, never sold: Old Battle Barrow.

items.name: Grudge Doll Charm
items.info: A thumb-sized straw doll in a scrap of somebody's robe. Curse-bearers carry it to give their curse a door to go through. 15 Mon, sold at Haibara Ash Market.

items.name: Grudge Well Water
items.info: A sealed flask of water drawn from a grudge well. Curses obey its bearer more readily, and the bearer's own grudges grow. Found, never sold: Grudge Well Sanctum.

items.name: Guardian Stone Chip
items.info: A chip of shrine stone that hums under the hand. Wards set on it outlast their makers. Taken from a beaten Stone Guardian; a market pays 9 Mon.

items.name: Guardian's Grey Tanto
items.info: A short blade with a grey-wrapped hilt, given to those who guard the heir.

items.name: Guild Factor's Letter of Credit
items.info: A letter of credit honoured at every guild counter in the isles.

items.name: How a Name Is Made
items.info:
A herald's primer from the Miyako post station, on how a name is made in the isles.

Renown is a counter from 0 to 100 for each character: how well the isles know you for good work. Only deeds move it, and it never falls. Every quest you finish pays some: the last part of a villain's arc pays most, a Grudge-Born or War-Born quest or the last part of any other line pays well, anything else a little. Clearing a lair pays 2. The Workshop's delivered orders and the island's restorations pay theirs too.

Titles come at thresholds, once, and are kept:
- 25: Known Blade
- 50: Name on the Road
- 75: Hero of the Isles

People treat a known name differently: doors open, villains take notice, and the honest come asking for help. A Barred or Kill on Sight name keeps its renown, but the doors infamy shuts stay shut. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: How Fighting Works
items.info:
A sword-school primer, the ink rubbed thin where students have pressed their thumbs. The first page says: read it before you fight, not after.

How a blow is decided
Every move you make is a roll of your skill, your attribute and a little luck against how hard the move is. The same move against the same foe is always rated the same, so trying it again is not a fresh chance. Luck alone never makes a critical success: that takes 70 or more, and most of it must be yours.

How a foe's blow is decided
A foe who attacks you lands it unless you defend. Say it: I parry, I guard, I step aside, I roll under it. A defence that succeeds weakens their strike; standing there and hitting back means you take it full. A failed roll of your own gives them an opening, and they take it.

Three ways to stand in a fight
- Tank (body): each point of body is +3 Health, +2% damage and 0.5% less damage taken. Armour stacks on top. You win by still standing.
- Dodge (guile): each point of guile is 1% less damage taken and 3 Slip. When a blow takes 8 or more Health in one turn, Slip gives back half of it and the hit lands as a graze, until the Slip runs out. It refills 4 a turn and fully on rest. You win by never being where the blade arrives.
- Will and spirit: will is 1% less damage taken a point and steadies the Hold; spirit fills Soul and adds 1% damage a point to everything you throw. Arts win fights; Soul pays for them.

Wounds and mending
A night's rest at an inn or a camp gives most of your Health back. Salves and dressings restore what they say. Only the healer lines (Healing Division, Kusurigi, shrine maidens, mountain ascetics, the kappa-blooded) close wounds with Soul. No single blow outside a fight's own result takes more than a third of your Health.

Gear
What drops or is found takes the quality of what it came from: Plain +1 damage or 10 armour; Fine +2 damage or 15 armour; Superior +3 damage or 20 armour; Master-made +4 damage or 30 armour; Named +5 damage or 40 armour. Only the isles' own named pieces, a lair's unique or a villain's arms, go further. Nothing raises an attribute.

Where to fight
The isles never soften a place for you. Your start sets you to its own ground's level, and for your first 30 turns what comes for you at home is the bottom of that ground. Beyond it, veterans warn you before the blood: listen, and leave if you must. Leaving can break a vow; dying sends you to the Veil, and the ferry does not take you, but something stays on the far bank. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Hundred-Duel Master's Tassel
items.info: A tassel of a hundred threads, one for each signed duel.

items.name: Hundred-Year Lacquer
items.info: A flake of lacquer from a thing that woke after a hundred years. Work made with it remembers. Taken from a beaten Tsukumogami, Empty Lantern; a market pays 12 Mon.

items.name: Hungry Mask Shard
items.info: A white fragment of a hungry dead's mask that did not dissolve. It shows the bearer what the mask wanted, and sometimes the bearer wants it too. Found, never sold: Mask Shore.

items.name: Hunter's Ear Charm
items.info: An owl feather bound to a tiny bell that does not ring. Hunters say it rings for them alone when something watches. 12 Mon, sold at Hunters' Supply Road.

items.name: Hunter's Half-Mask
items.info: A cloth-and-leather guard over mouth and nose, packed with herbs against ash, smoke and demon breath. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 5 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Hunter's Sun-Steel Tanto
items.info: A short blade forged at Hinode Hold from ore that has seen nothing but sunrise, carried beside the main weapon. It is warm in the hand and demons do not heal its cuts.

items.name: Hunter's Uniform
items.info: The Hold's dark uniform and a patterned haori, cut so the lungs can fill all the way. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 10 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Ice Cave Map
items.info: A map scratched on sealskin of the caves under the south shore.

items.name: Ice Grip Straps
items.info: Iron spikes on straw straps that tie under sandals. Good for one crossing of ice before they work loose. 3 Mon, sold at Shirokawa.

items.name: Ice Guard's Rope Belt
items.info: A thick rope belt knotted with the Vault seal, worn by the Wardens' guards.

items.name: Inner Rooms Hairpin
items.info: A gold hairpin worn by those admitted to the inner rooms of the palace.

items.name: Iron Face Guard
items.info: A samurai's iron half-face with a moustache of horsehair, made to take the cut meant for the throat. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 6 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Iron Oath Plaque
items.info: A small iron plaque stamped with an oath and worn under the armour. It turns one blow a day that should have gone deeper. 20 Mon, sold at Kurogane Armoury.

items.name: Iron Shin Guards
items.info: Lacquered iron greaves laced over leggings, the samurai's answer to a spear at the legs. 10 Mon, sold at Kurogane Armoury.

items.name: Iron War Fans
items.info: A pair of iron-ribbed fans.

items.name: Jade Prayer Beads
items.info: A string of green jade beads worn by senior monks. Counting them steadies a frightened mind. 14 Mon, sold at Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls.

items.name: Jinza's Village Register
items.info: A small charred register, every name in it still legible. The bearer remembers faces and names they have heard once, and the dead are a little readier to answer them. Left when the Headman of the Burned Village heard the names read. Found, never sold: Grey Pilgrims' Road, The Penitents' Road.

items.name: Jitte
items.info: An iron truncheon with a side hook for catching blades: the magistrate's constables carry it to take people alive. 8 Mon, sold at Miyako.

items.name: Journeyman's Hammer
items.info: A smith's hammer with the guild mark on the head.

items.name: Kagegi Captain's Scroll Case
items.info: A scroll case for contracts, sealed with the village mark.

items.name: Kagegi Cedar Plate
items.info: A small plate of black cedar carved with the shadow-tree mark, worn under the collar.

items.name: Kagegi Elite's Half-Mask
items.info: A black lacquer half-mask that only the village elite may wear.

items.name: Kagegi Runner's Cord
items.info: A dark cord for the sleeve, knotted in the village's running code.

items.name: Kama Pair
items.info: Two rice sickles sharpened past farming. Peasant fighters learned to use them when swords were forbidden. 6 Mon, sold at Hundred Fields Village.

items.name: Kanabo
items.info: An iron-studded war club as long as a man is tall. Oni carry them; the humans who can are few and terrifying. 35 Mon, sold at Kurogane Armoury.

items.name: Kappa Cucumber
items.info: A fresh cucumber with a name carved in its skin. A kappa offered one politely will usually let the giver cross its water. 1 Mon, sold at Kappa River Fords.

items.name: Kappa Plate Shard
items.info: A piece of a kappa's shell, green and wet-looking even when dry. Physicians grind it for setting bones. 10 Mon, sold at Kappa River Fords.

items.name: Karasuba's Black-Feather Yari
items.info: A crow general's spear, its haft wrapped in black feathers that never fall out, its point bright as an eye. The one unique piece of the depths under Crow Tengu Nests, left by General Karasuba. Found, never sold: Crow Tengu Nests.

items.name: Karasuba's Crown Feather
items.info: The crow general's crest feather, black edged with gold. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Crow Tengu Nests, never sold.

items.name: Karasuba's War-Plunder Mantle
items.info: A mantle of black feathers stitched with the crests of every army the crows picked clean. Nothing surprises its wearer. The one unique piece of the depths under Crow Tengu Nests after the war, left by General Karasuba. Found, never sold: Crow Tengu Nests after the war.

items.name: Katana
items.info: A curved single-edged sword.

items.name: Kawataro's River Pearl
items.info: A green pearl from a kappa's dish, always wet. Armour set with it sheds water and blows alike. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Kappa River Fords, never sold.

items.name: Kawataro's Riverstone Gauntlet
items.info: A wrestling gauntlet of river-smoothed stones laced on green cord, cold and always a little wet. It grips like a kappa. The one unique piece of the depths under Kappa River Fords, left by Kawataro. Found, never sold: Kappa River Fords.

items.name: Keeper's Sealed Scroll
items.info: A scroll sealed with grey wax, holding one of the Circle's secrets.

items.name: Kirisame Fog Lantern
items.info: A shuttered lantern the clan's captains signal with in fog.

items.name: Kirisame Poison Ring
items.info: A ring with a hollow bezel, given to the clan's poisoners.

items.name: Kirisame Rain Bell
items.info: A small bronze bell rung in the marsh to call the rain.

items.name: Kirisame Reed Charm
items.info: A knot of dried reed tied with blue thread: the marsh folk let its bearer pass.

items.name: Kodama Heartwood
items.info: A slip of wood from a fallen spirit tree, given, never cut. It makes the best shikigami frames and puppet joints. 20 Mon, sold at Kodama Grove.

items.name: Kunai and Wire
items.info: Six kunai and a coil of steel wire.

items.name: Kurogane Forge Key
items.info: A heavy key that opens the house's upper forges and armouries.

items.name: Kurogane Hatamoto Hammer
items.info: A ceremonial forge hammer carried by the house's sworn bannermen.

items.name: Kurogane Iron Crest
items.info: A round black iron crest of three interlocking rings, worn on the chest-plate: it marks a retainer of the iron house.

items.name: Kurogane Ironclad Plate
items.info: A single lacquered iron plate, stamped, given to a warrior who has earned full harness.

items.name: Kuroha's Mended Headband
items.info: A shinobi headband with its tear carefully sewn. The bearer moves unseen more easily and never loses a trail they mean to follow. Left when Kuroha had his answer. Found, never sold: Hanging Bridge Pass.

items.name: Kuroha's Torn Headband
items.info: The same headband, still torn. It still hides the bearer a little, but they wake some nights sure that someone has left them behind. Found, never sold: Hanging Bridge Pass.

items.name: Kusarigama
items.info: A sickle on a long weighted chain, the hidden villages' favourite for tangling a blade and then the throat. 28 Mon, sold at Kagegi Village.

items.name: Lacquer Resin
items.info: A pot of raw urushi sap. It makes armour, masks and puppets that last a lifetime, and a rash on careless hands. 5 Mon, sold at Polishers' Street.

items.name: Lacquered Armour
items.info: Plates of lacquered iron laced with silk cord, light enough to run in and heavy enough to matter. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 12 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Lacquered Cuirass
items.info: Iron plates lacquered black and laced with silk cord into a cuirass that sits close to the body. Armour +10. 14 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Lady's Messenger Fan
items.info: A folding fan with a hidden pocket for letters, given to the princess's messengers.

items.name: Lamp Oil Flask
items.info: Rapeseed oil for a lantern. Thrown and lit, it burns for a short while on whatever it soaks. 1 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Lay Brother's Prayer Beads
items.info: Plain wooden prayer beads given to those who keep the Order's rule.

items.name: Learning Omamori
items.info: A blue brocade amulet that students carry to the Bureau's examinations. 5 Mon, sold at Seimei.

items.name: Ledger Keeper's Seal
items.info: A cinnabar seal that authenticates guild ledgers and contracts.

items.name: Lieutenant's Armband
items.info: A white armband bearing a division's mark, worn by the Court's lieutenants.

items.name: Lieutenant's Road Map
items.info: A cloth map of the post road marked with paying inns, ambush sites and patrol hours.

items.name: Lockpick Roll
items.info: Thin steel picks and a tension bar in a leather roll, bought from someone who does not give a name. 10 Mon, sold at Lantern Row Gambling Den.

items.name: Long-Night Chain Link
items.info: A link of the thrall's cold chain that frosts the hand that holds it. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Burned Village of Kitamura, never sold.

items.name: Longbow

items.name: Lot Finder's Silver Needle
items.info: A needle that trembles near a sealed beast's host.

items.name: Lotus Councillor's Tablet
items.info: A lacquer tablet that admits its bearer to the princess's council.

items.name: Lotus Guard's Sash
items.info: A white silk sash embroidered with a lotus, worn by her guards.

items.name: Love Knot Charm

items.name: Magistrate's Jitte

items.name: Magma Glass

items.name: Mask of the Hundred Fields

items.name: Master Smith's Mark Stamp

items.info: Master-made, from an exotic material at a master's station. A strip of sutra paper written in cinnabar, wound round a hilt or a wrist before a fight. Damage +4. 40 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Master-made Cedar-Haft Spear
items.info: Master-made, from an exotic material at a master's station. A straight iron spearhead on a cedar haft, the soldier's weapon of the isles. Damage +4. 64 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.info: Master-made, from an exotic material at a master's station. Ginseng root steeped in rice wine, bitter and warming. Drunk, it eases fatigue and restores a potent amount of Soul. 32 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 22 Soul when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Mizuchi Deck Badge

items.name: Mizuchi Officer's Spyglass

items.name: Monk's Wrist Guards

items.name: Moon Hare's White Hair

items.name: Moon-Mind Charm

items.name: Mosquito Coil

items.name: Mother Urushi's Red Box

items.info: Ginseng root steeped in rice wine, bitter and warming. Drunk, it eases fatigue and restores a minor amount of Soul. 4 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 6 Soul when used (the engine adds it).

items.info: A bridle of black leather that fits no horse of the living road.

items.name: Night Steward's Guest Book
items.info: The station's guest book, with names that end mid-stroke.

items.name: Ninja-To
items.info: A short straight sword with a square guard and a scabbard that doubles as a step, a snorkel or a club. 20 Mon, sold at Kagegi Village.

items.name: Nodachi
items.info: A field sword longer than its wielder, drawn from the back and swung against horses and lines. 45 Mon, sold at Forge Guild Hall.

items.name: Noh Mask
items.info: A pale theatre mask with a face that changes with the angle; nobody can read you through it. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 6 Mon at any outfitter.

items.info: A cord dipped in Blight ash, worn by the Brotherhood's novices.

items.name: Nure-onna's Moon-Scale
items.info: One great scale from the serpent woman's coils, silver in the dark. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Heron Island, never sold.

items.name: Oaths and Ranks
items.info:
A clerk's handbook on the thirty-six factions and what an oath costs.

Swear an oath in a scene, naming the faction, before someone with the standing to accept it, and you hold that faction's first rank. You may be sworn to several factions at once, villains included. Each faction has five ranks in its own words, and each rank brings a technique and a token handed over in the scene.

Rising is earned: every faction keeps a job board at its seat. Ask an officer there for work; each job done adds merit, and 3 merit plus the level a rank asks (rank 2 from level 10, rank 3 from level 20, rank 4 from level 32, rank 5 from level 45) opens a promotion mission at the faction's seat. The 19 lawful factions deal with no party travelling with someone Barred: no oath, no job, no promotion. A job not done within 30 turns lapses without credit on your next ask, and a fresh one is given.

Sworn to two rivals and working one against the other, you build Exposure: 20 for each act, falling slowly while you lie low. At 100 you are caught: both oaths and every rank in them are lost, you are a Turncoat to both, their people refuse you, their elites hunt you, and every faction hears of it. A faction also refuses an oath from anyone travelling with its Turncoat.

Every faction also keeps a standing with your whole party: hostile, cold, neutral, friendly or honoured. Its people treat you by it. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Odachi
items.info: A great curved sword.

items.name: Officer's Black Robe
items.info: The court's black robe and white undersash, woven of something that is not quite cloth. It marks you to every other spirit.

items.name: Officer's Commission
items.info: A commission in Hidetsugu's hand, promising a post in the coming reign.

items.name: Okiyo's Cracked Comb
items.info: The same tortoiseshell comb, split down the middle. It still points to the nearest shore, but on still nights the bearer hears a woman asking a question they cannot answer. Found, never sold: Pirate Graves Reef.

items.name: Okiyo's Wedding Comb
items.info: A tortoiseshell comb, salt-white, warm to the touch. The bearer always knows which way the nearest shore lies and keeps their footing on a pitching deck. Left by the Lantern Bride when she was answered at last. Found, never sold: Pirate Graves Reef.

items.name: Old Bone
items.info: A long bone, grey and heavy with a grudge. Sealers carve it into pins that hold a curse. Taken from a beaten Gashadokuro, Soul-Forged Revenant; a market pays 5 Mon.

items.name: Old Court Ghost-Steel
items.info: A sliver of the old capital's court steel, bright and whispering. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Ruins of the Old Capital, never sold.

items.name: Old Matsu's Inn Sign
items.info: A tiny carved copy of the station's sign: the Keepers obey its bearer.

items.name: Oni Horn
items.info: A horn sawn from an oni's brow, red-black and heavy as iron. Smiths set it in club heads. Taken from a beaten Oni, Yamauba, Wanyudo; a market pays 12 Mon.

items.name: Oni Mask
items.info: A snarling red oni mask of lacquered wood that frightens the weak and steadies the wearer. Mask, worn in the head slot. Price: 5 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Onmyoji Licence Tablet
items.info: A wooden tablet licensing its bearer to practise spirit-craft in the isles.

items.name: Onmyoji Robes
items.info: Layered court robes and a tall lacquered hat; ward-script is stitched into the hems. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 8 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Ono War Axe
items.info: A long-hafted axe for timber and for doors that need breaking. Mountain monks and woodcutters swing it alike. 20 Mon, sold at Loggers' Camp.

items.name: Oshizu's Gate Token
items.info: A refugee's wooden entry token, cut for a gate that never opened, swollen with water and warm. Doors, gates and watchmen give way to the bearer a little more readily. Left when the Woman Who Knocks was let in. Found, never sold: Seimei, Behind Two Walls.

items.name: Palace Servant's Tally
items.info: A sandalwood tally that lets its bearer through the servants' gate of the palace.

items.name: Pale Spider's Lamp-Eye
items.info: A pale glowing eye from the shaft spider that shows what moves in the dark. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Revenant Shaft, never sold.

items.name: Paper Lantern
items.info: A folding paper lantern on a bamboo pole. It lights a road and tells everyone on it where you are. 2 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Paper Messenger Bird
items.info: A folded paper crane that wakes when breathed on and flies one short message to a person the sender has met. It cannot cross a sea and burns on arrival. 6 Mon, sold at Paper Familiar Workshop.

items.name: Paper Ward-Charm
items.info: A strip of blessed paper written in shrine ink, folded and worn against the body. Warding +1. 4 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Paths and Ladders
items.info:
A temple scroll on how every fighter grows.

Every art has a ladder of eight rungs, at skill 3 / 6 / 9 / 12 / 15 / 18 / 21 / 24. When an art crosses a rung you may buy that rung's ability with an ability point: the engine offers, you choose. A rung you have not taken is not yours.

Your own picks climb too: every Tradition, Element, Birthright and Path opens 4 techniques of its own as its key skill reaches 6 / 12 / 18 / 24, and some pairs of picks open a technique only the two together can learn, and a Veil Officer's blade releases at Blade 12 and takes its final shape at Blade 24. Your creator page lists them under each pick.

Each tradition branches: at level 10 you choose one of its two paths, at 30 the path's elder form arrives, and at 50 the tradition's apex, reachable from either elder form. A Named Soul-Blade has its own two stages, at 15 and 35, as its spirit wakes. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Peak Student's Wooden Sword
items.info: A wooden practice sword cut from a tree on Tengu Peak.

items.name: Pearl Earring of Saikai
items.info: A foreign pearl on a gold hook. In Saikai it says you have money; elsewhere it says you are a fool with money. 20 Mon, sold at Foreign Quay Warehouses.

items.name: Physician's Kit
items.info: Needles, silk thread, bandages, moxa and a small knife in a lacquered box. In trained hands it turns a bad wound into a scar. 12 Mon, sold at any apothecary or temple dispensary.

items.name: Pine Torch
items.info: A resin-soaked pine torch that burns for an hour. Some things in the Wood will not come near it. 1 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Plain Kimono
items.info: An ordinary kimono in an ordinary colour; in any crowd in the isles you disappear. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 6 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Plain Ring Mask
items.info: A blank paper mask: shown at the right tea house, it buys a meeting with the ring.

items.name: Plain Straw Mask
items.info: A woven straw mask with eye slits: the face every Straw Mask fights behind.

items.name: Post Rider's Bell
items.info: A small brass bell worn on the saddle by riders of the post.

items.name: Prayer Beads
items.info: Worn wooden prayer beads from the temple that raised you.

items.name: Prayer-Strip Wrappings
items.info: Plain clothes bound in layers of written prayer strips that keep a curse from leaking out. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 8 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Puppet Repair Kit
items.info: Joints, pins, lacquer and thread for mending a fighting puppet between battles. 8 Mon, sold at Polishers' Street.

items.name: Puppeteer's Thread Spool
items.info: A spool of silk thread spun with steel hair, carried on the wrist. Puppets answer it a finger faster. 12 Mon, sold at Polishers' Street.

items.name: Quay Master's Lantern
items.info: A brass harbour lantern: every pilot and porter on a guild quay answers to it.

items.name: Raider Captain's Powder Steel
items.info: A bar of foreign steel tempered with powder-smoke, harder than any isles bloom. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Old Coast Fort, never sold.

items.name: Ranked Demon's Rank Plate
items.info: A silver plate engraved with a demon's rank, hung on a cord at the throat.

items.name: Raptor Quill
items.info: A long flight feather, barred grey and black. Fletchers pay well for a true one. Taken from a beaten Sea Eagle, Ash Crow; a market pays 3 Mon.

items.name: Recruit's Sun Cord
items.info: A red-gold cord worn at the wrist by every hunter recruit.

items.name: Red-Corded Straw Mask
items.info: A straw mask bound with red cord, worn by those who have fought for the rising.

items.name: Refuge Elder's Staff
items.info: A staff of living wood that sprouts leaves in spring.

items.name: Refuge Guest's Leaf Token
items.info: A pressed leaf from the Refuge's great tree, given to accepted guests.

items.name: Relic Binder's Iron Nails
items.info: Five iron nails used to fix a curse into a thing.

items.name: Rice Ball Bundle
items.info: Three salted rice balls in a bamboo-leaf wrap, with a pickled plum in each. A day's food on the road. 1 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Road Guard's Lantern
items.info: A lantern with the road's charter mark, carried on night patrols.

items.name: Ronin's Hachimaki
items.info: A white headband with a word brushed on it, tied before a fight that matters. 1 Mon, sold at Ronin Hiring Hall.

items.name: Ronin's Travel Clothes
items.info: A weathered kimono, a grey travel cloak and a deep straw hat that has walked the whole Fifty Stations Road. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 6 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Rooted King's Amber Sap
items.info: A bead of amber sap from the king of roots, sweet and alive. A lair rarity: left by the boss of The Rooted Deep, never sold.

items.name: Safe Travel Omamori
items.info: A small brocade amulet from the Temple of Safe Voyages. Travellers swear the road is shorter with one. 5 Mon, sold at Temple of Safe Voyages.

items.name: Sagara's Captain's Whistle
items.info: A brass bosun's whistle, scorched black, its note still clear. Crews hear the bearer's orders over any storm or fire. Left when the Captain Who Lit the Fleet had confessed. Found, never sold: Mizuchi Naval Anchorage, The Burned Fleet.

items.name: Sake Oni's Ironwood Stave
items.info: A barrel stave of ironwood soaked in a century of sake. It bends and never breaks. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Bear Den Ridge, never sold.

items.name: Salt of Purification
items.info: A paper cone of shrine salt. Thrown across a threshold it keeps a hungry spirit from crossing for one night; thrown in a spirit's face it makes it recoil. 3 Mon, sold at Weeping Torii.

items.name: Seal Hunter's Harpoon Head
items.info: A slate harpoon head on a cord, worn by the Exiles' hunters.

items.name: Seal-Keeper's Ledger
items.info: A ledger of the seals in a keeper's charge and the date each was renewed.

items.name: Seal-Master's Iron Brush
items.info: An iron-handled brush whose ink does not freeze.

items.name: Sealer's Brush Charm
items.info: A tiny brush carved from a sealer's old handle and hung on a cord. Seals drawn by its wearer close a beat faster. 16 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Sealing Brush Case
items.info: A sealer's case of stiff brushes and cinnabar ink, ready to draw a seal on anything from paper to skin. 14 Mon, sold at Talisman Market.

items.name: Second Face Mask
items.info: A half-finished mask with no features yet, given to the ring's sworn agents.

items.name: Senkichi's Exam Brush
items.info: A student's writing brush that never blots. Seals and wards written with it hold firm. Left when Rakudai heard the confession at last. Found, never sold: Old Ward Stones.

items.name: Sergeant's Iron Whistle
items.info: An iron whistle that calls a band to order.

items.name: Serpent Scale
items.info: A palm of shed scale, slick and silent. It makes leggings that slide through reeds. Taken from a beaten Marsh Viper, River Serpent, Nure-onna; a market pays 6 Mon.

items.name: Shakujo Staff
items.info: A monk's staff topped with iron rings that jingle with every step. Spirits dislike the sound. 18 Mon, sold at Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls.

items.name: Shard of Sealing Stone
items.info: A chip of stone from a Vault seal, still humming. It makes seals stronger; the Vault Wardens hunt anyone who carries one. Found, never sold: The Sealing Vaults.

items.name: Shikigami Seal Slip
items.info: A long paper slip with a bound servant written into it. It makes calling paper familiars quicker and surer. 16 Mon, sold at Paper Familiar Workshop.

items.name: Shinobi Garb
items.info: Dark close-fitting layers with padded joints, a face wrap and pockets where nobody looks. Garb, worn in the body slot. Price: 10 Mon at any outfitter.

items.name: Shinobi Kit
items.info: Kunai, wire, smoke pellets, a grappling cord and seal paper in a roll that fits inside a sleeve.

items.name: Shinza's Register Page
items.info: A single page of the great register, ninety-seven duels in a neat hand and a hundredth line left clear. A blade drawn by its bearer finds the opening a little sooner. Left when the Drafted Duellist was written back. Found, never sold: Duelists' Teahouse, Teahouse of the Last Duels.

items.name: Shogunate Arrest Warrant
items.info: A sealed warrant that any garrison must honour.

items.name: Shuriken Set
items.info: Ten star-shaped throwing blades in a leather roll. They wound, distract and pin sleeves; they rarely kill. 8 Mon, sold at Hayate Ridge Village.

items.name: Signet Netsuke
items.info: A carved ivory toggle on a cord, its base cut as a merchant's seal that the guild recognises. 10 Mon, sold at Saikai.

items.name: Silk Tasuki Cord
items.info: A silk cord for tying back the sleeves before a fight or hard work. 3 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Sleeping Draught
items.info: A clear draught that tastes of nothing. Slipped into a cup it puts a drinker into deep sleep within the hour; a strong or wary drinker may notice. 7 Mon, sold at any apothecary or temple dispensary.

items.name: Small Black Lacquer Box
items.info: A palm-sized black lacquer box: slid across the right table, it buys a seat at the auction.

items.name: Small Red Lantern
items.info: A palm-sized red paper lantern: shown at a paying inn, it means you ride with the Federation.

items.name: Smith's Hammer and Tongs
items.info: A forging hammer and tongs blackened by years at a Hibana anvil. 10 Mon, sold at Hibana.

items.name: Smoke Pellets
items.info: Five clay pellets of sulphur and pine resin. Thrown down they fill a room with grey smoke for a few breaths: long enough to vanish, never long enough to fight in. 4 Mon, sold at Kagegi Village.

items.name: Smuggling Captain's Chart
items.info: A chart of the Mistmarsh channels with every patrol hour marked.

items.name: Snake-Venom Vial
items.info: Reed viper venom in a stoppered vial, sold under the counter. Coats one blade for one fight; a cut from it sickens and slows. 9 Mon, sold at Haibara Ash Market.

items.name: Soul-Taker's Chain
items.info: A short chain that a captive cannot slip.

items.name: Spirit Bell Bracelet
items.info: Tiny brass bells on a cord around the wrist. They chime when the dead come close, whether or not anyone moves. 9 Mon, sold at Tasogare.

items.name: Spirit Silk
items.info: Silk spun by spiders that live in shrines. Talismans and robes made with it hold a ward longer. 12 Mon, sold at Halls of the Nine-Tailed Lady.

items.name: Split-Toe Tabi Boots
items.info: Soft split-toe boots with a cloth sole that lets the foot feel every board before it creaks. 6 Mon, sold at Hayate Ridge Village.

items.name: Spoils of the Deep
items.info:
A ledger-keeper's notes on what comes out of the lairs, and what never comes out of anywhere else.

Every boss that goes down gives up one piece of loot, rolled on the guilds' own quality ladder: Plain 50%, Fine 28%, Superior 15%, Master-made 5.5%, Named 1.5%. A long hunt adds a hoard roll on the way out, a Bounty Head run a second roll for the head, and a Rich Hoard run leans every roll better. The ledger remembers bad luck: each roll that comes up Plain or Fine makes the next one at that lair a little better, until something good comes out. Until a lair has been cleared once, its boss never pays worse than Fine.

Each lair also hides one unique piece, a weapon or armour of its boss's own, found nowhere else and never sold. A boss kill gives it up about one time in 4; the ledger counts the misses, and by the fourth kill it always comes. Once a lair's piece has been taken, that lair pays ordinary loot only. The storyteller names the piece when it drops.

The pieces, as hunters tell them: Kappa River Fords: Kawataro's Riverstone Gauntlet; Smugglers' Caves: The Wreck-Raider's Gaff; Bear Den Ridge: Gonbei's Sake-Barrel Club; Pirate Graves Reef: The Umibozu's Tide Mantle; Old Coast Fort: The Night-Coast Cutlass; Heron Island: The Nure-onna's Scale Leggings; Earth Spider Pits: Broodmother's Silk Haori; Crow Tengu Nests: Karasuba's Black-Feather Yari; Mask Shore: The Devourer's Mask; Burned Village of Kitamura: The Carrion Thrall's Chain-Sickle; The Ash Plain: The Ash Oni's Kanabo; Old Battle Barrow: Gashadokuro Bone Kabuto; Revenant Shaft: The Tsuchigumo's Lantern Gauntlets; Bone Gully: Dairoku's Grave-Digger Spade; Ruins of the Old Capital: The Old Court Wraith-Blade; Frozen Pass of the Long Night: The Night Hunter's Fang Tanto; Frozen Battlefield: The Demon Noble's Frost Armour; Daylight Watch Ridge: The Great Mask's Faceguard; The Drowned Causeway: The Drowned Magistrate's Seal-Staff; The Rooted Deep: The Rooted King's Crown of Roots; Earth Sanctum: The Stone Warden's Bracers; Water Sanctum: The Tide Serpent's Coil Whip; Fire Sanctum: The Furnace Sprite's Ember Blade; Wind Sanctum: The Gale Lord's Cloud Sandals; Void Sanctum: The Hungry Nothing's Empty Cloak; The Dark Side: The Dark-Side Demon's Moon-Claw; The Hundredth Terrace: The Hundredth Duellist's Blade.

After the war the lairs changed hands, and so did their pieces: Kappa River Fords: The Drowned Captain's Sashimono; Smugglers' Caves: The Drowned Bosun's Pike; Bear Den Ridge: The Oni-Hunter's Iron Bow; Pirate Graves Reef: The War-Wreck Lantern Helm; Old Coast Fort: The Powder Store Gauntlets; Heron Island: The Sailor's-Face Mask; Earth Spider Pits: The Eldest's Venom Tanto; Crow Tengu Nests: Karasuba's War-Plunder Mantle; Mask Shore: The War-Fat Devourer's Jaw; Burned Village of Kitamura: The Second Thrall's Sun-Ward Coat; The Ash Plain: The Burned Villages' Tetsubo; Old Battle Barrow: The Warlord's Terms; Revenant Shaft: The New Tsuchigumo's Carapace; Bone Gully: The War Gashadokuro's Rib-Shield; Ruins of the Old Capital: The Greater Wraith's Grudge-Blade; Frozen Pass of the Long Night: The Cold Light Lantern-Staff; Frozen Battlefield: The Thawed Noble's Court Blade; Daylight Watch Ridge: The Army-Drawn Great Mask; Old Battlefield of Sekigane: The Levy General's Standing Banner; The Long Night Wall: The Tunnel-Mother's Digging Claws; Glacier Road: The Unbound Beast's Shed-Skin Coat; The Deep Forges: The Unforged Soul-Blade; Black Ferry Fortress: The Ferry-Sergeant's Mooring Pole; Sunken Well Village: The Well's Stolen Voice. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: Spring Trap
items.info: A coil of spring steel on a wooden stake that snaps shut on whatever steps into it. Set, it catches and holds a creature with minor force. 3 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Star Compass
items.info: A brass and lacquer compass with the twenty-eight lunar houses around its rim. It tells direction and the hour of the stars. 15 Mon, sold at The Old Observatory.

items.name: Station Maid's Lantern
items.info: A paper lantern whose light the dead follow.

items.name: Station Master's Register Seal
items.info: A seal for stamping a station's register.

items.name: Stone Warden's Core
items.info: A fist of living stone from the warden's chest, slow and heavy as a mountain. A lair rarity: left by the boss of Earth Sanctum, never sold.

items.name: Straw Rain Cape
items.info: A peasant's straw rain cape, better against weather than blades.

items.name: Straw Snow Boots
items.info: Tall boots of woven straw over fur. Nobody in the Reach walks far without them. 4 Mon, sold at Snowbound Trading Post.

items.name: Sun-Eating Crow Feather
items.info: A black feather that drinks the light around it, shed by the Sun-Eating Crow. Shadows deepen near it; the bearer fears noon. Found, never sold: Ash Crow Roost.

items.name: Sun-Oil Flask
items.info: Oil pressed from seeds grown on the eastern slopes and blessed at dawn. A blade wiped with it burns demons and hungry dead like sunlight for one fight. 8 Mon, sold at Hinode Fortress.

items.name: Sun-Steel Katana
items.info: A katana forged in the Sun-Steel Forge at dawn, its steel faintly warm. Demons will not stand near it; the Hold sells one only to hunters it trusts. 120 Mon, sold at Hinode Fortress.

items.name: Sun-Steel Ore
items.info: A fist of red-grey ore mined on the eastern slopes and kept from the dark. Only the Sun-Steel Forge can work it. 30 Mon, sold at Hinode Fortress.

items.name: Superior Artificer's Tool Roll
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A leather roll of awls, files, pins and fine saws for locks and mechanisms. Artifice +2. 24 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Superior Battle Sutra Strip
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A strip of sutra paper written in cinnabar, wound round a hilt or a wrist before a fight. Damage +3. 20 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Superior Cedar-Haft Spear
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A straight iron spearhead on a cedar haft, the soldier's weapon of the isles. Damage +3. 32 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Superior Clam-Shell Salve
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A grey-green salve of crushed healing herbs in beeswax, carried in a clam shell. Spread on a wound, it restores a strong amount of health. 12 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 28 Health when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Superior Lacquered Cuirass
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. Iron plates lacquered black and laced with silk cord into a cuirass that sits close to the body. Armour +20. 56 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Superior Mountain Root Tonic
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. Ginseng root steeped in rice wine, bitter and warming. Drunk, it eases fatigue and restores a strong amount of Soul. 16 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities. Restores 15 Soul when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Superior Paper Ward-Charm
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A strip of blessed paper written in shrine ink, folded and worn against the body. Warding +2. 16 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Superior Spring Trap
items.info: Superior work, made with a rare material. A coil of spring steel on a wooden stake that snaps shut on whatever steps into it. Set, it catches and holds a creature with strong force. 12 Mon. Made with the Artisan abilities.

items.name: Sworn Hunter's Sun-Steel Tsuba
items.info: A sword-guard of pale sun-steel, given at the hunter's oath.

items.name: Tadashige's Name-Tablet
items.info: A lacquered tablet bearing a retainer's name, newly restored. The bearer speaks with a retainer's authority: soldiers and servants follow their orders more readily. Left when the Unnamed Retainer was named again. Found, never sold: Ruined Summer Palace.

items.name: Takamori Banner Pole
items.info: A short command pole bearing the crane banner, given to an officer who may lead men.

items.name: Takamori Hatamoto Seal
items.info: A jade seal that stamps the regent's judgement on a dispute.

items.name: Takamori Retainer's Mon
items.info: A lacquered crane crest worn at the collar: it marks a retainer of the regent's house.

items.name: Takamori Travel Warrant
items.info: A sealed warrant on mulberry paper that every toll barrier must honour.

items.name: Talisman Case
items.info: A lacquered case of blank talisman paper, ink, brush and a star chart folded small.

items.name: Tamahagane Bloom
items.info: A rough lump of jewel steel from the Hibana furnaces, the start of every good blade. 15 Mon, sold at Forge Guild Hall.

items.name: Tanto
items.info: A straight dagger in a plain scabbard, easy to hide in a sleeve or an obi. 6 Mon, sold at any town market.

items.name: Tatsuzo's Last Die
items.info: A soldier's bone die, worn smooth, the six a little deeper than the rest. Luck runs a little straighter for the bearer, and they always know when the table is crooked. Left when the Soldier in the Black Book was paid out. Found, never sold: Lantern Row Gambling Den, Soldiers' Den.

items.name: Temple Incense Bundle
items.info: Seven sticks of mountain incense. Burned through a quiet hour of breathing it steadies the mind and returns a share of Hold to anyone carrying something sealed inside them. 4 Mon, sold at Mountain Temple of the Seven Falls. Restores 15 Hold when used (the engine adds it).

items.name: Tengu Disciple's Feather
items.info: A black tengu feather tied to the sword hilt.

items.name: Tengu Feather
items.info: A black feather as long as a forearm. Tengu do not sell them; someone always has one to sell anyway. 25 Mon, sold at Tengu Peak.

items.name: Tengu's Lost Sword-Guard
items.info: A sword-guard of black iron cut with feathers, lost by a tengu swordmaster. Tengu want it back and will test whoever has it. Found, never sold: Tengu Peak.

items.name: Tengu-Taught Master's Mask
items.info: A red long-nosed mask that marks a master taught on the peak.

items.name: Tessen Iron Fan
items.info: A folding fan with iron ribs: a courtier's ornament until someone draws a blade in the hall. 15 Mon, sold at Miyako.

items.name: Tetsuo's Hammer-Mark
items.info: A blade fragment stamped with Tetsuo's mark: the Cabal obeys its bearer.

items.name: The Admiral's Signal Fan
items.info: A war fan of whalebone and silk that the whole fleet reads from a distance.

items.name: The Army-Drawn Great Mask
items.info: A greater mask's face cut down to a helm. The army that passed the ridge left its marching song in it. The one unique piece of the depths under Daylight Watch Ridge after the war, left by the greater mask, drawn to the ridge by the army's passing. Found, never sold: Daylight Watch Ridge after the war.

items.name: The Ash Oni's Kanabo
items.info: An iron club studded with ash-black spikes, still warm at the grip from the fires it walked out of. The one unique piece of the depths under The Ash Plain, left by Ash Plain Oni. Found, never sold: The Ash Plain.

items.name: The Black Iron Lord's Ring
items.info: An iron ring from the lord's own hand: armouries open to it without question.

items.name: The Book-Keeper's Seal
items.info: The seal that records duels in the Circuit's great book.

items.name: The Burned Villages' Tetsubo
items.info: An iron war club blackened by the war's burnings, so heavy only an oni should lift it. The one unique piece of the depths under The Ash Plain after the war, left by an oni risen from the war's burned villages. Found, never sold: The Ash Plain after the war.

items.name: The Carrion Thrall's Chain-Sickle
items.info: A rusted kusarigama the Long Night's thrall dragged through the ash, its chain cold enough to burn. The one unique piece of the depths under Burned Village of Kitamura, left by Kitamura Carrion Thrall. Found, never sold: Burned Village of Kitamura.

items.name: The Cold Light Lantern-Staff
items.info: A staff topped with a cage of the cold light from the ice caves. Demons will not look at it. The one unique piece of the depths under Frozen Pass of the Long Night after the war, left by the cold light in the ice caves. Found, never sold: Frozen Pass of the Long Night after the war.

items.name: The Commander's Sunrise Banner
items.info: The Hold's sunrise banner in miniature: the whole wall obeys it.

items.name: The Commissioner's Road Map
items.info: The true map of the Fifty Stations Road, with the station that is not there.

items.name: The Council's Gold Anchor
items.info: A gold anchor badge worn by those who speak for the Guild Council.

items.name: The Courier's Bell
items.info: A post-road runner's bell that rings at last. The bearer's feet never tire on a road and they find the quickest way between two stations. Left when the Courier of Ghost Pine delivered his letter. Found, never sold: Ghost Pine Hill.

items.name: The Courier's Dented Bell
items.info: The same bell, dented and dumb. It still quickens the feet a little, but it rings by itself at every crossroads, as if asking the way. Found, never sold: Ghost Pine Hill.

items.name: The Cracked Second Hammer
items.info: The same hammer with a crack through the head. It still helps at the forge, but every tenth blow lands crooked and the bearer feels laughed at. Found, never sold: Ember Vent Fields.

items.name: The Craftsman's Primer
items.info:
A guild primer for anyone who makes things with their hands.

Buy the three Artisan abilities (one point each) and say what you want in plain words. Artisan: Design Recipe writes a recipe: a frost spear from iron spearhead and ice crystal (add at a forge to choose the station, or let the item choose it; leave out the materials and the narrator names them). Artisan: Craft makes one: Cedar-Haft Spear, at its station with the materials in hand. Artisan: Upgrade raises it one step: Fine Cedar-Haft Spear, named as it is now. The narrator names the finished piece in square brackets, and that is when the ledger records it.

Four crafts: Forging at a forge, anvil or smithy (blades, armour, tools); Medicine at an apothecary, still or kitchen (salves, tonics, poisons); Artifice at a workshop or workbench (traps, locks, tools); Warding at a shrine or writing desk (talismans).

Quality runs Base, Fine, Superior, Master-made, Named. Each step needs a higher craft skill (Fine 3, Superior 7, Master-made 12, Named 18) and a rarer material; Master-made and Named only at a master station (Forging: Forge Guild Hall, Hibana, The Workshop; Medicine: Hayate Ridge Village; Artifice: Mask-Maker's Workshop; Warding: Bureau of Yin and Yang, Crater Rim Shrine). Soul-blades, sealed beasts and their vessels can never be made at a bench. 40 recipes are known from the start: see The Isles Recipe Book.

Materials: buy them where they are sold, gather them there yourself (mine, dig, cut, pick), or take them from what you beat: every creature leaves its part (an oni its horn, a kappa a plate shard, a ghost its grave ash), and every lair's boss leaves a rarity found nowhere else. A craft uses up what it names; with nothing to hand it comes out Base, Master-made needs a lair rarity, and Named needs something rarer still. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Dark-Side Demon's Moon-Claw
items.info: A clawed gauntlet blade of moonless steel that only shows when it moves. The one unique piece of the depths under The Dark Side, left by The Dark-Side Demon. Found, never sold: The Dark Side.

items.name: The Delver's Guide
items.info:
A hunter's handbook for the lairs: the places a named foe holds, and the depths under them.

Every lair has a way down: an entrance at the lair itself. Say you go in (go in, go down, descend, enter the dark) at the entrance and you stand in the first room of its depths; the rooms run one after another to the boss's chamber at the bottom. Depths under 45 have five rooms before the boss's chamber, 45 and over six. A party that reaches the depths any other way finds itself back at the entrance.

Only the first room shows on the map when you go in. Win the fight in a room (beat it, bind it, drive it off or win it over; slipping past is not winning) and the way on to the next room opens. Rush past a room and its threats are not gone: reach the boss's chamber with any room left uncleared and the master calls them in, one wave for every room you skipped, all at once. Every descent starts fresh, rooms hidden again.

There are two ways out: back up through the first room, or the way up behind the boss's chamber.

The first time you act inside a lair a run begins. Ask for its length at the mouth or take the lair's own: Quick run: one area. The mouth, one fight or hazard, the boss as the finale, out. One loot roll; half the Tally.. Full run: every area of the lair in order, no filler between them. The boss rolls loot.. Long hunt: every area played as two or three beats, with a mid-run objective (a captive, a cache, a shrine to right). The boss rolls loot, plus a hoard roll on the way out; Tally x1.5.. Each run brings one condition with it: Night Hunt (the run falls at night: lanterns, sound and smell matter; stealth is stronger and so are ambushes); Stirred Nest (the lair expected trouble: one extra foe per fight and a wave before the boss); Bounty Head (a wanted head is inside; the boss carries a bounty and rolls a second loot roll when it falls); Veil Thin (the dead's side is close: a spirit or mask joins every second fight, and Veil Officers feel it); Collapsing Ground (the ground, ice or timber is unstable: hazards come often and techniques can set them off); Thin Numbers (few foes, each tougher and smarter than usual; fights are short and dangerous); Rival Hunters (another band is working the same lair: race them, bargain, or fight them for the hoard); Rich Hoard (the lair has been gathering for a season: loot rolls lean better this run).

A run ends three ways, and the storyteller marks each one: the boss beaten, bound or driven off (a kill is never needed: a quiet or merciful party clears a lair too), the lair left cleared, or the lair abandoned before that. A cleared lair lies quiet for about 40 turns before a fresh run; if its boss fell for good, its successor holds the deep chamber next time.

Every clear pays the Hunter's Tally, by the lair's band (10, 20, 35, 50 for a full run; a quick run half, a long hunt half again more), and the Tally names you: Lair Hunter at 100, Veteran Hunter at 300, Lair Breaker at 700, Legend of the Lairs at 1500. The Lair Ledger quest counts your first clear, your first Severe lair (30 and up) and your first Deadly one (45 and up). What the lairs pay in goods is in Spoils of the Deep. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Demon Lord's Blood Vial
items.info: A vial of the lord's own blood: drunk, it makes a demon; carried, it commands them.

items.name: The Demon Noble's Frost Armour
items.info: Black-and-white court armour of the Northern Court, rimed with frost that never melts. Blows ring off it like ice. The one unique piece of the depths under Frozen Battlefield, left by Frozen Battlefield Demon Noble. Found, never sold: Frozen Battlefield.

items.name: The Deserter's Broken Badge
items.info: A Veil officer's gate badge snapped in half: the Exiles obey its bearer.

items.name: The Devourer's Mask
items.info: A smooth white mask the tide gave up. Behind it no one can read the wearer's face, and it is never quite empty. The one unique piece of the depths under Mask Shore, left by Shore Devourer. Found, never sold: Mask Shore.

items.name: The Director's Ivory Fan
items.info: An ivory fan inscribed with the five phases: the Bureau obeys it.

items.name: The Drowned Bosun's Pike
items.info: A navy boarding pike, salt-rotted at the haft and sharp at the head, that the Regent's drowned bosun never let go of. The one unique piece of the depths under Smugglers' Caves after the war, left by the drowned bosun of the Regent's sailors. Found, never sold: Smugglers' Caves after the war.

items.name: The Drowned Captain's Sashimono
items.info: A captain's back-banner and cuirass, river-soaked, its crest washed off. Soldiers around the wearer hold their line. The one unique piece of the depths under Kappa River Fords after the war, left by the drowned soldiers' captain. Found, never sold: Kappa River Fords after the war.

items.name: The Drowned Magistrate's Seal-Staff
items.info: A magistrate's staff of office, waterlogged and heavy, its seal still able to bind a lie. The one unique piece of the depths under The Drowned Causeway, left by The Drowned Magistrate. Found, never sold: The Drowned Causeway.

items.name: The Elder's Founder Journal Page
items.info: A page of the founder's journal: every Brother obeys its bearer.

items.name: The Elder's Veiled Mask
items.info: A mask of grey silk and silver wire, worn by the Circle's masked elder.

items.name: The Eldest's Venom Tanto
items.info: A short blade grown from the eldest spider's fang, its edge always wet with something that numbs. The one unique piece of the depths under Earth Spider Pits after the war, left by the broodmother's eldest, spinning the pits anew. Found, never sold: Earth Spider Pits after the war.

items.name: The Ferry-Sergeant's Mooring Pole
items.info: A drowned ferry-sergeant's iron-shod pole. Pushed against the dead, it moves them back into line. The one unique piece of the depths under Black Ferry Fortress after the war, left by the drowned ferry-sergeant who keeps the lower docks. Found, never sold: Black Ferry Fortress after the war.

items.name: The Ferryman's Tally
items.info:
A Veil officer's tally book, the kind the ferry's clerks keep, copied out for the living who keep coming back.

When a character falls (Health to 0) they reach the Veil, and the ferryman marks them: a Veil Mark, counted on the sheet from 0 to 3. Lying on the ground for several turns is one fall, not one a turn. While a character carries fewer than 3 marks the ferry refuses them and they come back, with something left behind on the far bank. With one mark the ferryman's eyes linger; with two he says their name and warns them.

At 3 marks the ferry takes them. That character's story ends for good; the rest of the party plays on.

Marks fade with time and nothing else: every 100 turns one mark lifts from each character who carries one, the count starting with the first mark taken while nobody in the party carried any. Rest, healing, prayer and coin do not touch them. A careful fighter who dies now and then never meets the last crossing. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Fief Ledger
items.info:
A writ-holder's ledger, the first page a copy of a writ with the seal cut out.

After the war, a house or band the party stands at 20 or more with will write them a writ to one broken district (the best standing writes it; no lawful house writes one for the Barred). Claim it at the district's hub, in front of its steward. One writ is all a party gets.

Three projects open at the claim, and three more once two of the first are done. Each is a quest from the steward: pay its Mon, bring its materials (the ship's cargo counts), and do one deed. A finished project stands as a new place beside its ruin and pays every day from then on:
- Fifty Stations Road, held from Oiwake Station (Barricade Captain Tora keeps the count; Innkeeper Jinbei speaks for the people):
  - Rebuild the Burned Bridge (tier 1): 120 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Reopen the Last Inn East (tier 1): 150 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Raise the Cedar Pass Toll (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Restore the Wayside Jizo (tier 2): 80 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
  - Reopen the Porters' Lodge (tier 2): 120 Mon and two lots of rice; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of timber every 7 days for the ship
  - Light the Ghost Pine Road (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 2 Mon a day
- Ashfall Blight, held from Haibara (Keeper Hisako keeps the count; Headman Gosuke speaks for the people):
  - Dig New Wells (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Terrace the Ash Plain (tier 1): 150 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Reopen Haibara's Market (tier 1): 120 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 4 Mon a day
  - Clear the Pilgrims' Road (tier 2): 80 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
  - Quiet the Grudge Wells (tier 2): 130 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Lay the Gully's Dead (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
- Mistmarsh Coast, held from Ashiura (Headman Uozumi keeps the count; Farmer Oyone speaks for the people):
  - Dyke the Drowned Village (tier 1): 140 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day
  - Raise the Stilt Village (tier 1): 110 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Replant the Paddies (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Build a New Harbour (tier 2): 160 Mon and two lots of iron; pays 5 Mon a day and a lot of salt every 7 days for the ship
  - Retake the Coast Fort (tier 2): 130 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Relight the Dragon's Eye (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 2 Mon a day

The take piles up day by day; collect it from the steward. Unrest starts at 20 out of 100. It rises 4 for every 3 days the party stays away and 2 a day for every squatting threat still standing; it falls 10 with every finished project, and 20 once when the reeve's own trouble is settled. At 60 the take halves. At 90 the newest work is wrecked and pays nothing until the party puts it right at the steward (30 Mon), which also calms the district to 80. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Fire Master's Tongs
items.info: Iron tongs from the guild's oldest forge: every smith on the isle obeys them.

items.name: The Founder's Scale
items.info: A single scale from the founder's beast: every two-blooded of the Refuge obeys it.

items.name: The Furnace Sprite's Ember Blade
items.info: A short sword that glows like a coal in its scabbard and never quite cools; its cuts cauterise. The one unique piece of the depths under Fire Sanctum, left by The Furnace Sprite. Found, never sold: Fire Sanctum.

items.name: The Gale Lord's Cloud Sandals
items.info: Straw sandals bound with white cloud-thread. The wearer's step is lighter than it should be, and faster. The one unique piece of the depths under Wind Sanctum, left by The Gale Lord. Found, never sold: Wind Sanctum.

items.name: The Great Mask's Faceguard
items.info: A huge lacquered faceguard cut down from the great mask's own face. Spirits slide off the wearer's gaze. The one unique piece of the depths under Daylight Watch Ridge, left by Ridge Great Mask. Found, never sold: Daylight Watch Ridge.

items.name: The Great Tengu's Feather Cloak Pin
items.info: A pin of black feathers and gold: every tengu of the peak obeys it.

items.name: The Greater Wraith's Grudge-Blade
items.info: A sword that drank the war's grudges in the old palace; it hums when someone nearby hates. The one unique piece of the depths under Ruins of the Old Capital after the war, left by a greater wraith, woken by the war's grudges. Found, never sold: Ruins of the Old Capital after the war.

items.name: The High Abbot's Sutra Scroll
items.info: A sutra scroll in the founding abbot's hand, one of the seal's keys.

items.name: The Hiring Hall's Ledger Key
items.info: The key to a Saikai hiring hall's contract ledger.

items.name: The House on the Rock
items.info:
The household ledger kept at the Workshop counter, with the rules written on its first page.

Every room mended on Tomoshibi Isle opens a post, and the islander who lives there takes it first. A specialist from across the isles can take a post over and do it better; the islander stays on to help.
- Smith (The Workshop): Boatwright Hanzaemon at 6 Mon a week; Swordsmith Masamura at 12
- Steward (The Cliff House): Sora of the Lamp House at 4 Mon a week; Ledger-Girl Hosoi Fuku at 10
- Spring (The Hot Spring Cave): Sarumaru of the Spring at 3 Mon a week; Physician Ogata at 8
- Cook (The Garden Terraces): Old Goro at 3 Mon a week; Old Hisa of the Seventh Station at 8
- Drill (The Training Yard): Uncle Kesaburo at 5 Mon a week; Captain Ishimura at 12
- Priest (The Shrine on the Rock): Shrine-Keeper Akari at 3 Mon a week; Brother Ganseki at 8
- Boat (Fishers' Huts): Iwa the Net-Mender at 4 Mon a week; Hendrik van Aal at 10
- Fence (Smugglers' Cove): Captain Uosuke at 5 Mon a week; Gonroku the Broker at 12

Wages are due every 7 days, paid at the Cliff House, with 2 days' grace. Paid, each one warms by 3; each week overdue costs 8, and paying the arrears gives back 4 for every week owed. Nobody is paid or owed while away on an errand. A day's first scene with someone adds 1; every 10 days away from the island costs everyone 2. What you do in the isles reaches them too: each has things they admire and things they hate. A specialist steward keeps the books and says what is due.

At 40 or below they grumble and the post gives half. At 20 or below they leave in 3 days unless the arrears are paid or the grievance put right, and a steward at home warns you first. An islander never leaves; they go quiet and the post gives nothing. A specialist hired for wages alone can walk out, and one who reaches nothing, or leaves with wages owed, betrays you on the way. A specialist who joined through their own quest is sworn: they never fall below 70 and never betray. After the war, they serve under the names the war gave them.

Send one at a time on one errand: gather (2 days), deliver (3 days), trade (2 days), scout (4 days), spy (5 days). At most 3 away at once, and nobody hurt. Skill, loyalty and whether the errand suits them decide how it goes; a boatmaster at home makes scouting safer. Scouting and spying can go badly wrong, and someone taken must be brought home within 10 days or they are lost. Rescued, they never forget it. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Hundredth Duellist's Blade
items.info: A plain, perfect sword with a hundred notches filed into its spine, one for every duel it won on the terraces. The one unique piece of the depths under The Hundredth Terrace, left by The Hundredth Duellist. Found, never sold: The Hundredth Terrace.

items.name: The Hundredth Duellist's Whetstone
items.info: The whetstone the hundredth duellist kept; a blade sharpened on it remembers every cut. A lair rarity: left by the boss of The Hundredth Terrace, never sold.

items.name: The Hungry Nothing's Empty Cloak
items.info: A black cloak with no lining and no weight. Eyes slide off the wearer as if there were nothing there. The one unique piece of the depths under Void Sanctum, left by The Hungry Nothing. Found, never sold: Void Sanctum.

items.name: The Isles Almanac
items.info:
An almanac sold at every post station: the isles' year.

A day passes when a night does: sleep, a night's march, a skip over a night. The year runs Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter, each 10 days, early and late, 40 days in all, and every new season brings its weather.

Festivals keep their seasons and start only in them:
- Spring: The Spring Sun Rite, The Dragon Boat Race
- Summer: The Star Festival, Obon at Tasogare, The Mountain Fire Festival
- Autumn: The Whale Moon, The Foxfire Night, The First Harvest After the War
- Winter: The Snow-Bell Vigil, The First Sunrise, Demon Nights

The Workshop's orders fall due by the day, the garden's harvest is ready by the day, and a night at home turns the day over too. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Isles Recipe Book
items.info:
Every recipe the guilds teach, known to every party from the start. Use Artisan: Craft and name one (Craft to Smoke Bomb) at its station with its materials in hand.

Forging, at a forge, anvil or smithy: Cedar-Haft Spear (iron spearhead, cedar haft); Lacquered Cuirass (iron plates, lacquer, silk cord); Iron Katana (steel bar, ray-skin grip, iron guard); Oak-Haft Naginata (curved blade, oak haft); Tanto (steel bar, cord wrap); Iron-Studded Kanabo (oak club, iron studs); Iron Kabuto (iron plates, silk cord); Iron Kote (iron splints, cloth sleeve); Straw Mino (rice straw, hemp cord); Smith's Hammer (iron head, oak handle).

Medicine, at an apothecary, still or kitchen: Clam-Shell Salve (healing herb, beeswax); Mountain Root Tonic (ginseng root, rice wine); Willow-Bark Tea (willow bark, hot water); Charcoal Antidote Pill (charcoal, mugwort, honey); Blood-Stopping Powder (yarrow, rice flour); Mugwort Poultice (mugwort, clean cloth); Valerian Sleeping Draught (valerian root, rice wine); Viper Blade Poison (viper venom, camellia oil); Ginger Warming Broth (ginger, miso); Healer's Kit (bandages, needles, herb pouch).

Artifice, at a workshop or workbench: Spring Trap (spring steel, wooden stake); Artificer's Tool Roll (small tools, leather roll); Caltrop Pouch (iron spikes, cloth pouch); Smoke Bomb (saltpetre, charcoal, paper shell); Blowgun Darts (bamboo tube, thorn darts); Tripwire Bells (hemp cord, bronze bells); Flash Powder Shot (pine resin, sulphur, paper shell); Lock-Pick Set (steel wire, leather wrap); Grappling Hook (iron hook, hemp rope); Folding Bamboo Ladder (bamboo poles, hemp cord).

Warding, at a shrine or writing desk: Paper Ward-Charm (blessed paper, shrine ink); Battle Sutra Strip (sutra paper, cinnabar ink); Spirit-Binding Ofuda (blessed paper, shrine ink, a hair of the binder); Fire-Ward Charm (blessed paper, hearth ash); Thunder Strike Talisman (sutra paper, cinnabar ink, iron filings); Prayer-Bead Bracelet (wooden beads, silk cord); Exorcist's Sutra Scroll (sutra paper, sumi ink); Travel Omamori (silk pouch, blessed paper); Salt Barrier Tag (blessed paper, sea salt); Blade-Blessing Strip (sutra paper, cinnabar ink, whetstone dust). Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Lamp-House Notebook
items.info:
A notebook found in the Cliff House, in the keeper's widow's hand, and finished by whoever holds the deed now.

Tomoshibi Isle lies a morning's row west of Saikai. Widow Toki on the harbour post holds the deed and sells it for 150 Mon, or gives it to whoever finishes the island's opening work for her. Boats leave from her post; the crossing back lands at Saikai's harbour. After the war the island is still yours, and the crossing runs from post-war Saikai.

Every room is a ruin until a restoration quest mends it, and each mended room gives something:
- Soak at The Hot Spring Cave: 15 Health, 10 Soul, once in 8 turns.
- Drill at The Training Yard: 60 XP, once in 10 turns.
- Pray at The Shrine on the Rock: 15 Hold, once in 10 turns.
- Harvest at The Garden Terraces: 2 Rice Ball Bundle and 1 Ginseng Tonic, once in 3 days.
- Rest at The Cliff House: 40 Health, 20 Soul, 30 Hold, once a day.
The Workshop is a shop front once restored, and its Master's Bench is a second restoration on top of it.

The Workshop takes one order at a time at its counter: a customer, an item, a price in Mon and a day it is due. Deliver it there to be paid and to raise Shop Standing; a late order earns 50 per cent of the standing. Better orders come with standing: Back-Alley Bench at 0, Known Workshop at 100, Sought-After at 250, House of Masters at 450.

Once the Cliff House has a roof again, up to 4 people can live there: a love interest at Oath-Bound or closer, or a wanderer travelling in your party at Comrade or closer. Ask them, one at a time, wherever you are.

Stay away 40 turns or more and the island misses you: a raid on the Net Shed, a storm over the terraces, or smoke at the dead lighthouse, waiting when you row back. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Lantern Mother's Comb
items.info: A tortoiseshell comb from the Lantern Mother's hair: every band obeys it.

items.name: The Levy General's Standing Banner
items.info: A levy banner on a spear haft, torn and upright still. Soldiers who see it remember they have not run. The one unique piece of the depths under Old Battlefield of Sekigane after the war, left by the levy general who will not lie down, raised from the newest mound. Found, never sold: Old Battlefield of Sekigane after the war.

items.name: The Making of Techniques
items.info:
A school primer on making techniques of your own.

Create a technique by declaring it and saying what it does, in one of your arts. Its tier is your level in that art (Tier 1 from 3, Tier 2 from 7, Tier 3 from 12, Tier 4 from 18, Tier 5 from 24); below 3 the attempt is practice and nothing is written. Cost by tier: Tier 1 5 Soul, Tier 2 8, Tier 3 12, Tier 4 18, Tier 5 25, and 10 Hold more when it draws on a Birthright. Raise one to II and then III when your tier in its art has risen above it.

Fusions join two Elements in one move and cost 3 Soul more; fire and earth make magma, water and wind a storm, and two forces that cancel make no fusion. Joined techniques are made WITH a named ally who is present and takes part; each of you records your own half.

Awaken Art: once in a life you may reach for the technique that is yours alone. Use Awaken Art (one point, any level), name it, and it becomes your Awakened Art: once a fight, at the scale of your tier.

Training and study raise your arts: a real training scene with a teacher, a partner, a drill or a scroll lifts the art you trained. A scroll teaches up to 7, a teacher up to 12, practice beyond. Never in the middle of a fight. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Marshal's Seal of Passage
items.info: A seal that lets its bearer cross between the living and the dead and return.

items.name: The Mask-Maker's Own Mask
items.info: A mask Sorei made for you alone: it takes any face its wearer has touched.

items.name: The Matriarch's Heron Pin
items.info: A heron hairpin from the matriarch's own hair.

items.name: The Nephew's Black Fan
items.info: A black war fan: only those who act for him in the dark carry one.

items.name: The New Tsuchigumo's Carapace
items.info: Armour cut from the shaft spider's grey carapace, grown on the war's bodies, light and very hard. The one unique piece of the depths under Revenant Shaft after the war, left by the shaft's new tsuchigumo, grown on the war's bodies. Found, never sold: Revenant Shaft after the war.

items.name: The Night Hunter's Fang Tanto
items.info: A short blade made from the pack alpha's fang, white and cold, that leaves frost in the wound. The one unique piece of the depths under Frozen Pass of the Long Night, left by Pass Night Hunter. Found, never sold: Frozen Pass of the Long Night.

items.name: The Night-Coast Cutlass
items.info: A heavy foreign-made cutlass with a lantern-hook on the guard, taken from the raider who held the old fort. The one unique piece of the depths under Old Coast Fort, left by Night-Coast Raider. Found, never sold: Old Coast Fort.

items.name: The Nine-Tailed Lady's Jewel
items.info: A small round jewel that glows faintly: every fox of the Court obeys it.

items.name: The Nure-onna's Scale Leggings
items.info: Leggings sewn from shed serpent scale, slick and silent; the wearer slides through reeds without a sound. The one unique piece of the depths under Heron Island, left by Heron Island Nure-onna. Found, never sold: Heron Island.

items.name: The Old Court Wraith-Blade
items.info: A court sword of the old capital, its lacquer scabbard burned black, its steel still bright and whispering. The one unique piece of the depths under Ruins of the Old Capital, left by Old Capital Wraith. Found, never sold: Ruins of the Old Capital.

items.name: The Oni-Hunter's Iron Bow
items.info: A heavy northern bow of iron and horn, strung for killing oni, that the hunter carried down the ridge. The one unique piece of the depths under Bear Den Ridge after the war, left by the northern oni-hunter that followed Gonbei's trail. Found, never sold: Bear Den Ridge after the war.

items.name: The Post Road
items.info:
The post road's own guide, sold at every station.

Coaches run between the district towns for 12 Mon a seat, ferries across the straits for 30 Mon. Ask at the station yard to board, name where you are going, and pay. A clerk or ferryman refuses a party travelling with anyone Barred.

Every district's hub keeps a public notice board of bounties, open to anyone, sworn or not: ask the clerk for bounty work, take one, bring proof and be paid.

The isles are twelve districts on one map, from the gentle plain around Miyako to the deadly ice of Hyoga Reach. Each district's danger band covers everything in it: the further from the capital, the harder the road. Some places are on no map: you hear of them before you find them. Outfitters in every town sell garb and masks, and you start with a purse of Mon to spend. On your first day you also find a few goods your past left you: up to 3, at most 20 Mon in all, chosen from your background. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

items.name: The Powder Store Gauntlets
items.info: Scorched leather gauntlets proofed against fire, taken from what lived in the powder store. They never burn. The one unique piece of the depths under Old Coast Fort after the war, left by the thing in the powder store. Found, never sold: Old Coast Fort after the war.

items.name: The Princess's Mirror-Charm
items.info: A small bronze mirror from Ayame's own hand, given to her sworn shield.

items.name: The Regalia Keeper's Key
items.info: A silver key on a silk cord: it opens the cases of the imperial regalia.

items.name: The Regent's Crane Sword-Guard
items.info: A sword-guard cut with a flying crane, worn only by the regent's chosen blade.

items.name: The Regent's Hollyhock Seal
items.info: The regent's own seal, entrusted to the one who speaks for him.

items.name: The Rival's Letter
items.info:
A duellist's letter, copied and passed along the circuit: on the rival who grows with you.

Every tradition has one rival: a peer who tests you and is not cruel. You meet yours four times as you grow, when you reach levels 5, 15, 25, 40, each time stronger than before, and never two meetings with any rival closer together than 20 turns. The meeting comes to you wherever you are, on the isles before or after the war.
