Covers: locks, traps, mechanisms, clockwork, foreign firearms' loading and upkeep, rigging a door or a bridge. Not: smithing, which is forging, and puppets, which are puppetry. Easy: open a storehouse lock. Medium: set a snare that holds a man. Hard: pick a castle strongroom lock. Very hard: disarm a hidden village's trap corridor. Extremely hard: keep a foreign musket firing in the rain.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: artistry
skills.info:
Kagura dance, music, poetry, calligraphy, tea: the arts the courts and shrines read people by. A basic success pleases; a great success moves a lord or a spirit; a failure is a public embarrassment.

Covers: dance, music, poetry, calligraphy and tea. Not: talismans and wards, which are warding. Easy: play a tea house song. Medium: write a poem a lord keeps. Hard: dance the kagura at a festival. Very hard: move the regent's court to tears. Extremely hard: dance a spirit to rest.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: awareness
skills.info:
Noticing with the senses: the ambush in the reeds, the scratch by the lock, the thing out of place in a searched room. A basic success notices it in time; a great success notices what the others missed and why it matters; a failure is a surprise.

Covers: noticing with the senses: ambushes, small details, searching a room, the physical evidence a scene leaves. Not: feeling Soul, which is sensing, and following a trail, which is tracking. Easy: spot a pickpocket in a market. Medium: find the loose board in an inn room. Hard: see the ambush before the arrows. Very hard: notice the guard who is not a guard. Extremely hard: find what a shinobi hid in a searched room.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: beast-bond
skills.info:
Partnership with an animal or a lesser yokai: wolves, hawks, insect hives, a stubborn horse. A basic success gets the beast to do it; a great success fights as one with it; a failure is a beast that chose its own way.

Covers: partnership with animals and lesser yokai: wolves, hawks, hives, horses. Not: commanding summoned familiars, which is summoning. Easy: calm a frightened horse. Medium: send a hawk with a message. Hard: fight back to back with your wolf. Very hard: turn a hive on an army camp. Extremely hard: befriend a yokai beast in its own wood.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: blade
skills.info:
Swords, spears, naginata: anything with an edge on a haft or a hilt. A basic success lands the cut or turns one; a great success disarms, breaks a guard or ends the exchange; a failure leaves an opening a good fighter takes.

Covers: swords, spears, naginata and every edged weapon on a hilt or a haft, in a duel or a melee. Not: thrown blades and wire, which are hidden arms. Easy: cut down a bandit with a rusty spear. Medium: hold a samurai retainer to a draw. Hard: beat a house's sword master on Dawn Bridge. Very hard: cut a technique in half mid-flight. Extremely hard: win a duel against an awakened soul-blade's bearer.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: breathcraft
skills.info:
The breath hunters' forms: a breath drawn in a set way that pushes Soul through the body for one impossible movement. A basic success holds the form for a strike; a great success chains forms; a failure leaves the lungs empty at the worst moment.

Covers: breath forms that push Soul through the body for impossible movement. Not: raw Soul techniques, which are soulcraft. Easy: hold a breath form for one strike. Medium: cut faster than a samurai's draw. Hard: chain three forms in a fight. Very hard: fight a demon lord's general a full night. Extremely hard: a form no master has seen.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: command
skills.info:
Leading people in the open: rallying a broken line, giving orders a crew obeys, making an honest offer stick at a negotiation. A basic success is heard and followed; a great success turns a rout or a room; a failure is an order nobody takes.

Covers: rallying, leading troops and crews, open persuasion, negotiating terms and giving orders that are obeyed. Not: courtly manoeuvring, which is intrigue, and lies, which are deception. Easy: get a ferry crew rowing. Medium: talk a frightened village into barring its gates. Hard: rally ashigaru who are breaking. Very hard: turn a bandit band against its chief. Extremely hard: hold the Long Night Wall's line through a demon charge.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: cursecraft
skills.info:
Grudges given shape: laying, carrying, turning and feeding curses, and paying their price. A basic success lays a small curse or turns one; a great success lays a heavy one or breaks it; a failure turns it on the caster.

Covers: laying, carrying, turning, feeding and breaking curses. Not: purification and exorcism, which are warding. Easy: lay a minor ill-luck. Medium: turn a curse back on its caster. Hard: carry a curse that would kill another. Very hard: break a family curse three generations old. Extremely hard: lay a curse on a province.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: deception
skills.info:
Lies, false faces, misdirection, the feint in a fight and the forged pass at a barrier. A basic success is believed; a great success is believed and repeated; a failure is remembered.

Covers: lies, false faces, forged papers, feints and misdirection. Not: moving unseen, which is stealth. Easy: talk past an inn's bill. Medium: pass a toll barrier on forged papers. Hard: pose as a house retainer for a day. Very hard: convince a Veil Officer you are already dead. Extremely hard: deceive the regent to his face.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: divination
skills.info:
Star reading, lot casting, omens and lucky days: seeing the shape of what is coming. A basic success reads the obvious omen; a great success names the hour and the danger; a failure is a confident wrong prophecy.

Covers: star reading, lots, omens and lucky days. Not: reading people, which is intrigue. Easy: name tomorrow's weather. Medium: read an ill omen in a birth. Hard: name the day an ambush will come. Very hard: read the regent's fate in the stars. Extremely hard: see the hour a sealed beast will break.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: footwork
skills.info:
Running, climbing, leaping roof to roof, water-walking, balance on a branch: getting there. A basic success arrives; a great success arrives first and unseen; a failure is a fall.

Covers: running, climbing, leaping roof to roof, water-walking and balance. Not: staying unseen while moving, which is stealth. Easy: outrun a toll guard. Medium: cross Miyako's roofs at night. Hard: water-walk across the lake. Very hard: climb Tengu Peak's face. Extremely hard: outrun a demon across the night valleys.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: forging
skills.info:
Smithing, sharpening, repairing armour and weapons, and at the masters' anvils, folding Soul into steel. A basic success holds; a great success is better than new; a failure cracks the blade. The Artisan abilities roll it for crafting at a forge, anvil or smithy.

Covers: smithing, sharpening, repairing arms and armour, and folding Soul into steel. Not: binding a spirit into a blade, which is sealwork. Easy: sharpen a dull blade. Medium: repair a cracked helmet on the road. Hard: forge a sword a samurai would carry. Very hard: fold Soul into a blade so it wakes. Extremely hard: reforge a broken soul-blade without losing its spirit.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: hidden-arms
skills.info:
Thrown blades, needles, wire, chain-sickle, poison on an edge: the weapons a guard never sees. A basic success hits or binds; a great success disables before the target knows; a failure shows the hand.

Covers: kunai, needles, shuriken, wire, chain-sickle, blowpipe and poisoned edges. Not: swords and spears, which are blade. Easy: pin a sleeve to a post. Medium: put a needle in a guard's neck. Hard: bind a running man in wire. Very hard: hit three lanterns in the dark with one throw. Extremely hard: kill through a ward's gap without breaking it.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: horsemanship
skills.info:
Riding, mounted combat, the long gallop between post stations. A basic success stays in the saddle and arrives; a great success fights or shoots from it as if on foot; a failure is a thrown rider.

Covers: riding, mounted combat and long rides between post stations. Not: archery itself, which is archery. Easy: ride a post stage. Medium: fight from the saddle. Hard: outride a samurai patrol. Very hard: jump a toll barrier on horseback. Extremely hard: ride the Fifty Stations in five days.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: intrigue
skills.info:
Courts, clans and houses: etiquette, debts, who owes whom and who will betray whom. A basic success reads the room; a great success moves it; a failure makes an enemy who smiles.

Covers: courts, clans and houses: etiquette, debts, alliances and betrayals. Not: underworld dealings, which are streetwise. Easy: know which cup to drink first at a lord's table. Medium: learn who owes whom in a samurai house. Hard: turn a clan elder against a rival. Very hard: broker a truce between Kagegi and Hayate. Extremely hard: unseat the regent's chief retainer.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: lore
skills.info:
The isles' histories, the clans and houses, yokai and their rules, curses and how they were made. A basic success recalls what is commonly known; a great success recalls what was buried; a failure is a confident wrong answer.

Covers: histories, clans and houses, yokai and their rules, curses and how they were made. Not: the living politics of a court, which is intrigue. Easy: name a samurai house's crest. Medium: know which yokai a fox shrine serves. Hard: recall how the last war's curse wells were made. Very hard: name the beast in the Sealing Vaults by its old title. Extremely hard: recall the Veil Court's founding pact.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: medicine
skills.info:
Field medicine, herbs, poisons and antidotes, setting bones, and Soul-led healing for the five healer lines. A basic success stabilises; a great success heals beyond the herbs; a failure leaves the wound worse. The Artisan abilities roll it for crafting at an apothecary, still or kitchen.

Covers: field medicine, herbs, poisons and antidotes, setting bones and Soul-led healing for the five healer lines. Not: purifying curses, which is warding. Easy: clean and bind a cut. Medium: set a broken arm on the road. Hard: name a Kirisame poison by its smell. Very hard: keep a gutted man alive to the next station. Extremely hard: draw a curse-rot out of living flesh.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: might
skills.info:
Raw strength: lifting, carrying, breaking, forcing a door, holding a gate, dragging a cart out of the mud. A basic success moves it; a great success moves what takes three people; a failure is a pulled back or a door that holds.

Covers: lifting, breaking, carrying, forcing doors, holding a gate, raw strength feats. Not: fighting bare-handed, which is open-hand, and endurance, which is stamina. Easy: carry a wounded friend a mile. Medium: force a barred door. Hard: lift a cart off a trapped porter. Very hard: hold a castle gate against a ram. Extremely hard: move a fallen torii stone alone.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: mindwalk
skills.info:
Entering another's mind through Soul: reading surface thoughts, planting a false memory, walking a dream. A basic success hears what they think now; a great success moves or hides something in there; a failure lets them into yours.

Covers: reading, moving and hiding things in another's mind, and walking dreams. Not: sensing Soul strength and kind, which is sensing. Easy: hear a surface thought. Medium: plant a small doubt. Hard: walk a sleeping guard's dream. Very hard: hide a memory from a trained shinobi. Extremely hard: hold a mind against a clan elder's entry.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: open-hand
skills.info:
Fists, feet, throws, joint locks and the body as a weapon. A basic success lands or escapes; a great success drops, pins or throws; a failure is a grapple lost.

Covers: fists, feet, throws, holds and the body as a weapon. Not: edged weapons, which are blade. Easy: put a drunk on the floor. Medium: throw an armoured guard. Hard: break a shinobi's hold. Very hard: fight an oni barehanded and stand. Extremely hard: stop a blade-strike with bare hands.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: puppetry
skills.info:
Puppets of wood, steel and wire moved by threads of Soul: fighting dolls, decoys, the hidden blade in a lacquered arm. A basic success moves the puppet as meant; a great success makes it act like a living thing; a failure tangles the threads in the middle of the fight.

Covers: puppets of wood, steel and wire moved by Soul threads. Not: binding spirits into objects, which is sealwork. Easy: make a puppet bow to a lord. Medium: fight a guard with a puppet from cover. Hard: run two puppets in one fight. Very hard: pass a puppet off as a living person for an evening. Extremely hard: fight ten puppets at once.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: resolve
skills.info:
Holding steady: fear, pain, a curse's pull, a vow's limit, the thing inside. A basic success holds; a great success holds and steadies others; a failure gives ground.

Covers: holding steady against fear, pain, a curse's pull, a vow's limit and the thing inside. Not: physical endurance, which is stamina. Easy: keep your nerve in a haunted inn. Medium: stand your ground before an oni. Hard: refuse a curse's whisper for a night. Very hard: keep your vow with your life on the line. Extremely hard: hold your Hold at zero for one more breath.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: seafaring
skills.info:
Boats, ships, tides and weather at sea, and swimming when it goes wrong. A basic success makes the crossing; a great success makes it through a storm or a blockade; a failure is the sea's.

Covers: boats, ships, tides, sea weather and swimming. Not: the strait ferries' fares, which are the post road's. Easy: row across a harbour. Medium: sail a junk along the coast. Hard: cross Ember Strait in a gale. Very hard: run a merchant blockade. Extremely hard: cross White Strait in winter.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: sealwork
skills.info:
Hand seals, seal formulae, binding marks: Soul written into a fixed shape that holds. A basic success makes the seal; a great success makes it fast or makes it hold against something strong; a failure is a seal that breaks at the wrong moment.

Covers: hand seals, seal formulae, binding marks and the barriers they make. Not: talismans and purification, which are warding. Easy: seal a letter so only one hand opens it. Medium: make a barrier hold for a breath. Hard: bind a lesser yokai in a jar. Very hard: re-seal a cracked beast seal in a host. Extremely hard: seal a great beast into a living body.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: sensing
skills.info:
Feeling Soul: who is near, how strong, what kind, whether a mask or a beast hides behind a face, and where a presence came from. A basic success notices; a great success reads it exactly; a failure misses the thing in the room.

Covers: feeling Soul: presence, strength, kind, what hides behind a face, and the Soul a presence leaves behind (where it came from, how fresh, which way it went). Not: reading lies and motives, which is intrigue. Easy: feel someone in the next room. Medium: tell a shinobi from a farmer by their Soul. Hard: find a masked spirit in a crowd. Very hard: feel a sealed beast through its host's skin. Extremely hard: track a single Soul across a province.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: shapeshifting
skills.info:
A yokai's change of shape: a fox's illusion, an oni's horns grown, a cat's body, a tanuki's disguise. A basic success holds the shape; a great success fools those who know; a failure slips at the wrong moment.

Covers: a yokai-blooded body's change of shape and the illusions it casts. Not: disguise with clothes and paint, which is deception. Easy: grow ears or a tail at will. Medium: pass as a stranger for an hour. Hard: take a beast's shape in a fight. Very hard: fool a Veil Officer's sense. Extremely hard: hold a dragon's shape.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: soulcraft
skills.info:
Shaping raw Soul into force: a release, an elemental technique, a strike carried by the current. A basic success does what the technique says; a great success does more than it should; a failure spends the Soul and shows the shape.

Covers: shaping raw Soul into force: elemental techniques, releases, strikes carried by the current. Not: fixed seals and formulae, which are sealwork. Easy: light a lamp with a spark. Medium: throw a fist of wind across a room. Hard: hold a technique against an equal's. Very hard: break a fortress gate with one release. Extremely hard: turn a battlefield's weather.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: stamina
skills.info:
Enduring the road, the cold of the north, hunger, a long fight, a poison's slow work. A basic success endures; a great success endures and keeps others going; a failure is a collapse at the wrong time.

Covers: enduring the road, the northern cold, hunger, a long fight and a slow poison. Not: fear and curses, which are resolve. Easy: walk two post stages without rest. Medium: cross the Blight without water. Hard: fight through a night of the hunt. Very hard: survive a night on the Hyoga glacier. Extremely hard: march Fifty Stations in ten days.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: stealth
skills.info:
Moving unseen and unheard: shadows, crowds, a disguise held for a day. A basic success passes the careless; a great success passes the trained; a failure is a raised alarm.

Covers: moving unseen and unheard, shadows, crowds and a disguise held for a day. Not: lies spoken aloud, which are deception. Easy: slip past a sleepy gatekeeper. Medium: cross a samurai mansion's garden. Hard: pass Kagegi's outer checkpoint. Very hard: walk unseen through the regent's keep. Extremely hard: pass the Sealing Vaults' wardens.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: streetwise
skills.info:
Ports, gambling dens, bandit roads and black markets: finding the fence, the bounty, the boat that asks no questions. A basic success finds it; a great success finds it cheap; a failure finds you.

Covers: ports, gambling dens, bandit roads and black markets. Not: court politics, which is intrigue. Easy: find a cheap inn in Saikai. Medium: find a fence for a stolen blade. Hard: get a boat that asks no questions. Very hard: buy passage with the bandit federation. Extremely hard: find the society that trades in sealed beasts.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: summoning
skills.info:
Calling and commanding familiars: paper shikigami, contracted spirits, a bound animal from far away. A basic success calls a lesser servant; a great success calls a strong one that obeys; a failure calls one that does not.

Covers: calling and commanding paper familiars and contracted spirits. Not: animal partners, which is beast-bond. Easy: fold a paper bird that carries a note. Medium: call a shikigami to fight beside you. Hard: call two at once in a fight. Very hard: call a contracted spirit across a province. Extremely hard: bind a wild yokai into a contract mid-fight.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: tracking
skills.info:
Following a trail by sign, scent and broken twig; hunting man or beast. A basic success finds the trail; a great success finds the quarry before it knows; a failure loses it or walks into it.

Covers: following trails by sign, scent and broken ground; hunting. Not: feeling Soul, near or left behind, which is sensing. Easy: follow a cart's ruts. Medium: track a deer through the wood. Hard: track a shinobi across rooftops. Very hard: track a demon to its nest at night. Extremely hard: track one man across the Blight a week late.

Primary Attribute: Guile

skills.name: warding
skills.info:
Talismans, purification, exorcism, wards on a door or a person. A basic success keeps a lesser thing out; a great success drives a greater one back; a failure is a ward that something has now tasted. The Artisan abilities roll it for writing talismans at a shrine or writing desk.

Covers: talismans, purification, exorcism and wards on doors, places and people. Not: binding formulae, which are sealwork. Easy: ward a room for a night. Medium: drive off a hungry ghost. Hard: exorcise a possessed farmer. Very hard: hold a shrine against a masked spirit's tide. Extremely hard: purify a curse well.

Primary Attribute: Will

skills.name: wildcraft
skills.info:
Living off the land: foraging, shelter, fire, reading weather and ground, finding the way where no road runs. A basic success eats and sleeps dry; a great success leads a party through the wild faster than the road; a failure is a cold night or a wrong valley.

Covers: foraging, shelter, fire, reading weather and land, finding the way off the road. Not: hunting a quarry, which is tracking, and enduring cold, which is stamina. Easy: find water on a hillside. Medium: build a dry shelter in rain. Hard: read a typhoon a day before it lands. Very hard: lead a party through the Ayakashi Wood without a path. Extremely hard: keep a party alive a week on the Hyoga ice.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

books.name: The Soul Current
books.info:
A shrine primer on the one current every art draws on.

Soul (40 at the start, plus what your tradition and lineage add) is spent whenever a technique is really used: a flicker of sensing or a spark costs 0 to 5, a standard technique 5 to 12, a heavy technique, a release or a summoning 15 to 25, something that changes a battlefield 30 or more. A named technique carries its own price (Spends 12 Soul) and the world takes exactly that when you use it. Sensing a presence, talking about techniques or watching one costs nothing. A full rest restores all of it, a short rest about half, meditation at a shrine or a spring 10 more. Run dry and a technique you cannot pay for fails and costs 5 Health, every one you try until you rest.

Hold (100, full at the start) is the grip you keep on what lives inside you: a sealed beast, an inner mask, a curse, the spirit in a soul-blade. Only a Birthright, or a Veil Officer's blade release, spends it: 10 for drawing on its power, 25 for a full release. Ordinary techniques, wounds and fear never touch it, and only rest restores it. Without a Birthright or an unlocked blade release you never spend Hold. An officer who also carries a Named Soul-Blade has one blade and one spirit: its draws are the release, never charged twice.

When Hold falls the thing inside answers, once each fall: at 50 it starts to whisper; at 25 it bleeds through (eyes, voice, a hand that is not yours) and people notice; at 0 it takes your body for a scene, and you cannot act until the scene turns or someone brings you back. Climbing back to 90 resets it. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: Blood on the Ledger
books.info:
A ledger kept at Haibara's Vow Temple, copied for every traveller: what the isles do to a killer.

Infamy is a counter from 0 to 100, kept for each character. Every needless killing adds 15: someone who posed no threat, a surrendered, fleeing or helpless foe, a bystander, a merchant, a servant, a guard doing their job, a child, a quest-giver, anyone in a peaceful scene. It never counts self-defence or defending others, an ordered execution, a contract or bounty the story set up, an accepted duel, a battle or raid, a villain the story set up as a target, or demons, spirits, beasts and yokai. A victim already counted is not counted again.

At 25 you are Notorious: recognised, prices rise, nobles refuse you. At 50 you are Barred: no coach or ferry will carry your party while you travel with it, and lawful offices refuse you. At 75 you are Kill on Sight: guards attack on sight, and bounty hunters come for you every 30 turns. Each brand lifts again only below a lower mark (Notorious below 15, Barred below 40, Kill on Sight below 65).

The way back is penance at Haibara's Vow Temple: confess and atone there, and infamy falls by 10, at most once every 30 turns. One penance never erases one killing. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: Oaths and Ranks
books.info:
A clerk's handbook on the thirty-six factions and what an oath costs.

Swear an oath in a scene, naming the faction, before someone with the standing to accept it, and you hold that faction's first rank. You may be sworn to several factions at once, villains included. Each faction has five ranks in its own words, and each rank brings a technique and a token handed over in the scene.

Rising is earned: every faction keeps a job board at its seat. Ask an officer there for work; each job done adds merit, and 3 merit plus the level a rank asks (rank 2 from level 10, rank 3 from level 20, rank 4 from level 32, rank 5 from level 45) opens a promotion mission at the faction's seat. The 19 lawful factions deal with no party travelling with someone Barred: no oath, no job, no promotion. A job not done within 30 turns lapses without credit on your next ask, and a fresh one is given.

Sworn to two rivals and working one against the other, you build Exposure: 20 for each act, falling slowly while you lie low. At 100 you are caught: both oaths and every rank in them are lost, you are a Turncoat to both, their people refuse you, their elites hunt you, and every faction hears of it. A faction also refuses an oath from anyone travelling with its Turncoat.

Every faction also keeps a standing with your whole party: hostile, cold, neutral, friendly or honoured. Its people treat you by it. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Making of Techniques
books.info:
A school primer on making techniques of your own.

Create a technique by declaring it and saying what it does, in one of your arts. Its tier is your level in that art (Tier 1 from 3, Tier 2 from 7, Tier 3 from 12, Tier 4 from 18, Tier 5 from 24); below 3 the attempt is practice and nothing is written. Cost by tier: Tier 1 5 Soul, Tier 2 8, Tier 3 12, Tier 4 18, Tier 5 25, and 10 Hold more when it draws on a Birthright. Raise one to II and then III when your tier in its art has risen above it.

Fusions join two Elements in one move and cost 3 Soul more; fire and earth make magma, water and wind a storm, and two forces that cancel make no fusion. Joined techniques are made WITH a named ally who is present and takes part; each of you records your own half.

Awaken Art: once in a life you may reach for the technique that is yours alone. Use Awaken Art (one point, any level), name it, and it becomes your Awakened Art: once a fight, at the scale of your tier.

Training and study raise your arts: a real training scene with a teacher, a partner, a drill or a scroll lifts the art you trained. A scroll teaches up to 7, a teacher up to 12, practice beyond. Never in the middle of a fight. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: Paths and Ladders
books.info:
A temple scroll on how every fighter grows.

Every art has a ladder of eight rungs, at skill 3 / 6 / 9 / 12 / 15 / 18 / 21 / 24. When an art crosses a rung you may buy that rung's ability with an ability point: the engine offers, you choose. A rung you have not taken is not yours.

Your own picks climb too: every Tradition, Element, Birthright and Path opens 4 techniques of its own as its key skill reaches 6 / 12 / 18 / 24, and some pairs of picks open a technique only the two together can learn, and a Veil Officer's blade releases at Blade 12 and takes its final shape at Blade 24. Your creator page lists them under each pick.

Each tradition branches: at level 10 you choose one of its two paths, at 30 the path's elder form arrives, and at 50 the tradition's apex, reachable from either elder form. A Named Soul-Blade has its own two stages, at 15 and 35, as its spirit wakes. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Craftsman's Primer
books.info:
A guild primer for anyone who makes things with their hands.

Buy the three Artisan abilities (one point each) and say what you want in plain words. Artisan: Design Recipe writes a recipe: a frost spear from iron spearhead and ice crystal (add at a forge to choose the station, or let the item choose it; leave out the materials and the narrator names them). Artisan: Craft makes one: Cedar-Haft Spear, at its station with the materials in hand. Artisan: Upgrade raises it one step: Fine Cedar-Haft Spear, named as it is now. The narrator names the finished piece in square brackets, and that is when the ledger records it.

Four crafts: Forging at a forge, anvil or smithy (blades, armour, tools); Medicine at an apothecary, still or kitchen (salves, tonics, poisons); Artifice at a workshop or workbench (traps, locks, tools); Warding at a shrine or writing desk (talismans).

Quality runs Base, Fine, Superior, Master-made, Named. Each step needs a higher craft skill (Fine 3, Superior 7, Master-made 12, Named 18) and a rarer material; Master-made and Named only at a master station (Forging: Forge Guild Hall, Hibana, The Workshop; Medicine: Hayate Ridge Village; Artifice: Mask-Maker's Workshop; Warding: Bureau of Yin and Yang, Crater Rim Shrine). Soul-blades, sealed beasts and their vessels can never be made at a bench. 40 recipes are known from the start: see The Isles Recipe Book.

Materials: buy them where they are sold, gather them there yourself (mine, dig, cut, pick), or take them from what you beat: every creature leaves its part (an oni its horn, a kappa a plate shard, a ghost its grave ash), and every lair's boss leaves a rarity found nowhere else. A craft uses up what it names; with nothing to hand it comes out Base, Master-made needs a lair rarity, and Named needs something rarer still. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Isles Recipe Book
books.info:
Every recipe the guilds teach, known to every party from the start. Use Artisan: Craft and name one (Craft to Smoke Bomb) at its station with its materials in hand.

Forging, at a forge, anvil or smithy: Cedar-Haft Spear (iron spearhead, cedar haft); Lacquered Cuirass (iron plates, lacquer, silk cord); Iron Katana (steel bar, ray-skin grip, iron guard); Oak-Haft Naginata (curved blade, oak haft); Tanto (steel bar, cord wrap); Iron-Studded Kanabo (oak club, iron studs); Iron Kabuto (iron plates, silk cord); Iron Kote (iron splints, cloth sleeve); Straw Mino (rice straw, hemp cord); Smith's Hammer (iron head, oak handle).

Medicine, at an apothecary, still or kitchen: Clam-Shell Salve (healing herb, beeswax); Mountain Root Tonic (ginseng root, rice wine); Willow-Bark Tea (willow bark, hot water); Charcoal Antidote Pill (charcoal, mugwort, honey); Blood-Stopping Powder (yarrow, rice flour); Mugwort Poultice (mugwort, clean cloth); Valerian Sleeping Draught (valerian root, rice wine); Viper Blade Poison (viper venom, camellia oil); Ginger Warming Broth (ginger, miso); Healer's Kit (bandages, needles, herb pouch).

Artifice, at a workshop or workbench: Spring Trap (spring steel, wooden stake); Artificer's Tool Roll (small tools, leather roll); Caltrop Pouch (iron spikes, cloth pouch); Smoke Bomb (saltpetre, charcoal, paper shell); Blowgun Darts (bamboo tube, thorn darts); Tripwire Bells (hemp cord, bronze bells); Flash Powder Shot (pine resin, sulphur, paper shell); Lock-Pick Set (steel wire, leather wrap); Grappling Hook (iron hook, hemp rope); Folding Bamboo Ladder (bamboo poles, hemp cord).

Warding, at a shrine or writing desk: Paper Ward-Charm (blessed paper, shrine ink); Battle Sutra Strip (sutra paper, cinnabar ink); Spirit-Binding Ofuda (blessed paper, shrine ink, a hair of the binder); Fire-Ward Charm (blessed paper, hearth ash); Thunder Strike Talisman (sutra paper, cinnabar ink, iron filings); Prayer-Bead Bracelet (wooden beads, silk cord); Exorcist's Sutra Scroll (sutra paper, sumi ink); Travel Omamori (silk pouch, blessed paper); Salt Barrier Tag (blessed paper, sea salt); Blade-Blessing Strip (sutra paper, cinnabar ink, whetstone dust). Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Post Road
books.info:
The post road's own guide, sold at every station.

Coaches run between the district towns for 12 Mon a seat, ferries across the straits for 30 Mon. Ask at the station yard to board, name where you are going, and pay. A clerk or ferryman refuses a party travelling with anyone Barred.

Every district's hub keeps a public notice board of bounties, open to anyone, sworn or not: ask the clerk for bounty work, take one, bring proof and be paid.

The isles are twelve districts on one map, from the gentle plain around Miyako to the deadly ice of Hyoga Reach. Each district's danger band covers everything in it: the further from the capital, the harder the road. Some places are on no map: you hear of them before you find them. Outfitters in every town sell garb and masks, and you start with a purse of Mon to spend. On your first day you also find a few goods your past left you: up to 3, at most 20 Mon in all, chosen from your background. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Delver's Guide
books.info:
A hunter's handbook for the lairs: the places a named foe holds, and the depths under them.

Every lair has a way down: an entrance at the lair itself. Say you go in (go in, go down, descend, enter the dark) at the entrance and you stand in the first room of its depths; the rooms run one after another to the boss's chamber at the bottom. Depths under 45 have five rooms before the boss's chamber, 45 and over six. A party that reaches the depths any other way finds itself back at the entrance.

Only the first room shows on the map when you go in. Win the fight in a room (beat it, bind it, drive it off or win it over; slipping past is not winning) and the way on to the next room opens. Rush past a room and its threats are not gone: reach the boss's chamber with any room left uncleared and the master calls them in, one wave for every room you skipped, all at once. Every descent starts fresh, rooms hidden again.

There are two ways out: back up through the first room, or the way up behind the boss's chamber.

The first time you act inside a lair a run begins. Ask for its length at the mouth or take the lair's own: Quick run: one area. The mouth, one fight or hazard, the boss as the finale, out. One loot roll; half the Tally.. Full run: every area of the lair in order, no filler between them. The boss rolls loot.. Long hunt: every area played as two or three beats, with a mid-run objective (a captive, a cache, a shrine to right). The boss rolls loot, plus a hoard roll on the way out; Tally x1.5.. Each run brings one condition with it: Night Hunt (the run falls at night: lanterns, sound and smell matter; stealth is stronger and so are ambushes); Stirred Nest (the lair expected trouble: one extra foe per fight and a wave before the boss); Bounty Head (a wanted head is inside; the boss carries a bounty and rolls a second loot roll when it falls); Veil Thin (the dead's side is close: a spirit or mask joins every second fight, and Veil Officers feel it); Collapsing Ground (the ground, ice or timber is unstable: hazards come often and techniques can set them off); Thin Numbers (few foes, each tougher and smarter than usual; fights are short and dangerous); Rival Hunters (another band is working the same lair: race them, bargain, or fight them for the hoard); Rich Hoard (the lair has been gathering for a season: loot rolls lean better this run).

A run ends three ways, and the storyteller marks each one: the boss beaten, bound or driven off (a kill is never needed: a quiet or merciful party clears a lair too), the lair left cleared, or the lair abandoned before that. A cleared lair lies quiet for about 40 turns before a fresh run; if its boss fell for good, its successor holds the deep chamber next time.

Every clear pays the Hunter's Tally, by the lair's band (10, 20, 35, 50 for a full run; a quick run half, a long hunt half again more), and the Tally names you: Lair Hunter at 100, Veteran Hunter at 300, Lair Breaker at 700, Legend of the Lairs at 1500. The Lair Ledger quest counts your first clear, your first Severe lair (30 and up) and your first Deadly one (45 and up). What the lairs pay in goods is in Spoils of the Deep. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: Spoils of the Deep
books.info:
A ledger-keeper's notes on what comes out of the lairs, and what never comes out of anywhere else.

Every boss that goes down gives up one piece of loot, rolled on the guilds' own quality ladder: Plain 50%, Fine 28%, Superior 15%, Master-made 5.5%, Named 1.5%. A long hunt adds a hoard roll on the way out, a Bounty Head run a second roll for the head, and a Rich Hoard run leans every roll better. The ledger remembers bad luck: each roll that comes up Plain or Fine makes the next one at that lair a little better, until something good comes out. Until a lair has been cleared once, its boss never pays worse than Fine.

Each lair also hides one unique piece, a weapon or armour of its boss's own, found nowhere else and never sold. A boss kill gives it up about one time in 4; the ledger counts the misses, and by the fourth kill it always comes. Once a lair's piece has been taken, that lair pays ordinary loot only. The storyteller names the piece when it drops.

The pieces, as hunters tell them: Kappa River Fords: Kawataro's Riverstone Gauntlet; Smugglers' Caves: The Wreck-Raider's Gaff; Bear Den Ridge: Gonbei's Sake-Barrel Club; Pirate Graves Reef: The Umibozu's Tide Mantle; Old Coast Fort: The Night-Coast Cutlass; Heron Island: The Nure-onna's Scale Leggings; Earth Spider Pits: Broodmother's Silk Haori; Crow Tengu Nests: Karasuba's Black-Feather Yari; Mask Shore: The Devourer's Mask; Burned Village of Kitamura: The Carrion Thrall's Chain-Sickle; The Ash Plain: The Ash Oni's Kanabo; Old Battle Barrow: Gashadokuro Bone Kabuto; Revenant Shaft: The Tsuchigumo's Lantern Gauntlets; Bone Gully: Dairoku's Grave-Digger Spade; Ruins of the Old Capital: The Old Court Wraith-Blade; Frozen Pass of the Long Night: The Night Hunter's Fang Tanto; Frozen Battlefield: The Demon Noble's Frost Armour; Daylight Watch Ridge: The Great Mask's Faceguard; The Drowned Causeway: The Drowned Magistrate's Seal-Staff; The Rooted Deep: The Rooted King's Crown of Roots; Earth Sanctum: The Stone Warden's Bracers; Water Sanctum: The Tide Serpent's Coil Whip; Fire Sanctum: The Furnace Sprite's Ember Blade; Wind Sanctum: The Gale Lord's Cloud Sandals; Void Sanctum: The Hungry Nothing's Empty Cloak; The Dark Side: The Dark-Side Demon's Moon-Claw; The Hundredth Terrace: The Hundredth Duellist's Blade.

After the war the lairs changed hands, and so did their pieces: Kappa River Fords: The Drowned Captain's Sashimono; Smugglers' Caves: The Drowned Bosun's Pike; Bear Den Ridge: The Oni-Hunter's Iron Bow; Pirate Graves Reef: The War-Wreck Lantern Helm; Old Coast Fort: The Powder Store Gauntlets; Heron Island: The Sailor's-Face Mask; Earth Spider Pits: The Eldest's Venom Tanto; Crow Tengu Nests: Karasuba's War-Plunder Mantle; Mask Shore: The War-Fat Devourer's Jaw; Burned Village of Kitamura: The Second Thrall's Sun-Ward Coat; The Ash Plain: The Burned Villages' Tetsubo; Old Battle Barrow: The Warlord's Terms; Revenant Shaft: The New Tsuchigumo's Carapace; Bone Gully: The War Gashadokuro's Rib-Shield; Ruins of the Old Capital: The Greater Wraith's Grudge-Blade; Frozen Pass of the Long Night: The Cold Light Lantern-Staff; Frozen Battlefield: The Thawed Noble's Court Blade; Daylight Watch Ridge: The Army-Drawn Great Mask; Old Battlefield of Sekigane: The Levy General's Standing Banner; The Long Night Wall: The Tunnel-Mother's Digging Claws; Glacier Road: The Unbound Beast's Shed-Skin Coat; The Deep Forges: The Unforged Soul-Blade; Black Ferry Fortress: The Ferry-Sergeant's Mooring Pole; Sunken Well Village: The Well's Stolen Voice. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: How Fighting Works
books.info:
A sword-school primer, the ink rubbed thin where students have pressed their thumbs. The first page says: read it before you fight, not after.

How a blow is decided
Every move you make is a roll of your skill, your attribute and a little luck against how hard the move is. The same move against the same foe is always rated the same, so trying it again is not a fresh chance. Luck alone never makes a critical success: that takes 70 or more, and most of it must be yours.

How a foe's blow is decided
A foe who attacks you lands it unless you defend. Say it: I parry, I guard, I step aside, I roll under it. A defence that succeeds weakens their strike; standing there and hitting back means you take it full. A failed roll of your own gives them an opening, and they take it.

Three ways to stand in a fight
- Tank (body): each point of body is +3 Health, +2% damage and 0.5% less damage taken. Armour stacks on top. You win by still standing.
- Dodge (guile): each point of guile is 1% less damage taken and 3 Slip. When a blow takes 8 or more Health in one turn, Slip gives back half of it and the hit lands as a graze, until the Slip runs out. It refills 4 a turn and fully on rest. You win by never being where the blade arrives.
- Will and spirit: will is 1% less damage taken a point and steadies the Hold; spirit fills Soul and adds 1% damage a point to everything you throw. Arts win fights; Soul pays for them.

Wounds and mending
A night's rest at an inn or a camp gives most of your Health back. Salves and dressings restore what they say. Only the healer lines (Healing Division, Kusurigi, shrine maidens, mountain ascetics, the kappa-blooded) close wounds with Soul. No single blow outside a fight's own result takes more than a third of your Health.

Gear
What drops or is found takes the quality of what it came from: Plain +1 damage or 10 armour; Fine +2 damage or 15 armour; Superior +3 damage or 20 armour; Master-made +4 damage or 30 armour; Named +5 damage or 40 armour. Only the isles' own named pieces, a lair's unique or a villain's arms, go further. Nothing raises an attribute.

Where to fight
The isles never soften a place for you. Your start sets you to its own ground's level, and for your first 30 turns what comes for you at home is the bottom of that ground. Beyond it, veterans warn you before the blood: listen, and leave if you must. Leaving can break a vow; dying sends you to the Veil, and the ferry does not take you, but something stays on the far bank. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Lamp-House Notebook
books.info:
A notebook found in the Cliff House, in the keeper's widow's hand, and finished by whoever holds the deed now.

Tomoshibi Isle lies a morning's row west of Saikai. Widow Toki on the harbour post holds the deed and sells it for 150 Mon, or gives it to whoever finishes the island's opening work for her. Boats leave from her post; the crossing back lands at Saikai's harbour. After the war the island is still yours, and the crossing runs from post-war Saikai.

Every room is a ruin until a restoration quest mends it, and each mended room gives something:
- Soak at The Hot Spring Cave: 15 Health, 10 Soul, once in 8 turns.
- Drill at The Training Yard: 60 XP, once in 10 turns.
- Pray at The Shrine on the Rock: 15 Hold, once in 10 turns.
- Harvest at The Garden Terraces: 2 Rice Ball Bundle and 1 Ginseng Tonic, once in 3 days.
- Rest at The Cliff House: 40 Health, 20 Soul, 30 Hold, once a day.
The Workshop is a shop front once restored, and its Master's Bench is a second restoration on top of it.

The Workshop takes one order at a time at its counter: a customer, an item, a price in Mon and a day it is due. Deliver it there to be paid and to raise Shop Standing; a late order earns 50 per cent of the standing. Better orders come with standing: Back-Alley Bench at 0, Known Workshop at 100, Sought-After at 250, House of Masters at 450.

Once the Cliff House has a roof again, up to 4 people can live there: a love interest at Oath-Bound or closer, or a wanderer travelling in your party at Comrade or closer. Ask them, one at a time, wherever you are.

Stay away 40 turns or more and the island misses you: a raid on the Net Shed, a storm over the terraces, or smoke at the dead lighthouse, waiting when you row back. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: How a Name Is Made
books.info:
A herald's primer from the Miyako post station, on how a name is made in the isles.

Renown is a counter from 0 to 100 for each character: how well the isles know you for good work. Only deeds move it, and it never falls. Every quest you finish pays some: the last part of a villain's arc pays most, a Grudge-Born or War-Born quest or the last part of any other line pays well, anything else a little. Clearing a lair pays 2. The Workshop's delivered orders and the island's restorations pay theirs too.

Titles come at thresholds, once, and are kept:
- 25: Known Blade
- 50: Name on the Road
- 75: Hero of the Isles

People treat a known name differently: doors open, villains take notice, and the honest come asking for help. A Barred or Kill on Sight name keeps its renown, but the doors infamy shuts stay shut. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Rival's Letter
books.info:
A duellist's letter, copied and passed along the circuit: on the rival who grows with you.

Every tradition has one rival: a peer who tests you and is not cruel. You meet yours four times as you grow, when you reach levels 5, 15, 25, 40, each time stronger than before, and never two meetings with any rival closer together than 20 turns. The meeting comes to you wherever you are, on the isles before or after the war.

Each meeting is a bout. Win it, lose it, or win and spare them out of respect: the isles keep the record. The last meeting decides how it ends. Spare them then and they become a friend for good. Win without sparing and they leave the roads. Lose and they walk away the better, and tell you so.

Each of the eight traditions has its own: Shinobi, Samurai, Ronin, Veil Officer, Half-Yokai, Onmyoji, Breath Hunter, Curse-Bearer. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Isles Almanac
books.info:
An almanac sold at every post station: the isles' year.

A day passes when a night does: sleep, a night's march, a skip over a night. The year runs Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter, each 10 days, early and late, 40 days in all, and every new season brings its weather.

Festivals keep their seasons and start only in them:
- Spring: The Spring Sun Rite, The Dragon Boat Race
- Summer: The Star Festival, Obon at Tasogare, The Mountain Fire Festival
- Autumn: The Whale Moon, The Foxfire Night, The First Harvest After the War
- Winter: The Snow-Bell Vigil, The First Sunrise, Demon Nights

The Workshop's orders fall due by the day, the garden's harvest is ready by the day, and a night at home turns the day over too. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: Behind the Gates
books.info:
A master's note left at the Gate Ring for whoever comes through next.

The Otherworld lies behind the isles' oldest gates. A gate opens for a party when one member holds its kin at level 20 or higher, and then the whole party crosses. The gates and the kin they know:
- Weeping Torii: Veil Officer or Curse-Bearer
- Kodama Grove: Half-Yokai or Onmyoji
- Kitsune Shrine Road: Half-Yokai or Onmyoji
- Crater Rim Shrine: the Fire Element or Shinobi
- Salt Marsh Shrine: the Water Element or Shinobi
- Wind Shrine of the Pass: the Wind Element or Shinobi
- Sun-Rite Shrine of the Plain: the Earth Element or Shinobi
- Grey Thread Shrine: the Void Element or Shinobi
- Ascetics' Peak: Breath Hunter
- Shrine of the Fallen Feather: Samurai or Ronin

It is one country with five faces: The Far Shore, The Hidden Court, The Five Sanctums, Sun Peak, The Hundred Blades, around The Training Ground, where the masters of all eight traditions keep lodges, so no one has to split up to train. Ask a master for your tradition's training there; each tradition's trial is set in its own quarter. The Gate Ring sends you home to any gate you name.

Those who would rather start here can: one story start opens on the Training Ground already through the gates, at level 20. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: After the War
books.info:
A veteran's account, written after the war for the ones who were not there.

The war is reached by The War Road, in the Otherworld. Its keeper tells the party who the masters have finished with and who they have not when the party first stands on it. Once he has spoken, march and the party goes. The road does not come back: the isles before the war are closed behind you.

The isles after the war are a harder country, for levels 20 to 60. Places and people have changed: the war's mark is on them, some are dead, and new faces hold what the old ones lost. Who you knew, and what they thought of you, carries over. The villains' fates are what your choices made them. Eight War-Born walk the ruins, and every hub's board carries war bounties. Tomoshibi Isle is still yours, reached from post-war Saikai.

Four story starts open on the isles after the war at level 20, for those who would rather begin there. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The House on the Rock
books.info:
The household ledger kept at the Workshop counter, with the rules written on its first page.

Every room mended on Tomoshibi Isle opens a post, and the islander who lives there takes it first. A specialist from across the isles can take a post over and do it better; the islander stays on to help.
- Smith (The Workshop): Boatwright Hanzaemon at 6 Mon a week; Swordsmith Masamura at 12
- Steward (The Cliff House): Sora of the Lamp House at 4 Mon a week; Ledger-Girl Hosoi Fuku at 10
- Spring (The Hot Spring Cave): Sarumaru of the Spring at 3 Mon a week; Physician Ogata at 8
- Cook (The Garden Terraces): Old Goro at 3 Mon a week; Old Hisa of the Seventh Station at 8
- Drill (The Training Yard): Uncle Kesaburo at 5 Mon a week; Captain Ishimura at 12
- Priest (The Shrine on the Rock): Shrine-Keeper Akari at 3 Mon a week; Brother Ganseki at 8
- Boat (Fishers' Huts): Iwa the Net-Mender at 4 Mon a week; Hendrik van Aal at 10
- Fence (Smugglers' Cove): Captain Uosuke at 5 Mon a week; Gonroku the Broker at 12

Wages are due every 7 days, paid at the Cliff House, with 2 days' grace. Paid, each one warms by 3; each week overdue costs 8, and paying the arrears gives back 4 for every week owed. Nobody is paid or owed while away on an errand. A day's first scene with someone adds 1; every 10 days away from the island costs everyone 2. What you do in the isles reaches them too: each has things they admire and things they hate. A specialist steward keeps the books and says what is due.

At 40 or below they grumble and the post gives half. At 20 or below they leave in 3 days unless the arrears are paid or the grievance put right, and a steward at home warns you first. An islander never leaves; they go quiet and the post gives nothing. A specialist hired for wages alone can walk out, and one who reaches nothing, or leaves with wages owed, betrays you on the way. A specialist who joined through their own quest is sworn: they never fall below 70 and never betray. After the war, they serve under the names the war gave them.

Send one at a time on one errand: gather (2 days), deliver (3 days), trade (2 days), scout (4 days), spy (5 days). At most 3 away at once, and nobody hurt. Skill, loyalty and whether the errand suits them decide how it goes; a boatmaster at home makes scouting safer. Scouting and spying can go badly wrong, and someone taken must be brought home within 10 days or they are lost. Rescued, they never forget it. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Sea Ledger
books.info:
A salt-stained ledger from the Landing's net shed, Boatwright Hanzaemon's hull drawings in the back.

Hanzaemon builds three hulls at the Landing, one after another:
- The fishing boat: 30 hull, 2-6 hands, 2 lots of cargo, coastal lanes only, no guns
- The coaster: 60 hull, 6-16 hands, 6 lots of cargo, every lane, 1 gun
- The war junk: 100 hull, 12-30 hands, 4 lots of cargo, every lane, 3 guns
A hull is mended at The Landing, Saikai, Mizuchi Naval Anchorage for 2 Mon a point. A ship sunk at sea is a wreck: the cargo is lost, half the hands drown, and Hanzaemon rebuilds her for 40 Mon (the fishing boat), 150 Mon (the coaster), 400 Mon (the war junk).

Hands are hired at Saikai, Ashiura Fish Docks, Mizuchi Naval Anchorage for 1 Mon a head a week, paid in port on the household's terms (7 days, 2 days' grace). Their morale rises with pay, prizes and quiet crossings; at 30 or below, a quarter of them walk off at the next port.

Four officers can sign on, each through their own quest (sworn) or for wages:
- Navigator: Old Captain Hamada Gennai, 12 Mon a week; takes a day off any lane of three days or more and calms the weather
- Gunner: Mizuchi Toranosuke, 12 Mon a week; makes the broadside hit harder
- Bosun: Aoi of the Wreck, 8 Mon a week; patches hull after a fight and loses fewer hands
- Pilot: Chidori the Runner, 10 Mon a week; keeps the navy off a smuggling run and helps the ship slip a fight

Ports and what they trade (prices drift week to week; contraband sells for about 2.5 times its price where it is wanted, and raises infamy):
- The Landing: makes dried fish; wants timber, rice, iron
- Saikai: makes sake, silk; wants iron, dried fish; buys under the counter: forbidden books
- Ashiura Fish Docks: makes dried fish, salt; wants rice, timber
- Foreign Quay Warehouses: makes foreign glass; wants silk, sake; buys under the counter: forbidden books, yokai relics
- Mizuchi Naval Anchorage: makes timber; wants iron, salt, rice
- Drifting Fish Market: makes salt; wants sake, silk, foreign glass
- Black Sand Beach: makes timber; wants salt, dried fish; buys under the counter: foreign powder
- Heron Island: makes rice; wants iron, sake; buys under the counter: yokai relics
- Pirate Graves Reef: an anchorage, no market
- Hibana: makes iron; wants timber, rice, salt; buys under the counter: untaxed salt-iron, foreign powder

14 lanes join the ports, one to four days each. Every crossing makes one roll: a quiet passage, weather, a wreck to pick over, pirates, the drowned, or a navy patrol if the hold carries contraband. A fight lasts at most 3 rounds; order broadside, board, run or ward, and bribe or submit to a patrol (20 Mon and 10 more a contraband lot, or lose the contraband and pay 30 Mon). Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Fief Ledger
books.info:
A writ-holder's ledger, the first page a copy of a writ with the seal cut out.

After the war, a house or band the party stands at 20 or more with will write them a writ to one broken district (the best standing writes it; no lawful house writes one for the Barred). Claim it at the district's hub, in front of its steward. One writ is all a party gets.

Three projects open at the claim, and three more once two of the first are done. Each is a quest from the steward: pay its Mon, bring its materials (the ship's cargo counts), and do one deed. A finished project stands as a new place beside its ruin and pays every day from then on:
- Fifty Stations Road, held from Oiwake Station (Barricade Captain Tora keeps the count; Innkeeper Jinbei speaks for the people):
  - Rebuild the Burned Bridge (tier 1): 120 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Reopen the Last Inn East (tier 1): 150 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Raise the Cedar Pass Toll (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Restore the Wayside Jizo (tier 2): 80 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
  - Reopen the Porters' Lodge (tier 2): 120 Mon and two lots of rice; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of timber every 7 days for the ship
  - Light the Ghost Pine Road (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 2 Mon a day
- Ashfall Blight, held from Haibara (Keeper Hisako keeps the count; Headman Gosuke speaks for the people):
  - Dig New Wells (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Terrace the Ash Plain (tier 1): 150 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Reopen Haibara's Market (tier 1): 120 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 4 Mon a day
  - Clear the Pilgrims' Road (tier 2): 80 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
  - Quiet the Grudge Wells (tier 2): 130 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Lay the Gully's Dead (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of timber; pays 2 Mon a day
- Mistmarsh Coast, held from Ashiura (Headman Uozumi keeps the count; Farmer Oyone speaks for the people):
  - Dyke the Drowned Village (tier 1): 140 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 4 Mon a day
  - Raise the Stilt Village (tier 1): 110 Mon and two lots of timber; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Replant the Paddies (tier 1): 100 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 4 Mon a day and a lot of rice every 7 days for the ship
  - Build a New Harbour (tier 2): 160 Mon and two lots of iron; pays 5 Mon a day and a lot of salt every 7 days for the ship
  - Retake the Coast Fort (tier 2): 130 Mon and one lot of iron; pays 3 Mon a day
  - Relight the Dragon's Eye (tier 2): 90 Mon and one lot of salt; pays 2 Mon a day

The take piles up day by day; collect it from the steward. Unrest starts at 20 out of 100. It rises 4 for every 3 days the party stays away and 2 a day for every squatting threat still standing; it falls 10 with every finished project, and 20 once when the reeve's own trouble is settled. At 60 the take halves. At 90 the newest work is wrecked and pays nothing until the party puts it right at the steward (30 Mon), which also calms the district to 80. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

books.name: The Ferryman's Tally
books.info:
A Veil officer's tally book, the kind the ferry's clerks keep, copied out for the living who keep coming back.

When a character falls (Health to 0) they reach the Veil, and the ferryman marks them: a Veil Mark, counted on the sheet from 0 to 3. Lying on the ground for several turns is one fall, not one a turn. While a character carries fewer than 3 marks the ferry refuses them and they come back, with something left behind on the far bank. With one mark the ferryman's eyes linger; with two he says their name and warns them.

At 3 marks the ferry takes them. That character's story ends for good; the rest of the party plays on.

Marks fade with time and nothing else: every 100 turns one mark lifts from each character who carries one, the count starting with the first mark taken while nobody in the party carried any. Rest, healing, prayer and coin do not touch them. A careful fighter who dies now and then never meets the last crossing. Every new character carries this book; a copy costs 2 Mon at any post station or temple.

lore.name: After the Great War
lore.info: The end of the last great war is remembered in the isles less for its battles than for what came after. When the old capital burned, the surviving houses made peace because there was nothing left on the plain worth fighting over, and the court moved to a new city on the river delta, Miyako, where the throne could be guarded by walls rather than armies. The war's fortresses were pulled down and their timbers carted to the edge of the ash to build a waystation, which grew into Haibara. Onmyoji drew a great ward along the Blight's edge to hold the curse-fog in, and the old folk still praise them for it. It is said that the first post stations of the great highway were laid out in those years to carry rice to the new capital. The war's dead were too many to bury properly, and the grey pilgrims who walk out from Haibara still pray for them. Old people say the isles have spent three centuries making sure such a war never comes again, and that the coming succession is the first real test of it.

lore.name: After the War: The Bought Peace
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The succession war ended at Sekigane, and Lord Takamori Masanobu won it. He rules the isles as Regent from the blackened keep of Miyako, a capital still ringed by siege earthworks nobody can afford to clear, and he has not left the keep since. The emperor is dead: for a year the court called him sleeping, and the poem about his long sleep is quoted now as a poem about his death. His funeral has been put off three times because no house will pay for it. The Regent's soldiers stand at every bridge in the capital, and Saikai's factors walk the castle as if they owned it. People call it the bought peace, and lower their voices when they do.

lore.name: After the War: The Burned Fleet
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): House Mizuchi's navy burned at its moorings in the war's last season, ship by ship in one night. Sailors say the fire was bought; nobody has proved by whom. The admiral is believed dead. The Brine Tide flies its flags openly over the marsh coast now; Ashiura's headman pays the smugglers instead of the Kirisame, the stilt markets sell navy timber and navy swords, and the lighthouse keeper of the Dragon's Eye wrecks any ship that does not pay. The sailors' widows float lanterns over the moorings.

lore.name: After the War: The Crack in the Vaults
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): Something in the war cracked the Sealing Vaults of Hyoga Reach. A fissure has cut the Glacier Road halfway to the Vaults; seals fail at night; the beasts that were bound are not all bound any more, and hosts who carried sealed beasts are waking all over the isles. The Wardens hunt the hosts and stop everyone at Shirokawa's ice pier; the exiles argue every night over whether to help the Wardens hold the Vaults or help the hosts stay free. The Seimei Bureau has raised a second ward wall around its city since the war, and does not say why.

lore.name: After the War: The Cut Road
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The Fifty Stations Road is cut in three. The Straw Masks hold the barricade at Oiwake Station and the road behind it, because the Regent cannot afford to take it back; the Regent's posts hold the stations nearest the capital; bandits and the Red Lanterns' old bands hold the hills between. The river bridge burned, and one ferry carries the whole road across. Post riders still run the mail through the barricade, two sets of posts and a lantern hill, and the Road Commissioner governs a road whose nine stations no longer answer to him.

lore.name: After the War: The Debt Harbour
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): Saikai came through the war untouched by fire and richer than ever, and every house in the isles owes it money; people whisper that the guild lent to every side. When the fighting ended it called in the debts. Losing houses are sold lot by lot on the black decks of the drifting fish market, their swords, horses, ships and retainers' contracts included, and winning houses pay interest on their victories. A chain-boom closes the harbour at dusk. The guild's counting house is called the Seat of the Debt, and its books decide which claimant the guild will back next. Soldiers' debts are bought cheap in the dens and collected from their widows.

lore.name: After the War: The Demon Peace
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The hunters of Hinode Hold were away south in the war's last season, and the Northern Court's demons came through the Long Night Wall the week they left; the hunters do not say aloud who sent them. The wall is broken, the north gate is rubble, the burned villages of the valleys are empty, and the Northern Court's nobles have gone south into the Daylight Valleys. The Hold holds its fortress with children in cut-down uniforms, and the dawn bell rings twice: once for the hunt riding out, once for the count of those who did not come back. A truce with the Long Night is spoken of, and a demon envoy has come south under a white banner; most hunters would sooner kill the envoy than talk.

lore.name: After the War: The Grudge Line
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The grey of the Ashfall Blight has spread north past the old road since the war; the curse-hunters say every grudge the war left went into the wells. A ring of new shrines a day's walk north of Haibara, the Grudge Line, holds it back, kept by old keepers who sweep ash off the ward stones. Soldiers of every side walk the penitents' road to the Vow Temple in grey over their armour to atone for what they did in the war, and the sick among them grow sicker. The curse-hunters of the Brotherhood cannot break the war's curses as fast as they appear, and the sorcerers bottle grudges faster than ever. The war also made its own oni: see the War-Born.

lore.name: After the War: The Long Procession
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The Veil Court cannot ferry the war's dead fast enough. They queue at the great pale torii of Tasogare in a line that reaches the sea, they wait in the city's streets under black banners, and some of them refuse to go and walk toward the moorland graves instead. Living soldiers have been deputised to help ferry them; the deputies' hands glow, and some of them come back from the crossing quieter than they went.

lore.name: After the War: The Soul-Blades
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): House Kurogane came out of the war the richest house in the isles: it sold soul-forged blades to every side, and every side paid. Warship banners fly beside its crest. The blades whisper now, in their racks and on the polishers' benches, and one forge on Hibana's Forge Row burns blue. House agents and foreign captains bid for soul-blades openly at the hot spring inn, and a few people in the isles buy them only to break them, so the souls in them can go.

lore.name: After the War: The Straw Masks
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The villages of the Miyako plain rose in the war's last year behind a woman in a straw mask, Ine of the Hundred Fields. The rising broke the rice levies, burned half the capital's markets with fire-arrows, held the Oiwake barricade and drove the Red Lanterns out of their camp. The Straw Masks hold the post road now and call their leader the Lady of the Straw Masks; the Regent calls them bandits and leaves them alone. The dikes of the plain broke in the war and the Hundred Fields flooded, and the first harvest after it was thin.

lore.name: Asahi Gate, the Hunters' Town
lore.info: Asahi Gate is the snowbound town under Hinode Fortress, and the isles know it as the place the demon hunters ride out from at dawn. Nearly everyone in it works for the hunters: smiths who shoe their horses and mend their gear, cooks for the mess halls, stable hands, furriers, physicians, carters on the supply road, and the families of hunters who never returned. Asahi people are blunt and hardy, short with southern complaints about the cold, and they drink to their dead rather than weep for them, because every fallen hunter's name is cut into the mess beams. Their great morning is the First Sunrise, when hunters raise sun-steel at the gate and the orphans who lived through the winter receive their first blades. A visitor must stand still and silent when the dawn bell rings for a hunt riding out, must never touch a hunter's sun-steel without leave, and must never call the Demon Nights a northern tale. Southerners who come to gawk at the hunters are tolerated; those who come to carry supplies up the snow road are welcomed at every table.

lore.name: Ash on the Wind
lore.info: Ash on the wind is the weather of the Ashfall Blight, where the soil is grey ash and every gust lifts it. On a still day the ash lies quiet in drifts like old snow; when the wind rises it comes up in thin stinging veils, and in a strong blow the whole plain goes grey and the sun turns into a pale coin. Footprints fill within minutes, so travellers out of Haibara mark their way with piled stones, and anyone caught in the open turns their back to the wind and waits. The people of Sunken Well Village wear cloth masks against it all day, and travellers are advised to do the same, with a wet cloth when the wind is high. The ash gets into water, rice and eyes, and coughs that start on the Ash Plain can last a season. Saikai's harbour folk know an easterly that smells of ash is coming off the Blight, and they cover their drying fish.

lore.name: Ashiura, the Stilt Town
lore.info: Ashiura is the largest stilt town of the Mistmarsh Coast, and to the rest of the isles it is the place where the road ends and the boats begin. Its trades are fish, reeds, boatbuilding and ferrying, along with the salt, sake and foreign silver that move through the channels without troubling the tax offices. Navy sailors, smugglers and marsh folk all buy at the same stalls, and Ashiura people have learned to be friendly to all three and loyal to none. Elsewhere they are called close-mouthed, superstitious and in debt to somebody, which is mostly true. The coast's great day is the Dragon Boat Race through the reed channels, which ends at the Ashiura landing with the whole town betting on the navy, the smugglers or the rain clan. A visitor should hire a local boatman rather than pole into the channels alone, should leave a small offering at the Drowned Shrine before going out on the water, and should never ask a stranger what is in a cargo. It is also unwise to boast of friendship with House Mizuchi in one tavern and with Brine Tide captains in the next, since both hear everything in the end.

lore.name: Bakeneko: Beasts That Were Beasts
lore.info: Bakeneko are yokai born when a cat grows old and strange and decides to become more than a cat. They walk on hind legs and speak in human tongues and develop appetites that cats never had. A bakeneko can be small as a housecat or large as a tiger, and they are universally unpredictable. Some are kind to humans who treat them well; others hunt humans for amusement. The great bakeneko are beings of deep magic whose age can be read in their eyes; the oldest ones remember when the isles were still being born. They are not in any court and do not make oaths; a bakeneko's word is worth nothing but its pride and appetite. Those few humans who have befriended a bakeneko say it is like befriending a force of nature: beautiful, dangerous, and never quite trustworthy.

lore.name: Bathhouses
lore.info: Bathhouses stand in every town and city, some simple and some luxurious with hot springs. A public bath costs a few copper coins and is divided by gender; commoners, samurai and nobles share the same water once it is drawn. Washing before entering is the rule; scrubbing in the bath itself is not permitted. A bathhouse is a place to relax and gossip; business deals are discussed in baths, secrets are shared quietly by the hot water, and a bathhouse frequented by samurai is better information than a tavern. Some bathhouses have private rooms for the wealthy or those who wish privacy.

lore.name: Bathing Etiquette
lore.info: Bathing etiquette in the isles is learned young and noticed when it is broken. A bather undresses in the outer room, folds their clothes into a basket, scrubs and rinses on a low stool with a bucket, and only then lowers themselves into the hot water, slowly and without splashing. Towels stay out of the water, often folded on the head, and soap stays out of it entirely. Nobody stares at another bather's scars, nobody swims, and voices stay low under the beams. Hot springs have their own customs. At Snow Monkey Springs travellers tie their packs and food shut before getting in, and at the Hot Spring Inn near Hibana swordsmen soak with their blades wrapped and within reach, which everyone politely ignores. Attendants bring hot water, towels and warm sake to those who pay for them. At an inn guests bathe in order of rank, and to be offered the first bath is an honour. What is said in the water is supposed to stay there, which is why everyone in it is listening.

lore.name: Beasts of Farm and Road
lore.info: The working beasts of the isles are oxen, horses and the plain's few sheep and dogs. Oxen pull ploughs in the paddies and haul the creaking supply carts up the Hunters' Supply Road to Hinode Hold. Horses belong mostly to samurai, post riders and the horse houses; a farmer who owns one is a rich farmer. Shepherds graze sheep on the moors beyond the Lake of Stars, and the hill farms keep goats. Village dogs bark at strangers and are fed on scraps. Cats are kept to hunt rats in the granaries, and every household knows that a cat should be treated kindly, though nobody says why aloud. Chickens scratch in every yard and are kept for eggs more than meat. On the post road, porters and palanquin bearers do the work that beasts do elsewhere, and pack horses are hired from station to station like the bearers themselves.

lore.name: Bestiary of the Isles
lore.info: The isles are crowded with things that are not human. Yokai live in every wood and river: kappa in the shallows, tengu on the peaks, foxes in borrowed faces, and older, stranger things that remember wars a thousand years gone. The hungry dead who refuse the Veil Court's ferry grow white masks over their faces and hunt the living for their souls; only void, or an officer's blade, truly tears them. In the north the demons of the Northern Court come south on the long winter nights, and they die hardest to anything but sunlight and sun-steel. The curse wells of Ashfall make things of grudge and ash that curses cannot touch. Spirits of fire, wind, earth, water and void obey the old bane cycle: water drowns fire, fire eats wind, wind wears earth, earth dams water, and sunlight thins the void. And beneath it all lie the nine great beasts, their bodies bound in seals, most of them in the Sealing Vaults of Hyoga; where the others lie, few know. The power that would not stay bound was sealed into living hosts, who walk the isles carrying it and are hunted for it.

lore.name: Birds, Fish and Wild Things
lore.info: The wild things of the isles change with every district. Herons nest in their thousands on Heron Island in the Mistmarsh, and frogs sing in every flooded paddy until something walks past and they fall silent in a wave. Gulls follow the fishing boats and quarrel over the gutting tubs on every coast. The Lake of Stars is rich in fish, and carp rise in the ponds of the rich in Miyako. In summer cicadas shrill along the post road from dawn to dusk. In the north, seals are hunted from the Exiles' Shore Towns, and under the whale moon the great whales pass the Hyoga coast and every exile who can row goes out after them. Crows follow death everywhere, and in the Ashfall Blight the grey ash crows follow it more closely than anywhere else. Foxes and tanuki are seen in every wood, and country folk are polite to both, just in case.

lore.name: Black Bears of the Mountains
lore.info: Black bears are the huge, short-tempered bears of the mountain forests of the Kurosugi Range, Hinode Hold and the Ayakashi Wood. A bear avoids people until someone comes between it and its food or its cubs, and then it charges. Hunters go to Bear Den Ridge for skins and never in spring, when the mothers come out of the dens hungry with their young. The ridge is known for a huge she-bear with a white crescent on her chest, restless and ill-tempered, who prowls the slope below the Great Den. Woodcutters hang bells from their belts so a bear hears them coming and moves off. If one stands up on the path, the advice is to speak low, keep facing it and back away slowly, which works more often than fighting. Bear gall is sold as medicine in every market, and the hunters who fetch it are respected and rarely old.

lore.name: Bone Gully and the Old Capital's Dead
lore.info: Bone Gully is a gully in the Ashfall Blight where, the tale says, the old capital's dead were thrown when there were too many to burn or bury. So many bones lie in it that the stream runs milky white and leaves a pale crust on the stones. The people of Haibara say that on dark nights the bones gather themselves into a skeleton taller than the gully walls, which walks the rim looking for the rest of its dead. Few claim to have seen it, but nobody in Haibara will camp within sight of the gully, and pilgrims on the Grey Pilgrims' Road turn and bow toward it as they pass. Robbers dig the bone heaps for teeth and grave goods to sell in Haibara, and even the curse-bearers think it the lowest trade in the Blight. Water from the White Stream is never drunk, not even by the desperate, and a pot that has held it is broken afterwards.

lore.name: Bounties
lore.info: When a serious crime is committed, the magistrate issues a bounty through the Shogunate offices, posting a reward in Mon for the criminal's capture alive or proof of death. Bounties are public knowledge passed along the post road, offered in taverns and inns, and bounty hunters make their living claiming them. A thief's bounty buys a few nights at an inn; a murderer's or a bandit chief's buys a year of them. The bounty is paid only when the criminal is confirmed by the magistrate or the body is witnessed by at least two town officials.

lore.name: Breath Forms: The Techniques of Hinode Hold
lore.info: The breath hunters of Hinode Hold teach eight breaths, each drawing on a different element and a different part of the breath. Ember Breath burns with heat, Tide Breath flows like water, Gale Breath tears like wind, Stone Breath is slow and steady as earth itself, Thunder Breath strikes like lightning, Mist Breath hides and poisons, Blossom Breath charms and confuses, Beast Breath is raw and primal. Each form requires mastery of the breath itself before the technique can be learned. A hunter with perfect breath can string the forms together into combinations and sequences that defeat enemies who rely on any single strength.
