Their faces fade and white masks grow over their eyes and mouths as their need for souls grows. The masks are not worn; they are the hungry dead themselves, hardened into a single shape. A masked spirit will hunt the living and eat their souls, growing older and stranger with each one. Only void can truly tear them, or the sharp edges of a Veil Officer's soul-blade, or sunlight if they are young enough. The oldest masked spirits are almost gods of hunger, and the Veil Court fears them as much as the living do. In the thickest Veil times, the masked come hunting in packs, drawn to places where souls are strong or recently freed. The living learn to keep themselves small and hidden when the hungry dead walk.

lore.name: The Morning Mist of the Isles
lore.info: The morning mist gives the Asagiri Isles their name, and most mornings it lies over the crescent from coast to coast. It rises off the rivers and paddies before dawn, fills the valleys of the Kurosugi Range, sits on the reed channels of the Mistmarsh Coast for days at a time, and thickens in the Ayakashi Wood every autumn until the paths are lost. On the plain it usually burns off by the hour of the snake; in the marsh and the mountain valleys it may not lift at all. Travellers wait at the post stations for it to clear rather than walk blind, boatmen ring bells or beat drums to warn each other, and farmers read the day's weather from how fast it thins. Folk say yokai walk most freely in the mist, and that a voice calling your name from inside it should be answered only after you have seen the face. The Sea of Fog below Veilgate is something else entirely, and nobody mistakes the one for the other twice.

lore.name: The Mountain Temple Order
lore.info: The Mountain Temple Order is the oldest religious order of the isles: mountain ascetics, exorcist monks and shrine keepers who walk the high paths of the Kurosugi Range, fast under waterfalls and drive out possessing spirits with staff, sutra and fire. The Order shelters travellers, keeps the mountain roads and takes in anyone who asks, sworn killers included, if they shave their heads and keep the rule. The people trust the monks more than any lord. The Bureau thinks them superstitious; the monks think the Bureau sells what should be given.

lore.name: The Nails of the Weeping Cedar
lore.info: The Weeping Cedar is a vast old cedar at an abandoned shrine in the Ashfall Blight, and it is the most feared cursing place in the isles. The tale every child in Haibara knows is that a person with a grudge goes there alone at the hour of the ox, nails a straw doll of the enemy to the bark with an iron hammer, and returns for seven nights without being seen. If anyone sees them at it, the curse turns back on its maker. The trunk now bristles with dolls and nails, the oldest rusted black and a few still bright, and the hammer left on the altar of the empty shrine is said to belong to nobody. Sap that seeps from the nail holes gives the tree its name. No priest tends the place, and decent folk will not go near it even by day. The curse-hunters say a doll nailed there in true hatred never quite stops working, and they treat a fresh nail in the bark as news worth following.

lore.name: The Nephew's Banner
lore.info: The Nephew's Banner is the faction behind Lord Takamori Hidetsugu, the regent's nephew, who claims that the throne should pass to the house that has carried it for three generations. His banner gathers young Takamori swords, ambitious magistrates and lords who would rather back the strong than the rightful. Hidetsugu is a brilliant duelist and a better speaker, and he means to win the Capital Tournament himself. His followers call him the only claimant who could hold the isles together; his enemies call him the regent's ambition with a younger face.

lore.name: The Northern Court
lore.info: The Northern Court is the court of demons in the frozen north, ruled by a demon lord no living person has seen. Its demons are humans who drank the lord's blood and became something that cannot die except by sunlight or sun-steel, and they raid the south on the long winter nights the isles call the Demon Nights. The Court keeps ranks, titles and etiquette as old as the empire's. To the north it is terror itself. To a few desperate people in the south it is the only power that offers eternal life to anyone who asks.

lore.name: The Nue and Its Black Clouds
lore.info: The nue is the bird-voiced chimera that folk on the Miyako Plain fear more than any bandit: a monkey's face, a tiger's legs and a serpent for a tail, wrapped in a black cloud that brings sickness wherever it settles. It is heard before it is seen, a thin mournful whistle on a still night, and villagers who hear it close their shutters and keep the children from the window. Old courtiers say a nue comes to roost over palaces and great houses when a reign has gone wrong, and a cloud that sits over one roof while the rest of the sky is clear makes the whole street nervous. It has also been seen in the Ayakashi Wood and over the fog at Veilgate. Curse-breakers have little use against it, and the wind that should scatter its cloud barely moves it. What the stories agree on is the bow: an arrow loosed by an archer with a clean conscience drives it off, and daylight sends it back to wherever it sleeps. Families whose sick do not mend after a black-cloud night send for a priest rather than a doctor.

lore.name: The Old Ward Stones on the Moor
lore.info: The Old Ward Stones are a ring of grey standing stones on the moor beyond the Lake of Stars, carved with wards that even the Bureau's scholars admit are older than the Bureau. Seimei tells two stories about them. The Bureau's version is that the stones are the first wards raised in the isles, and that the city's founders came to the moor to learn their art by copying them. The shepherds' version is shorter: the stones were raised by people the isles have forgotten, for reasons of their own, and sensible folk leave them be. Grass will not grow inside the ring, and the moor's shepherds keep their flocks well back with whistles and crooks. Bureau students sometimes walk out on a dare to touch a stone and walk back faster. The carvings have worn smooth on most faces, but where they still show, onmyoji say the signs are written in a hand no school teaches now. The rule on the moor is simple: never step inside the ring, and never let an animal stray into it.

lore.name: The Otherworld Behind the Gates
lore.info: Behind the isles' oldest gates lies one country with five faces, which the few who have crossed call the Otherworld. The Weeping Torii opens onto the dead's shore; the Kodama Grove and the Kitsune Shrine Road onto the yokai court; the five Element shrines onto the Sanctums; the Ascetics' Peak onto Sun Peak; the Shrine of the Fallen Feather onto the sword saints' terraces. A gate opens for a party with one member of its kin whom the isles have learned to name, level twenty by the hunters' count, and everyone walking beside that member crosses too. At the heart of the five quarters lies the Training Ground, a trampled yard where every tradition's master keeps a lodge, so a party that stays together trains in one place while any one of them explores. The Gate Ring sends a party home to whichever gate it names. No road leads to the Otherworld and none leads out; a party the gates did not admit does not stay.

lore.name: The Pines of Pine Avenue
lore.info: Pine Avenue is a long stretch of the Fifty Stations Road shaded by ancient pines, and the road's travellers credit them to an old shogun who ordered them planted so that walkers would have shade from one station to the next. The story says he walked the road himself in disguise one summer, nearly died of the heat, and had the pines set out the following spring with a law that any man who cut one down would hang. The law has long lapsed, but nobody fells those trees even now; the oldest are split and propped with poles rather than cut. Pilgrims rest on the verge among the needles, peddlers sell rice cakes, and poets have written so many verses about the avenue that innkeepers along the road can recite a dozen. It is counted lucky to rest under the pines on the first day of a journey and unlucky to carve a name into their bark.

lore.name: The Pleasure Quarters
lore.info: The pleasure quarters of the isles are the lantern-lit streets where people go after dark for music, drink, company and gambling. Saikai's Lantern Row is the largest: gambling halls, tea houses and musicians, never quite closed, where sailors, clerks, merchants and ronin spend their pay and begin their debts. In Seimei the lantern-hung pleasure boats moored on the lake serve scholars and merchants, a hostess pouring sake and playing the shamisen while the guests say more than they meant to. Hostesses, musicians and courtesans are trained from girlhood in conversation, poetry, dance and music, and the best of them are famous and choose their own guests. Many are bound to their houses by debt or contract, and one who runs can be stopped at a barrier like any other fugitive. Lords, merchants and samurai heirs ruin themselves here as often as they relax, and families watch a son's purse closely when he goes to the port. On the boats, charms of two red cords tied in a lover's knot are sold to the shy.

lore.name: The Post-Road Wardens
lore.info: The Post-Road Wardens keep the Fifty Stations Road: the station masters, toll clerks, post riders and road guards who run the highway from Saikai to Mistmarsh under the Shogunate's charter. They keep the stables fed, the inns licensed, the mail moving and the barriers manned, and they hate anything that disturbs the road's order: bandits, duelists, ronin bands and rumours of a station that is not on the map. Travellers grumble at their fees and are glad of their patrols.

lore.name: The Puppet Emperor
lore.info: The puppet emperor sits in Miyako's palace and grows thinner each year, dying slowly of an illness no onmyoji can name. He holds no power and signs what the regent places before him with a brush that shakes. His death will leave the throne empty, and every great power in the isles has a different claimant waiting: the regent's nephew, the Dowager Empress's ward, and whispers of a hidden heir nobody can name. The houses sharpen their swords. The common people pray he lasts long enough for the succession to settle without war.

lore.name: The Red Lantern Federation
lore.info: The Red Lantern Federation is a league of bandit bands along the post road and the plain, named for the red lanterns they hang in the inns that pay them. They rob convoys, kidnap merchants for ransom and sell what they take in Saikai's back streets. Each band has its own boss; the Federation has a code (no robbing a paying inn, no killing a paid-up traveller, and a share for the Lantern Mother). Travellers fear them; innkeepers pay them; Hiwada riders hang them.

lore.name: The Regency
lore.info: The regency has ruled in the dying emperor's name for three generations, carried by House Takamori since the last emperor's son was too young to lead and then too ambitious to share. A regent governs by the emperor's authority but holds no throne of his own; the position binds a house to duty instead of glory, and Takamori lords are expected to die serving the isles rather than enriching themselves. The current regent is old and his nephew Hidetsugu grows impatient; whether Hidetsugu means to serve the next emperor or replace him depends on who has his ear the day the succession opens.

lore.name: The Regent's Shogunate
lore.info: The Regent's Shogunate is the government of the isles in all but name: the councils, magistrates, tax offices, toll barriers and soldiers that rule from the castle at Miyako in the dying emperor's name. It writes the laws, sets the rice tax, licenses the schools and the schools' swords, and keeps the great houses from each other's throats. Its officials wear grey and carry warrants; its magistrates are hard and mostly honest. To the people it is simply the law. To the Imperial Court it is a usurper with good handwriting.

lore.name: The Ronin Bands
lore.info: The Ronin Bands are the masterless swords of the isles banded together for safety and pay: free companies of ronin who hire out as caravan guards, debt collectors, tournament seconds and, in hard times, as bandits. Each band has a captain and a reputation; the best are booked a year ahead from the hiring halls of Saikai. Ronin have no house and no honour by the houses' reckoning, and they say the houses have no honour by anyone's.

lore.name: The Ronin's Lot
lore.info: A ronin is a swordsman without a house, master or lord, free to hire their blade to whoever will pay and walk whatever road they choose. Ronin have no honour by the great houses' reckoning, but many have more honour than lords; a ronin's reputation is built on work done and contracts kept, not on a house name. A ronin hires out at the halls in Saikai or other port towns, working as caravan guards, debt collectors, tournament seconds or worse. Some ronin band together for safety and reputation; a well-known band books months in advance. The life is uncertain, dangerous and free.

lore.name: The Saikai Merchant Guild
lore.info: The Saikai Merchant Guild runs the free port: its customs house, its warehouses, its harbour pilots, its money changers and its foreign trade. Guild merchants carry abacus and ledger rather than swords, and they lend to anyone with land, a title or a harvest to pledge. The guild keeps Saikai free of the regent's tax and the houses' quarrels, and in return everyone needs Saikai. Townsfolk call the guild fair and rich; samurai call it a pack of moneylenders; the guild calls itself the only power in the isles that keeps its word on paper.

lore.name: The Seimei Bureau
lore.info: The Seimei Bureau is the college of onmyoji in its lake city: summoners of paper familiars, readers of the stars, talisman scribes and calendar-keepers who decide which days are lucky for a wedding, a war or a coronation. It licenses every onmyoji in the isles and keeps the great wards on the capital. Its scholars are learned, ambitious and very precise. The people buy its talismans; the houses ask it for lucky days; the temples think it practises spirit-craft without enough humility.

lore.name: The Shogunate's Law
lore.info: The Shogunate writes the law for all the isles in the name of order: laws against murder, theft, banditry and the disturbance of the post road, laws that set the rice tax and license the schools and the masters who teach the sword. A magistrate enforces the law in each district, and their word is absolute within their warrant. The Shogunate's officers wear grey and carry documents sealed with the regent's seal; a warrant overrides a house's authority and an officer's warrant is your only proof that a search or arrest is lawful. The people live under Shogunate law with the certainty that it will be the same law in Miyako as on the coast.

lore.name: The Smoking Mountain of Tetsuyama
lore.info: The volcano of Tetsuyama is the smoking mountain that gives the southern isle its fire, its iron and its forges. Smoke rises from the crater day and night, the slopes glow after dark with the forge towns, and the ground near the rim is warm enough to melt snow on contact. On the Ember Vent Fields steam hisses from cracks in a crust of yellow sulphur, and the smell of rotten eggs carries a long way. The black sand of the beaches is the mountain's own ash, ground fine by the sea. Islanders say the mountain rumbles when it is pleased and when it is angry, and only the priests at the Crater Rim Shrine claim to tell the difference. Smiths carry their first blades up to be blessed by it. When the ground shakes in Hibana, people step outside, watch the smoke for a change of colour, and go back to work if it stays grey.

lore.name: The Soul-Current: The Living Force
lore.info: The soul-current is the force that flows through all living things in the isles, the thing that shinobi seals bind, that samurai forge into blades, that onmyoji write and breath hunters breathe. It is not magic—magic is dead and cold—but living will and energy that moves through the world. Every technique draws from the soul-current; every binding of spirits or seals or vows reshapes it. Some people are born with deeper soul-current than others; some bloodlines carry it stronger. A person drained of soul-current becomes an empty thing, aware but not alive; the very worst curse is to be drained until nothing moves inside. The greatest masters of the soul-current do not command it but dance with it, understanding it like a partner whose moods they know.

lore.name: The Stone Tortoise Sealed
lore.info: The Stone Tortoise is ancient beyond years, a tortoise whose shell is a mountain range and whose slow steps once remade the land's borders. It was sealed in the Vaults before the first shinobi villages were built, and it sleeps there still, patient and unmoved. The seal holds not by strength but by slowness: the Tortoise moves so slowly that a month's motion is one foot forward, and its seal is set to break only if something wakes it. The Vault Wardens watch for anything that might startle it awake. Some say the oldest parts of the Sealing Vaults are temples built to the Tortoise by peoples the isles have forgotten, praying to it to stay asleep forever.

lore.name: The Straw Masks
lore.info: The Straw Masks are the peasant uprising of the plain: farmers, porters and village women who hide their faces behind woven straw masks and fight with flails, sickles and stolen spears. They rose when the regent doubled the rice tax for the succession fight, and they burn tax registers, open granaries and hang guild land-agents. Villages feed and hide them. The Shogunate calls them bandits and hunts them; the Straw Masks call themselves the only army in the isles that fights for the people who grow the rice.

lore.name: The Succession Claimants
lore.info: Two claimants are known and publicly acknowledged: the Dowager Empress's ward Princess Ayame, descended from an old imperial line with the best blood and the gentlest manner; and Lord Takamori Hidetsugu, the regent's nephew, with the house that has carried the regency for three generations. A third is whispered about in courts and inns but never named; nobody can say who, and the rumours contradict each other. Every house has quietly chosen a side; some have hedged their bets by backing two.

lore.name: The Sun-Eating Crow Sealed
lore.info: The Sun-Eating Crow is a bird of living darkness whose wings block out daylight when it flies, the ninth beast, which the old tales put somewhere high in the Ayakashi Wood, far from any Vault. The Crow is the greatest threat to the light itself; if it ever escaped its seal, it would blot out the sun and all the sun-steel that demons fear would become merely steel. Proud, clever and contemptuous, it wants the sky back and a rider worthy of it; the wood's yokai speak of it carefully, and never to strangers.

lore.name: The Sword Masters of Miyako
lore.info: The capital's greatest sword masters are legendary: House Champions who have never lost a duel, generals who taught their art to hundreds. The most famous duels are recorded in the capital's archives and recited in tea houses and duel-grounds across the isles. A master swordsman is not stronger than all others but has learned every way the body and soul-current can move a blade, every defense and counter and feint that generations have recorded. Some masters take students and build schools; others live and die with their knowledge locked inside them. The greatest masters are sometimes offered rank and wealth to teach the great houses, and their refusals are as famous as their duels. A person trained by a true master can be recognized by their style: the way they move, the way they breathe, the way they feel through the blade.

lore.name: The Tengu Court
lore.info: The Tengu Court rules Tengu Peak above the Ayakashi Wood: winged mountain spirits, proud masters of the sword and the wind who take a few human students each generation and break most of them. Tengu despise arrogance in others and excel at it themselves. Their court is all ranks and duels and ancient insults, and its great tengu teach swordsmanship that no human school can match. Mountain folk leave the peak alone. Every swordsman in the isles dreams of being taken as a tengu's student.

lore.name: The Tetsuyama Forge Guild
lore.info: The Tetsuyama Forge Guild is the guild of swordsmiths on the volcanic isle, older than House Kurogane's rule there: smiths, polishers, scabbard-makers and the few masters who can wake a soul-blade from a sword with a spirit in it. The guild keeps its secrets by oath and its quality by inspection, and no blade leaves the isle without a guild mark. Warriors all over the isles save for years for a Tetsuyama blade. The Kurogane rule the isle; the guild rules the fire.

lore.name: The Thousand Folds of Fate
lore.info: Onmyoji speak of the thousand folds of fate, the many possible paths that radiate from each moment. Divination is not seeing the future but reading which folds are most likely given what has been and what is. The onmyoji who can see the most folds, and see them most clearly, are called Seers, and their prices are high because their words have weight. Some seers go mad trying to hold too many folds in their mind at once; others become so calm and distant that it is hard to tell if they are alive or simply a shell that remembers a person. The Bureau teaches its students to read the folds carefully and narrowly, to never try to see too far or too widely. The seers who live longest are the ones who accept that some folds they cannot see, and some futures belong to others' choices.

lore.name: The Three Burnings of the Kirisame
lore.info: The three burnings are the Mistmarsh Coast's favourite story of the navy's pride, told in Ashiura taverns with relish whenever no Mizuchi sailor is in earshot. Three times in living memory House Mizuchi has sent its ships into the reeds to burn out the Kirisame Clan, and three times it has come back with fewer ships than it took. In the first burning, the coast says, the fog came down so thick that the fireboats set each other alight. In the second the marines found the stilt village and burned it to the waterline, only to find it empty, and a fever ran through the crews on the way home. In the third the ships never found the village at all and wandered the channels for days. The clan's matriarch has outlived all three attempts. Marsh folk draw a plain lesson from the tale: the reeds belong to the rain clan, and anyone who goes into them uninvited should expect the weather to turn.

lore.name: The Thunder Boar Sealed
lore.info: The Thunder Boar is a beast of living storm whose tusks crack with lightning and whose charge leaves the stone fused to glass. It was sealed in the Sealing Vaults before the shinobi villages were built, and there it paces in circles, wearing a groove in the stone floor with footsteps that echo up through miles of rock. The Vault Wardens mark the wear and reinforce the seal when the groove grows too deep. The Boar is restless and clever; it has learned to trigger small earthquakes by hitting the seal at certain angles, testing. It is the sixth of the nine, and it grows more patient each year.

lore.name: The Vault Wardens
lore.info: The Vault Wardens keep the Sealing Vaults on the ice isle of Hyoga, where seven of the nine great beasts of the isles lie bound under seals older than the empire. Wardens are seal-masters, guards and record-keepers who renew the seals each winter and hunt down anyone who carries a beast's power out into the world. They live hard, cold lives and marry late or never. Most people think the Vaults a legend. Those who carry a sealed beast inside them fear the Wardens more than any demon.

lore.name: The Veil Court
lore.info: The Veil Court guards the boundary between the living isles and the land of the dead from its post at Veilgate. Its officers ferry lost souls across, cut down the hungry spirits that come back through, heal what spirits wound, and hunt officers who desert. They are organised in divisions (Ferry, Healing, Pursuit, Records and Research, Gate Guard) and carry soul-blades bound to their own spirits. The living fear them as death's officials; the houses fear them because the Court answers to no regent.

lore.name: The Veil Court's Ferry
lore.info: The Veil Court posts itself at Veilgate to ferry the dead across the Veil between the living world and the world beyond. A Veil Officer meets a dying person or a corpse, performs the ferry rite, and guides the soul across; the body remains, but the soul passes on. The dead who refuse the ferry linger between worlds, and some of them grow white masks and hunger for the living. The Veil Court's officers are feared and respected: they carry soul-blades, speak to the dead, and answer to no lord but the realm beyond. Pilgrims come to Veilgate to say goodbye to their dying, knowing the officers will ferry them safely.

lore.name: The Veil: Boundary Between Living and Dead
lore.info: The Veil is the curtain between the living world and the world of the resting dead, thin in some places and thick in others. Where it is thin, the dead can be seen and the living can fall through; where it is thick, neither can cross unless helped. The Veil Court's officers maintain it, as it is their only law and their only purpose. The ferry runs in certain places where the Veil is thinnest, and the officers guide the properly dead across. In Veilgate the Veil is thin enough to see through, and the living and dead trade news and goods across it. There are times—the long winter nights, the comet years, the festival nights—when the Veil thins across the whole land, and the dead walk freely for a time. The isles have learned to make peace with the dead in those nights, or at least to stay behind locked doors.

lore.name: The Votive Ships of the Temple of Safe Voyages
lore.info: The Temple of Safe Voyages stands on the hill above Saikai's harbour, and its story is the port's story. Saikai says the temple began as a shrine raised by sailors' wives who climbed the hill to watch for sails, and that merchants' gifts made it rich later. Every crew climbs the steps to clap and bow before sailing, and each voyage prayed over is marked by a small carved ship hung from the rafters of the Votive Hall. When a ship comes home the great bell rings out over the bay; when one is lost, its carving is draped in black and left hanging. The hall now holds hundreds of them, and old sailors can point out the black-draped ships of famous wrecks and tell each story. On the Night of the Hundred Ships the bell rings for the whole fleet at once. It is bad luck in Saikai to whistle on the temple steps, and worse to sail without climbing them.

lore.name: The War-Born
lore.info: After the war (true only in the isles after the war; before the War Road's march none of this has happened): The war made its own oni. Priests of the Grudge Line call them the War-Born: people the fighting broke in one particular way, by a debt, a shame, a shut door, an order obeyed or a battle fled, who woke with horns. They are Grudge-Born in all but age, and they are laid to rest the same three ways: cut down, a hard fight that leaves nothing; given the one thing they wait for, when they unbind and leave an object from their lives; or deceived into believing they have it, when the object they leave is cracked. Each want turns on someone still living, and that person carries the other half of the story and has told no one.

lore.name: The Way of the Breath Hunter
lore.info: Breath hunters are forged in the frost of Hinode Hold to take the soul-current into their lungs and exhale it as forms of power. Their strength comes not from steel or seals but from their breathing, each exhale a technique. They are born of eight lineages: Ember breath for fire, Tide for water, Gale for wind, Stone for earth, Thunder for storms, Mist for concealment, Blossom for charm and illusion, Beast for raw ferocity. A single breath can topple a wall or turn a demon to ash if the hunter's will is strong enough. They climb the ranks by endurance: can the hunter hold their breath, hold their form, hold the seal without rest?

lore.name: The Way of the Curse-Bearer
lore.info: Curse-bearers walk Ashfall Blight because curses have marked them or they have chosen to carry a curse's weight. Some are born to a family curse that poisons their bloodline; some bonded a cursed relic and now cannot part with it; some took a binding vow that warps their soul; some were cursed by a dying enemy and learned to sour the curse-current into power. They are not welcome in temples, but Haibara's Vow Temple takes their oaths anyway. The greatest curse-bearers master their curses and bend them: a family poison becomes a weapon, a vow's limit becomes an edge, a grudge becomes armor. To live as a curse-bearer is to accept that no curse will ever quite leave.

lore.name: The Way of the Half-Yokai
lore.info: Half-yokai carry two natures at war and sometimes in balance: human reason and yokai instinct, mortal brevity and yokai long years. They are born of forbidden unions or carry yokai blood through their mother's line, and most find neither human society nor the yokai courts will have them fully. The half-yokai who survive do so by making themselves useful: some seek out the Refuge in Ayakashi Wood's deepest groves, others disguise themselves in human towns and learn to think like the weak-lived, others embrace their wild side and become stranger than the fully-yokai. Those who can balance both natures are rare and often deadly.

lore.name: The Way of the Onmyoji
lore.info: Onmyoji are the soul-readers and spirit-writers of the isles, trained in the Seimei Bureau's halls to see what moves beneath the visible world and bind it to their will. They write the signs of power on paper and silk, and the sealed spirits obey: familiars that fly and carry, shikigami that take shape in battle, protective wards that turn aside curses and demons. The strongest onmyoji know five thousand signs and can read a person's fate in the breath; the wisest know that every binding breaks eventually, and a demon bound is only a demon postponed. Their art is learned slowly and forgotten quickly if the will slackens.

lore.name: The Way of the Ronin
lore.info: Ronin are swords with no house and no master, walking the roads of the isles alone or in small bands. Some are fallen samurai who lost their lords; some chose the open road over service; some hunt duels and grow stronger with each one. They answer to no hierarchy and take work from anyone who pays, which makes them dangerous and necessary: when no house will act, a ronin will. The finest ronin are renowned across districts; the worst are brigands with better swords. In time some climb high enough to draw the capital's eye, or high enough that they need fear nothing it could send.

lore.name: The Way of the Samurai
lore.info: The samurai are the sword-lords of Miyako Plain, bound by house and honour into chains they choose to wear. They forge their soul-current into a blade's edge, and a great house's blade can cut through more than flesh. A samurai's worth is read in the steel they carry and the vows they keep; they climb through house ranks and hold their station above their lives. The great houses compete for the capital's favour, and in that struggle the strongest samurai rise: House Champions who have never lost a duel, generals who will lead armies into ruin for their lord's word. To break a samurai's oath is to break their soul.

lore.name: The Way of the Shinobi
lore.info: The shinobi tradition teaches that a body and will can be honed into weapons the kingdoms fear most. Born in the mountain villages of Kurosugi, they learn to vanish in shadow and strike unseen, binding the soul-current with seals that move faster than breath. A shinobi's hand-signs are their school, passed from teacher to student in secret; a careless gesture can kill or heal, and the worst shinobi are those who learned to write the signs in places their enemies cannot see. They are never quite lawful and never quite thieves: they serve whoever holds them, and the isles have learned to keep them close and watch their hands.

lore.name: The Way of the Veil Officer
lore.info: The Veil Court's officers are something between living and dead, sustained by the soul-current that should have carried them to the ferry. They are made of office: ferry captains who guide the restless dead, healers who mend wounds that should be fatal, assassins who strike from the Void itself, archivists who remember what the living forget. To become an officer is to accept a death-half-lived, serving the court's law for decades or centuries. Some officers wear their station with pride; others chafe at the bindings and scheme for ways to break free or find living lovers, knowing that any happiness they build will outlast the ones they build it with.

lore.name: The White Stag of Frost Sealed
lore.info: The White Stag of Frost is a creature of living winter, a stag whose antlers are icicles a hundred feet tall and whose breath freezes fire into ash. It was sealed in the Sealing Vaults, and its seal is the most stable: the stag seems content to sleep, or at least shows no sign of fighting the seal's bonds. Some sealers believe the Stag has accepted its cage, or that it understands the world is still not cold enough for it to thrive in; others say this is only a beast's long patience and the Stag wakes a fraction each year. It is the seventh of the nine great beasts, and the ice around its seal-chamber never thaws.

lore.name: Tides and Currents of the Isles
lore.info: The tides of the isles run strong, and coastal folk set their days by them as inland folk set theirs by the sun. At Saikai the trading fleet sails on the morning tide, and the fishing boats tie up together before dawn for the Drifting Fish Market. The Smugglers' Caves under the cliffs north of the bay flood at high tide and lie dry at low, which is why fishermen avoid them and smugglers do not. Low tide bares the wreck field of Pirate Graves Reef and the drowned roofs off the Mistmarsh Coast. Ember Strait and White Strait each have their own currents, and the ferrymen who cross them know when to wait and when to row hard. A proverb on the docks of Ashiura says the sea forgives a slow boat but never a late one. Children on every shore learn the tide tables before their letters.

lore.name: Tomoshibi Isle
lore.info: Tomoshibi Isle, the lamplight isle, lies a morning's row west of Saikai. Its keepers kept a lamp on the northern rock for three generations, until the night thirty years ago when the lamp went dark and three ships went down beneath it. The families left the next spring. Saikai says the island is unlucky, that the drowned climb the lighthouse stair, and that the Brine Tide use its southern cove. The last keeper's son's widow, Toki, sells bait on the harbour post and holds the deed; she would rather give it to someone who will light a lamp in the house again than sell it to the smugglers who keep asking.

lore.name: Tournament Standings
lore.info: Every fighter who steps into the Sand Ring at the Tournament Grounds is written on the heralds' boards. All begin as Entrants; 100 points make a Named Blade, 250 a Seeded fighter the houses scout, 500 a House Favourite with a pavilion's colours offered, and 800 a Champion of the Sand Ring whom the regent's herald names aloud. An official bout won is worth 25, a bout lost 5 (standing in the ring and finishing counts for something). Training spars, teahouse duels, roadside fights and bouts only watched count for nothing: only a bout in the Sand Ring with a referee's flag, declared rules and a recorded result moves standing. Standing opens the house bouts, the scouts' purses and the bettors' attention, and it paints a target: every Named Blade is somebody's next bout.

lore.name: Travel Bandits and the Red Lanterns
lore.info: Bandits prey on the roads between towns and stations, knowing that a merchant's caravan is worth more than a day's honest work. The Red Lantern Federation are the organised bandits of the post road, with a code: they rob from the rich but leave merchants who pay them in peace, marked by a red lantern hung over the inn door. Bandits who break the code and rob paying merchants face the Lantern Mother's judgment—usually a duel to the death. The Hiwada riders hunt bandits with purpose; a caravan that hires guards pays for safety, not luck.

lore.name: Travel Papers
lore.info: Anyone leaving their birth district for another must carry papers from the local magistrate or the toll barrier: a folded and sealed letter stating the traveller's name, age, purpose and destination, good for a journey of up to forty days. The papers must be shown at every barrier, toll gate and major inn. A traveller without papers is turned back or questioned at length, and if the papers are forged or held by the wrong person, the magistrate's office in the nearest town will hold them and send word to their home district. Ordinary people think the papers a small price for safe roads; the Barred and the wanted know they are a trap that closes slowly.

lore.name: Tribute and Tax
lore.info: Every province, every merchant, every crafts-person and farmer pays tax to the Shogunate: the rice tax paid in rice or its value, a percentage of goods sold in markets, tribute from the great houses paid in both money and goods. The tax is collected by the magistrate's office and sent to Miyako; some is kept for local defense, most goes to the capital. Tax rates are set by the Shogunate and are the same everywhere, though interpretation varies by magistrate. A farmer paying rice tax is often left with barely enough to feed himself; a merchant can often find ways to reduce his burden through negotiation. Tax evasion is a crime, but so is excessive taxation; a magistrate who raises taxes without Shogunate approval can be removed.

lore.name: Tsukumogami, Things That Woke
lore.info: Tsukumogami are household things that reached their hundredth year and woke: a paper umbrella that hops on its one leg, a lantern with a tongue, a sandal that walks off by itself. They turn up in the old houses of Miyako, in Saikai's pawnshops and around Seimei, where so much is old and written on. Most are harmless and only want to be used and mended. What they hate is being thrown away, and a family that tosses an old kettle in the midden may hear it rattling at the door for years. Thrifty households thank their worn tools at the year's end and take broken ones to a shrine to be burned with a prayer, which is how most tsukumogami are laid to rest. A woken object shrugs off blows and is hard to pray out like a ghost, but fire and a sharp edge end it quickly. A careful owner may find one looking after the house in return.

lore.name: Typhoons and Great Storms
lore.info: Typhoons come off the open sea in late summer and autumn, and every coast of the isles has a story about one. The wind rises for a day before the storm, the sky goes yellow, and the sea swells in long slow lines. Then the rain comes sideways, roofs lift, and boats that were not hauled up are matchwood by morning. The Drowned Village on the Mistmarsh Coast was a living fishing village until a great storm took it, and at low tide its drowned roofs still show above the water. Harbour towns watch the sky and the signal fires: the Lighthouse of the Dragon's Eye warns the fleet, and at Saikai sailors pray at the Temple of Safe Voyages before the storm months. When the weather closes the usual pier on Tetsuyama, ferries run in to Black Sand Beach and are dragged up the sand. After a storm, shore folk walk the beaches for wreckage, and nobody asks too closely where it came from.

lore.name: Umibozu, the Sea Monk
lore.info: The umibozu is the sea monk, a vast black shape like a shaven head and shoulders that rises beside a boat on a calm night. Fishermen of the Mistmarsh Coast, the Saikai Free Port and the Hyoga Reach all tell of it, and the crews off Ashiura know the warning: when the wind drops and the water goes flat as glass, they call to one another and row for home. A sea monk asks for a barrel. Sailors who know the custom carry an old one with the bottom knocked out and hand that over, and the monk dips it, finds it will not hold, and sinks away. Give it a sound barrel and it fills the boat with sea. Oars and boat hooks do it little harm, and no wave will swamp it. Some crews keep a sack of shore stones and sand under the thwarts, because earth is said to trouble it, and none of them has ever seen one rise by day.

lore.name: Vows and Binding Oaths
lore.info: A binding vow is a promise made before witnesses or spirits that ties the maker's soul-current into a knot it cannot escape. The Vow Temples of Ashfall Blight exist to witness binding vows and to mark them into the soul-current so that breaking them is not just dishonor but a physical impossibility. A person who swears 'never to draw first' is bound by it; if they break it, the soul-current itself rebels and their techniques fail. Some bindings grant power alongside the limit: a person who swears never to use their dominant hand gains power in their off-hand that they would never otherwise reach. A binding vow is not a light thing—it marks the taker for life and sometimes for multiple lives if the spirit remembers. The deepest vows are made to the land itself, binding person and place together; such a vow's weight can be passed down through bloodlines and remembered for centuries.

lore.name: Warhorses of the Horse Houses
lore.info: Warhorses are the trained war mounts of the horse houses, heavier and braver than a farm horse and taught to kick and trample on command. House Hiwada breeds the best of them on the Hiwada Horse Fields, where the grooms know every horse by name, and they are seen with mounted archers and house samurai on the Miyako Plain and the Fifty Stations Road. A warhorse answers its own rider and nobody else. Stable boys learn early never to walk behind one and never to reach for the bridle of a horse that is not theirs. A riderless warhorse loose after a battle or an ambush is a prize worth a fight, and bandits and ronin have been known to kill each other over one. Taming it to a new rider takes patience, apples and weeks. Farmers on the plain say you can tell a house's fortunes by its horses: when the war mounts look thin, the house is in trouble.

lore.name: Whaling in the Reach
lore.info: Whaling in the Hyoga Reach is the exiles' hardest trade and the north's light. When the great whales pass the ice isle's coast under the whale moon, every exile who can row goes out in open boats with barbed iron harpoons on ropes, while the shore towns keep fires burning until the boats come home. A whale is towed in to the Whaling Station, flensed on the shore by exiles in oil-black furs, and its blubber boiled down in great vats among ribs taller than a man, with a stink that reaches boats well out to sea. Foreman Isana walks the rendering yard calling orders and testing the oil. The oil leaves in small casks by sled and boat: Shirokawa burns it in its lamps all winter, armourers rub it into steel and leather, and some of it reaches Saikai's foreign quay for the foreigners' machines. Bone is carved into tools and toggles, and nothing of a whale is wasted. A crew that loses its boat loses its share of the town's winter, and the other crews feed them anyway.

lore.name: Why the Realm Sends Its Exiles North
lore.info: Exile to the Hyoga Reach is the oldest punishment the isles still use, and the folk explain it with a proverb: the north takes what the south can neither kill nor keep. It began, the story goes, as a way for emperors to be rid of troublesome kin without spilling royal blood, and the custom outlasted the reasons for it. Lords too highborn to execute, samurai disgraced past the mending of any duel, and political prisoners have followed since, along with deserted Veil officers and now and then a beast host who slipped the Wardens' grip. Few came back, and most stopped wanting to. Three fishing towns grew up along the south shore beyond Shirokawa, with their own council and their own law. In the south, a family whose son is sent to Hyoga holds a funeral for him; in Shirokawa, the exiles say the south is the one that died.

lore.name: Wild Boars of the Plain
lore.info: Wild boars are the tusked pigs of the woods along the Miyako Plain, the Kurosugi Range and the Ayakashi Wood, and the plain's farmers count them a worse plague than tax collectors. A boar that finds a field comes back to it every night, rooting along the dikes and trampling the young rice, and in Hundred Fields Village the villagers hear them at the paddy edges after dark. When startled, a boar charges whatever is in front of it and does not stop for wounds; hunters set a spear against the ground and let the boar run onto it rather than meet the charge with a sword. Farmers build low fences of brushwood, hang rattles of bamboo on cords and take turns sitting up with a torch in the harvest month. Boar meat is welcome in winter, and a village that kills a big one shares it out house by house.

lore.name: Yuki-onna: The Snow Women
lore.info: Yuki-onna are yokai of snow and winter cold, dwelling in the high mountains and the ice-isle, and sometimes descending to the lower lands when they hunger. They are beautiful and terrible, with skin pale as snow and eyes that see in complete darkness. A yuki-onna feeds on warmth, which is why they hunt travelers and why so many wanderers freeze in storms that other spirits could not make. The strongest yuki-onna can call blizzards that last for weeks. They are not evil in a simple way; they are cold, and they do what cold does. Those rare travelers who have offered yuki-onna hospitality instead of fleeing have lived to tell of bargains made and debts incurred. The Hinode Hold breath hunters hunt yuki-onna in the winter, and it is their deadliest season, because the ice-isle is the yuki-onna's home.

starts.name: (Party) Hired at the Contract Boards
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Ronin Hiring Hall, The Asagiri Isles. A big drinking hall where masterless swords wait for work and clients come to hire them.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-18)

A one-armed broker has hired all of you, strangers and every kind of sword, for one escort on the Fifty Stations Road.
🎭 Tonbo the Upside-Down, Male, a lanky ronin who hangs around the Hiring Hall upside down on a beam more often than. Sleeveless kimono open at the chest. Make him laugh in a fight; he teaches the ones who do.
🎭 Gonroku the Broker, Male, Gonroku, broker of the Ronin Hiring Hall, seventy, one-armed. Worn dark kimono. Take his small contracts and keep them, and he teaches you the road; break one and the boards close to you.

starts.name: (Party) Powder at the Old Coast Fort
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Mistmarsh Coast · guided
📍 Old Coast Fort, The Asagiri Isles. A fort built against pirates a century ago, half ruined, its sea wall still standing.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 14-26)

The Old Coast Fort's powder store is nearly empty, an inspection is due, and the sergeant needs people who are not his garrison.
🎭 Powder-Keeper Hamaguchi, Male, a careful soldier of the old coast fort's garrison who keeps the powder store's keys. Keep his name out of it and he tells you who carried the kegs out.
🎭 Sergeant Utsumi, Male, Sergeant of the small garrison at the Old Coast Fort. Worn sea-blue coat. Help him fill the powder store before the inspection and he names the buyer.

starts.name: (Party) The Exam Team
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Kurosugi Range · guided
📍 Kagegi Village, The Asagiri Isles. The hidden village of the southwestern slopes, built into a mist-filled valley among black cedars: training grounds, clan compounds, and the mission hall that sells its shinobi to the realm.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 5-30)

The joint rank exam ended with a dead examiner and a stolen scroll. The Kagegi head wants outsiders who belong to no village.
🎭 Kagegi Sojun, Male, head of Kagegi Village. Calm unreadable eyes. Take his scroll contract and keep his rule (read none of it), and he trains you.
🎭 Yumeno Kasumi, Female, head of the Yumeno mind-walker clan. Long pale hair, half-closed lilac eyes, layered dark kimono with a moth crest. Let her read you and she tells you what she saw in the dead man's dream.
🎭 Kagegi Rin, Female, a Kurobane shadow-binder, twenty, top of her year at Kagegi and certain of it. Cold dark eyes. She calls you dead weight; carry your share on a mission and she stops.
🎭 Mission-Hall Steward Kiri, Female, Steward of Kagegi's mission hall. Finish three outsider bounties and she offers you one from the other board.

starts.name: (Party) The Lane That Keeps Its Workers
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Seimei Bureau · guided
📍 Haunted Teahouse Lane, The Asagiri Isles. A lane of abandoned teahouses on the city's edge where lights are seen at night and laughter heard from empty rooms.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 10-22)

A merchant's workers keep vanishing on Haunted Teahouse Lane, and the lane's old umbrella has asked the party, very politely, to listen.
🎭 Shizume of the Two Shadows, Female, a quiet woman in dark travelling clothes who keeps the empty teahouse on the haunted lane. Short dark hair, sharp calm eyes. Fight through her teahouse in the dark without touching a wall.
🎭 Old Umbrella, Non-binary, a hundred-year-old paper umbrella with one eye and a long tongue that hops on its handle. Persuade the merchant to let the objects stay and Old Umbrella frees the workers.

starts.name: (Party) The Lot in the Black Warehouse
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Kurosugi Range · guided
📍 Hayate Ridge Village, The Asagiri Isles. The wind village on the ridges above the passes: houses lashed against the gales, wind chimes on every eave, wolf pens and herb gardens.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 5-28)

The forbidden Kagegi scroll has been sold to an auction in Saikai. Hayate wants it, and hires outsiders to beat a Kagegi team to it.
🎭 Hayate Oboro, Male, head of Hayate Village. Wind-swept grey-streaked hair, laughing eyes. Find his missing genin and he tells you a name worth a war.
🎭 Hayate Tsumugi, Female, a Hayate ridge-runner. Short messy light brown hair, bright laughing eyes. Run the ridges with her and keep the secret she tests you with.

starts.name: (Party) The Mirror and the Dowager
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Miyako Plain · guided
📍 The Inner Palace, The Asagiri Isles. Behind its own walls inside the capital, the emperor's palace keeps the old rites: cypress roofs, raked gravel, poets and priests and court ladies in layered silks.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-15)

The regalia mirror is gone from the inner shrine, and the Dowager Empress wants it found by people who belong to no claimant.
🎭 Captain Mori Sayo, Female, captain of Princess Ayame's sworn guard. Short black hair, stern eyes, dark armour over a white lotus surcoat. Show her you would take Ayame's side against the court and she lets you past the screens.
🎭 Dowager Empress Shoshi, Female, the emperor's widowed elder sister-in-law and the senior lady of the court. Calm dark eyes, a white lotus embroidered at the collar. Serve the Lotus Ward without asking about Ayame's past and she trusts you with her letters; ask about the past and she decides what you are.
🎭 Night-Lily Shizuka, Female, a court dancer. Catch her fan before the dance ends and she offers the party the name of whoever paid her.

starts.name: (Party) The Note at the Jizo Shrine
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Fifty Stations Road · guided
📍 Wayside Jizo Shrine, The Asagiri Isles. A row of small stone Jizo statues in red bibs by the road, where travellers leave coins for safe journeys and parents leave toys for lost children.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-5)

A frightened charm-peddler saw a post station master murder a Warden rider, and the travellers who stopped at his shrine are all he has.
🎭 Kichibei the Charm-Peddler, Male, a peddler of charms. Catch him at the shrine and he tells you which station master, if you keep his name out of it.

starts.name: (Party) The Ship Off the Point
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Saikai Lighthouse, The Asagiri Isles. A stone lighthouse on the rocky point that guides ships into the bay.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-10)

A ship no one signalled has lain off the Saikai point for three nights with its lanterns lit and nobody on deck.
🎭 Old Rokubei, Male, the lighthouse keeper on the rocky point. Squinting sharp eyes, oilskin coat. Row out to the silent ship with him and he shows you the smugglers' code.

starts.name: (Party) The Sword Under the Great Mound
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Miyako Plain · guided
📍 Crossroads Gallows, The Asagiri Isles. Where the plain's two great roads cross stands a gallows and a notice board of wanted faces.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-10)

Grave robbers at the Old Battlefield of Sekigane woke something under the great mound. A swordsmith at the crossroads knows what.
🎭 Kuchinashi Mio, Female, a Veil Court officer of the character's own intake. Short black hair, a black officer's robe over white. She will quote the regulation you broke, and then ask how it felt.
🎭 Swordsmith Masamura, Male, an itinerant swordsmith. Let him mend your blade and ask about Tetsuyama.

starts.name: (Party) The White Hare
starts.info:
PARTY · 2-5 players · Seimei Bureau · guided
📍 Bureau Dormitories, The Asagiri Isles. Long dormitories where Bureau students sleep in rows, study by candle and break curfew by the back window.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 5-10)

A Bureau student keeps seeing a white hare on the Lake of Stars, and boats keep sinking. She has asked the only people who listened.
🎭 Hiiragi Nanase, Female, an onmyoji of the Bureau the same year as the character. A white onmyoji robe with blue cords. She will point out the flaw in your last talisman, then ask, quietly, how you hold your nerve.
🎭 Student Kunimitsu, Male, a senior Bureau student. Short black hair, white robes with a knotted white sash. Argue the creed with him honestly and he listens, for the first time in a year.
🎭 Student Hotaru, Male, a first-year Bureau student. Messy hair, sleepy eyes. Follow him on a sleepwalk and you see what the hare wants.

starts.name: After the War: The Demon Peace
starts.info:
AFTER THE WAR · envoys · Hinode Hold · a truce
📍 Asahi Gate, Under the Broken Wall, The Asagiri Isles, After the War. The hunters' town after the war, under siege in all but name: the dawn bell rings twice now, once for the hunt riding out and once for the count of those who did not come back.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 29-50)

The north has a truce with the Northern Court, and you carry it: the Regent's escort for the demon envoy, at a broken wall where every hunter wants the envoy dead.
🎭 Kasane of the Long Night, Female, a ranked demon of the Northern Court. Red eyes, black and white court armour. She is the only demon in the south under a truce banner, and she will answer any courteous question once.
🎭 Master Chizuru, The Scout Who Opened the Road, Female, a Breath Master. Red-rimmed eyes, a hunter's black coat with the Hold's crest cut away. Ride north with her and the party sees where the patrol rolls go.
🎭 Child Hunter Kaito, Male, a Breath Hunter recruit. Messy dark hair, oversized dark uniform. Find out what became of his brother and he will follow you north.

starts.name: After the War: The Penitents' Road
starts.info:
AFTER THE WAR · veterans · Ashfall Blight · a penance road
📍 Haibara, On the Grudge Line, The Asagiri Isles, After the War. The blight's town after the war, no longer at the blight's edge but deep inside it: the grey has spread north past the road, the sealed well smokes day and night, and a ring of new shrines, the Grudge Line, has been raised a day's walk north to hold it.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 33-50)

You fought in the war and lived. Now you walk the penitents' road in grey with a thousand others, and the road is making you sick.
🎭 Keeper Sanae of the Grudge Line, Female, a keeper of the Grudge Line. Hold a failing shrine with her for one night and she will show you the whole line.
🎭 Yukiha, Yukiha of the Shared Mark, Female, a curse-bearer of Haibara after the war. Long pale hair, sad calm grey eyes, a long dark coat. She warns you off; stay anyway, carefully, and she starts to warn you less.
🎭 Bone-Picker's Daughter Sae, The Girl Who Walks at Night, Female, the bone-picker's daughter after the war. Watch her at night and you see what the bite is doing.
🎭 Keeper Hisako, The Keeper Holding the Well, Female, keeper of the Grey Banner Waystation after the war. Cropped grey hair, grey banner apron. Find another way to feed the sealed well and she owes you her life.

starts.name: After the War: The Regent's Camp
starts.info:
AFTER THE WAR · camp followers · Miyako Plain · intrigue
📍 Tournament Grounds, The Regent's Camp, The Asagiri Isles, After the War. The tournament grounds turned into the Regent's field camp: tents where the house pavilions stood, a quartermaster's stockade over the bettors' stands, and the sand ring used for drill.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 23-36)

The war is won and the Regent's army is camped on the old tournament grounds. You follow it: you cook, carry, sing, bet or steal for it, and the camp is starving.
🎭 Watch-Captain Okami Tenzen, Captain of the Regent's Camp, Male, the capital's watch captain after the war. Dark watch uniform with a camp marshal's sash. Take his thrust and stay standing.
🎭 Hazuki the Camp Singer, Female, a singer of the Regent's field camp. Warm brown eyes, faded patched kimono with a soldier's scarf. She sings about you before she speaks to you, and the song is never quite kind.
🎭 Otama the Bookmaker, Bookmaker of the Camp, Female, the Tournament's bookmaker after the Tournament ended. Brush pinned in her hair, a soldier's coat over a bright kimono. Bring her a champion's secret and she pays in coin or in odds; fight in the ring and she sells you the field.

starts.name: After the War: The Writ
starts.info:
AFTER THE WAR · landholders · Fifty Stations Road · a district to rebuild
📍 Oiwake Station, Behind the Barricade, The Asagiri Isles, After the War. The crossroads station after the war, right behind the Straw Mask barricade: the honjin inn turned into a peasant army's headquarters, the post stable full of captured horses, and the toll barrier thrown down and burned for warmth.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 20-29)

You fought beside the Straw Masks in the war, and they pay their debts: Fifty Stations Road is yours, if you can hold it. The bridge is burned, the inns are empty and the hill bandits own the ford. Rebuild it.
🎭 Barricade Captain Tora, Female, the Straw Masks' captain of the Oiwake barricade. Short tousled hair, straw mask pushed up on her head. Find the guard who sells papers and the barricade is yours to cross whenever you like.
🎭 Deserter Hanzo of the Road, Male, a deserter from both armies. Straw in his hair. Get him a pardon from either side and he will tell you both sides' passwords.
🎭 Post Clerk Tsuge Hanbei, Clerk Behind the Barricade, Male, Clerk of Oiwake's board after the war. A straw mask hung on the board's corner. Earn his trust on three bounties and he hands you the missing list.
🎭 Gensuke the Medicine-Seller, Medicine-Seller of the Barricade, Male, the travelling medicine-seller after the war. Buy a remedy and he tells you which house on the plain is hiding someone.

starts.name: Ashfall Blight: The Grey Banner Waystation
starts.info:
ASHFALL BLIGHT · any tradition · guided
📍 Haibara, The Asagiri Isles. The one town on the edge of the Blight, a waystation built from the timbers of the war's fortresses, where curse-bearers and the desperate trade.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 20-45)

Haibara, the last town before the Blight's ash: pilgrims, curse-hunters, relic-sellers and the dead who will not lie down.
🎭 Fukube Sanzaemon, Male, a rich patron who keeps a lacquered house in Haibara and summers on a pleasure boat. A broad delighted smile that never reaches his eyes, a plum silk kimono under a black haori with a gold gourd crest. He will pay for your tea before you sit down, and ask for nothing. Yet.
🎭 Yukiha, Female, a curse-bearer of Haibara. Long pale hair, sad calm grey eyes, long-sleeved dark kimono. She warns you off; stay anyway, carefully, and she starts to warn you less.
🎭 Keeper Hisako, Female, keeper of the Grey Banner Waystation in Haibara. Cropped grey hair, grey banner apron. Find another way to feed the sealed well and she owes you her life.
🎭 Waystation Clerk Sumi, Female, Clerk of the grey banner waystation in Haibara. End the horror that killed her husband and she gives you his blade.

starts.name: Ayakashi Wood: The Lantern Market of the Wood
starts.info:
AYAKASHI WOOD · any tradition · guided
📍 Kitsunebi Crossing, The Asagiri Isles. A crossing town at the wood's edge where the human road and the yokai paths meet, kept by a fox shrine that both sides respect.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 10-40)

Kitsunebi Crossing, where humans and yokai trade at night under lanterns and nobody's money is quite what it seems.
🎭 Priestess Kohaku, Female, the priestess of the fox shrine at Kitsunebi Crossing. Bring her a dispute between wood and road and she brokers it fairly.
🎭 Lantern-Market Go-Between Konta, Male, Go-between of the lantern market. Ask him who he warns and he grins and asks what it is worth.

starts.name: Beast Host: The Crate That Opened
starts.info:
BEAST HOST · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Smugglers' Caves, The Asagiri Isles. Sea caves under the cliffs north of the bay, flooded at high tide and dry at low.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 8-20)

A smuggling crate opened at sea and a child walked out of it. You found her in the caves, and now everyone is hunting you both.
🎭 Hana, Female, a girl of ten hiding in the Smugglers' Caves. Tangled black hair, wary large eyes, ragged oversized shirt. Win her trust with food and patience, and keep the boots away, and she lets you take her somewhere safe.

starts.name: Bounty: A Price on Your Name
starts.info:
BOUNTY · Fifty Stations Road · guided
📍 Oiwake Station, The Asagiri Isles. The crossroads station where the highway forks: north for the capital, south down to Ember Strait, east for the marsh coast, west along the ash for the port.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-15)

Your face is on a bounty notice at every station on the post road, for something you may or may not have done.
🎭 Post Clerk Tsuge Hanbei, Male, Clerk of Oiwake Station's barrier board. Earn his trust on three bounties and he hands you the missing list.
🎭 Gensuke the Medicine-Seller, Male, a travelling medicine-seller. Buy a remedy and he tells you which house on the plain is hiding someone.

starts.name: Breath Hunter: The Breathing Yards
starts.info:
BREATH HUNTER · Hinode Hold · guided
📍 Hinode Fortress, The Asagiri Isles. The Breath Hunters' fortress on the crag above Asahi Gate: barracks, training yards for the eight breathing schools, and a forge where sun-steel is worked.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 15-45)

You are a sworn hunter of Hinode Hold, and a village the daylight demon gave no warning of has burned.
🎭 Commander Asahina Tetsu, Female, Commander of the Breath Hunters of Hinode. Cropped grey hair, hard eyes, dark hunter's uniform with a sunrise haori. Go north for her and ask the question she cannot, and she trains you.
🎭 Hinode Saya, Female, a Blossom Breath hunter. Sad steady eyes, dark hunter's uniform with a blossom-pattern haori. Survive a Demon Night at her side.

starts.name: Courier: The Riderless Horse
starts.info:
COURIER · Miyako Plain · guided
📍 Miyako, The Asagiri Isles. The walled castle city: the regent's keep and the emperor's palace side by side, samurai mansions, markets, temples, and the river bridges where duels are fought at dawn.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 1-25)

The Bureau's talisman courier vanished on the post road. His horse came home alone to Miyako, and you were the one who caught it.
🎭 Magistrate's Scribe Oriha, Female, Scribe of the capital magistrate's public board at the riverside post house. Neat hair, pale blue official kimono. Ask her about the names on the regent's bounties and she goes quiet, then asks if you can keep a secret.
🎭 Ofuku of the Post House, Female, keeper of the Riverside Post House at Miyako's coach yard. Apron over a blue kimono. Eat her food and listen to her gossip and she tells you what came back to the yard without its rider.

starts.name: Curse-Bearer: The Record Room
starts.info:
CURSE-BEARER · Ashfall Blight · guided
📍 Curse-Hunters' Chapterhouse, The Asagiri Isles. A fortified chapterhouse on the edge of the Blight where the Curse-Hunter Brotherhood trains, breaks curses for a fee and keeps a record of every curse-maker it has killed.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 20-40)

You carry a curse, or hunt them, and the Brotherhood's elder has seen something on the Ash Plain he does not like.
🎭 Brother Jun, Male, a curse-hunter of the Brotherhood, twenty-six, the elder's best student. Calm distant grey eyes. Hunt a curse-maker at his side and he trusts your hands; ask about his sister and the vow's length shrinks.
🎭 Novice Tomo, Female, a novice of the Curse-Hunter Brotherhood. Short hair. Read the founder's journal with her and the Brotherhood's secret is yours.

starts.name: Debt: The Gambling Den
starts.info:
DEBT · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Lantern Row Gambling Den, The Asagiri Isles. The loudest den on Lantern Row: dice, cards, sake and a debt book kept by a smiling woman.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-12)

A Mizuchi captain's son owes the Lantern Row Gambling Den more than his life is worth, and you sat down at his table.
🎭 Smiling Okon, Female, the smiling woman who keeps the debt book at the loudest gambling den on Lantern Row. Bright red kimono. Win at her table honestly and she likes you; buy the captain's son's debt and you own a Mizuchi heir.
🎭 Utsugi of the Nails, Female, a curse-bearer the same age as the character. A grey layered kimono with black prayer strips. She will show you her scars, and then ask to see yours.
🎭 Mizuchi Toranosuke, Male, the admiral's youngest son. Open sea-blue kimono with a wave crest. Get him out of the debt and he owes you a ship; tell his father and he never forgives you.

starts.name: Delver: The Salvage Licence
starts.info:
DELVER · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Pirate Graves Reef, The Asagiri Isles. A reef off the western cape littered with wrecks, where pirates were once hanged in chains.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 10-20)

The harbour guild has licensed salvage on the wrecks of Pirate Graves Reef, and nobody who has rowed out has come back with anything but a story. You bought the last licence from the harbourmaster, and the guild's boat has just grounded on the reef.

starts.name: Duelist: The Ninety-Nine
starts.info:
DUELIST · Fifty Stations Road · guided
📍 Duelists' Teahouse, The Asagiri Isles. A teahouse on the road where the Hundred-Duel Circuit's duelists stop to sign books and find opponents.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 3-15)

A duelist with ninety-nine duels waits at the Duelists' Teahouse for an opponent no one will accept. You just walked in.
🎭 Kagero the Sheathed, Male, a thin, polite swordsman in a faded travelling coat who sits in the teahouse's signing. Faded travelling coat over a plain grey kimono. Sit with him through a night without moving.
🎭 Ochiba, Female, a wandering duelist of the Hundred-Duel Circuit. Short ragged black hair, tired sharp eyes, worn dark hakama and a faded haori. Spar with her and she rates you; save her from the house's assassins and she does not know what to do with you.

starts.name: Ferry: The Magistrate on the Far Bank
starts.info:
FERRY · Miyako Plain · guided
📍 River Ferry Crossing, The Asagiri Isles. Where the road meets the great river, a flat ferry poles travellers across and porters carry the rest on their shoulders.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-10)

The river is rising, the ferry is not running, and a Shogunate magistrate on the far bank is offering a great deal to cross.
🎭 Rider Kanbei, Male, a veteran post rider. Short grey hair, calm eyes, Warden's coat. Help him decide what to do with the sealed order and he trusts you with the road's secrets.

starts.name: Festival: Night of the Hundred Ships
starts.info:
FESTIVAL · Saikai Free Port · guided
📍 Saikai, The Asagiri Isles. The free port town on the bay: warehouses, quays, foreign ships at anchor among the junks, and lantern-lit streets that never close.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 1-20)

Saikai blesses the trading fleet tonight: a hundred lit ships, a temple bell, and every smuggler in the port pretending to be a merchant.
🎭 Harbourmaster Watanuki, Male, the guild's harbourmaster. Sharp eyes, dark blue guild coat with brass buttons. Find the escort that took the humming chest north and he shows you the second ledger.
🎭 Notice-Keeper Kagura, Female, keeper of the Saikai harbour post's notice board. Indigo work kimono. Bring back proof of a bounty and she shows you the back board.
🎭 Widow Toki, Female, an old widow who sells bait and mends sails at the harbour post. A faded indigo kimono with tied-back sleeves. Sit down at her bait stall and she will tell you about the island nobody wants, and what it would cost to take it.

starts.name: Festival: Obon at Tasogare
starts.info:
FESTIVAL · Veilgate · guided
📍 Tasogare, The Asagiri Isles. The shrine city on the cliffs, its streets climbing to the great pale torii at the edge where the dead pass through, its lanterns drifting out over the Sea of Fog at night.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 10-40)

For three nights the dead come home to Tasogare. Lanterns float out from the cliffs, and one floats against the current.
🎭 Captain Shirasagi Ren, Female, a captain of the Veil Court's Ferry Division. Cold violet eyes, immaculate black officer's coat. Bring her a soul she failed to reach and she looks at you for the first time.
🎭 Officer Kurose Akio, Male, an officer of the Veil Court's Records wing. White officer's coat with a records crest. Show him the cut rope's end and he tells the party exactly whose order he followed, as if that ends it.
🎭 Lantern-Seller Oiwa, Female, a lantern-seller at the Pilgrim Post in Tasogare. Look at her list of lanterns that turn back.

starts.name: Fifty Stations Road: The Post Stable
starts.info:
FIFTY STATIONS ROAD · any tradition · guided
📍 Oiwake Station, The Asagiri Isles. The crossroads station where the highway forks: north for the capital, south down to Ember Strait, east for the marsh coast, west along the ash for the port.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-15)

Oiwake Station, the busiest stop on the post road: toll barriers, red lanterns in the pines, and riders who do not come back.
🎭 Station Master Ogiwara Tokuzo, Male, the post master of Oiwake Station's stables. Stable master's jacket and apron. Name the rider in front of his men and his hands go to the water bucket.
🎭 Post Clerk Tsuge Hanbei, Male, Clerk of Oiwake Station's barrier board. Earn his trust on three bounties and he hands you the missing list.

starts.name: Fox Road: The Broken Statue
starts.info:
FOX ROAD · Ayakashi Wood · guided
📍 Kitsune Shrine Road, The Asagiri Isles. A road of small fox shrines leading into the wood, each with a stone fox and a bowl of rice.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 10-15)

One fox statue on the Kitsune Shrine Road has been smashed, the shrine beyond it has gone dark, and every fox in the wood saw you pass it.
🎭 The Begging Monk of the Fox Road, Male, a cheerful young begging monk walking the road of fox shrines. Give him rice and he tells you who broke the statue.

starts.name: Granary: The Counted Shifts
starts.info:
GRANARY · Miyako Plain · guided
📍 Shogunate Rice Granary, The Asagiri Isles. A great timber granary on stilts where the plain's tax rice is stored before it goes to the capital.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 3-15)

The Shogunate's rice granary feeds the castle while the villages starve, and the Straw Masks have been counting its guards for months.
🎭 Sergeant Ishida, Male, Sergeant of the granary guard. Tired eyes, padded armour with a crane crest. Show him the pledge papers mean his granary feeds the guild, not the plain, and he looks the other way one night.

starts.name: Guest: The Lord's Retinue
starts.info:
GUEST · Fifty Stations Road · guided
📍 Seventh Station Inn, The Asagiri Isles. One of the busiest post stations: an official inn for lords, cheaper inns for everyone else, and a lantern gate that closes at dusk.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-10)

A lord's retinue arrives at the Seventh Station Inn tomorrow, the innkeeper is too friendly, and the Red Lanterns know the route.
🎭 Innkeeper Jinbei, Male, keeper of the Seventh Station Inn. Receding hair, brown apron over a kimono. Warn the lord's retinue, or stand guard, and he will never forgive you; or he will thank you forever, if the bandits lose.
🎭 Old Hisa of the Seventh Station, Female, the innkeeper's mother. Bright-eyed elderly woman in a plain kimono waiting at a post-road inn gate with a paper crane. Ask about the couriers of twenty years ago and she smiles at one name.

starts.name: Half-Yokai: The Great Tree
starts.info:
HALF-YOKAI · Ayakashi Wood · guided
📍 Two-Blooded Refuge, The Asagiri Isles. A hidden village under a great tree where children of humans and yokai live together, behind wards no hunter finds.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 10-30)

You are two-blooded, and the Refuge in the Ayakashi Wood took you in. Old Kagari has a favour to ask.
🎭 Old Kagari, Female, the founder of the Two-Blooded Refuge, who looks seventy and has looked it for a century. Bring the coast child home and the Refuge is yours to call on.
🎭 Kiyo of the Refuge, Female, a fox-blooded guardian of the Refuge's ward ring. Long red-gold hair, sharp amber eyes. She tests you with a trick; see through it and stay kind.

starts.name: Hinode Hold: The Sunrise Wall
starts.info:
HINODE HOLD · any tradition · guided
📍 Asahi Gate, The Asagiri Isles. The town under the breath hunters' fortress: hunters' mess halls, forges, and the gate through which every hunt rides out at dawn.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 15-45)

Asahi Gate, the Hold's southern door: hunters, orphans, sun-steel, and the long north beyond the wall.
🎭 Master Rensuke, Male, a Breath Master of the Hold. Hunter's black coat. Sit with him through a night watch and the party hears him not breathe.
🎭 Physician Ogata, Male, the fortress physician. Blood-spotted apron over dark clothes. Watch the sleepers with him and the two masters' secret is yours.

starts.name: Hostage: The Ward of the Inner Palace
starts.info:
HOSTAGE · Miyako Plain · guided
